verdict.rationale: The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

points.point: Earliest reference in the window: integration of the acquired distribution business plus offline pharmacy growth is framed as the path to HealthCo's 'strategic intent' over three years, before any demerger language appears.
points.quote: Transaction integration and healthy growth in offline pharmacy distribution revenues will drive Apollo HealthCo towards its stated strategic intent in the next 3 years.

points.point: The restructuring is still presented as a merger-plus-breakeven story, with Sanjiv Gupta quantifying the FY27 target for the combined entity at INR 25,000 crore of revenue and 6-7% EBITDA, against a then run-rate of ~INR 17,000 crore at 6.5% excluding digital losses.
points.quote: So, we are looking at about INR 25,000 crore of revenue and about 6% to 7% of EBITDA in FY 27.

points.quote: The Keimed merger process is also progressing well, which will further enhance scale and margin resilience in our Pharmacy business.

points.point: Sanjiv Gupta gave the margin bridge that underpins the 7% target: removing Apollo 24/7's operating losses and the ESOP charge (INR 100 cr in FY26, falling to a third thereafter) lifts the blended 3.2% to 6.4% even on then-current numbers.
points.quote: If I remove these two things, if I assume these two things even today and remove these losses and the ESOP cost, the new number that comes for the EBITDA percentage is 6.4%.

points.quote: So , technology, data, people, and product categories , all the four synergies should start playing out as this merger comes in place.

points.quote: The statutory processes for the restructuring within Apollo HealthCo and the Keimed merger continue to proceed as per plan, and we remain well positioned to capture the full benefit of scale within Apollo HealthCo.

points.quote: We have also made progress with respect to the regulatory integration process for the com posite scheme of Keimed merger and demerger of Apollo HealthCo and remain well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore in combined revenues with 7% EBITDA.

points.point: Obul Reddy itemised the approvals obtained (CCI, SEBI) and the NCLT filing, and confirmed Keimed had been cleaned up so that its subsidiaries are 100% owned before the merger.
points.quote: We have obtained Competition Commission approval and SEBI approval. We have filed with NCLT.

points.point: The purpose is stated in value terms for the first time in opening remarks — sharpening focus and unlocking long-term value across the integrated platform — in the same breath as HealthCo crossing INR 10,000 crore of annual revenue.
points.quote: During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long -term value across our integrated health care platform.

points.point: Timeline and end-state confirmed: NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on June 24, 2026, listing of Apollo Healthtech around end-December/early Q4 FY27, annualised revenue of INR 25,000 crore at listing.
points.quote: And hopefully, by Q4 FY27, end of December or early Q4 FY27 is when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed.

points.point: A second, separate disposal: AHLL's Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr revenue, INR 45 cr EBITDA) go into a Cloudnine-combined platform at INR 1,550 crore — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with INR 750 crore of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics.
points.quote: One is the valuation, which is clearly key to get a valuation of INR 1,500 for EBITDA at a multiple of 35 in this market is something that you cannot ignore.

points.point: The Scheme's stated core problem: the pharmacy/digital undertaking is a different business from hospitals and needs its own strategy, risk posture and growth path; separation gives each side focus, management and control.
points.quote: The Scheme would enable carving-out of the Identified Business Undertaking, which is distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company, necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory.

points.point: The Keimed leg is justified as consolidating pharmacy distribution into a single pure-play vehicle, with the Scheme also citing supply-chain integration, wider assortment, counterfeit prevention, administrative efficiency and board rationalisation.
points.quote: The Scheme would also result in consolidation of pharmacy distribution business of Transferor Company 1 and Transferor Company 2, in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution, enabling synergies;

points.point: Governance package embedded in the Scheme: a 12-member board with 6 independents, the AHL Promoter as Executive Chairperson, three promoter nominees, one AHEL nominee and one nominee for investor Rasmeli Limited, plus the Rasmeli-funded upside-sharing arrangement with Ms. Shobana Kamineni and identified employees.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all: the scheme filing is an amalgamation (absorption) of a subsidiary — the Transferor Company — into Ambuja Cements Ltd., the Transferee Company, and no business is being carved out. The stated starting point is ownership: the Transferee is already the promoter of the Transferor, holding 58.08% of its paid-up equity share capital (as on June 30, 2025) and 100% of its 8% non-convertible cumulative redeemable preference shares, and both are part of the Adani Group. Because 'both the companies are under the same line of business,' management argues the merger lets Ambuja 'absorb the business of Transferor Company completely for carrying on more effectively and beneficially.' The operating case given is integration economics: better resource utilization, reduced overheads, cost savings, economies of scale, elimination of duplicated efforts and streamlined compliance, plus 'reduction and rationalisation of multiple entities in the group.' The value case is stated only generically — enhanced business potential of the Transferor, value added to both companies and increased shareholders' value — with no margin, synergy-rupee or capacity figures in the rationale section. A second, distinct purpose is governance/shareholding: on effectiveness, certain Promoters/Promoter Group/related persons of the Transferor are to be reclassified from 'Promoter and Promoter Group' to 'Public' in the Transferee under SEBI LODR Regulation 31A, on the stated basis that they will not hold more than ten percent of total voting rights, exercise no direct or indirect control, hold no special rights or shareholder agreements, have no board seat or nominee director, are not KMP, and are neither wilful defaulters nor fugitive economic offenders. Process support is documented rather than argued: two valuation reports dated December 17, 2024 (BDO Valuation Advisory LLP for the Transferor; GT Valuation Advisors Private Limited for the Transferee) with fairness opinions from Vivro Financial Services (Transferor) and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities (Transferee), unanimous approval by both boards on December 17, 2024 (6 directors at the Transferor, 8 at the Transferee, including Gautam Adani as Chairman), NSE as Designated Stock Exchange, no-objection applications to the exchanges on January 3, 2025, and complaint reports to BSE (March 6, 2025) and NSE (March 25, 2025, updated June 16, 2025). Nothing in the texts attributes the transaction to a request from investors, lenders or partners.
verdict.evolution: The only tagged call material is February 2026 (transcript header: January 30, 2026), and it contains no mention of any separation, demerger or amalgamation — the Q&A with Rajesh Ravi of HDFC Securities covers clinker commissioning and prior-period tax refunds only, so no call-by-call evolution of the idea can be traced from these texts. The documented timeline comes entirely from the filing: audit committee, independent-directors committee, M&A committee and both boards acted on December 17, 2024 on valuation reports of the same date; exchange no-objection applications followed on January 3, 2025; complaint reports went to BSE on March 6, 2025 and NSE on March 25, 2025, with an updated NSE complaint report on June 16, 2025; share-capital data is stated as on August 31, 2025 and the 58.08% holding as on June 30, 2025. The only change visible across the sequence is procedural (exchange queries raised by NSE/BSE and addressed, and the updated complaint report), not a change in rationale or structure. On the one call, management's forward narrative is organic capacity expansion — four new 4 mt kilns plus a fifth line in Assam — rather than any portfolio separation.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation of a 58.08%-owned subsidiary into Ambuja (the Transferee is also the promoter of the Transferor and holds 100% of its 8% non-convertible cumulative redeemable preference shares), justified by the two companies being in the same line of business.
points.quote: As both the companies are under the same line of business, this amalgamation will enable the Transferee Company to absorb the business of Transferor Company completely for carrying on more effectively and beneficially.

points.point: The operating rationale is integration economics — consolidating operations for cheaper, simpler management.
points.quote: This includes better resource utilization, reduced overheads, cost savings, economies of scale, elimination of duplicated efforts, and streamlined compliance requirements through amalgamation.

points.point: A structural aim is cutting the number of group legal entities.
points.quote: The amalgamation will lead t o reduction and rationalisation of multiple entities in the group.

points.point: The value claim is stated only in general terms, without quantification.
points.quote: The amalgamation will enhanc e business potential of the Transferor Company, add value to both the companies, and ultimately increase the shareholders’ value.

points.point: A separate purpose is reclassifying certain Transferor promoters to 'Public' in Ambuja under SEBI LODR Regulation 31A, conditioned on a sub-10% voting stake, no control, no special rights, no board seat and no KMP role.
points.quote: Accordingly, reclassification of the Promoters/Persons belonging to the Promoter Group/Persons related to the Promoters Seeking Reclassification of the Transferor Company from ‘Promoter and Promoter Group’ category to ‘Public’ category in the Transferee Company has been contemplated upon the coming into effect of this Scheme, in accordance with the requirements of Regulation 31A of the Securities and Exchange

points.point: Independent valuation and fairness support was obtained on December 17, 2024, and both boards approved unanimously that day; the Transferee's board meeting was chaired by Gautam Adani with eight directors attending by video conference.
points.quote: None of the directors of the Transferee Company who attended the meeting voted against the Scheme.

points.point: Management's growth narrative on this call is organic clinker capex: four kilns of about 4 mt each — the three being commissioned over the next three to four months plus Mundra — totalling roughly 16 mt of clinker, which at a ~1.5x conversion implies about 24 mt of grinding capacity.
points.quote: So 4 million tons x 4 million tons, 16 million tons x ballpark 1.5 million tons.

points.point: A fifth 4 mt clinker line in Assam has been agreed with the state government (greenfield), alongside brownfield Mundra and Maratha and Penna due up in February, taking the programme to about 20 mt of clinker.
points.quote: by the way, Assam also, we have signed up -- we have entered into agreement with the government in terms of setting up another 1 line of 4 million tons in Assam, which is the fifth one, by the way.

points.point: Asked about below-EBITDA value unlocking at ACC and Ambuja, the CFO framed prior-period tax refunds as a working-capital and balance-sheet item, together with resolution of a substantial share of legal cases — not as part of any corporate restructuring.
points.quote: Tax refunds of the prior period, I think we have done a major efforts on that and unlocked the working capital.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation benefits are claimed anywhere. For the amalgamation the filing expects Ambuja to absorb the subsidiary's business, run it more effectively, and gain better resource utilization, lower overheads, cost savings, scale economies, no duplicated effort and simpler compliance; fewer group entities; enhanced business potential, added value to both companies and higher shareholder value; plus promoter-to-public reclassification. No margin, capital or valuation numbers given.
verdict.gaps: No separation is discussed, named or quantified. The Transferor is never named here; no synergy, margin, capital-structure, tax or share-exchange-ratio figures; no investor, lender or partner request.

verdict.measure_notes: No separate revenue or profit line for Sanghi Industries Limited appears on the tagged pages. Sanghi was amalgamated into Ambuja Cements Limited (w.e.f. April 1, 2024); the only Sanghi-specific figures are purchase-accounting entries — goodwill addition of 540.64 crore and intangible-asset additions of 2,094.53 crore (mining reserves 2,044.53, dealer network rights 50.00) plus 10.69 crore accumulated amortisation on amalgamation (Annual Report 2026 — pages 240, 241). verdict.rationale: Astral Limited says it has grown into two distinct verticals — (a) Plumbing: pipes, fittings, water tanks, faucets and sanitaryware, and (b) Chemicals: adhesives, polyvinyl acetate (PVA), cyanoacrylates, solvent cements, silicone sealants, epoxy resins, construction chemicals, putties and allied products, further scaled into specialty chemicals through recent strategic acquisitions. The Board (approval dated June 25, 2026) adopted a Composite Scheme that (i) demerges the Chemicals/Chemical Undertaking of Astral Limited (the Demerged Company) on a going-concern basis into Astral Chemie Limited, formerly Astral Coatings Private Limited, a 100% subsidiary that already manufactures and supplies paints and coatings for residential, commercial and industrial end-users, and (ii) amalgamates Al-Aziz Plastics Private Limited, another 100% subsidiary making electrofusion fittings, compression fittings, saddles, electrical fittings and allied accessories for gas, water, electricity and solar distribution/transmission, into Astral Limited because it is complementary to the Plumbing Business. The size cited: the Demerged Undertaking's turnover for the year ended March 31, 2026 was ₹12,663 million, 21% of the Demerged Company's total turnover, against Astral Limited's standalone FY26 turnover of ₹59,076 million and net worth of ₹41,058 million; Al-Aziz was small at ₹373 million turnover and ₹215 million net worth. The stated problems it solves: each business has different products, customer segments, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles and growth opportunities and operates under different macroeconomic environments, regulatory frameworks and market risks, so one corporate roof blurred focus — the demerger puts chemicals plus paints under a single dedicated platform run by a focused leadership team with deep sector-specific expertise, and isolates the operational, cyclical and compliance risks of each business. It is also framed as a capital-structure fix: each entity can independently determine capex, working capital, funding and investment strategy based on its own growth prospects, capital intensity, cash-flow profile and risk-return characteristics, and as separately listed entities both can independently access debt and equity capital and attract strategic and financial investors with different investment objectives. For Al-Aziz, the added reasons are integration of its manufacturing facilities, products and customer relationships with Plumbing, plus reduced legal and regulatory compliance burden and administrative costs. Mechanics are value-neutral to holders: no cash consideration, 1 equity share of Astral Chemie (₹1 face value) for every 1 Astral share (₹1 face value), a mirrored shareholding pattern (promoters 54.22%, public 45.78% post-Scheme versus 100% promoter-held pre-Scheme), Astral's existing shares in Astral Chemie cancelled, no change in Astral's own shareholding, and listing sought on NSE and BSE.
verdict.evolution: The reasoning cannot be traced call by call from the material supplied: the only earnings-call passage provided is [May 2025], and it is entirely about end-market sizing — PVC at about 4.5 million tons in fiscal 25, CPVC at roughly 2.5 lakh tons or about 5% of PVC, and fire-sprinkler pipes as the next leg of CPVC demand — with no mention of a demerger, of the chemicals vertical, or of Astral Coatings/Astral Chemie. The separation therefore appears in these texts only at the Board approval of the Composite Scheme on June 25, 2026, sized off FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) financials, by which point Astral Coatings Private Limited had already been renamed Astral Chemie Limited and the chemicals portfolio had been expanded 'through recent strategic acquisitions' into specialty chemicals — the one hint of a build-up preceding the announcement. One drafting shift is visible inside the filing itself: the rationale annexure and disclosure tables describe the demerger of the 'Chemical Undertaking'/'Chemicals Business Undertaking', while the press-release text describes 'the demerger of its Adhesive Business', a narrower label for the same undertaking.

points.point: Management sized CPVC at about 2.5 lakh tonnes versus a roughly 4.5 million tonne PVC industry in fiscal 25 — about 5% — calling it a niche product today, confined mainly to hot-and-cold internal plumbing. Nothing in this passage touches the separation.
points.quote: It is about 2 and half lakh tons now.

points.point: Kairav Engineer said the real CPVC expansion depends on fire-sprinkler pipes, where Astral holds UL and local-body approvals, because a building uses more fire pipes than plumbing pipes; Sandeep Engineer added that standards changes are still needed.
points.quote: CPVC real value unlocking will happen when the ■re products pick up.

points.point: The Chemicals Business is described as having diversified across adhesives, PVA, cyanoacrylates, solvent cements, silicone sealants, epoxy resins, construction chemicals and putties, and scaled into specialty chemicals via recent acquisitions, all complementing Astral Chemie's existing paints and coatings business.
points.quote: The reorganisation will consolidate the Chemicals Business of Demerged Company  with the existing paints and coatings business of the Resulting Company  under a single, dedicated corporate platform managed by a focused leadership team with deep sector -specific expertise.

points.point: Size of the carve-out is quantified: the Demerged Undertaking turned over ₹12,663 million in FY26, 21% of Astral's total turnover (standalone FY26 turnover ₹59,076 million, net worth ₹41,058 million).
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended March 31, 2026 stood at ₹  12,663 million .

points.point: Capital-allocation independence is the fourth stated principle: each business sets its own capex, working capital and funding according to its own capital intensity and cash-flow profile, and the demerger isolates each one's operational, cyclical and compliance risks.
points.quote: The reorganisation will enable each business to independently determine its capital expenditure, working- capital requirements, funding and investment strategies based on their respective growth prospects, capital intensity, cash- flow profile and risk -return characteristics.

points.point: Separate listing is justified as widening the investor and funding base rather than as an immediate valuation claim — no re-rating or multiple is asserted anywhere in the rationale.
points.quote:
As separately listed entities, the Resulting Company  and Demerged Company will 
have the flexibility, subject to Applicable Laws, to independently access debt and 
equity capital and attract strategic and financial investors interested in different 
investment objectives, thereby aligning investment strategies and risk profiles to each 
business.

points.point: Management teams are to be freed to run their own plans: independent capacity expansion, new products, new markets and their own bolt-on acquisitions and collaborations — the same language is repeated for the Al-Aziz amalgamation.
points.quote:
The reorganisation will enable the respective management teams to independently 
formulate and execute business plans, undertake capacity expansion, develop new 
products, enter new markets and pursue focused acquisitions, collaborations and other 
growth opportunities relevant to their respective businesses.

points.point: The simultaneous amalgamation folds Al-Aziz Plastics (FY26 turnover ₹373 million, net worth ₹215 million; electrofusion and compression fittings, saddles, electrical fittings) into Astral's Plumbing Business, with compliance-cost reduction cited explicitly; its shares held by Astral are extinguished and it is dissolved without winding up.
points.quote: The amalgamation will enable the integration of its manufacturing facilities and capabilities, products, and customer relationships with the Plumbing Busi ness, while also reducing legal and regulatory compliances burden and related administrative costs.

points.point: Shareholders are kept whole on a mirror basis: 1-for-1 share issue at ₹1 face value, no cash consideration, no change in Astral's shareholding pattern, and Astral Chemie moving from 100% promoter-held to promoters 54.22% / public 45.78%, with NSE and BSE listing sought.
points.quote:
“1 (One) Equity Share of Resulting Company of a face 
value of ₹1/ - each, fully paid- up shall be issued for every 
1 (One) Equity Shares of a face value of ₹ 1/- each, fully 
paid- up held in Demerged Company”

points.point: The announcement frames the split as a response to two verticals having structurally diverged, requiring separate administrative control — the overarching 'why now'.
points.quote:
Each business has evolved into a distinct business vertical with different products, customer 
segments, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles and growth opportunities, demanding 
focused operational, financial and administrative expertise.

verdict.what_management_expects: Astral Chemie: chemicals combined with paints and coatings on one dedicated platform under focused leadership, yielding operational efficiencies, cost optimisation, specialisation, pooled R&D and technologies, and its own capex, working-capital and funding calls. Astral: plumbing-only focus, strengthened by Al-Aziz's fittings and lower compliance and administrative costs. Both: separate listings, independent debt and equity access, investors matched to each risk profile, isolated cyclical risk.
verdict.gaps: No call discussed the separation: no margin, valuation, debt-allocation, royalty or management-split detail; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it; "Adhesive" versus "Chemicals" undertaking unreconciled.

Segment revenue is external only — the notes state there were no inter-segment sales in any year. Segment PAT is not disclosed; no segment-level balance of tax exists. Investor presentations give the same business as 'Paints and Adhesives Business' EBITDA (FY24 2,031; FY25 1,948) and PBT before exceptional item (FY24 1,334; FY25 1,005) — Presentation May 2025 page 60. verdict.rationale: Management frames the separation as a strategic re-alignment of a company that had grown into two very different businesses: Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry on one side, and Space, Meteorology and Hydrology on the other, the latter being carved into Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL), a wholly owned subsidiary that will be listed separately while AMPL continues as a pure-play Defence and Aerospace company retaining its JVs (Astra Rafael Comsys) and other wholly owned subsidiaries. The stated objective is sharper strategic and operational focus, with dedicated management teams free to pursue sector-specific growth, plus enhanced governance and accountability, a simpler corporate structure, clearer investment propositions and a broader investor base. The Scheme filing is explicit that Space/Met/Hydrology 'operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile', so it needs a differentiated growth strategy and its own capital allocation, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests. The press release adds the capital angle bluntly: Space and Weather is a scaled-up, profitable, high-growth opportunity in satellite design/assembly and satellite data, but it is capital-intensive and execution-dependent, and the demerger 'creates the structural clarity to attract capital and talent at scale'. The numbers cited are modest but real: the demerged undertaking did roughly INR157 crores of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of AMPL's total (space plus meteorology was ~16% of FY26 revenue); cumulative ISRO orders of over INR750 crores across two decades with INR250 crores still to execute by FY28, and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts with a INR285 crores book to FY28; at December 2025 the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores already contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology/hydrology. Consideration is a 1:1 share entitlement (one INR2 ASTPL share for every INR2 AMPL share), no cash, so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters indicatively 6.45%, public 93.55%), with listing sought on BSE and NSE and completion targeted by Q1 FY28. Leadership was split to match: Managing Director S. Gurunatha Reddy stepped down on 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL as a Director, Dr M. V. Reddy became MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026, and CFO Rahul Rungta had already moved to ASTPL in February 2026. The texts name no investor, lender or partner as having demanded the split; it is presented throughout as board-initiated, with the benefit framed as 'unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaces obliquely as a valuation argument: on 14 Aug 2025 Atim Kabra says the separately incorporated space subsidiary is 'very, very valuable' given how thinly-revenued space peers are priced, and on 13 Nov 2025 he extrapolates space alone to near AMPL's whole market capitalisation while flagging heavy space investment and Astra SAT-1; on 13 Feb 2026 he turns to financing, saying the balance sheet must be 'creative' so blue-sky projects are not starved, and teases 'a few very interesting options'. Structurally it moves fast after that: CFO Rahul Rungta is shifted to ASTPL on 11-12 Feb 2026, the Board grants in-principle approval on 27 Feb 2026 with a same-day press release (revised the same day), and SGR announces it on the 27 May 2026 call. The Board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on 10 June 2026 with the 1:1 ratio and the INR157 crores / 13.58% disclosure, SGR's exit as MD was confirmed on 10 Aug 2026 effective 30 Sep 2026, and BSE/NSE observation letters with no adverse observations/no objection arrived on 29 Oct 2026.

points.point: A year before the demerger was announced, management had already carved space into a separate wholly owned subsidiary (Astra Space Technologies Private Limited) with its own hiring and Bangalore clean rooms, and Atim Kabra pitched it as undervalued inside AMPL on a space order book of about INR230-239 crores.
points.quote: And given where companies with very limited indigenous capabilities are valued, you might find that our space business is actually very, very valuable.

points.point: Kabra sharpened the hidden-value argument, saying space peers with almost no revenue were being valued at $750-800 million and that extrapolating Astra's space business alone approached AMPL's entire market capitalisation.
points.quote: Companies are raising money at like $750 million, $800 million valuation with hardly any revenue numbers to their credit.

points.point: Two weeks before the Board's in-principle approval, Kabra devoted his remarks to the criticality of adequate financing for development and 'blue sky' projects and hinted at structural options to come, while the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology and hydrology.
points.quote: So watch the space. There are a few very interesting options as they crystallize, we'll be letting you know.

points.point: S. G. Reddy announced the Board's in-principle approval of the demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business and listed the objectives: dedicated management teams, better governance, a simpler structure and clearer investment propositions, with the formal scheme to follow within weeks; space and meteorology were ~16% of FY26 revenue of INR1,157 crores.
points.quote: The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.

points.point: Management tied the restructuring to global as well as Indian opportunity and to capital allocation and efficiency over the medium to long term, alongside FY27 guidance of 15-20% growth and FY26 operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores.
points.quote: Furthermore, this restructuring will position us to capitalize on emerging opportunities both in India and globally.

points.point: The 27 Feb 2026 press release states the purpose as unlocking shareholder value and creating two focused listed platforms - AMPL for Defence and Aerospace, ASTPL for Space, Meteorology and Hydrology - and lists broader investor base, better oversight and less structural complexity as benefits.
points.quote: The proposed demerger is aimed at unlocking shareholder value and enhancing strategic focus across business verticals.

points.point: The same release argues the space and weather business is profitable and high-growth but capital-hungry and execution-dependent, and that the separation is what makes it possible to raise capital and hire for it at scale, on a 20-year base of over INR750 crores of cumulative ISRO orders and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts.
points.quote: The Indian and global markets are opening simultaneously, India's geopolitical positioning is aligned with this opportunity, and the demerger of ASTPL creates the structural clarity required to attract capital and talent at scale.

points.point: The 10 June 2026 Scheme of Arrangement filing gives the formal rationale, including that the segment faces a different regulatory and risk environment and needs its own strategy, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners and lenders.
points.quote: The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.

points.point: The filing sizes the demerged undertaking and sets the terms: no cash consideration, a 1:1 share entitlement ratio so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% indicatively), transfer on a going-concern basis, and listing on BSE and NSE targeted by Q1 FY28.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores, representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.

points.point: Management was reorganised around the split: CFO Rahul Rungta moved to ASTPL in February 2026, MD S. Gurunatha Reddy resigned effective 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL's board, and Dr M. V. Reddy was elevated to MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026; BSE and NSE issued no-adverse-observation/no-objection letters on 29 October 2026.
points.quote: In continuation to my earlier letter dated 03/04/2026 informing my resignation from the post of Managing Director wish to inform you that I am resigning from the position Directorship also with effect from the close of business hours on 30th September, 2026, to oversee the ongoing demerger of the Space and Meteorology business pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement.

verdict.what_management_expects: AMPL: a pure-play defence/aerospace company keeping JVs and subsidiaries, with simpler structure, focused management and better capital allocation. ASTPL: an independently listed, profitable, high-growth space-and-weather platform spanning upstream hardware, integration and data, able to attract sector-specific investors, partners, lenders and talent. Both: sharper focus, improved operational efficiency, clearer investment propositions and unlocked shareholder value over the medium to long term.
verdict.gaps: No valuation basis, standalone ASTPL financials, margins, capex, debt or working-capital split, transaction costs, or who initiated it; calls never field demerger questions.

verdict.segment_name: Space (sector-wise sales line; the Demerged Undertaking is the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business, for which no combined line is given)
verdict.measure_notes: No profit line exists for this business: the company reports a SINGLE product segment under Ind AS 108 (AR2024 p191/p270, AR2025 p215/p288, AR2026 p251/p326), so there is no segment result/EBIT/EBITDA/PBT by business. Revenue shown is standalone 'Sector-wise Sales' from MD&A (AR2026 p191) — external revenue; 'Exports (including deemed exports)' of Rs. 16,228 lakhs (FY26) / 10,959 lakhs (FY25) is a separate line there, so any space/met export content is excluded from the Space figure. Meteorology is reported combined as 'Metrology/Civil Telecom/Others' (FY26 4,584; FY25 3,437) and Hydrology has no revenue line at all.

verdict.rationale: Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.
verdict.evolution: On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

points.point: An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years.
points.quote: We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.

points.point: Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases.
points.quote: And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.

points.point: Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses.
points.quote: So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.

points.point: The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex.
points.quote: This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.

points.point: An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point.
points.quote: Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.

points.point: The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin.
points.quote: Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.

points.point: Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total.
points.quote: In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.

points.point: Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32.
points.quote: And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.

points.point: The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it.
points.quote: The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.

points.point: The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies.
points.quote: The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.

points.point: Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26.
points.quote: the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements;

points.point: Stated benefit two: a distinct legal entity lets Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific capital, investors, acquisitions and partnerships, with simpler ownership and intra-group arrangements cancelled or rationalised.
points.quote: the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders;

points.point: Consideration is 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2; ARL holders get 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL keeps 51%, so ACPL remains a subsidiary and ARL holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest; listing on BSE and NSE via the Rule 19(7) exemption.
points.quote: Overall, the shareholders of ARL will hold 100% of the ultimate beneficial economic interest in the Resultant Company, ACPL ( direct holding of 49% and indirect holding of 51% throughARL).

points.point: Days before the Scheme, the Finance and Investment Committee funded the shell resultant company: a ₹74,86,45,106 rights issue of 37,43,22,553 ₹2 shares in ACPL (incorporated Oct 11, 2021; nil turnover in FY24, FY25 and FY26) to meet data centre and cloud development funding.
points.quote: ACPL proposes to raise the fund to meet the funding requirement for development of its data centres and cloud business.

points.point: The press release frames the outcome as two independent platforms — ARL in real estate/infrastructure and Ashok Cloud in data centres, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure and DC/DR services — citing separate growth trajectories, operational priorities and capital needs.
points.quote: "Our real estate, infrastructure business and Data Centre & Cloud Services Business have evolved into two distinct platforms, each with its own growth trajectory, operational priorities, and capital needs.

verdict.what_management_expects: Ashok Cloud: pure-play digital-infrastructure valuation and independent market recognition, sector-specific growth capital, partnerships and acquisitions, dedicated leadership, consolidated ownership (75% EBITDA-margin colocation/cloud, 357 MW plan, ~₹20,000 cr capex). Anant Raj: sharper focus on real estate, infrastructure and hospitality, low debt, continued execution. Both: operational efficiency, agility, faster decision-making, transparency, unlocked shareholder value, with holders participating directly in each.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention the demerger; no appointed date, debt/cash/asset split, valuation or swap basis, why ARL keeps 51%, how ₹20,000 cr capex gets funded, or listing timeline.

Both standalone and consolidated accounts state a single reportable segment (real estate development) under Ind AS 108, so no segment result/EBIT/EBITDA/PBT is disclosed for the data centre business. The only own figure is a revenue disclosure in the quarterly presentations — 'Revenue from Data Center, Infrastructure and Allied services', a component of consolidated revenue from operations (external; inter-segment treatment not stated). All headline Revenue/EBITDA/PAT charts are consolidated company totals that merely 'include Data Center & Cloud Services', not the business standalone.

Annual Report 2025 — page 154 (consolidated P&L only; no data centre breakout)
Presentation May 2026 — page 7
