verdict.latest_quarter_notes: Q4 FY26 EBITDA of 566 is the total Power segment (FY26 full year 1,623 = 1,534 discontinued + 89 continuing), not merchant power alone; that page gives sales volumes and realisations, no segment revenue. The Oct 2026 (Q2 FY27) presentation carries no Power segment, the demerger being effective 1 May 2026.
verdict.not_found: No segment PAT/net profit, no quarterly Power revenue, no standalone merchant-power entity (TSPL/Athena/Meenakshi) P&L; FY2024 has no continuing/discontinued Power split.

verdict.rationale: Triveni's board approved a Composite Scheme of Arrangement on 10 December 2024 with two legs: amalgamating its ~61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL, the Shamli sugar/distillery unit) into TEIL, and demerging the Power Transmission Business (PTB — high-speed/turbo gearboxes at Mysuru plus the incubating defence business) into Triveni Power Transmission Limited (TPTL), a wholly-owned subsidiary, for separate listing. Management framed it consistently as 'value unlocking' and, by Feb 2026, 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' — the logic being that PTB is a technology business with robust, predictable economics (FY25 turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, margins >34%; order booking ₹475 crore) sitting inside a conglomerate whose sugar and ethanol businesses are, in Tarun Sawhney's words, 'regulated from every corner' on both input and output pricing, producing mercurial quarterly outcomes that investors (notably Bharat Shah, Feb 2025) said made the group hard to value. Separation also lets PTB fund its own growth: the board approved capex in three tranches totalling ₹340 crore (gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026, plus a defence facility of just north of ₹100 crore); ₹231 crore was incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore was defence, and management said TPTL 'is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet' to complete it. Critically, TEIL deliberately retained ~30% of TPTL rather than a clean 100% distribution — Sawhney said the defence business, co-located in Mysuru and sharing the same facility and offices, needs group balance-sheet backing to secure pre-qualifications and the ability to bid, and he cited the earlier Triveni Turbine separation as a positive precedent, pushing back on investor Resham Jain's holdco-discount objection. The SSEL leg removes a separately listed, loss-making subsidiary (plantation-white sugar selling at a discount, white-fly-hit recoveries, two breakdowns, a Shamli distillery that had not operated since acquisition) and folds its crush, varietal and distillery de-bottlenecking upside into TEIL's commodities platform. Mechanically: SSEL holders got 100 TEIL shares (₹1 FV) per 137 SSEL shares; TEIL holders get 1 TPTL share (₹2 FV) per 3 TEIL shares; scheme appointed date 1 April 2025, demerger appointed date 1 April 2026. Post-approval ICRA reaffirmed TEIL's long-term rating at AA+ Stable, lifting it from 'under watch', and management committed to separate boards, published results and earnings calls for TEIL and TPTL from Q1 FY27.
verdict.evolution: The scheme was announced on 10 December 2024 and first discussed on the Feb 2025 call, where Sawhney tied it to 'value unlocking', guided to NCLT approval by end-CY2025, and defended the retained ~30% stake in TPTL against investor pushback; the same call approved the incremental ₹60 crore gears capex. Through Jun 2025 and Aug 2025 the file sat with SEBI ('we're following up continuously with SEBI', possibly 'another 30-odd days'), and investors began asking for granular PTB disclosure ahead of a separate listing, which management accepted; by Nov 2025 the stock exchanges had cleared it (observation letters 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings were set for end-November/early December, with TPTL also acquiring the Swiss subsidiary Triveni Power Transmission GmbH. Shareholders and creditors approved on 7 December 2025, and on the Feb 2026 call Sawhney said 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies' and described systems work to let TPTL 'hit the ground sprinting'. NCLT sanctioned it (orders 7 and 18 May 2026), effective 19 May 2026; on the Jun 2026 call Sawhney called it a 'historic call', guided to a TPTL listing by end-August 2026, and TPTL shares were in fact allotted on 28 July 2026 and listed on 12 October 2026.

points.point: First investor call after the 10 December 2024 board approval; Sawhney explicitly tied the two-part scheme (SSEL amalgamation into TEIL; PTB demerger into wholly-owned TPTL) to value unlocking as a board priority.
points.quote: I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.

points.point: Asked by Resham Jain (DSP) why TEIL would keep ~30% of TPTL instead of a clean split that avoids a holdco discount, Sawhney gave two reasons: the positive Triveni Turbine precedent, and the need for group balance-sheet strength to win defence pre-qualifications.
points.quote: The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.

points.point: He added that the defence business is co-located with PTB in Mysuru and must not be handicapped by the separation, which he said was being done 'because it's the right time'.
points.quote: we should not handicap a business just because we're separating the business, the Power Transmission business because it's the right time, we are separating it with the Defence business, which is co-located in the same city and utilising the same facility and offices that exist today.

points.point: Investor Bharat Shah (ASK) framed the core valuation problem the demerger addresses: PTB has robust, predictable economics while the rest of the group produces 'mercurial' outcomes; Sawhney conceded sugar and ethanol are regulated on both input and output pricing.
points.quote: Turning then to large businesses, as far as Sugar and Ethanol are concerned, you are absolutely right. They are regulated industries, they are regulated from every corner. The pricing of your raw material and the pricing of your end product.

points.point: The same board meeting approved an incremental ~₹60 crore of gears capex (gears only, not defence), taking PTB gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026 — the growth the separately listed entity is meant to fund.
points.quote: The Board meeting of the Directors concluded yesterday had an important announcement of an incremental capex of ₹60 crore for the enhancement of capacity in the Power Transmission business . This will take the gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026.

points.point: Initial regulatory timeline guidance: NCLT approval expected by end of calendar 2025.
points.quote: As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.

points.point: PTB's FY25 standalone performance — the asset being separated — was record: turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%), margins above 34%, order booking over ₹475 crore, with growth not costing profitability.
points.quote: And the PB IT grew by 18.4% to ₹126.8 crore with PBIT margins in excess of 34%, which is a very much in line with our long -term average.

points.point: Scheme status: pending with SEBI, with NCLT and court-convened meetings to follow; Sawhney reiterated separation of the PTB business by Q4 FY26 / middle of Q1 CY2026.
points.quote: With respect t o the scheme of arrangement that is underway, I'd like to just briefly comment that this lies with SEBI at this particular point in time. We are awaiting the approval for SEBI.

points.point: Resham Jain asked for far more granular PTB disclosure precisely because it would be separately listed — an investor-driven push for transparency that management accepted.
points.quote: I would request maybe if you can start giving more colour on the Power Transmission business from like what kind of customers you are targeting ? What kind of mix you have between various industries going forward? That would be very helpful , given that this is going to get separately listed in the next one year.

points.point: Still awaiting regulatory clearance; Sawhney flagged possible slippage of about 30 days but held to Q4 FY26, and said the board would run workshops on what post-demerger TEIL does with its cash flows.
points.quote: The amalgamation with Sir Shadi Lal and the demerger of the Power Transmission business. We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.

points.point: On post-demerger TEIL, Sawhney said the board intends to evaluate options for deploying the commodities businesses' cash flows to rebuild the FY23-type margin structure, but had nothing concrete to share.
points.quote: Now with respect to Triveni, after the demerger, looking at other things, we have some time for that demerger to happen, yet the thought process is on and the Board is going to conduct workshops, et c., and evaluate a series of different options.

points.point: Stock exchange approvals received (observation letters dated 7 and 11 August 2025); NCLT stakeholder meetings scheduled for end-November and early December 2025, keeping Q4 FY26 on track. TPTL also bought 100% of the Swiss entity Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, building out the standalone export engine.
points.quote: The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT . The meetings of stakeholders under the NCL T process has been scheduled for the end of November and early December for the 2 companies.

points.point: Disclosed PTB order-book split showing the defence weighting that justified keeping group balance-sheet support: of a ~₹395 crore book, ₹185 crore was long-tenure and 'the vast majority of that is defence'.
points.quote: In terms of the break up of short -tenure and long -tenure, as of September 2026, our short -tenure is ₹210 crore and long is ₹185 crore .

points.point: The clearest statement of purpose: unlock value and drive operational efficiencies. Shareholders and creditors approved in December 2025; an NCLT hearing was set for February 2026.
points.quote: Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.

points.point: Standalone-readiness work was underway so TPTL could operate as an independent listed company with TEIL-level efficiency from day one.
points.quote: Looking at the Power Transmission business, gaining a lot of skill sets in terms of ability to operate as a separate company. A lot of systems work is being done as we speak to let them hit the ground sprinting, frankly speaking, and have the same kind of efficiencies that we've had at Triveni Engineering.

points.point: Sawhney signalled the split was imminent and thanked investors for years of feedback on the combined entity's call.
points.quote: I think the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.

points.point: On the SSEL leg, Sawhney conceded Shamli would still be loss-making in SS 2025-26 (white fly in ratoon, urea dosing by farmers, two breakdowns) and that turnaround comes the following year — context for folding it into TEIL.
points.quote: Shamli being a new unit and the relationships speak new, our sway over the farming population needs to improve and increase

points.point: Scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval; Sawhney called it a 'historic' call, with the scheme appointed date 1 April 2025 and the demerger appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.

points.point: A concrete financial benefit of the approval: ICRA reaffirmed TEIL's long-term rating at AA+ Stable and removed the 'under watch' status the pending scheme had caused.
points.quote: I am very proud to announce that post the scheme having been approved, ICRA has reaffirmed our long -term credit rating as AA+ Stable, lifting it from its previous under watch status.

points.point: Total approved PTB capex is ₹340 crore in three tranches (₹700 crore of gears output, excluding defence); ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026 of which ₹78 crore was defence; TPTL will carry the remaining ~₹109 crore on its own balance sheet.
points.quote: Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.

points.point: Independent listing described as the business's strategic push, with the Swiss subsidiary and new AVL qualifications (pumps, compressors, gas, defence test rigs) as the growth engine; FY26 order book just under ₹500 crore, 25% higher.
points.quote: Within the Power Transmission Business, our strategic push to clearly move towards, of course, the independent listing of TPTL.

points.point: Asked directly whether margins change after the demerger, CFO Suresh Taneja guided to continuity at roughly 35% PBIT for the standalone PTB.
points.quote: As regards to the PTB business, it has got its own dynamics, as a matter of fact. So far, we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT. I think the same trend is expected to continue in future also.

points.point: Record dates and listing plan: SSEL share issuance record date 3 June 2026, TEIL/TPTL record date within four weeks, TPTL listing expected by end-August 2026, with separate Q1 FY27 results and earnings calls for both companies.
points.quote: In a nutshell, one is anticipating that by the end of August, we will have a listing of Triveni Power Transmissions Limited.

points.point: Sawhney framed the split as an inflection point, pairing TPTL's growth trajectory with excitement about TEIL's remaining commodities and water businesses.
points.quote: We're at a very important inflection point for Triveni. The growth trajectory for TPTL looks extremely robust.

points.point: Demerger consideration: 1 TPTL share of ₹2 face value for every 3 TEIL shares of ₹1 face value, issued without any application by shareholders.
points.quote: For every 3(three) equity shares of the Demerged Company with a face value of INR 1 each held in the Demerged Company, every equity shareholder of the Demerged Company shall, without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 1 (One) equity share of the Resulting Company with a face value of INR 2 each, credited as fully paid up on the same terms and conditions of issue as prevalent in the Demerged Company

points.point: On 28 July 2026 TPTL allotted 7,34,54,338 shares to TEIL shareholders out of 10,47,54,338 total, leaving TEIL with 3,13,00,000 shares (~29.9%) — exactly the retained stake Sawhney defended on the Feb 2025 call.
points.quote: Accordingly, the Company ceased to be a subsidiary and become an associate of TEIL.

points.point: The amalgamation leg: SSEL shareholders received 100 TEIL shares of ₹1 each for every 137 SSEL shares of ₹10 each (record date 3 June 2026; 14,65,048 shares allotted 9 June 2026), and SSEL was dissolved without winding up.
points.quote: For every 137 (One Hundred and Thirty Seven) equity shares of the Amalgamating Company of face value of INR 10 each held in the Amalgamating Company, every equity shareholder of the Amalgamating Company, shall without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 100 (One Hundred) equity shares of face value of INR 1 each of the Amalgamated Company, credited as fully paid

points.point: The split of cost of acquisition between the two entities gives the only quasi-valuation marker in the filings: TEIL 86.60%, TPTL 13.40%.
points.quote: Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 86.60% 13.40% Triveni Power Transmission Limited

points.point: TPTL's 10,47,54,338 shares were listed and admitted to trading on BSE (544824) and NSE (TRIVENIPT) with effect from 12 October 2026, with promoter lock-ins of 2,09,50,868 shares to 2029 and 1,03,49,132 to 2027.
points.quote: Accordingly, the equity shares of the Company shall be listed and admitted to dealings on BSE and NSE with effect from October 12, 2026

points.point: Post-separation TPTL was given its own board and management: Dhruv M. Sawhney as Non-Executive Chairman, Tarun Sawhney as Vice Chairman & Managing Director, a dedicated CFO, Company Secretary and a full senior-management slate under CEO Rajiv Rajpal.
points.quote: Mr. Tarun Sawhney (DIN: 00382878) as Managing Director (designated as Vice Chairman & Managing Director) and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company for a period of five years and subject to approval of the shareholders.

verdict.what_management_expects: TPTL: an independently listed gearbox and defence company, funding ₹340 crore capex from its own cash flows and balance sheet, sustaining ~35% PBIT margins, exports above half of OE sales. TEIL: a cleaner sugar/distillery/water platform with Shamli integrated; ICRA reaffirmed AA+ Stable post-approval, off watch. Separate boards, results and earnings calls from Q1 FY27.
verdict.gaps: No quantified value-unlock or valuation basis, no explanation of the exact ~30% retained stake, no standalone TPTL financials, debt/working-capital split, separation costs, or lender/partner requests.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the demerger of Sammaan Finserve Limited's (SFL) entire NBFC lending business — the 'Demerged Undertaking' — into its parent Sammaan Capital Limited (SCL), leaving SFL as an empty-of-lending vehicle for a strategically distinct new business. The binding trigger management cites is regulatory: when RBI granted SCL a fresh NBFC-ICC certificate of registration on June 28, 2024 (N-14.03624) on its conversion from an HFC, RBI directed that no other entity in the group may hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC CoR within a prescribed timeline, and SCL had been running on an RBI dispensation for an NBFC owning an NBFC that Gagan Banga said 'is not a structure which will be long term enabled' (May 2025). The original plan had been the opposite — in Q2 FY25 SCL recreated SFL as a standalone affordable-housing/micro-LAP lender, transferred ~₹3,000 Cr of common legacy book from SFL up to SCL at arm's-length fair market value (bids invited from third parties, advisers Deloitte, BDO, CAM, IndusLaw), ran ~₹4,000 Cr of credit cost through SFL's P&L leaving only ₹25 Cr net NPA there, and brought ~₹2,500 Cr of the fair-value discount into SCL as a general provision buffer (total imputed provisions ₹9,575 Cr, ~30% of the legacy book) — explicitly so SFL could be monetised, since 'peer companies in this space typically trade at valuations of more than 4x their net worth' against SFL's ~₹3,000 Cr net worth, ₹6,100 Cr retail AUM, ₹2,900 Cr own book and seven co-lending partners. By Aug 2025 the decision was to sell a stake in SFL to a 'rating accretive' strategic partner within 9 months, with independent leadership, branches, tech and people, and a Deputy CEO hired for SCL. IHC's ₹8,850 Cr preferential allotment for 41.2% (announced Oct 2025) changed that: Banga said in Nov 2025 the Finserve strategy 'is still something which is being planned out with the investor,' and by Feb 2026 the plan had flipped to merging SFL's lending business into SCL — 'post the announcement of the proposed preferential allotment to IHC, this was the next logical step' — consolidating lending and distribution so SCL alone offers the full mortgage-backed suite (prime home loans ₹30 lakh, LAP ₹75 lakh, affordable home loans ₹15 lakh, micro-LAP ₹25 lakh) and later widens beyond mortgages, with the AIF platform (~₹6,200 Cr lent, top 8 cities) kept as the wholesale/credit vehicle. Management also said the merger was tactical for approvals: it 'is facilitating an expeditious approval from both the RBI and SEBI' for the IHC preferential issue and open offer. The Scheme adds that SFL is 'contemplating entry into a new industry, namely the insurance broking and insurtech business, which is strategically distinct from its existing NBFC operations,' needing a dedicated management and operational structure, and that SFL will prospectively house other financial services under IHC's guidance; SFL's listed NCD holders get 1:1 SCL NCDs on identical coupon, tenure, ISIN, redemption price and security, and since SFL is a wholly owned subsidiary no shares are issued as consideration.
verdict.evolution: Aug 13, 2024: Banga flags a 'completely new corporate structure,' six small subsidiaries being merged and fee-based businesses identified. Nov 15, 2024: SFL is made the designated vehicle for the incubated Smart City/affordable line, the common legacy book is transferred to SCL, a 'clean separation of the business' is declared and SFL is framed as a quick monetization tool at >4x book, while Banga notes the RBI forbearance on an NBFC owning an NBFC; Feb 11 and May 16, 2025 add FY27 targets for SFL (AUM ₹15,000 Cr, disbursals ₹9,000 Cr, 4-5%+ ROA, ~14-15% ROE) and the admission that the dispensation 'will not be long term enabled,' with de-subsidiarisation or listing as options. Aug 13, 2025: a formal decision to bring a 'rating accretive' strategic equity partner into SFL within 9 months, with full isolation of people, tech and distribution; Oct 31, 2025: after the IHC deal is announced, the SFL strategy is put on hold pending the investor's views. Feb 4, 2026: direction reverses — SFL's lending business merges into SCL as 'the next logical step' after IHC, helping expedite RBI/SEBI approvals, with SFL kept alive for other financial services; the Scheme (board approval Dec 31, 2025; RBI no-objection May 7, 2026; NCLT first motion June 12, 2026; shareholder approval 99.97% on Sept 10, 2026; second motion admitted Sept 21, 2026) grounds it in RBI's one-licence condition and SFL's planned insurance broking/insurtech entry.

points.point: First signal of a structural redraw: six small subsidiaries being merged and fee-based businesses identified, with a new corporate structure to be unveiled with Q2 FY25 results, shaped by RBI and other stakeholder feedback.
points.quote: We would also like to unveil a completely new corporate structure they have as part of the Board outcome gathered that we are merging six of our smaller subsidiaries.

points.point: SFL is converted from a mirror image of the parent into the designated vehicle for the Smart City affordable line, after a deep scrub leaving just ₹25 Cr net NPA in SFL and the common legacy book (~₹3,000 Cr) consolidated into SCL.
points.quote: Sammaan Finserve Limited is now going to be our designated vehicle for pursuing a new line of business, which we had been incubating for the last 2 years under the Smart City program.

points.point: The separation's stated purpose is a clean split of processes, systems and focus between SCL's prime housing/urban MSME book and SFL's new line, aiding shareholder transparency, regulatory compliance and the eventual partner search.
points.quote: We've also been able to achieve a clean separation of the business.

points.point: Valuation arbitrage is given as an explicit motive: affordable-housing peers trade above 4x net worth versus SFL's ~₹3,000 Cr net worth and ~₹5,000 Cr AUM, making SFL a quick monetization tool.
points.quote: Peer companies in this space typically trade at valuations of more than 4x their net worth.

points.point: Asked by Prithvi (VicAsset/Oaktree) about monetization, Banga names the regulatory constraint — RBI's forbearance for an NBFC owning an NBFC — and says SCL must de-subsidiarise at an appropriate time in consultation with the regulator.
points.quote: As far as the monetization plan is concerned, we are extremely mindful of the fact that there is RBI forbearance, which is there where an NBFC is owning an NBFC.

points.point: Pressed by Niraj Chhajer (Pransh Capital) on whether RBI requires dilution and on the 12-month dispensation expiring June 2025, Banga confirms the two-NBFC structure is not sustainable, with de-subsidiarisation or listing as optionality once SFL hits ₹10,000 Cr AUM.
points.quote: There is RBI dispensation that we currently enjoy as far as an NBFC owning an NBFC and that is not a structure which will be long term enabled.

points.point: A formal decision is taken to induct a strategic equity partner into SFL within about 9 months, requiring complete isolation of SFL's tech, people and distribution plus organisational restructuring and a Deputy CEO appointment.
points.quote: We would be looking to, over the next 3 quarters, bring in into Sammaan Finserve, a strategic partner who is rating accretive.

points.point: The partner's purpose is credit-rating uplift: a reputable equity partner would be rating accretive for SFL (then ~₹7,121 Cr balance sheet, ₹3,071 Cr net worth) and rub off positively on SCL's own rating and cost of funds.
points.quote: The arrival of a new equity partner with a strong market reputation should be rating accretive for the Sammaan Finserve entity and should also have a positive rub-off on Sammaan Capital.

points.point: After IHC's ₹8,850 Cr preferential allotment for 41.2% is announced, the SFL plan is suspended pending the incoming promoter's views; SFL (₹6,200 Cr AUM) stays a small-ticket mortgage player for the interim.
points.quote: The strategy around Finserv, the subsidiary in light of this investment is still something which is being planned out with the investor.

points.point: Direction reverses: SFL's lending business will be merged into SCL, consolidating lending and distribution so SCL offers the full mortgage suite (home loans ₹30 lakh/₹15 lakh, LAP ₹75 lakh/₹25 lakh) and can later widen beyond mortgages.
points.quote: To start off, in this quarter, one of the major developments was the announced proposed merger of our subsidiary, Sammaan Finserve into Sammaan Capital.

points.point: The consolidation is framed as the direct consequence of the IHC transaction rather than a standalone idea, replacing the earlier plan to sell a stake in SFL.
points.quote: Post the announcement of the proposed preferential allotment to IHC, this was the next logical step.

points.point: A tactical approval motive is stated: simplifying to one lending NBFC helps secure faster RBI approval for the preferential allotment and SEBI approval for the open offer, with both IHC and SCL engaged with regulators.
points.quote: We believe that the proposed merger of Sammaan Finserve, is facilitating an expeditious approval from both the RBI and SEBI.

points.point: SFL is deliberately kept alive as the forward vehicle for non-lending financial services under IHC's guidance, while the AIF platform (~₹6,200 Cr lent, good investor returns, top-8-city experience) remains the wholesale credit platform.
points.quote: Sammaan Finserve as a company will continue to exist and whatever other financial services we propose to offer in due course of time, under the guidance of IHC, would be housed prospectively under Sammaan Finserve.

points.point: The Scheme's legal rationale is RBI's one-licence condition attached to SCL's June 28, 2024 NBFC-ICC certificate of registration (N-14.03624) issued on conversion from a housing finance company; the demerger transfers SFL's NBFC business to SCL on a going-concern basis to comply.
points.quote: While issuing the CoR, RBI directed SCL to ensure that no other entity in the group shall hold CoR as an NBFC-ICC/HFC within the prescribed timeline.

points.point: Benefit one is scale and capital consolidation of both entities' lending activity into a single platform, with stated synergies, pooled resources and knowledge, a more diversified product suite and improved scalability, funding access and long-term credit growth.
points.quote: Entire NBFC Business activities of SCL and SFL shall be consolidated into a single entity, with a wider and stronger capital and asset base, having greater capacity for conducting its operations more efficiently and competitively;

points.point: The other half of the rationale is SFL's planned entry into insurance broking and insurtech — needing a focused management and operational structure, justified by industry growth, broking-channel dependency, digital disruption, favourable regulatory reform and investor interest.
points.quote: SFL is contemplating entry into a new industry, namely the insurance broking and insurtech business, which is strategically distinct from its existing NBFC operations.

points.point: Capital allocation is explicitly split: SCL optimises capital toward lending, provisioning and regulatory buffers while SFL deploys resources to product development, platform enhancement and digital innovation, improving transparency for shareholders, lenders, rating agencies and regulators.
points.quote: SCL will be able to optimise its capital allocation towards lending, provisioning and regulatory buffers, while SFL will deploy its resources towards product development, platform enhancement and digital innovation.

points.point: Creditor protection is the stated reason no meetings were needed: SFL's listed NCDs transfer to SCL on identical terms 1:1, no shares are issued as consideration since SFL is a wholly owned subsidiary, and employees transfer with continuity of service.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme, the NCDs of the Demerged Company shall be vested with the Resulting Company on the same terms, including the coupon rate, tenure, ISIN, redemption price, quantum, and nature of security.

verdict.what_management_expects: SCL: all NBFC lending in one entity, wider capital and asset base, full mortgage suite, scalability, better funding access, capital to lending and provisioning buffers. SFL: clean vehicle for insurance broking/insurtech and other IHC-guided financial services, resources to product, platform, digital innovation. Both: simpler structure, easier compliance, cost rationalisation, clearer transparency for lenders, rating agencies, regulators.
verdict.gaps: No deadline date for RBI's licence condition, no insurance-broking capital, licence or revenue numbers, no explanation of dropping the rating-accretive partner search, and the May 2026 call never mentioned the scheme.

No revenue (external or inter-segment) and no EBIT/EBITDA/PBT line for this entity appears on the tagged pages.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is the green mobility (electric-vehicle fleet) business — Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML), a 100% subsidiary of Refex Industries (RIL) running B2B employee transportation and B2B2C fleets (~1,300–1,400 EVs across Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai) — which is being carved out into a separately listed Refex Mobility Limited (RML) via a composite scheme: first RGML merges into RIL, then the Mobility Undertaking is demerged from RIL into RML with mirror 1:1 shareholding (appointed date 1 April 2025). Management's stated reason is that mobility attracts a fundamentally different investor base: Dinesh Agarwal said on the May 2026 call that 'the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited,' and the scheme documents add that the risk, competition, financial profiles and return ratios of Ash & Coal handling are 'distinct' from green mobility, and that mobility can attract its own investors, lenders and strategic partners. The second problem it solves is the drag on consolidated earnings: in Q1 FY26 green mobility ran at a minus 50% segment margin, pulling consolidated PAT down to INR20.4 crore against INR33 crore standalone, and investor Narayana on the August 2025 call called this 'a miscalculation in your capital allocation,' to which Anil Jain replied 'Point well taken.' The green mobility losses were large and recurring — a PBT loss of roughly INR13.9 crore in Q1 FY27 alone and INR38.2 crore of segment EBIT loss in FY26 — because EMIs start the day a vehicle is bought while 100% utilisation takes 6–9 months. Separation also moves the mobility balance sheet out of RIL: Agarwal confirmed about INR220 crore of net assets transfer to mobility and Anil Jain said 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity,' leaving RIL as a focused ash & coal handling (plus wind, via Venwind) platform where 95–100% of standalone revenue comes from ash and coal. Lenders were an explicit gating item — in January 2026 the company was 'waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders' before the scheme could be filed. Management frames the outcome as 'sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery,' with RML free to pursue an asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led growth strategy independently; it had crossed INR100 crore of revenue in three years and is described as 'in the path to profitability.' Because RGML is wholly owned and shareholding mirrors across, no valuation was required and no cash consideration is paid — one RML share of INR2 for every one RIL share of INR2.
verdict.evolution: Through FY25 there was no separation plan at all — on the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 calls management defended diversification as 'optimally diversified,' and the Apr 24, 2025 call offered only a narrower fix: exiting the Bengaluru airport EV taxi contract to save INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost and refocus on B2B/B2B2C. The idea surfaced as a capital-allocation complaint on the Aug 13, 2025 call, when an investor confronted management with mobility's minus 50% margin and the standalone-versus-consolidated profit gap, and Anil Jain conceded the point and promised to 'rework' the business; the Board approved the draft composite scheme on Sept 22, 2025 (RML incorporated Sept 12, 2025) and it was announced on the Nov 6, 2025 call as a two-step scheme to 'unlock focused value creation,' with no valuation needed and a 6–7 month estimate. By the Jan 21, 2026 call the plan had hardened into numbers and dependencies — INR220 crore of net assets and the mobility debt moving across, lender NOCs pending, mobility reclassified as discontinued operations, completion guided to end-April — and it then slipped repeatedly: BSE/NSE observation letters came on Mar 16, 2026, the NCLT application on Mar 26, 2026, and on the May 27, 2026 call Agarwal reset guidance to another 75–90 days, blaming only court timelines ('from our side, 100% of the all compliances is done'). Shareholders and creditors approved on Aug 5, 2026 (99.999% of equity votes in favour), but the Oct 28, 2026 press release still showed NCLT hearings underway with the next hearing on Oct 28, 2026 — i.e. roughly a year of regulatory drift against the original timeline.

points.point: Before any demerger was contemplated, the fix proposed for mobility was operational pruning — exiting the Bengaluru airport B2C EV taxi contract to cut INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost and refocus on B2B/B2B2C, with the fleet having grown from 24 vehicles in March 2023 to over 1,300.
points.quote: The withdrawal of service from Bangalore Airport will help us save an annual fixed cost of INR6.82 crores and other variable expenses pertaining to the operation over there.

points.point: Management disclosed green mobility's segment margin at minus 50% while power trading was also negative; this quantified the drag that the separation later addresses.
points.quote: The margin for coal and ash handling is roughly about 11.77%. Refrigerant gas has been 0.9%. Green Mobility has been minus 50%.

points.point: An investor (Narayana, TrueWealth Advisors) directly attacked the capital allocation, pointing to standalone PAT of ~INR32 crore versus consolidated PAT of ~INR20 crore because of mobility and wind losses, and asked why the company did not just focus on the coal business.
points.quote: And you are making nearly 50% losses on mobility segment and your wind energy is also in loss. It seems to be there is a miscalculation in your capital allocation, sir.

points.point: Anil Jain accepted the criticism and committed to reworking the business, explaining the structural cause of the losses — EMIs begin on vehicle acquisition while full utilisation takes 6–9 months, so a growing fleet is permanently loss-making at the consolidated level.
points.quote: Point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses to ensure that we remake them profitable, sir.

points.point: First formal announcement on a call of the two-step composite scheme — merger of RGML into RIL, then demerger of the Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a new separately listed Refex Mobility Limited — framed as unlocking focused value creation.
points.quote: On this note, I would like to briefly mention that the de-merger of Refex Green Mobility Limited from Refex Industries Limited is in progress through a composite scheme comprising two steps. That is, first the merger of RGML into RIL, followed by a de-merger of Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a separate listed entity called Refex Mobility Limited, in line with our strategy to unlock focused value creation for all our stakeholders.

points.point: Asked by Smit Jain (KTech Family Office) what valuation had been ascribed to the mobility vertical, the CFO said none was needed: RGML is a 100% subsidiary and shareholding mirrors across, so value discovery is left to the market post-listing; filings with BSE/NSE were done and NCLT next, with a 6–7 month estimate.
points.quote: As per the company and the process of merger and demerger process there is no valuations requirement to be done since the company holds 100, it is a 100 subsidiary and a mirror shareholding will happen, all the shareholder of Refex Industries Limited will be same shareholding as per the scheme which has been disclosed there.

points.point: Lenders were the binding constraint on filing the scheme — the company was waiting on final no-objection certificates from them, with completion then guided to end-April 2026.
points.quote: On the demerger, I think we currently are waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders.

points.point: The separation is explicitly a balance-sheet separation as well as an operational one: mobility's debt travels with it into the new entity, giving RML independent liberty to run its own business.
points.quote: Once it is demerged, the Refex Mobility will run as a separate entity where it will have more liberty to do its own business and also it will have its own, all the debt etc. will also move to that entity.

points.point: Quantum of the carve-out: in answer to Vivek Joshi asking what share of consolidated net assets moves to mobility, the CFO put the figure at INR220 crore, and confirmed RML will be 'a parallel separate listing completely.'
points.quote: Rs.220 Crores.

points.point: The clearest statement of purpose on any call, in answer to a shareholder (Maya) asking how the demerger creates value: the EV/sustainability business needs a different investor base than Refex Industries, and the structure is meant to unlock value for shareholders, with mobility itself 'in the path to profitability.'
points.quote: The purpose of the demerger is because the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited.

points.point: Management's statement of the expected benefits for each side — independent operation with dedicated strategic and financial focus, sharper operating focus, clear capital allocation and value discovery — alongside mobility crossing INR100 crore of revenue in three years on an asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led strategy.
points.quote: Post completion of the demerger, the mobility platform will operate independently with a dedicated strategic and financial focus. We believe this structure will create sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery for all the stakeholders.

points.point: Timeline slippage was attributed entirely to the NCLT calendar, not to the company — BSE and NSE approvals obtained, NCLT filing done, courts in summer vacation until 1 June, 75–90 days more expected; compliance 100% complete from Refex's side.
points.quote: Yes, sir. It all depended on the court time and other process. But from our side, 100% of the all compliances is done.

points.point: The filed scheme's rationale rests on business dissimilarity: ash & coal handling and green mobility differ in risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios, so housing them together obscures both.
points.quote: The nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios involved in the Ash & Coal handling business of RIL are distinct from Green Mobility Business presently undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary RGML.

points.point: The scheme names the external constituencies the separation is meant to serve — a distinct set of investors, lenders and strategic partners for the mobility business — which is the written counterpart of management's 'different set of investor' remark on the call.
points.quote: The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.

points.point: Listed benefits include an independent global-scale mobility company, greater management focus, independent collaboration and expansion by each entity, letting investors choose exposure by risk profile, and — most concretely — separate access to debt and equity markets.
points.quote: Enabling focused and sharper capital market access (debt and equity) and thereby unlocking the value of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking and creating enhanced value for shareholders.

points.point: Consideration mechanics: no shares are issued for the RGML merger (investment cancelled, wholly owned), and the demerger pays RIL shareholders in RML shares on a 1:1 basis, with RML's existing 50,000 shares held by RIL cancelled; RML to be listed on BSE and NSE; appointed date 1 April 2025.
points.quote: 1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of Rs.2 each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted as fully paid up for every 1 (One) Equity Shares of Re. 2 each fully paid up held in the Demerged Company.

points.point: Stakeholder approval was overwhelming at the NCLT-convened meetings of 5 August 2026: equity shareholders 99.999% in value in favour (7,91,07,251 votes for versus 603 against), three secured creditors representing 47.2% of INR158.91 crore of secured dues voted unanimously in favour, and 37 unsecured creditors representing 6.1% of INR347.68 crore voted unanimously in favour.
points.quote: Based on the above, the resolution approving the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement has been "unanimously" voted in favor by all the Secured Creditors of the Company.

points.point: Green mobility was reclassified as a discontinued operation pending the scheme, quantifying the drag it removes from RIL: consolidated discontinued-operations loss before tax of INR52.96 crore in FY26 and INR13.94 crore in Q1 FY27, with green mobility segment EBIT losses of INR38.24 crore in FY26 and INR13.61 crore in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on September 22, 2025, had approved the draft Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement amongst Refex Green Mobility Limited ("Transferor Company" or "RGML"), Refex Industries Limited ("Transferee Company" or "Demerged Company" or "RIL") and Refex Mobility Limited ("Resulting Company" or "RML") and their respective shareholders and creditors, under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the rules framed thereunder ("Scheme"), subject to receipt of requisite regulatory approvals, as may be applicable.

verdict.what_management_expects: For RIL: a focused ash & coal handling (plus wind) platform, mobility's ~INR220 crore of net assets and its debt off the books, better earnings quality and 15–18% EBITDA margins. For RML: independent operation with dedicated strategic and financial focus, its own investors, lenders and strategic partners, separate debt and equity market access, asset-light enterprise-led scaling toward profitability, and market-led value discovery via 1:1 mirror listing.
verdict.gaps: No standalone funding plan, margin targets or profitability date for RML; no valuation or asset/debt split detail; no reason given for merging RGML into RIL first.

verdict.segment_name: Green Mobility (labelled "Electric Vehicle" in FY2024 and FY2025 segment tables; "Green mobility" from FY2026) — Refex Green Mobility Ltd. / Refex EV Fleet Services Pvt. Ltd., the Demerged Undertaking transferring to Refex Mobility Limited
verdict.measure_notes: Revenue = consolidated 'Segment Revenue (Net Sales/Income)' per Ind AS 108 note; no inter-segment split is disclosed, so it is the segment revenue as reported. Operating profit = 'Segment Results' i.e. EBIT before other income and exceptional items (finance cost, other income and tax are unallocated at company level, not by segment). No segment-level PAT, EBITDA, depreciation or tax is disclosed anywhere on these pages. FY2026 figures are from the consolidated note where Green Mobility is classified as a discontinued operation.

verdict.rationale: Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.
verdict.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

points.point: Asked outright about demerging Care and the other subsidiaries from the holdco and about removing the holdco discount, Pratul Gupta said nothing was decided — the board was weighing options and wanted to strengthen the businesses first, after the INR1,500 crore raise, before any capital-market action.
points.quote: On the second question about how the structure will look like in some future time, what I can very clearly assure you is that the management and the Board is evaluating various options which can add value to the shareholders.

points.point: Investors were already framing the choice as Care IPO versus demerger; Dixit Doshi asked it explicitly alongside questions on NBFC yields, showing the separation idea originated with shareholders rather than management.
points.quote: And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can just touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health business or we will be better off with the de -merger of the business?

points.point: Gupta presented the demerger as a strategic imperative rather than a housekeeping exercise, announced two days after the REL and RFL boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026.
points.quote: It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long -term growth.

points.point: The trigger was three converging conditions — the Burman takeover as promoters, the INR1,500 crore warrant raise covering funding needs for the foreseeable future, and the businesses reaching a scale that demands specialised focus.
points.quote: Each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories.

points.point: Mechanics: lending, broking and ancillary support services move from REL to RFL on a going-concern basis, the Care stake stays in REL, RFL issues one share per REL share and then lists, with a 15–18 month process ending in Q1 FY28.
points.quote: The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.

points.point: A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars.
points.quote: The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.

points.point: Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value.
points.quote: I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?

points.point: Gupta positioned this as stage one of a longer restructuring, with a Care reverse merger possible later once unspecified milestones and minimum-shareholding thresholds are met.
points.quote: Well, I think this is -- as I mentioned, this is the first step in that direction.

points.point: The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law.
points.quote: So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.

points.point: Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation.
points.quote: This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.

points.point: Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: Pressed by Vikas Srivastava on whether the scheme could be amended to fold Care in once the promoters reach 26%, Lamba ruled out amending it but left a subsequent scheme open.
points.quote: No, I'll answer your last question first. We don't want to amend the scheme.

points.point: Lamba conceded the value is concentrated in Care and said the separation is intended to create value in the other entity too, as promoters moved from ~26% toward ~34% diluted.
points.quote: Yes, we understand that the value is in Care. We are cognizant of that. That's why we are separating the entities, creating clear paths, and we hope to create value in the other entity as well

points.point: The 14 Feb 2026 filing states the demerged undertaking is all of REL's financial services activity — lending, broking, investment and ancillary/support services — explicitly excluding the retained insurance business, i.e. the Care Health shareholding.
points.quote: Provided that, the Demerged Undertaking shall exclude the Remaining Business ( as defined in the Scheme ) compris ing of all the units, divisions, undertakings, assets and liabilities in relation to the Demerged Company’s insurance business, comprising of its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited .

points.point: The scheme quantifies how small the demerged half is: FY25 turnover of INR457.29 crore on a consolidated basis, just 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31  March , 202 5 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis  representing 6.2% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31 March , 202 5.

points.point: Stated rationale includes that the two businesses face different competition and attract different investors, partners and lenders, and that a separately listed vehicle enables sector-focused talent and growth opportunities.
points.quote: The nature and competition involved in the businesses comprising of the Demerged Undertaking is distinct from the other businesses and it is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The press release lists four objectives — streamlining businesses, listing financial services, focused management with performance mapped to each business, and segment-tailored risk and compliance frameworks — with 1:1 mirror shareholding in RFL and listing targeted for Q1 FY28.
points.quote: Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of employee p erformance and rewards to respective business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and retention of sector -specific talent and resources.

points.point: SEBI's comments routed through the NSE observation letter of 7 July 2026 require REL to disclose the need for the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, risks and the RBI approval position to shareholders — i.e. the rationale was not yet fully documented for them.
points.quote: Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Execution setback: after exchange no-objections on 7 July 2026, RBI declined the no-objection/prior-approval applications of both REL and RFL in letters dated 6 and 7 August 2026, and the companies said they would go back to the regulator.
points.quote: The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026 , from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to .

verdict.what_management_expects: REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.
verdict.gaps: No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

Annual reports instead split this business into 'Investment and Financing Activities' and 'Broking Related Activities' (₹ lakhs) and report 'Segment Results', so they carry no single 'Financial Services' line.

verdict.rationale: This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

points.point: Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 1: Seamless pipe manufacturing business of the Demerged Company located at Mangaon, Maharashtra (125,000 MTPA), captive solar power plant at Beed, Maharashtra (10 MW), along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 1.

points.point: Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.

points.point: The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately.
points.quote: The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.

points.point: The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split.
points.quote: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.

points.point: Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started.
points.quote: Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.

points.point: The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years.
points.quote: Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.

points.point: The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business.
points.quote: The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.

points.point: Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins.
points.quote: Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality.
points.quote: The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.

points.point: Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring.
points.quote: The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.

points.point: The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%).
points.quote: This is further to the intimation dated 22nd May, 2026, about the approval of the Scheme of Arrangement by the Board of Directors of the Company, we have to inform you that the said Scheme is under further review and would be placed before any subsequent Board Meeting for its approval and would be submitted to Stock Exchanges thereafter.

points.point: The first hint of any separation was about the rig: asked whether MSL would keep two verticals, the Chairman declined to commit, while noting day rates had risen (~$40,000/day, expecting a new contract above $80,000).
points.quote: Well, we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time.

points.point: An investor asked outright about demerging or selling the rig business post-May 2025; management confirmed intent but no board discussion and no valuation expectation.
points.quote: It is something which we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval.

points.point: After an investor said the rig arrangement (MSL renting the rig to group company Jindal Drilling, which sub-contracts to ONGC) looked out of line with MSL's governance clean-up, management personally agreed and promised a communication once board approvals came.
points.quote: You are right, and I personally agree with you, but once suitable decisions and Board approvals are received, we will send communication on this.

points.point: Management confirmed a rig exit had been contemplated but that the board had given no update, while re-committing to pipes only — the rig had just been recontracted to Jindal Drilling at ~$35,000/day L1, with MSL to get ~$17,000-18,000/day.
points.quote: There was a view of getting out of the rig business, but we've not received any update from the Board in the Board meeting, which concluded yesterday.

points.point: A five-year shareholder explicitly demanded the company be split so investors could choose the pipe business over the treasury/holding activity, arguing the merged picture was unclear; management offered no response.
points.quote: Either divide the company in two parts. One should be a holding company, one should be a seamless company.

points.point: Six months before board approval, an analyst asked specifically about getting the Jindal Explorer rig off the books and was told there was no update, with the rig about to start a new ONGC contract.
points.quote: There is no update on the proposal that you mentioned.

points.point: On the last call before the first board approval, management described the future as cash conservation and opportunistic distressed acquisitions, with no mention of any restructuring, while defending the INR3,500 crore treasury against shareholders noting ~50% of market cap was cash.
points.quote: We are conserving cash as of now and we are on the lookout for any inorganic opportunity that may arise, but that inorganic opportunity should be at a cost level at which we are comfortable.

points.point: The same call set out the economics of the Telangana asset that now forms United Seamless Limited: INR477 crores purchase plus INR73 crores reactivation, INR100-200 crores of EBITDA a year, and ~INR375 crores of tax saved from USTPL's INR1,500 crore-plus accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation.
points.quote: We acquired it for INR477 crores, and we invested an additional INR73 crores to reactivate the mill.

verdict.what_management_expects: Per the Scheme only: each mill run as a focused vertical with dedicated management and technology-specific modernization; sharper assessment and deployment of capital across pipes, drilling and renewables, with more flexibility for expansion; solar assets aligned to the mills they serve; the rig managed on its own terms; independent reporting improving transparency and performance evaluation; identical proportionate shareholding, so value-neutral. No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.
verdict.gaps: No call ever mentioned it. Silent on where the ~INR3,500 crore treasury, debt, ERW and premium-connections subsidiary sit, on margins, valuation, lost shared overheads, and NCLT timing.

Quarterly figure is EBITDA (pre-depreciation) for the Seamless business only, from the presentation's Operational & Financial Performance slide; ERW EBITDA is given separately (Q1 FY27: 2). No segment-level PAT is disclosed anywhere in these pages.
