verdict.rationale: This is not a spin-off of a business away from Sunteck Realty Ltd. (SRL) — it is an internal reorganisation that pulls a business up into the listed parent. On 1 October 2026 the board approved a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 between Satguru Corporate Services Private Limited (the Demerged Company, a wholly owned subsidiary of Sunteck) and Sunteck Realty Limited (the Resulting Company), demerging Satguru's 'Sunteck City 4th Avenue Undertaking' — the residential real estate project at ODC, Goregaon West — into Sunteck on a going-concern basis. The business being separated out of Satguru is large: its turnover for the year ended 31 March 2026 was approximately Rs 869 crore, about 77% of Sunteck's total consolidated turnover for FY26. That concentration is explained by the calls and accounts: Sunteck follows the project completion method, not percentage completion (Jan 2024 call), 4th Avenue received its occupation certificate and 'came up for revenue recognition' in FY26 (May 2025 call), and the Q3 FY26 revenue jump was attributed by CFO Prashant Chaubey directly to the completed 4th Avenue project (Feb 2026 call). The consequence visible in the Q1 FY27 filing is a hollow parent: FY26 standalone revenue from operations was only Rs 209.41 crore with a standalone loss after tax of Rs 19.67 crore, against consolidated revenue of Rs 1,123.84 crore and consolidated PAT of Rs 202.07 crore — i.e. the group's largest profit pool sat one level down in Satguru. The three stated benefits are purely structural: (1) consolidation of the Demerged Business Undertaking, (2) administrative and operational efficiencies, and (3) efficient pooling and deployment of financial and managerial resources, facilitating project-specific capital allocation and funding strategies — which echoes management's FY26 funding narrative of simultaneous capital needs at Nepeansea Road, Dubai and the 5th Avenue commercial build (Oct 2025 call, when Rs 500 crore of warrants were placed). No external party is named as having asked for it: the filings cite no investor, lender or JV-partner demand, no consideration, no share exchange ratio (Satguru is 100%-owned, so no shares are issued), no change in either shareholding pattern and no new listing; the Scheme is subject to statutory/regulatory approvals including the NCLT.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced on any earnings call in the 36-month window: across Jan 2024, Jun 2024, Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Jan 2025, May 2025, Jul 2025, Oct 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026 and the Jul 22, 2026 Q1 FY27 call, neither the demerger, nor Satguru, nor any scheme of arrangement is mentioned — on 22 July 2026 Kamal Khetan instead said the Rs 2,250 crore fundraising resolution was 'obviously, enabling' with 'absolutely no planning of any fundraising'. What the calls did build was the predicate: the project completion method was reiterated in Jan 2024, 4th Avenue's occupation certificate and FY26 revenue recognition were flagged in May 2025, the Rs 500 crore preferential issue for Nepeansea/Dubai/5th Avenue funding came in Oct 2025, and the completed 4th Avenue was named as the FY26 revenue driver in Feb 2026 and Apr 2026 (FY26 operating revenue Rs 1,124 crore). Alongside, filings in Mar 2026 (Magenta Buildcon, Sunteck Infracon) and Apr 2026 (Mantavya Real Estates) show continuous subsidiary-level reshuffling into step-down holdings. The plan appears fully formed only at the 1 Oct 2026 board meeting (6.45-7.05 p.m.), where the Scheme was approved together with the appointment of EY as internal auditor to 31 March 2027.

points.point: The business separated is Satguru's residential project undertaking at ODC Goregaon West, demerged into listed parent Sunteck on a going-concern basis — an internal reorganisation, not a market spin-off.
points.quote: The Demerged Business Undertaking of the Demerged Company comprises of the residential real estate project under “Sunteck City 4th Avenue Undertaking” (as defined in the Scheme).

points.point: Size of what moves: ~Rs 869 crore of turnover for FY26, roughly 77% of Sunteck's entire consolidated turnover — the group's dominant revenue block sat inside the subsidiary.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Business Undertaking of Satguru for the year ended 31 March 2026 was Rs. ~869 Crs representing ~77% of the total consolidated turnover of Sunteck for the year ended 31st March 2026.

points.point: The stated problems solved are structural, not commercial: consolidation, administrative and operational efficiency, and the ability to allocate and fund capital project by project.
points.quote: Efficient pooling and deployment of financial resources, managerial resources and facilitate project-specific capital allocation and funding strategies.

points.point: No consideration, no share exchange ratio, no shareholding change and no new listing — confirming the purpose is balance-sheet and governance plumbing rather than value unlocking for shareholders.
points.quote: Since, Satguru is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sunteck, hence, no shares are proposed to be issued pursuant to the Scheme.

points.point: Execution risk is regulatory: the Scheme needs NCLT sanction, and the same 1 Oct 2026 board meeting also appointed EY as internal auditor to 31 March 2027.
points.quote: The Scheme is subject to the requisite statutory / regulatory approvals including the approval of National Company Law Tribunal.

points.point: Q1 FY27 filing shows the hollow-parent problem the demerger addresses: FY26 standalone revenue Rs 209.41 crore and a standalone loss of Rs 19.67 crore versus consolidated revenue Rs 1,123.84 crore; the parent also moved to the 115BAA tax regime in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: During the quarter ended 30 June 2026, the Company exercised the option to adopt the concessional tax regime under Section 115BAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

points.point: Pattern of ongoing intra-group reshuffling in the months before the Scheme: wholly owned subsidiaries pushed down into step-down holdings for Rs 1,00,000 each (Magenta/Sunteck Infracon in Mar 2026, Mantavya in Apr 2026).
points.quote: Pursuant to this Mantavya continues to be the subsidiary by way of Step down wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: CFO attributes the Q3 FY26 revenue jump squarely to the completed 4th Avenue project — the very undertaking later demerged out of Satguru.
points.quote: So Rishith, as you are aware, we have completed our Sunteck City 4th Avenue project in ODC Goregaon West. So the revenue jump that you see is coming from that project.

points.point: Management had pre-announced that 4th Avenue's occupation certificate would drive FY26 revenue recognition, which is why FY26 turnover concentrated in Satguru.
points.quote: With regards to revenue recognition definitely with the occupation certificate getting received for Sunteck City 4th Avenue so that project will come up for revenue recognition in FY26.

points.point: Project completion accounting explains the lumpy, entity-level concentration of revenue that the consolidation addresses.
points.quote: With respect to revenue recognition in the financial statement, I would like to reiterate today that per Ind AS, the Indian Accounting Standard, the company follows the project completion method and not the percentage completion method of accounting.

points.point: Context for 'project-specific capital allocation and funding': the Rs 500 crore preferential issue was raised against simultaneous funding needs at Nepeansea Road, Dubai and 5th Avenue commercial plus new BD.
points.quote: But at the same time, we were seeing that there will be a lot of requirement of the funds, which will be required in Nepeansea Road and Dubai, as well as commercial building of 5th Avenue, plus the new business development.

points.point: FY26 scale against which the Rs 869 crore demerged turnover should be read: consolidated operating revenue Rs 1,124 crore, EBITDA Rs 305 crore, PAT Rs 202 crore, net debt/equity 0.06x.
points.quote: On the full year basis, operating revenue stood at INR1,124 crores for FY '26.

points.point: Ten weeks before the board approved the Scheme, management disclosed nothing about restructuring and said the Rs 2,250 crore enabling resolution was routine with no fundraising planned.
points.quote: So, this is, obviously, enabling resolution. And if you see every year, we take this enabling resolution.

verdict.what_management_expects: Sunteck gains 4th Avenue's ~Rs 869 crore turnover — 77% of FY26 consolidated revenue — into standalone books that showed just ~Rs 209 crore revenue and a ~Rs 20 crore loss in FY26. Group-wide: administrative/operational efficiencies, pooled financial and managerial resources, project-specific capital allocation and funding. No margin, valuation or shareholding claims; no shares issued.

verdict.rationale: Management says the separation is a consolidation, not a divestment: a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved 20 February 2026 that (1) merges UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS, the India crop protection business, 90.91% UPL-owned, FY25 turnover INR 24,120 Mn = 31.15% of UPL 1's turnover) into UPL Limited, (2) demerges that India Crop Protection Business into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2), and (3) amalgamates UPL Crop Protection Holdings (UPL Cayman, 77.78% owned, FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn) into UPL 2 — leaving two listed companies: UPL Limited as a diversified agri-plus-specialty-chemicals platform (SUPERFORM stays with it as the manufacturing arm, and it keeps incubating new verticals) and UPL 2 as what the press release calls the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform across 140+ countries, with 9 R&D centres, 25 formulation facilities and a 14% innovation rate, led by Mike Frank. The problems they said it solves: a conglomerate/single-multiple valuation (Bikash Prasad: the market applies 'a single conglomerate multiple' and there is a 'huge conglomerate discount'), a complicated holding structure left over from the 2022 shareholder-approved simplification project that split India crop protection into UPL SAS while international crop protection sat under UPL Cayman, and private-market value not reaching the parent — Toshan Tamhane said that on the KKR and Alpha Wave valuations of Advanta 'the full value of that is not flowing through to UPL Limited.' They argue crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation needs, citing Corteva's own announced crop-protection/seeds split, and that independent capital and governance structures will let each platform raise capital separately, optimise its own capital structure and grow faster (Jai Shroff: 'at least 3x-4x the other players'). Deleveraging was the stated precondition and is now largely done — gross debt down from $3.8bn (FY24) to $2.3bn (FY26), net debt $3.1bn to $1.6bn, gearing 4.6x to below 1.6x — with Jai Shroff saying leverage 'was an issue which kept the multiple of the company' and 'is gone away now.' Who asked: investors/analysts drove it (the whole agenda came from investor feedback on the four below-EBITDA line items, debt and liquidity), KKR and Alpha Wave as platform-level investors wanted liquidity, and the Upswing Trust (an existing UPL SAS investor) swaps into UPL Cayman and ends up with 16.78% of UPL 2 as a public shareholder with one board nomination right; promoters locked their UPL 2 holding for 18 months from listing. Consideration is all-share: 1,000 UPL 1 shares per 48 UPL SAS shares; 1 UPL 2 share per 1 UPL 1 share on demerger; 1,000 UPL 2 shares per 213 UPL Cayman shares — no cash.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as monetisation rather than separation: on the Jan 2025 call management announced Alpha Wave's $350m into Advanta ($100m primary, $250m secondary from UPL Ltd for ~12.44%) plus the $200m rights issue, all framed around getting net debt/EBITDA to ~2x. By Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had become an open-ended structural review — Bikash Prasad said advisors were being engaged 'to explore unlocking value across all platforms' with no firm structure and no timeline, alongside a promise to 'significantly deleverage' over one to two years; Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) repeated the same formula (restructuring, strategic fundraising, potential IPO) and added the DECCO post-harvest integration into Advanta, with Bikash hinting a corporate action would help fund the ~$900m FY27 maturities. Feb 2026 (Q3 FY26) was the first concrete step — Advanta's DRHP filed 19 January 2026 as a pure offer-for-sale (KKR 2.2%, UPL Ltd 7.8%) with proceeds 'largely for deleveraging', justified by the crop-protection-versus-seeds capital-allocation argument and the Corteva precedent, plus a stated 1-to-3-year window for corporate actions across all platforms; the crop-protection scheme itself was then approved on 20 February 2026 and, by the May 2026 Capital Markets Day, had drawn open shareholder opposition (Old Bridge's Tarang Agarwal warning of a HoldCo discount), with Bikash saying ten structures had been examined and that two months of unfiltered investor feedback would go to the board 'in a month or two'. Execution continued regardless: CCI approval 2/3 June 2026, BSE and NSE observation letters 29 July 2026, and the Swap and ESOP Swap Transactions completed 31 July 2026, with the Scheme still pending shareholder, creditor and NCLT approval as of the 2 November 2026 results.

points.point: The core move is consolidating the India crop protection business (UPL SAS) and the global crop protection business (UPL Cayman) into one entity, UPL 2, with its own manufacturing base, R&D, registrations and independent management.
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: Two listed entities are meant to let investors choose their exposure — UPL 1 as diversified agri/specialty chemicals plus incubation, UPL 2 as dedicated crop protection.
points.quote: This will enable clearer value discovery by providing flexibility to the investors to select investments which best suit their investment strategies and risk profile.

points.point: Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each entity is given as a core benefit, alongside cost efficiencies from consolidated manufacturing and market access.
points.quote: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.

points.point: The press release positions UPL 2 by scale — world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform, 140+ countries — as the route to faster innovation delivery and market share.
points.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: Bikash Prasad named the valuation problem directly: the market prices UPL on one conglomerate multiple, and separation is meant to make the sum of the parts visible.
points.quote: You know that even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple, they are applying on us.

points.point: He said the chosen structure was picked after reviewing roughly ten alternatives with advisors, and that independent capital and governance structures per platform will accelerate growth.
points.quote: So once these platforms have their independent capital structure, independent governance structure, it will grow much faster.

points.point: Jai Shroff framed it as brand-led, IP-rich, high-growth businesses needing autonomy, with SUPERFORM staying inside UPL Limited as the manufacturing platform.
points.quote: All these businesses need long-term need a kind of independent life, right?

points.point: He tied the timing to deleveraging being complete — leverage had suppressed the multiple and is no longer the constraint, so the re-rating can now come from structure.
points.quote: We've also made sure that the as in the past leverage was an issue for which kept the multiple of the company.

points.point: Old Bridge's Tarang Agarwal pushed back on the announced structure as value-destructive for existing UPL shareholders and urged alternative structures; Bikash said investor feedback would go unfiltered to the board.
points.quote: But the challenge is that the manner in which that the current structure has been announced, it's likely to trigger a significant HoldCo discount .

points.point: Toshan Tamhane gave the separation logic for seeds versus crop protection — different cash flows and capital allocation — explicitly citing Corteva's own split, and calling Advanta the eighth largest global seeds player.
points.quote: And lastly, third, we believe that the needs of crop protection in terms of the cash flows, capital allocation are very different from that of the seeds business.

points.point: He also said private-market valuations of Advanta (KKR, then Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price — the public-market unlock argument.
points.quote: Because , if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at , at least we feel that the full value of that is no t flowing through to UPL Limited.

points.point: The Advanta DRHP (filed 19 January 2026) was a pure offer for sale — KKR 2.2%, UPL Limited 7.8% — with no money going into Advanta and proceeds earmarked for group deleveraging.
points.quote: But it will come to the group largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet.

points.point: Management kept the options open publicly — restructuring, strategic fundraising or an IPO — and linked a possible corporate action to meeting the ~$900m FY27 maturities.
points.quote: UPL continues to evaluate various strategic opportunities to unlock shareholders' value across platforms, including restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO.

points.point: The first explicit signal: advisors were being engaged with no structure chosen and no timeline, framed as value unlock across all four platforms while deleveraging continued.
points.quote: The idea behind engaging advisors is to explore unlocking value across all platforms.

points.point: The precursor was private-market monetisation of a platform — Alpha Wave's $350m into Advanta ($100m primary, $250m secondary from UPL Ltd for ~12.44%), with the secondary going entirely to debt repayment.
points.quote: This marks second investment in the enterprise by a global investor in a span of two years.

verdict.what_management_expects: UPL 1: a diversified agri plus specialty-chemicals platform retaining SUPERFORM as manufacturing arm, incubating new verticals. UPL 2: world's second-largest listed pure-play crop protection company, 140+ countries, independent capital structure, governance and board focus, growing 3x-4x peers. Both: independent fundraising, clearer sum-of-parts, removal of the conglomerate discount, cost synergies in manufacturing and market access.
verdict.gaps: No debt/leverage split between UPL 1 and UPL 2, no quantified synergies, no UPL 2 standalone financials, no answer to the HoldCo-discount and dilution objection, no Advanta-IPO interaction.

verdict.rationale: SKF India separated its Industrial bearings business out of the listed company into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving SKF India Ltd as a pure-play Automotive bearings company (management called it a "reverse carve-out" mirroring SKF AB's global split of Automotive, ~30% of group revenue versus 34-35% in India). Management's stated logic rested on three pillars: fundamentally different macro drivers (Automotive: EV/CAFE and BS-VII emission norms, 30% EV penetration target by 2030, premiumization/SUVs, last-mile commercial vehicles; Industrial: infrastructure spend, Make in India/NIP/PLI, China-Plus-One, railways/metro/Vande Bharat, wind and renewables doubling by 2030); different customer needs (a few large auto OEMs needing application-specific, longer-cycle engineered products — 60-65% engineered order in Auto versus ~25-30% in Industrial — against hundreds of industrial verticals wanting uptime, condition monitoring and remanufacturing); and a different manufacturing philosophy (Auto = large batch, small/medium bearings, automation and cycle-time efficiency; Industrial = wide assortment, small/large sizes, flexible lines with fast changeover plus a large traded component). The problems they said this solves: management attention split across two unlike businesses, capital allocation that could not be tailored (Auto was short of capacity, Industrial needed a brand-new Pune plant and localization from ~30-35% toward 70%), slow decision-making and launches, mismatched innovation cycles, and poor financial visibility for investors in a combined P&L. Operationally the split was defined down to the line: Bangalore 10 lines (7 Auto, 3 Industrial, with those 3 moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Auto), Pune 22 lines (12 Auto, 10 Industrial), Haridwar 4 lines all Auto; land 85:15 in Bangalore, 52:48 in Pune, 100% Auto in Haridwar; manpower 55-60% Auto versus 40-45% Industrial; cash allocated on the two businesses' last three years of profits. Shareholders received one SKF Industrial share of Rs 10 for every SKF India share held (PwC Business Consulting share entitlement report dated 24 December 2024; Saffron Capital fairness opinion 25 December 2024), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial. Pro forma FY24 economics shown to investors were Auto ~18% EBITDA and Industrial ~17%, both ~16% PBT, off a combined FY24 revenue of INR 45.7 billion; FY25 combined revenue was INR 4,919.9 crore (+7.65%) with PBT INR 763.1 crore (+3.71%). Nobody external demanded the separation — it was a group-level decision, with investors on the calls supportive (one explicitly "wholeheartedly supported" it) while pressing for structural clarity given SKF would still have three Indian entities including the unlisted SKF Engineering & Lubrication (Ahmedabad plant, global technical centre, lubrication and sealing factories); no lender or partner requirement was ever cited.
verdict.evolution: The demerger was announced in Q4 CY2024 and first explained in detail on a dedicated update call on 9 April 2025, which laid out the three macro/customer/manufacturing drivers, the six enablers (management focus, manufacturing efficiency, tailored capital, agility, innovation, investor visibility), pro forma FY24 carve-out financials and a 12-15 month timeline, plus an aspiration of "2 to 3 more points" of EBITDA. By the 19 May 2025 Q4 call the plant allocation had firmed up (Haridwar 100% Auto, Bangalore ~80-85% Auto, a new Industrial factory beside the Pune plant), and the 30 June 2025 investor meet added line-by-line, land and manpower splits, segment revenue mixes from FY22-FY25, three-year guidance (Auto 10-12%, Industrial 8-10% to FY28, margins held at 17-19%) and a step-up in capex from ~INR 150 crore to roughly INR 350-400 crore a year (INR 450-500 crore Pune industrial plant by 2028, INR 500-600 crore Auto capex to 2030); the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on 14 July 2025 approved the 1:1 scheme, and the 6-7 August 2025 AGM and Q1 FY26 call quantified the cost for the first time (INR 184 million in Q1, mostly SAP/IT separation and consultants, 1.5-2% margin drag running into H1 FY27, plus stamp duty on asset transfer) while conceding the businesses were "so deeply integrated" that separation was complex. After NCLT sanction on 26 September 2025, effectiveness on 1 October 2025 and a 15 October 2025 record date, the story changed tone: the 21 May 2026 call presented SKF India as a standalone automotive company guiding to only 11-12% PBT margin (FY26 EBITDA 15.3%) with investors complaining that disclosure had "dropped substantially" post-demerger and that margins were far below what was promised in the run-up to the demerger vote, management answering that royalty was unchanged and this was a transition.

points.point: The stated purpose: two independent, fit-for-purpose companies that each accelerate growth and profitability, driven by three differences — industry dynamics, customer needs and manufacturing philosophy.
points.quote: The intention of this demerger is to create 2 fit-for-purposes independent companies, which will accelerate both growth and profitability of both companies.

points.point: Management summarised the rationale as three separate axes of difference, with manufacturing efficiency and customer service as the payoff.
points.quote: So to summarize, macro drivers are different. Customer drivers and innovation is different; and third, the manufacturing itself, the process of manufacturing itself is very different, what will make us most efficient and help us serve the customer needs.

points.point: Manufacturing philosophy was the concrete operating problem: Auto runs large batches of small/medium bearings for few OEMs with automation and economies of scale, while Industrial needs flexible lines, customised solutions and a large traded/regional component.
points.quote: Automotive has a large batch sizes with small and medium-sized bearings.

points.point: Margin ambition attached to the separation: 2-3 percentage points of EBITDA upside in both businesses, from more efficient manufacturing, procurement and value-based pricing of premium products such as ceramic and energy-efficient bearings.
points.quote: So I would say while the margins are typically relatively thin, we would hope that we can get at least 2 to 3 more points on our EBITDA going forward.

points.point: Shareholders were told the split was economically neutral — a mirror shareholding with a 1:1 share issue and listing of SKF Industrial on both exchanges.
points.quote: The new company will mirror the shareholding of the existing listed company with each shareholder of SKF India receiving one share of SKF Industrial as a consideration of the demerger.

points.point: Investor visibility into the two businesses' separate performance was explicitly listed as one of the demerger benefits, alongside tailored capital deployment and two different manufacturing philosophies.
points.quote: and finally, just more visibility for the -- our investors, all of you, to be able to see the performance of the 2 entities independently.

points.point: Pro forma FY24 carve-out economics given to investors: Automotive ~18% EBITDA, Industrial ~17%, both around 16% PBT, with capex set to double from INR 130-150 crore as a new Industrial plant is built next to the existing Pune site.
points.quote: So if you look at FY '24, our EBITDA margins for automotive was around 18%. And industrial was around 17%.

points.point: The asset split was disclosed line by line — Bangalore 10 lines 70:30 with three lines moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Automotive, Pune 52:48 land, Haridwar 100% Automotive, manpower roughly 55:45.
points.quote: There are three main plants, as we said, Bangalore, Pune and Haridwar. Bangalore, today there are 10 lines that will be split in the ratio of 70 to 30.

points.point: Three-year guidance for the two entities: Automotive 10-12% growth, Industrial 8-10% (held back until the new Pune plant and localization land in FY27-28), with margins maintained at 17-19% and upside beyond FY28.
points.quote: Next 3 years till '28, we expect growth in automotive to be in the 10 % to 12% range, industrial to be a little lower, 8% to 10% range.

points.point: Capital allocation was the hard constraint being fixed: a brand-new Industrial-only Pune plant (DGBB, TRB, unitised bearings) costing INR 450-500 crore by 2028 plus INR 350-450 crore of additional lines, on top of INR 500-600 crore of Automotive capex to 2030.
points.quote: Pune, we will be setting up a new plant, fully industrial, for industrial, making primarily DGBBs, which are deep groove ball bearings, tapered roller bearings, and unitized bearings, which are UCs.

points.point: At the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting, management conceded the separation was complex precisely because the two businesses were deeply intertwined, and said the total demerger cost was still being accumulated.
points.quote: As you know, it's a complex project primarily because the businesses both automotive and industrial, they are so deeply integrated that having two independent businesses is a complex process.

points.point: An existing institutional shareholder (Ravi Purohit) publicly backed the demerger while asking why India would still be left with three SKF entities when the group was simplifying structures; management said no merger of entities was contemplated until the demerger completed.
points.quote: And first of all, we'd like to congratulate and have wholeheartedly supported this demerger initiative that SKF Group is undertaking.

points.point: First quantification of the cost: INR 184 million in Q1 FY26, mainly SAP and separate data infrastructure plus compliance consultants, with a 1.5-2% margin drag expected to run to H1 FY27 and extra stamp duty/registration cost on asset transfer in the Industrial entity.
points.quote: So if you look at our current quarter, cost of demerger was around INR184 million.

points.point: At the FY25 AGM the Chairman framed the demerger as strategic repositioning to sharpen focus, improve execution agility and deepen customer alignment, with manufacturing roadmaps diverging (Automotive automation-led high throughput; Industrial modular and demand-responsive).
points.quote: The announcement of our demerger, which is separating the automotive and industrial businesses into two focused publicly listed entities was a significant milestone.

points.point: Post-demerger, management clarified the direction of the carve-out — Industrial was hived off and the listed SKF India Limited is the automotive division, a reverse of the group-level split.
points.quote: But in India, it is a reverse carve -out where industrial has gone out. So SKF India Limited remains as automotive division.

points.point: The promised margin uplift did not appear: FY26 PBT fell 694 bps, EBITDA was 15.3%, and guidance was reset to 11-12% PBT, with Auto still buying medium DGBB and tapered roller bearings from SKF Industrial because of its own capacity shortage.
points.quote: Now talking about the sustainable margin, we could be looking at 11 -12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.

points.point: A long-term shareholder attacked the post-demerger communication gap, noting pre-demerger guidance of 16-19% (even 18-19%) EBITDA for a 95%-localised Auto business and a 50-70% valuation discount to Schaeffler and Timken; management replied royalty was unchanged and there is now no pure-play comparable.
points.quote: Increasingly, our post demerger, what we are realizing is that the investor communication and the disclosures have dropped substantially.

points.point: Management's closing framing still rested on focus and agility as the value-unlock, with restructuring costs described as a temporary hit.
points.quote: The demerger positions us to unlock greater value by enabling sharper focus and agility in our business.

points.point: The scheme transferred the Industrial business as a going concern into SKF India (Industrial) Limited under Sections 230-232, effective 1 October 2025 (NCLT order 26 September 2025, record date 15 October 2025), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial — i.e. Industrial was the larger half.
points.quote: The Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, vide its Order dated 26th September, 2025, sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited ("the Company" or "Demerged Company") and SKF India (Industrial) Limited ("SKF Industrial" or "Resulting Company") and their respective shareholders and creditors under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 ("Scheme"), providing for the demerger of the Company's Industrial Business (Demerged Undertaking as defined in the Scheme ) into SKF Industrial on a going concern basis

points.point: The post-completion press release restated the purpose as two focused entities with independent boards and governance, and attached separate investment plans — Industrial INR 8,000-9,500 million by 2030 including a new Pune facility by 2028, Automotive INR 4,100-5,100 million by 2030 across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end capacity in Haridwar, Pune and Bangalore.
points.quote: The demerger, sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and approved by shareholders earlier this year, has formally separated SKF India's business into two focused entities — SKF Industrial and SKF Automotive — each equipped with independent boards and governance structures.

points.point: The FY26 AGM presentation codified the five official reasons for the separation and rebranded the automotive entity as SKF Vertevo, reporting FY26 revenue of INR 21,295 million, 15% EBITDA margin and EPS of INR 23.7.
points.quote: Why the Demerger? Different Market Dynamics Distinct Customer Needs Focused Capital Allocation Faster Decision Making Independent Growth Strategies

verdict.what_management_expects: Two fit-for-purpose entities growing faster and more profitably: automotive 10-12% and industrial 8-10% growth to FY28, both holding 17-19% EBITDA with 2-3 points of upside later; sharper management focus, tailored capital deployment and manufacturing efficiency, plus separate financial visibility attracting more aligned investors.
verdict.gaps: Never quantified: total demerger cost, dis-synergies, inter-entity trading/rent/service charges, or why post-demerger margins (11-12% PBT) fall far below the 16-19% promised pre-demerger.

verdict.rationale: The separation is a two-part composite Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation approved by the Thermax board on July 30, 2026 (Sections 230–232, Companies Act 2013; Appointed Date April 1, 2026; subject to NCLT Mumbai), involving two wholly owned subsidiaries: Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited (TBSPL) and Thermax Cooling Solutions Limited (TCSL). First, the Bio-CNG EPC undertaking of TBSPL — described as the 'Technology, Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-Compressed Natural Gas (Bio CNG) projects', with FY26 turnover of Rs. 239.35 crore, i.e. 3.67% of the listed entity's standalone turnover — is demerged out of TBSPL and merged into Thermax Limited, while the Operations & Maintenance (O&M) business stays behind in TBSPL. The stated reason is that the EPC undertaking 'is in line with the business of the Company', so similar businesses are consolidated into the listed parent, leaving TBSPL's management free to 'focus on the remaining segment O&M'; the broader objective is to 're-organize and segregate the different business verticals and focus on core businesses', so that 'the two entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability'. Second, TCSL — a near-dormant entity (FY26 total income Rs. 0.8 crore, net worth Rs. 0.6 crore, paid-up capital Rs. 10.0 crore, doing energy projects, an Energy Exchange Platform, electrostatic precipitators and regenerative air preheaters) — is merged into Thermax Limited 'to simplify overall group structure and reduce administrative overheads', with management expecting 'a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios', 'annual cost savings for the Thermax Group' and metrics that 'convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics'. The financial backdrop for the Bio-CNG leg is weak: TBSPL carried a negative net worth of Rs. (106.9) crore on FY26 total income of Rs. 260.9 crore, Thermax took a Rs. 30 crore impairment on its TBSPL investment in Q3 FY26, bio-CNG was repeatedly cited as a drag (low-margin legacy orders, orders 'not as per our expectations'), and in Q1 FY27 the group reclassified TBSPL out of Industrial Infra into Green Solutions. Mechanically it is a pure internal reorganisation: both entities are wholly owned, no shares or cash consideration pass, Thermax's shares in TCSL are cancelled, TBSPL remains an unlisted wholly owned subsidiary, there is no change in shareholding pattern or control, and the Scheme 'will have no impact on the consolidated financial statements / results of the Company'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaces in the filings as a sequence of group-simplification steps rather than in any call: Thermax first took TBSPL from 65% to 76.97% via a rights issue (May 7, 2025) and then to 100% by buying Everenviro's 23.03% (completed August 20, 2025), making a clean demerger possible; on October 17, 2025 the board approved the merger of Buildtech Products India into Thermax on consolidation/compliance-reduction logic (NCLT sanction June 2, 2026, received June 3, 2026), and on February 4, 2026 two step-down wind subsidiaries (Jalansar into Kanakal) were amalgamated on the same consolidation, synergy and compliance-cost reasoning. Alongside, the Feb 2, 2026 Q3 FY26 release and the May 8, 2026 Q4 FY26 call flagged bio-CNG as the weak spot — low-margin legacy orders being worked off, orders 'not as per our expectations', projects in performance-trial stage — and a Rs. 30 crore impairment was taken on the TBSPL investment in Q3 FY26. The composite Scheme itself was only approved and disclosed on July 30, 2026, with Appointed Date April 1, 2026, in the same board meeting as Q1 FY27 results; the Q1 FY27 filing also recorded the segment realignment of TBSPL from Industrial Infra to Green Solutions, so by then the plan had become 'EPC into the listed parent, O&M left in TBSPL' plus the absorption of TCSL. No earnings call in the readable record discusses the Scheme, because the only call with extractable text (May 2026) predates the July 30, 2026 board approval.

verdict.rationale: Management is demerging the Sugar Business of Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd. (PAIL) into Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL), a wholly owned subsidiary, so that PAIL becomes a pure-play premium alco-bev company; CFO Natwar Aggarwal framed it on the April 29, 2026 call as "we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio," with the scheme Board-approved April 28, 2026, filed with SEBI, KPMG as adviser, and completion envisaged in FY27. The stated intent is to pool human and capital resources behind the Alco-Bev portfolio (Indri single malt, Camikara rum, Cashmir vodka, Whistler blended whisky) and to list sugar — described as a "traditional heritage business" — as a separate entity rather than sell it. The economics behind it are visible in the numbers management cited: Alco-Bev revenue grew 42% to INR 908 crore (from INR 639 crore) with 31.5% EBITDA margins and 45–50% IMFL margins, while sugar was only INR 233.05 crore of turnover (20.53% of the listed entity) and dragged Q4 standalone EBITDA margin down ~300 bps as sugar's quarterly EBITDA margin collapsed from 11% to 2%; the segment tables show the sugar segment result at a loss of INR 904.62 lakh in FY26 versus a loss of INR 327.13 lakh in FY25, with sugar segment assets of INR 10,553.97 lakh against segment liabilities of INR 22,166.79 lakh. Management also repeatedly blamed sugar seasonality for making quarter-to-quarter margins hard to read. The scheme's own rationale (Annexure B) lists focused attention for each core business and the ability to attract required investment, greater business focus and enhanced shareholder value, more efficient use of financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, value unlock "through price-discovery of the individual entities," the "right operating architecture" with sharper individual strategies and "clear capital allocation," and separately listed companies attracting a specific set of investors with financial flexibility and "stronger capital market outcomes." Mechanically it is a mirror listing: no cash consideration, 1 PFEL share of INR 10 for every 9 PAIL shares (ratio fixed on sugar's turnover and assets), PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, producing "two listed companies with proportionate shareholding." No investor, lender or business partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as a management/Board decision, recommended by the Audit Committee and Independent Directors, alongside the unrelated FY27 agenda of INR 250–300 crore incremental Indri revenue, INR 300–400 crore from the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh plant, 60–70% growth and brand-side inorganic options.
verdict.evolution: Only one earnings call falls in the window, the FY26 call of April 29, 2026, and the demerger appears there already as a done decision rather than an idea being floated — announced in the CFO's opening remarks the day after the April 28, 2026 Board meeting approved the scheme and filed it with the exchanges/SEBI, with KPMG as partner and FY27 as the completion target. It resurfaced later in the same call only when Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital pressed on intent (sell or separately list), drawing the explicit answer that sugar would be listed separately, not sold. The filings then track execution rather than rationale: the April 28, 2026 Regulation 30 outcome with the full Annexure B rationale, share entitlement ratio and sugar turnover of INR 233.05 crore (20.53%), the April 28, 2026 press release restating the pure-play framing, and the August 17, 2026 intimation of BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 (SEBI comments dated August 13, 2026) clearing the way for the NCLT petition. Earlier filings in the window (November–December 2025) concern only CCD and warrant conversions and never mention a separation.

verdict.rationale: Pricol's board (approval announced June 27, 2026) is demerging its Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions ('DICVS') undertaking — driver information systems including connected, electronic, mechanical and electro-mechanical instrument clusters, integrated infotainment, advanced e-cockpit solutions, telematics, battery management systems and a few sensors — into Pricol Autotech Limited, leaving Pricol Limited with the Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems ('ACFMS') and Precision Products ('P3L') businesses. The scale cited is material: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crores for FY ending March 31, 2026, or 61.17% of consolidated turnover, with management stating both halves have 'acquired sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses.' The stated problem is that the two sides operate with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles inside one structure, which creates operational complexity, slow decision-making, and shared processes, policies, systems and governance that fit neither business. The fix is two focused platforms — an automotive technology entity and an automotive & industrial precision engineering entity — each with dedicated management, independent capital allocation, and its own governance, described as 'simpler, sharper and more agile' to meet fast-changing technology needs and dynamic market realities. Capital-markets reasoning is explicit: clearer visibility of each business's stakeholder value, growth prospects and investment merits, improved ability to attract strategic and financial investors, greater flexibility to access capital, and unlocking shareholder value. Mechanically it is value-neutral at the shareholder level — no cash consideration, 1:1 share entitlement (1 Pricol Autotech share of INR 1 face value per Pricol share), no change in Pricol's shareholding pattern, and Pricol Autotech's register mirroring Pricol's at 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public, with listing sought on NSE and BSE. Valuation rests on SSPA & Co's Share Entitlement Ratio Report dated 27th June 2026, with a fairness opinion from Saffron Capital Advisors.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied in this prompt — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so the call-by-call emergence of the idea cannot be reconstructed from these texts. The only dated evidence here is the scheme filing itself: board approval of the scheme of arrangement announced Coimbatore, June 27th, 2026, with the share entitlement ratio report of the same date (27th June 2026). The filing's own framing — 'Over the years' the DICVS business 'has evolved into a differentiated platform,' and 'Over time with a well thoughtout and clear strategic intent' both businesses reached standalone scale — implies a multi-year build-up to the decision, but the filing does not date those earlier steps.

points.quote: The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.

points.point: Stated strategic motive: build a simpler, sharper, more agile entity able to keep pace with the technology cycle and market conditions specific to DICVS.
points.quote: The demerger of the DICVS Business is a strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper and more agile corporate entity, to meet the fast changing needs and technologies related to this business and its dynamic market realities.

points.point: The core problem named is mismatch inside one company — the two businesses differ on customers, competition, capital allocation and risk, and each has now reached standalone scale.
points.quote: The Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company currently operates with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles.

points.point: Both halves are said to have outgrown the combined structure, which is the filing's justification for separating now rather than earlier.

points.point: Benefit list includes independent capital allocation and faster decision-making via reduced complexity, plus dedicated management teams for each business.
points.quote: Financial flexibility for each entity to pursue investment decisions aligned with their respective business portfolios and market requirements ;

points.point: Explicit investor-facing rationale: separate platforms should make each business's value and growth visible and make it easier to attract strategic and financial investors and access capital.
points.quote: Creation of focused and independent business platforms for the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company, with clear and enhanced visibility of their respective stakeholder value, growth prospects and investment merits, improved abilit y to attract strategic and financial investors to meet the needs of the respective business, greater flexibility to access capital, pursue growth and technology opportunities and implement their respective long -term strategies .

points.point: The structure created is two named platforms — an automotive technology entity (Pricol Autotech, DICVS) and an automotive & industrial precision engineering entity (Pricol Limited, holding ACFMS and P3L).
points.quote: Strategic demerger to create two focused  business platform s – an Automotive Technology Entity and an Automotive  & Industrial  Precision Engineering Entity, for a simpler, sharper and more agile structure meeting the fast -changing technological needs and the dynamic market realities

points.point: DICVS is characterised as having evolved into a differentiated platform needing its own long-term strategy, technology capabilities and partnerships for integrated solutions.
points.quote: The proposed demerger  recognises this evolution and enables the business to pursue independent long -term strategies, strengthen technology capabilities , partnerships for integrated solution offerings  and respond more effectively to changing industry dynamics.

points.point: Retained-business case: ACFMS is backed by growing domestic and export footprints in fluid management and control, and P3L is positioned for expanding precision components demand.
points.quote: The ACFMS and P3L businesses will continue to remain part of Pricol  Limited, with the ACFMS business being supported by growing domestic and export footprint s and opportunities in fluid management and control  solutions , and the P3L business being strategically positioned to capitali se on the expanding opportunity in precision  components.

points.point: Consideration is a value-neutral mirror split: no cash, 1:1 entitlement, Pricol Autotech's shareholding mirroring Pricol's (promoters 38.51%, public 61.49% post-scheme), with listing sought on NSE and BSE.
points.quote: Shareholders of Pricol Limited will receive one fully paid -up equity share of Pricol Autotech Limited for every one fully paid -up equity share held in Pricol Limited (1:1 share entitlement ratio) , resulting in the shareholding of Pricol Autotech Limited mirroring the shareholding of Pricol Limited , subject to the Scheme becoming effective.

points.point: CMD Vikram Mohan frames timing as businesses having diverged on customers, technology priorities, capital requirements and growth, making independent operation right now.
points.quote: Over the years, our businesses have evolved into strong and differentiated platforms with distinct customer needs, technology priorities , capital requirements  and growth opportunities.

points.point: Valuation and fairness are documented: SSPA & Co's share entitlement ratio report dated 27th June 2026 with a fairness opinion from SEBI-registered merchant banker Saffron Capital Advisors.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and the Digital Innovation business of Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly owned Global Capability Centre (GCC), carved out into a new wholly owned subsidiary, Pivot Path Private Limited, under a Sections 230–232 Scheme of Arrangement, and then majority-sold. Management's stated reason is that this unit — built inside Arco Lab across life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, and technology-enabled operational services — outgrew its captive role: 'As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.' The filings name four problems the separation solves: supporting its next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — none of which a cost-centre inside a pharma manufacturer can fund or staff. The numbers cited are modest and explain why it is not core to Strides: FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) — just 3% of Strides' turnover — with EBITDA of ₹169 million, net worth of ₹100 million standalone (0.3% of Strides' net worth) and ₹360 million consolidated (1%). Ascent Capital (through Ascent Growth Trust) with co-investor Vintage Classic Limited values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300 million post-money; Strides realises ~₹1,000 million (₹750 million at closing, ₹250 million on the first anniversary), keeps 19.95%, and Ascent injects ₹500 million of primary capital, leaving Investors 65.05% and a 15% ESOP pool, with Pivot Path reclassified as an Associate. Badree Komandur frames it as Strides' repeatable playbook — 'Strides' proven capability to identify, incubate and scale high-potential businesses' — that 'unlocks value for Strides, provides Pivot Path with the resources to scale independently, and allows Strides to retain meaningful participation in its future success,' while also 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet.' No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the pull came from external life-sciences customers and from the incoming financial investor, whose rationale (per Raja Kumar) is to pair 400+ subject matter experts with technology and agentic AI in 'core, non-discretionary segments of the pharmaceutical industry.' Pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is declared not a related party transaction and outside Regulation 37A.
verdict.evolution: The idea does not appear in a single one of the thirteen earnings calls; it exists only in the filings, which reference an intimation of May 15, 2025 for the Arco Lab–Pivot Path scheme, with an Appointed Date of April 10, 2025 — i.e. the carve-out was in motion for more than a year unmentioned. NCLT Bengaluru pronounced approval on May 18, 2026 (the same day as the Q4 FY26 board meeting whose call, on May 18, 2026, discussed only US/ex-US growth, margins and deleveraging), the order hit the NCLT portal May 20, 2026, the certified copy arrived May 25, 2026, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Only on June 27, 2026 did the plan's second leg surface: the board approved selling a majority stake to the Ascent Capital consortium, converting what the Scheme had set up as a wholly owned subsidiary into a ~20%-held Associate. The nearest the calls come is context on the earlier OneSource/softgel playbook — Arco Lab named as the wholly owned subsidiary parking the OneSource stake (May 22, 2025 call) and the ₹78.8 billion returned to shareholders via that demerger and listing (July 29, 2025 call).

points.point: The separated business is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business plus its Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path under Sections 230–232, with Appointed Date April 10, 2025 and NCLT approval pronounced May 18, 2026.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).

points.point: The stated purpose of the carve-out is growth capacity, global customer service, agentic-AI platform building and access to outside capital — things it could not do as a captive GCC unit.
points.quote: To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.

points.point: The trigger was external demand: a unit originally serving Strides internally began winning third-party pharma and life-sciences customers and became a standalone platform.
points.quote: As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.

points.point: Strides positions it as a repeatable incubate-and-unlock model rather than a disposal of a problem asset, keeping economic participation.
points.quote: The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.

points.point: Scale cited: FY26 revenue ₹1,447 million (3% of Strides' turnover) and EBITDA ₹169 million; net worth ₹100 million standalone (0.3%) and ₹360 million consolidated (1%) — small enough that it is clearly non-core.
points.quote: For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.

points.point: Economics: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m realised by Strides (₹750m at closing, ₹250m after one year), ₹500m primary infusion by Ascent, Strides left at 19.95% with Investors 65.05% and a 15% ESOP pool.
points.quote: The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.

points.point: Badree Komandur's framing of the three-way benefit — cash and balance-sheet strength for Strides, independent scaling resources for Pivot Path, retained upside.
points.quote: This transaction unlocks value for Strides, provides Pivot Path with the resources to scale independently, and allows Strides to retain meaningful participation in its future success.

points.point: Accounting consequence: Pivot Path drops out of consolidation and becomes an Associate; the deal is declared non-related-party, priced off an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation.
points.quote: Upon completion of the transaction, Pivot Path shall be reclassified as an Associate Company.

points.point: The incoming investor's rationale: 400+ subject matter experts applying technology and agentic AI to compliance, digital transformation and drug safety in non-discretionary pharma spend.
points.quote: Pivot Path brings deep domain expertise across the core, non-discretionary segments of the pharmaceutical industry, capabilities that have been rigorously honed within the Strides stable.

points.point: The Q4 FY26 call, held May 18, 2026 — the very day NCLT pronounced the Pivot Path order — never mentions Pivot Path, Arco Lab or any carve-out; the three-year strategy is described purely in pharma terms.
points.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have been very clear on our priorities, geographical diversification, profitability and balance sheet strength.

points.point: The only call-level support for the value-unlocking logic is the OneSource precedent, cited as the company's demonstrated way of returning value to shareholders.
points.quote: And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.

points.point: Arco Lab — the entity Pivot Path was later carved out of — is discussed on the calls only as the wholly owned subsidiary holding the residual 1.6% OneSource stake, with no hint of a services business inside it.
points.quote: So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, resources to scale independently, serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, access external capital and Ascent's expertise, plus a 15% ESOP pool. For Strides: ~₹1,000m realised (₹750m at closing, ₹250m at one year), a strengthened balance sheet, and a ~20% associate stake retaining upside. No margin, focus or re-rating claims are made.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention Pivot Path or Arco Lab's demerger. No use of proceeds, no reason for selling majority rather than listing, no customer, employee or related-party-pricing detail.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is the hospitality business of Prestige Estates Projects Ltd., housed in subsidiary Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited (PHVL), out of the listed real-estate development parent. Management's stated reason is capital, not distress: Irfan Razack said hospitality is where "a lot of capex will be required," that the currently trading hotel assets are already "booming" and throwing "positive numbers from all the assets," and that there is "a huge pipeline of new assets which are either under planning or under construction or approval" that "will definitely require fresh spending" — "hence an IPO will be the need of the day." The demerger-plus-IPO is therefore framed as giving "additional bandwidth to grow the hospitality business," i.e. a dedicated capital pool for a capex-hungry annuity business instead of funding it from the developer's balance sheet. The only parent-side numbers given are balance-sheet ones: management guided that by end-FY2025 cash flows would be "pretty robust" and debt would fall — clarified as debt-to-equity, not absolute debt — helped by land already paid for at Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel turning into positive cash flows. The push came from the sell side and retail holders asking for updates and for a shareholder quota in the IPO (Kunal Lakhan, Rajeev Venkatesh); no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. A related theme is staying within core competence — on data centres, Zayd Noaman said operations are "completely different, and it's not our expertise," preferring build-to-suit (NTT) and partnerships. The structure ultimately executed was a subsidiary IPO: PHVL filed a DRHP on April 24, 2025, then withdrew it on September 25, 2026 "on account of strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions," with a fresh DRHP possible later.
verdict.evolution: On the May 2024 call the hospitality demerger was already "a work in progress" and management committed to the direction — demerger then IPO — on capex and growth-bandwidth grounds. By the October 2024 call it had moved only to the structuring stage: "too early," with Board approval and the appointment of bankers still ahead, and the retail-quota question deferred. The filings then show execution and reversal: a PHVL DRHP dated April 24, 2025, withdrawn on September 25, 2026 for strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions, with a possible refiling subject to market conditions and approvals.

points.point: Asked for an update on the hospitality demerger, Irfan Razack confirmed it was under way and endorsed the direction as the right one.
points.quote: That's a work in progress and I believe that that's the way to go.

points.point: The core driver given is the capital intensity of hospitality — the demerger plus IPO is meant to create headroom to grow it, since trading assets are performing and a large pipeline is in planning, construction or approval.
points.quote: And once we do the demerger and we do an IPO that will give us additional bandwidth to grow the hospitality business because currently the hospitality business is booming and we're getting positive numbers from all the assets, current assets which are trading and we do have a huge pipeline of new assets which are either under planning or under construction or approval.

points.point: The new pipeline needs fresh money, which management said makes the IPO necessary rather than optional.
points.quote: So all this will definitely require fresh spending and hence an IPO will be the need of the day.

points.point: Parent-side context: land already funded at Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel turns into cash inflows, supporting deleveraging through FY2025 — clarified as debt-to-equity, not absolute debt.
points.quote: So we believ e that the debt levels for the end of financial year 2025 of course there'll be blips up and down quarter -on-quarter, but the cash flows will be pretty robust, and we will try and bring down the debt level from what it is today.

points.point: Five months later the transaction was still only being structured, with Board approval and banker appointments yet to come — so no terms, ratio or timeline were available.
points.quote: It is too early right now. We are in the structuring process.

points.point: A retail shareholder asked for a reserved shareholder quota in the hospitality IPO; management deferred the decision to a later stage.
points.quote: So maybe how much will be the retail quota for the existing shareholders, we'll figure at that point of time once we -- more advanced.

points.point: On data centres, management drew a competence boundary — it will sell land and build to suit (NTT) but not operate — consistent with housing operating-intensive businesses separately or with partners.
points.quote: So with that, we'll build some expertise, but the operations of a data center are completely different, and it's not our expertise.

points.point: The separation was executed as a subsidiary IPO: Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited filed a DRHP dated April 24, 2025 with SEBI, NSE and BSE.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that our subsidiary, Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited ( “PHVL ”), filed a Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated April 24, 2025 (“DRHP ”) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI ”), the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited (“Stock Exchanges ”).

points.point: On September 25, 2026 the PHVL board withdrew the DRHP, citing strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions — no further rationale was disclosed.
points.quote: However, the board of directors of PHVL has decided to withdraw the DRHP on account of strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions, pursuant to its resolution dated September 25, 2026 and corresponding communication dated September 25 , 2026 made to the book running lead managers to the Offer .

points.point: The listing is deferred, not abandoned: PHVL may refile a DRHP later, conditional on markets, approvals and other considerations.
points.quote: Additionally, PHVL may consider filing a fresh draft red herring prospectus with SEBI in the future for an initial public offering of its equity shares in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, subject to suitable market conditions, receipt of requisite approvals and other considerations.

verdict.what_management_expects: Hospitality: demerger plus IPO gives bandwidth and fresh equity for heavy capex on its pipeline under planning, construction and approval, while trading assets already give positive numbers. Parent: cash flows from Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel land bring debt-to-equity down by FY2025. No margin or valuation targets stated.
verdict.gaps: No hospitality revenue, EBITDA, keys or capex numbers; no debt quantum, scheme rationale text, entitlement ratio, asset-debt split, lender or partner consent, valuation, timeline, or what "strategic considerations" meant.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.
verdict.evolution: These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

points.point: The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.

points.point: The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India.
points.quote: The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.

points.point: MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering.
points.quote: As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.

points.point: Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals.
points.quote: During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".

points.point: The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.

points.point: Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative.
points.quote: I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.

points.point: The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%.
points.quote: Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.

points.point: A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth.
points.quote: The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.

points.point: Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts.
points.quote: We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.

points.point: The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual.
points.quote: In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.

points.point: Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant.
points.quote: So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.

points.point: Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim.
points.quote: So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.

points.point: Q1 FY27 (12 August 2026) validates the focused-entity framing: revenue INR 9,707.7 million, up 18.3% YoY, PBT INR 869.2 million at 9.0%, with growth in Wind, General Machinery and Agriculture (Tractors) despite currency and residual demerger costs.
points.quote: In our 3rd quarter as a focused, independent business, SKF India (Industrial) delivered 18.3% year-on-year Sales growth, while maintaining a healthy 9% PBT (in spite of headwinds from currency and demerger-related expenses).

verdict.what_management_expects: For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.
verdict.gaps: No pre-demerger call rationale; no named requester (investors, lenders, partners); no synergy loss, standalone-cost, tax or valuation quantification; nothing on the automotive entity's economics or arm's-length agreement terms.

verdict.rationale: Per the scheme's own rationale, HEG Advanced Materials Ltd. (the First Petitioner / Demerged Company, CIN L23109MP1972PLC008290, incorporated 27 October 1972, registered office at Mandideep near Bhopal, Dist. Raisen, M.P.) says its two core businesses — manufacturing graphite electrodes (including other carbon products) and generation of thermal and hydel power — have each 'acquired critical mass' and now each need flexibility and independence to grow faster in a fast-changing, technology- and innovation-driven environment. The filing argues the two have differentiated strategies, different industry-specific risks, different market dynamics and different growth trajectories, and that the nature of competition in each is distinct, so each is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders; a structure 'amenable for future growth' is therefore required. The claimed benefits of segregation are unlocking value of each business for shareholders of the Demerged Company, better flexibility in accessing capital, separating businesses with different risk/return profiles so investors can choose what suits their strategy, focused growth strategy and focused management per business, greater visibility on each business's performance, enhanced operational efficiency, and de-risking the businesses from each other. The filing concludes the Scheme is in the interests of all stakeholders of the Demerged/Transferee, Transferor and Resulting Companies.
