verdict.rationale: Inox Green Energy Services Ltd (IGESL) is demerging its Power Evacuation / substation business — roughly 84 substations, 33kV and EHV transmission lines and common project infrastructure — and merging it into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services), Inox Wind's EPC arm, so that IGESL is left as a pure-play, asset-light renewable O&M annuity company and the evacuation infra sits with the business that actually builds it. Management's core explanation is historical and structural: when IGESL was carved out of Inox Wind before its IPO, the EPC business was slump-sold to Resco, but already-commissioned substations could not be moved because, in Devansh Jain's words, it 'would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers' who would have used that consent to renegotiate O&M contracts — so IGESL was left as a 'trustee' of assets whose balance sheet it 'unnecessarily inflated'; the NCLT scheme route avoids those customer consents. The quantified benefits management repeated every call: gross block of ~INR 1,000 crore (described as ~INR 750 crore net block in Aug 2024) leaves the balance sheet, annual depreciation of ~INR 50–55 crore (~INR 13–17 crore a quarter) is eliminated, while only ~INR 3–4 crore of quarterly revenue (~INR 10 crore a year, later ~INR 4–5 crore 'yearly' at one point) goes out — so Akhil Jindal said it adds '~INR 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis', taking reported PAT from ~INR 6 crore to ~INR 18–20 crore per quarter, with 'significant improvement in ROE and ROCE'. Because there is no capex, no finance cost and a ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax loss shield that stays with IGESL, management says EBITDA ≈ PBT ≈ cash PAT — hence the FY27 guidance of 'upwards of INR 600 crore' EBITDA converting almost entirely into operating cash profit. The scheme itself adds the strategic logic: the two businesses have 'separate and distinct' risk, reward, financial profile, competition and opportunities; evacuation infra 'is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders'; and consolidating the same line of business into IRSL unlocks value and gives enhanced focus. Management also framed it as optionality for shareholders — IRSL lists automatically and IGESL holders receive 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 IGESL shares (~20% of IRSL to IGESL shareholders, ~10% to minorities), so Akhil Jindal said shareholders now have 'a choice to hold any part of the business', which he called 'the intention of separating these businesses'. On the other side, the infra is becoming more valuable inside IRSL: INR 175 crore was raised at IRSL at ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, CERC's hybridisation amendment turns the base into ~10 GW of 'plug and play' evacuation-ready infra, and IRSL is being built up with in-house cranes, transformers and power electronics.
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaced as a problem, not a plan: on the 9-Feb-2024 call management conceded IGESL carried ~INR 13 crore quarterly depreciation on a legacy 4 GW block with 'no future CapEx under Inox Green at all', all new infra going into Resco. By the 9-Aug-2024 call the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate demerging the power evacuation business (net block then put at ~INR 750 crore, timeline 6–9 months), the 25-Oct-2024 call quantified it (~INR 3–4 crore revenue out, ~INR 12 crore added to quarterly PAT), and the board approved the scheme on 13-Nov-2024 with appointed date 1-Oct-2024. Through FY26 it was a slow regulatory grind — exchange no-objections and NCLT filing by the 1-Sep-2025 call (approval expected in 2–3 quarters), shareholder and creditor approvals by 14-Nov-2025, 'final stages of hearing' on 13-Feb-2026 — with the gross block figure restated upward to ~INR 1,000 crore and the pitch widening from 'depreciation elimination' to 'unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green'. NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned it on 13-Mar-2026, the scheme became effective 4-May-2026, the 29-May-2026 call reported the block and depreciation gone with ROE/ROCE improved, and 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares were allotted on 24-Aug-2026 at 122 per 1,000.

points.point: Before any demerger was proposed, management admitted IGESL was carrying depreciation on a legacy 4 GW substation block (3 GW commissioned, 1 GW unutilised) while all future common-infrastructure capex would be incurred in Resco, not Inox Green — i.e. a shrinking asset with permanent P&L drag.
points.quote: So, no future CapEx under Inox Green at all.

points.point: The board appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger of the power evacuation business, with the stated objective of a clean, asset-light balance sheet and elimination of depreciation; net block to be removed was put at ~INR 750 crore and the process at six to nine months.
points.quote: Demerger of power infrastructure facilities currently on the balance sheet of Inox Green will result in a cleaner and asset light balance sheet.

points.point: Devansh Jain explained the historical accident being corrected: IGESL originally housed both EPC and O&M, the EPC business was slump-sold to Resco before IGESL's listing, but commissioned substations stayed behind even though customers had already paid for them, leaving IGESL merely a trustee of an inflated balance sheet.
points.quote: Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.

points.point: The reason it could not be fixed at the time of the IPO carve-out, and why the NCLT scheme route is being used now: a direct transfer would have required consent from more than 200 O&M customers, handing them leverage to reopen contracts.
points.quote: We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.

points.point: Akhil Jindal quantified the trade for Pritesh Chheda: ~INR 3–4 crore of quarterly revenue leaves with the substation business but the entire depreciation goes, so reported quarterly PAT would move from ~INR 6 crore to ~INR 18–20 crore; shareholders of IGESL receive Resco shares in lieu, valuation then still undetermined.
points.quote: So, broadly that will add around Rs. 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis.

points.point: Akhil Jindal told investors to model EBITDA as the proxy for PAT because post-demerger there is no depreciation; the next year's balance sheet would be asset-light and IGESL shareholders would receive ~20% of Resco (~10% to minorities, ~10% to promoters).
points.quote: So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset-light balance sheet.

points.point: Challenged by Bhavik Shah that removing the assets would simply convert depreciation into opex and compress the 50% O&M margin, Mathusudhana said the evacuation and common infrastructure is not needed to deliver O&M at all — it belongs to the EPC game — and confirmed the ~INR 700 crore tax losses stay in IGESL because they sit at company, not asset, level.
points.quote: So as far as the power evacuation and the common infrastructure, we have developed is not required for O&M services per se.

points.point: Scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad after exchange no-objections; management restated the removal as ~INR 1,000 crore of gross block and INR 50–55 crore of annual depreciation lifting PBT by that amount and improving ROE/ROCE, and disclosed INR 175 crore raised at IRSL at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation — i.e. the infra is being valued separately.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: Asked by Hansal Thakkar whether IGESL and IRSL would themselves be demerged out of Inox Wind to IWL shareholders, Devansh Jain refused, and Akhil Jindal reframed the separation as deliberately giving shareholders a menu — O&M, infrastructure, or the whole chain via Inox Wind — stating this was the purpose of splitting the businesses.
points.quote: As management, we have provided enough window for a shareholder to be present where he wants to be. And I think that was the intention of separating these businesses.

points.point: With shareholder and creditor approvals in hand, the framing widened from accounting cleanup to value creation across two entities, with IRSL to be listed as Inox Wind's EPC arm and IGESL freed of demerged depreciation.
points.quote: I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.

points.point: At the final NCLT hearing stage management stressed the asymmetry of the trade — only about INR 10 crore of annual revenue leaves versus ~INR 50 crore of depreciation — and confirmed no material impact on the INR 600 crore+ FY27 EBITDA math, with PBT equal to EBITDA and no tax outgo given the tax shield.
points.quote: It will also lead to significant improvement in the ROE and ROCE of Inox Green.

points.point: Post-NCLT approval, Mathusudhana reported the removal as done and Sanjeev Agarwal confirmed IRSL would list automatically; management declined to give IRSL's top line or EBITDA profile until the demerger dates were announced.
points.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been eliminated from Inox Green's balance sheet.

points.point: The scheme's first stated rationale is segregation of two verticals with fundamentally different economics — O&M services versus Power Evacuation — each capable of standing alone.
points.quote: The nature of risks, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities are separate and distinct for the O&M services business and the Power Evacuation Business.

points.point: The scheme states the separated infra business can attract a different capital base than an O&M annuity company, and that consolidating the same line of business into IRSL unlocks value and lends enhanced focus.
points.quote: Further, the Power Evacuation Business is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The explicit end-state objective, with two listed entities — one pure O&M, one EPC plus power evacuation — pursuing independent strategies; share entitlement set at 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 IGESL shares (valuation by Finvox Analytics, fairness opinion by Marwadi Chandarana), appointed date 1-Oct-2024, effective 4-May-2026, 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares allotted 24-Aug-2026.
points.quote: The Demerger aims to establish IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, and as a result, is considering hiving off the Power Evacuation Business

verdict.what_management_expects: Inox Green: pure-play, zero-capex O&M annuity — ~INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore depreciation gone, ~50% EBITDA margins, FY27 EBITDA above INR 600 crore converting almost fully to cash profit against a INR 700 crore tax shield, sharply better ROE/ROCE, EBITDA ≈ PBT ≈ cash PAT. IRSL: a focused, separately listed EPC and evacuation-infrastructure platform (INR 175 crore raised at ~INR 7,400 crore) able to draw its own investors and lenders, unlocking value for Inox Wind and Inox Green shareholders.
verdict.gaps: No IRSL revenue/EBITDA disclosure, no basis for the 122:1000 ratio, no explanation of how losing owned substations affects O&M stickiness that previously justified 50% margins.

verdict.segment_name: Power Evacuation (Demerged Undertaking — power evacuation / substation business demerged into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited)
verdict.measure_notes: Revenue = segment revenue per Ind AS 108 primary business segments; for FY2026 and FY2025 the Power Evacuation segment revenue is entirely external and is shown as 'External Revenue - Discontinuing Operations-Power Evacuation' (no inter-segment revenue in either year). Operating profit = 'Segment Result' (EBIT-level, before unallocable other income, finance cost and tax; not EBITDA — segment depreciation for Power Evacuation was 5,226.86 lakh in FY2025 and nil in FY2026). PAT is not disclosed per segment; the FY2026 figure shown is consolidated 'Net Profit/(Loss) After Tax - Discontinuing Operations' (-90.97), which for FY2026 relates to Power Evacuation alone since Power Generation discontinued revenue was nil (standalone MD&A shows -91 lakh). FY2025 discontinued PAT of -1,413.41 lakh is not usable as it combines Power Evacuation and Power Generation, so left null.

years.source: Annual Report 2024 — page 285 / 286 (no Power Evacuation segment reported; segments were O&M, EPC, Trading, Power generation)
Annual Report 2026 — page 344 (comparative FY2025 column)
Annual Report 2026 — page 344 (revenue, segment result); page 345 (discontinued operations PAT)

verdict.not_found: No FY2024 Power Evacuation segment disclosure; no segment PAT line; FY2025 PAT not separable from Power Generation; no quarterly Power Evacuation revenue/EBITDA in any presentation.

verdict.rationale: The texts do not describe a separation at all: GODIGIT is doing the opposite — a reverse merger that collapses its promoter/holding company, Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited, into the listed insurer, Go Digit General Insurance Limited, with Infoworks dissolved without winding up and its entire 67,48,09,606-share (c.73%) stake in GODIGIT cancelled. The trigger management gives is regulatory: an IRDAI advisory dated 10 October 2023, reaffirmed 2 May 2024, told GODIGIT to stop availing facilities-management and technology-advisory services from Infoworks; that arrangement was discontinued from 1 November 2024, and Infoworks then 'ceased carrying on all business activities as on 30th September 2025 and only holds shares' — i.e. the holdco became an empty shell with no business and only INR 83,32,714 of unsecured creditors. The Scheme's stated rationale is therefore simplification: removing a shareholding tier, cutting administrative overheads and duplicate compliance across two companies, speeding decision-making, and aligning with 'the regulatory intent to move towards leaner holding structures in the insurance business, with fewer layers.' It also puts Oben Ventures LLP (3,78,975 equity shares), Kamesh Goyal (1,53,000) and FAL Corporation (4,90,959 equity plus 63,00,000 CCPS-1 and 15,00,000 CCPS-2) directly on GODIGIT's register, which management says lets them fund 'the Transferee Company's capital infusion needs, and growth objectives' and 'strengthen the Transferee Company's ownership structure and serve to enhance investor confidence.' Economically it is close to neutral for minorities: swap ratios of 2,62,589 GODIGIT shares per 1,000 Infoworks equity shares, 55,925 per 1,000 CCPS-1 and 36,694 per 1,000 CCPS-2 (RBSA valuation and EY fairness opinion, both 19 December 2025, on 30 September 2025 audited accounts) issue roughly 11,69,000 net new shares, 'negligible, at approximately 0.03%' dilution, at a price of INR 375.10 versus a then market price Kamesh Goyal cited as INR 343–345. Nobody outside — no investor, lender or partner — is said to have asked for it; the only outside actors named are IRDAI, CCI and NCLT, and the only analyst intervention is Sanketh Godha of Avendus Spark asking where the reverse merger stood and whether Fairfax would keep its 58% stake.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced outside the quarterly cycle: the board approved the Scheme on 19 December 2025 (Kamesh Goyal abstaining as an interested director) and the company held what he called 'a very short call' in December 2025, so the first full explanation on an earnings call came only in the CALL Feb 2026 (held 22 January 2026), where he walked through the three-way split of Infoworks' stake, the ~0.03%/INR 375.10 issuance and the promoters' roughly INR 43 crore commitment, stressing nothing changes in board, management or the two-promoter arrangement. By CALL May 2026 (28 April 2026) an analyst had to prompt him for a status update and he had nothing to add — 'there is no news as such in terms of what the next steps are or the time frame' — pivoting instead to Fairfax's 58% and open-offer mechanics. After that the story moves entirely into filings rather than calls: stock-exchange observation letters 22 April 2026, IRDAI Section 35 application 20 April 2026, CCI notice 12 May 2026 and approval 28 July 2026, NCLT order 13 August 2026, an IRDAI-driven clarificatory modification to the Scheme in September 2026, and the shareholder meeting set for 5 November 2026 — while CALL Jul 2026 (23 July 2026), the 10th earnings call, never mentions the amalgamation at all.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation, not a separation: Infoworks (the promoter/holding company) merges into the listed insurer and is dissolved without winding up, with shares of GODIGIT issued to Infoworks' shareholders.
points.quote: The Scheme, provides for inter-alia: amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Transferee Company ("Amalgamation") with effect from the Appointed Date (as defined hereinafter) in accordance with Section 2(1B) and other applicable provisions of the IT Act (as defined in the Scheme) and/or Section 2(6) of the Income-tax Act, 2025) and consequent dissolution of the Transferor Company without being wound up, and the issuance of shares of the Transferee Company to the shareholders of the Transferor Company.

points.point: The operative cause is an IRDAI advisory of 10 October 2023, reaffirmed 2 May 2024, that forced GODIGIT to stop buying facilities-management and technology-advisory services from Infoworks; the arrangement ended 1 November 2024, hollowing out the holdco.
points.quote: Pursuant to an advisory issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India dated 10th October 2023 and further reaffirmed on 2nd May 2024, the Second Applicant Company was advised to discontinue the services it was availing from the First Applicant Company, and the arrangements between the Applicant Companies for the provision of such services was discontinued with effect from 1st November 2024.

points.point: Post that advisory Infoworks has no business left at all — it is a pure holding shell sitting on the GODIGIT stake, with only INR 83,32,714 of unsecured creditors as at 31 March 2026 and no material liabilities.
points.quote: Subsequent thereto, the First Applicant Company has ceased carrying on all business activities as on 30th September 2025 and only holds shares in the Second Applicant Company.

points.point: The headline stated benefit is removing a shareholding tier, with a parallel claim that it matches the regulator's direction of travel for insurance group structures.
points.quote: Eliminate the complexity of the holding company structure, and result in a simplified structure of holdings, which will also be in line with the regulatory intent to move towards leaner holding structures in the insurance business, with fewer layers.

points.point: Second stated benefit is cost and compliance: one company instead of two, lower administrative overhead and faster decisions; the cost-benefit note concedes transaction and regulatory fees but says long-run benefits outweigh them.
points.quote: Simplifies the corporate structure, reducing administrative overheads, formalities and compliance requirements associated with maintaining multiple companies. This can lead to lower operational costs and streamlined decision-making processes.

points.point: Third stated benefit is capital access — putting Oben Ventures, Kamesh Goyal and FAL Corporation directly on GODIGIT's register so they can fund the insurer's own capital needs rather than through a layer.
points.quote: The holding of shares directly in the Transferee Company will enable the shareholders of the Transferor Company to contribute to the Transferee Company's capital infusion needs, and growth objectives, thereby creating a much stronger entity with greater access to capital and resources for expansion.

points.point: Consideration: 2,62,589 GODIGIT shares per 1,000 Infoworks equity shares, plus 55,925 per 1,000 CCPS-1 and 36,694 per 1,000 CCPS-2, against cancellation of Infoworks' 67,48,09,606 GODIGIT shares; public dilution is put at about 0.03%.
points.quote: The resulting dilution to the public shareholding of the Transferee Company is expected to be negligible, at approximately 0.03%.

points.point: First full earnings-call explanation (22 January 2026): Infoworks' stake splits to three named holders, with a small share issuance quantified.
points.quote: Basically, the shares which are held by Go Digit Infoworks are being split into three shareholders, which is Oben Ventures, FAL, and in my individual name. In addition, about 11,69,000 shares, roughly about 0.03% of the shares are being issued at a price of about Rs. 375.10.

points.point: Management pre-empted governance fears by insisting the merger changes nothing operationally — same board, same management, same inter-promoter arrangement — and framed the above-market issue price as promoter conviction.
points.quote: Other than that, there is no difference. The management stays the same, both stays the same, and the way the company is managed in terms of between the two promoters, that also stays the same.

points.point: In closing remarks he repeated the no-impact message and cited roughly INR 43 crore of promoter money going in at INR 375 versus a INR 345 market price.
points.quote: The shareholders intend to buy 43 crores of shares at a price of 375, the promoters. So you can actually see the confidence of the promoters when they're actually putting money at a substantially higher price than the market price at that time of 345.

points.point: An analyst (Sanketh Godha, Avendus Spark) had to raise it, explicitly calling it a reverse merger and asking whether increased liquidity would tempt Fairfax to sell down.
points.quote: And lastly, one more technical question. On this reverse merger, where we are standing and maybe whenever the reverse merger goes through, do you think Fairfax will continue to hold the stake what it is holding or they have intention to pair the stake given it will become more liquid for them to sell?

points.point: Kamesh Goyal gave no timeline at all, and answered the Fairfax question with structural logic — 58% held, a drop below 51% would make regaining majority prohibitively expensive — rather than any sell-down intent.
points.quote: On amalgamation, there is no news as such in terms of what the next steps are or the time frame.

points.point: On promoter stability he argued Fairfax is structurally locked in, recalling that it exited a 35% minority position in 2017 specifically to get majority control of this venture.
points.quote: And secondly, I think they are at 58%. If they decide to go, I am saying, below 51%, below this, then for them to come up and gain a majority would trigger a massive open offer.

points.point: Approvals sequence: exchange observation letters 22 April 2026; IRDAI Section 35 application 20 April 2026 (still pending, with an addendum on 3 August 2026 after IRDAI amended its 2024 Registration Regulations on 30 July 2026 to expressly permit such a transaction); CCI cleared it 28 July 2026.
points.quote: the IRDAI (Registration, Capital Structure, Transfer of Shares and Amalgamation of Insurers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 were notified on 30th  July 2026, which amended the erstwhile IRDAI (Registration, Capital Structure, Transfer of Shares and Amalgamation of Insurers) Regulations, 2024 ("Registration Regulations, 2024") to expressly permit transactions such as the Proposed Amalgamation.

points.point: IRDAI also forced textual changes to the Scheme so it expressly invokes Section 35 of the Insurance Act, 1938 — described as clarificatory only, with the shareholder meeting then fixed for 5 November 2026 under the NCLT order of 13 August 2026.
points.quote: The aforesaid modifications are clarificatory in nature and have been incorporated solely to address the observation of IRDAI, and that all other terms and conditions of the Scheme shall remain unchanged and continue to be in full force and effect.

points.point: Risk disclosure is deliberately thin because the merging entity is empty: no capital, solvency or policyholder-obligation impact is expected, and the only flagged risks are unforeseen liabilities and approval delay.
points.quote: The Transferor Company has ceased all business activities except holding shares in the Transferee Company and has no material liabilities.

verdict.what_management_expects: Not a split, so no two-entity outcome. For GODIGIT: one fewer shareholding tier, lower administrative and compliance cost, faster decisions, a stronger ownership structure and greater investor confidence, with promoters able to fund capital infusion and growth directly. No cash outflow, ~0.03% public dilution, no change to margins, solvency, capital position, board, management or its IRDAI Registration No. 158 business.
verdict.gaps: No earnings-call discussion of financial effect, tax, timeline or IRDAI's pending verdict; Jul 2026 call omits it entirely; Fairfax's own intentions admittedly unknown to management.

verdict.rationale: The separation is a demerger, approved by the board in February 2025, in which Kitex Childrenswear Limited (KCL, the Demerged Company) carves out its "Textile Business Division" and transfers it into the listed Kitex Garments Limited (KGL, the Resulting Company) under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013, with KGL issuing new equity shares to KCL's shareholders on a Share Entitlement Ratio. The demerged undertaking is KCL's infant-wear garment manufacturing at the Kizhakkambalam, Kochi facility plus its 30% equity in Kitex Apparel Parks Limited (KAPL) and its 50% stake in Kitex USA LLC; what stays behind in KCL (the "Remaining Business") is its investments in various subsidiaries including outstanding advances, its equity in KGL, and its investment in land and building. Management's stated problem is that KCL ran two verticals whose "nature of risks, returns, growth and competition... are distinct and requires attribution of dissimilar technical and managerial focus," and that segregating the textile division lets management pursue independent organic and inorganic growth plans with access to increased resources. The second problem is a tangled operating structure: KCL has 56 production lines it had "traditionally" used both for its own revenue and as job work for KGL "with final revenue booked in KGL," alongside KGL's own 42 lines and ~4,900 employees each, and KGL's FY2024 turnover of ₹617 crore; the group also runs an enormous intra-group web (proposed FY27 RPT ceilings of ₹1,992 crore KGL-KAPL, ₹1,472 crore KAPL-KCL, ₹331 crore KGL-Kitex USA, ₹248 crore KGL-KCL, plus a KGL corporate guarantee on KAPL's ₹2,02,300 lakh sanctioned bank lines, ₹1,01,203.99 lakh outstanding at 30 June 2026). The cited commercial trigger is capacity demand — "Global drive by US and Europe customers to move out of China... along with turmoil in Bangladesh has opened up huge potential for India" and "Considering the huge demand for capacity, KCL has decided to use its full capacity for its own revenue." The claimed benefits are economies of scale, a common pool of production, better utilisation of resources, increased customer focus and market share from putting similar activities in one entity; efficient capital allocation and the ability to "attract different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders"; insulating and de-risking the businesses from one another; and "unlocking value... through better price discovery of individual platforms," including scope for future divestments and acquisitions. Post-scheme, KAPL and Kitex USA LLC become 100% subsidiaries of KGL, and the filings show a resultant KGL shareholding of roughly 59.46% / 29.65% / 10.89% across promoters, public and KCL. No party is named as having demanded the separation; the only hard dependency disclosed is KGL's own ₹3,000 crore QIP, which the AGM notice makes "subject to completion of ongoing scheme of arrangement," with proceeds earmarked for capex, repayment of borrowings and long-term working capital including the new Telangana project.
verdict.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the idea is traceable only through filings: the board approved the Scheme in February 2025 (per the quarterly results notes), stock-exchange observation letters followed from BSE on 4 December 2025 and NSE on 5 December 2025, and the NCLT Kochi Bench ordered convening of meetings on 22 January 2026. The notice went out on 10 June 2026 and was supplemented by an Addendum dated 8 July 2026 (filed 10 July 2026) adding the NSE "Annexure M" additional information — pre/post assets, liabilities, revenue and net worth, comparable companies used in the multiples method, unlisted share-capital build-up, and Revenue/PAT/EBITDA justification. On 24 July 2026 equity shareholders approved it with 13,08,74,373 votes for versus 9,88,084 against (public shareholders 1,78,25,340 for, 9,88,084 against) and unsecured creditors 17,19,50,344 for versus 75,225 against; the petition was filed 7 August 2026, admitted 3 September 2026 and is listed for hearing on 12 October 2026. The plan's scope widened on 14 August 2026, when the board approved a ₹3,000 crore QIP explicitly conditioned on completion of the Scheme, tying the restructuring to funding the Telangana expansion.

points.point: The stated core objective is to consolidate KCL's textile manufacturing into KGL so that KCL can focus on its other activities.
points.quote: The main objective of the scheme is for consolidation of Textile business division of KCL in KGL for better growth so that Kitex Childrenswear Limited can concentrate on its other core activities

points.point: The problem identified is that KCL houses two verticals — Textile Business Division and Remaining Business — whose economics and management needs differ.
points.quote: The nature of risks, returns, growth and competition involved in each such undertaking are distinct and requires attribution of dissimilar technical and managerial focus.

points.point: Segregation is said to free management to pursue independent growth, organically and by acquisition, with better access to resources.
points.quote: The segregation of Textile Business Division of the Demerged Company would allow the management to effectively cater to the independent growth plans (both through organic and inorganic means) by enabling access to availability of increased resources.

points.point: A separate capital-allocation and stakeholder rationale is given — different investors, partners and lenders for each business.
points.quote: Enable each business to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The operating case is scale: putting the two similar infant-wear manufacturing operations in one entity pools production capacity.
points.quote: By Combining similar business activities under a single entity optimize business operations, achieve economies of scale, create operational efficiency, common pool of production and better utilisation of resources

points.point: Risk separation between the two verticals is listed as a distinct benefit.
points.quote: insulating and de-risking the businesses from one another;

points.point: A valuation argument is made explicitly — separate platforms should price better, opening scope for divestments and acquisitions.
points.quote: unlocking value for the over-all business portfolio through better price discovery of individual platforms.

points.point: The scheme also cleans up the group's ownership chain: KAPL (70% KGL / 30% KCL) and Kitex USA LLC (50:50) both become wholly owned by KGL.
points.quote: The scheme of arrangement of consolidating the textile manufacturing division into KGL will help the business grow and gain better market share. Kitex Apparel Parks Limited and Kitex USA LLC will also become 100% subsidiary of Kitex Garments Limited.

points.point: The job-work arrangement that blurred the two companies' revenue is described: KCL's 56 lines served both its own sales and KGL's, with revenue booked in KGL.
points.quote: It has 56 production lines which it has been traditionally using for own revenue as well as for KGL as job work with final revenue booked in KGL.

points.point: The trigger cited is a capacity squeeze — KCL now wants its full capacity for its own revenue.
points.quote: Considering the huge demand for capacity, KCL has decided to use its full capacity for its own revenue

points.point: The demand backdrop given is China+1 sourcing and disruption in Bangladesh pushing volumes to India, with buyers hunting for capacity.
points.quote: Global drive by US and Europe customers to move out of China which is the dominant player today along with turmoil in Bangladesh has opened up huge potential for India.

points.point: Scale of the businesses being combined: KGL has 42 lines, ~4,900 employees and FY2024 turnover of ₹617 crore; KCL has 56 lines, ~4,900 employees and exports mainly to The Children's Place.
points.quote: It has 42 garment manufacturing lines and employs around 4900 employees.

points.point: Consideration is paid in KGL shares to KCL's shareholders — effectively promoter-level, since Sabu M. Jacob and relatives hold 99.99% of KCL.
points.quote: As consideration for the demerger of Demerged Undertaking, Resulting Company shall issue and allot New Equity Shares to the equity shareholders of the Demerged Company based on Share Entitlement Ratio as mentioned in the Scheme in proportion to their shareholding in the Demerged Company.

points.point: The ₹3,000 crore QIP approved on 14 August 2026 is expressly gated on the demerger closing, tying the restructuring to funding for capex, debt repayment and the Telangana project.
points.quote: The proposed issue of capital is subject to completion of ongoing scheme of arrangement between Kitex Garments Limited and Kitex Childrenswear Limited and their respective shareholders and creditors.

points.point: Context for why consolidation matters financially: KGL carries a corporate guarantee on KAPL's bank borrowings, and KCL, KAPL and Kitex USA were all loss-making in FY2025-26.
points.quote: The Company has provided guarantee for borrowings availed by a Subsidiary, Kitex Apparel Parks Limited (KAPL) from banks for sanctioned amount of Rs 2,02,300 lakhs of which Rs.1,01,203.99 lakhs is outstanding as on June 30, 2026.

points.point: Shareholders and unsecured creditors approved on 24 July 2026 with only token opposition (25 shareholders and one creditor against).
points.quote: The proposed resolution approving the Scheme was passed by the majority of equity shareholders representing three -fourth in value of the equity shareholders who voted.

verdict.what_management_expects: KGL: similar infant-wear manufacturing consolidated in one entity — economies of scale, a common pool of production, operational efficiency, better resource utilisation, increased customer focus and market share; 100% ownership of KAPL and Kitex USA; and eligibility for the ₹3,000 crore QIP. KCL: concentration on its remaining core activities. Both: insulated and de-risked, with value unlocked through better price discovery, efficient capital allocation and different investor and lender sets.
verdict.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts on file. Share entitlement ratio, appointed date, valuation multiples, quantified margin or synergy gains, KAPL/Kitex USA losses, and who requested the separation go unexplained.

verdict.segment_name: Textile Business – Infant / Kids Apparel manufacturing (the Company's single operating segment); the entity being combined/separated is labelled Kitex Childrenswear Limited (KCL) in the presentations
verdict.unit: ₹ crore (Apr 2025 presentation); annual-report financials are stated in ₹ lakh
verdict.measure_notes: No profit line of any kind is disclosed for the business on its own. All three annual reports (standalone and consolidated) state that operations relate to ONE operating segment — Textile – Infant / Kids Apparel manufacturing — and that 'no separate segment information has been furnished', so there is no segment result / EBIT / EBITDA / PBT and no inter-segment or external segment revenue split. The only stand-alone revenue figure for the business being separated is KCL's 'Revenue: INR 425 Cr' on the pre-merger structure chart, which carries no period label and no profit figure.

years.source: Annual Report 2024 — page 203 (segment note: single segment, no separate segment information)
Annual Report 2025 — page 189 (segment note: single segment, no separate segment information)
Annual Report 2026 — page 207 (segment note: single segment, no separate segment information)

verdict.not_found: No separate revenue, operating profit or PAT for the demerged/merging business — single-segment reporting. Only unlabelled KCL revenue INR 425 Cr (Presentation Apr 2025 — page 7); no quarterly data.

verdict.rationale: The separation at issue is L&T's Realty (real-estate development) business, which the Board resolved on 8 December 2025 to transfer out of the listed parent into L&T Realty Properties Limited (LTRPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary, as a going-concern slump sale under a Sections 230-232 Scheme of Arrangement — not a demerger to shareholders, so there is no dilution and LTRPL stays 100% owned. Management's stated reasons are threefold in the Scheme: (a) to run Realty under a separate, focused management structure with industrial and sectoral expertise for 'greater efficiency, focus, and accountability' and to maximise the undertaking's value; (b) to keep leveraging L&T's brand equity, institutional strengths, goodwill and group cross-synergies while sitting in a separate legal entity; and (c) critically, to let the entity 'effectively raise financial resources through equity and debt from investors, strategic partners and collaborations, whose investment strategies and risk profiles are focused on the Realty Business.' The capital argument is the operative one: R. Shankar Raman said on 5 May 2026 that L&T's own land bank is nearly exhausted ('by the time Lakshya 31 ends, I don't think we'll be left with much land out of L&T's bank'), so land must be bought at current prices, making 'capital calls... frequent and consistent' — and that 'one of the reasons why we are restructuring the Realty business is at some point in time to enable the company like Financial Services to be market-facing.' Scale justifies it: pre-sales more than doubled to Rs 94 billion in FY26 (CMD cited ~Rs 10,000 crore, only 0.59% of consolidated revenue), Q3 FY26 alone was a record ~Rs 50 billion with the Noida Green Reserve launch doing >Rs 40 billion in week one, against ~71 million sq ft of development potential (100 mn sq ft pursued, 70% residential/30% commercial) in Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Bengaluru, NCR and Chennai, and a 25% pre-sales CAGR target over Lakshya 31. It also fixes a reporting problem management itself described — Realty revenue and margin are recognised in lumps on flat handovers, distorting the Projects & Manufacturing margin line, so from FY27 Realty is carved out as a standalone reporting segment and the restated FY26 PP&M margin is 7.8%. The business being moved is small in the parent's accounts (H1 FY26 standalone revenue Rs 640.57 crore, 0.93% of revenue; net worth Rs 2,148.86 crore, 3.16%) but is valued at an enterprise value of Rs 6,300 crore, settled by LTRPL issuing 3,93,53,93,685 equity shares of Rs 10 face value at a Rs 6 premium to L&T. Management added that governance and execution standards are being tightened 'to support listing readiness,' with Rs 44 billion of Lakshya 31 capital earmarked for commercial real estate plus near-term parent support for land, after which the entity 'may explore external fundraising options including debt and/or equity.'
verdict.evolution: On the 8 May 2025 Q4 FY25 call there was no Realty separation plan at all — only a promise that the FY27-31 strategic plan would be communicated later; on 29 July 2025 an analyst (Parikshit Kandpal, HDFC) pushed that Realty 'gets hidden in your SOTP' and asked about capital allocation, and P. Ramakrishnan deferred, saying the real-estate business 'will be covered in detail' in the Lakshya 31 exercise. By 29 October 2025 the answer was still only an operating roadmap — expand in MMR/NCR/Bengaluru/Chennai via own-land monetisation, land acquisition and joint development — plus an explanation that Realty's lumpy handover-based accounting swings reported P&M margins. The Board approved the Scheme on 8 December 2025, and the 28 January 2026 call formally announced that L&T 'has initiated a transfer of its Realty business undertaking' as 'the start of a phased consolidation of all real estate assets into a unified platform'; stock-exchange observation letters followed (BSE 18 March, NSE 19 March 2026). By the 5 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call the plan had hardened into structure and capital: Realty became a standalone reporting segment outside PP&M, Rs 44 billion was allocated, external debt/equity was flagged, and governance was being built 'to support listing readiness'; shareholders approved the Scheme on 4 August 2026 (99.07% of votes in favour) at a Rs 6,300 crore enterprise value, and the NCLT admitted the petition on 18 August 2026 for hearing on 6 October 2026.

points.point: The 8 December 2025 filing sets out the first rationale: a dedicated, sector-expert management structure for Realty to improve focus and accountability and maximise the undertaking's value.
points.quote: It will empower the Transferee Company to undertake the business of the Realty Undertaking under a separate, focused management structure with industrial and sectoral expertise, facilitating strategic opportunities, greater efficiency, focus, and accountability and maximizing the value of the Realty Undertaking.

points.point: The capital-access rationale is explicit: a separate entity can raise equity and debt from investors and strategic partners whose mandates are specifically real-estate focused.
points.quote: The Scheme will enable the Transferee Company to effectively raise financial resources through equity and debt from investors, strategic partners and collaborations, whose investment strategies and risk profiles are focused on the Realty Business thereby achieving greater growth of the Companies.

points.point: Separation is deliberately structured to retain group benefits — LTRPL keeps L&T's brand, institutional strengths and goodwill while being a distinct legal entity, with no shareholder dilution (CMD's 4 August 2026 address).
points.quote: The Transferee Company, while operating as a separate legal entity within the group, will continue to leverage from the Company's institutional strengths, brand equity, and goodwill, thereby ensuring long-term stability and strategic support while enabling the Companies to leverage cross-synergies and enhance value creation across the group.

points.point: CMD S. N. Subrahmanyan quantified the opportunity on 4 August 2026: ~71 million sq ft of development potential across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Bengaluru, NCR and Chennai, with FY26 pre-sales of ~Rs 10,000 crore but only 0.59% of consolidated revenue; EV Rs 6,300 crore, settled in 3,93,53,93,685 LTRPL shares (Rs 10 face value, Rs 6 premium).
points.quote: The proposed structure will also provide greater flexibility to access growth capital, attract strategic partners and engage with sector-focused investors.

points.point: First formal disclosure on a call: the slump-sale transfer to LTRPL under a Scheme of Arrangement is the start of consolidating all group real-estate assets onto one platform.
points.quote: This marks the start of a phased consolidation of all real estate assets into a unified platform, positioning L&T Realty for greater scale, agility and financial strength to capitalize on India's real estate growth.

points.point: Shankar Raman gave the operative reason — the land bank is running out, so land must be bought at market prices and the business will need repeated capital calls, which is why it is being restructured to eventually face the market like L&T Finance does.
points.quote: One of the reasons why we are restructuring the Realty business is at some point in time to enable the company like Financial Services to be market-facing.

points.point: The depletion of owned land is stated directly, with 100 million sq ft being pursued (70% residential, 30% commercial, commercial providing annuity cash flows) and roughly another 100 million sq ft contemplated beyond that.
points.quote: Much of the land that L&T currently owns, have been in the monetization mode for the last few years. So, looking forward, by the time Lakshya 31 ends, I don't think we'll be left with much land out of L&T's bank.

points.point: Funding sequence disclosed under Lakshya 31: Rs 44 billion from the parent mainly for commercial development plus near-term land support, then external capital — and governance work is explicitly aimed at a future listing.
points.quote: In parallel, sustained focus will be placed on operational execution and governance standards to support listing readiness.

points.point: Realty is pulled out of the core margin line from FY27, the only material change to segment reporting, with restated FY26 PP&M margin of 7.8%; FY26 Realty pre-sales more than doubled to Rs 94 billion and a 25% pre-sales CAGR is assumed over Lakshya 31.
points.quote: The only material change is the segregation of the Realty as a standalone reporting segment while all other businesses remain broadly comparable with selective internal realignments to sharpen the strategic focus.

points.point: Management explained the reporting distortion that separate segmentation later solves: Realty revenue and margin land in lumps on flat handovers, unlike percentage-of-completion P&M work, swinging consolidated P&M margins quarter to quarter.
points.quote: So this is at a point of time, recognition of sales and margin. To that extent, you can have some quarters margins dipping at the overall P&M level because of lower residential -- lower handing over of residential units.

points.point: Pre-separation, the roadmap was purely operational — city-by-city expansion funded by monetising existing land, buying new parcels and joint development, with Rs 120 billion sold-but-not-handed-over and Rs 40 billion unsold inventory.
points.quote: So as of now, the way we are focusing is that we will try to expand the presence in the cities of the Mumbai Metropolitan region, National Capital Region, Bengaluru, Chennai and this development will be happening through a mix of monetizing of our existing land parcels, acquisition of new land real estate parcels and also increasing growth through the joint development route.

points.point: An analyst (Parikshit Kandpal, HDFC Securities) pressed that Realty's value was invisible inside the conglomerate and asked about capital allocation; management deferred the answer to the Lakshya 31 (FY27-31) plan exercise.
points.quote: Because this segment seems to be promising, but it gets hidden in your SOTP or your overall business. How are you thinking about this more on mid-to-longer term?

points.point: At that stage Realty was still a small, land-monetisation-led book — quarterly order inflow ~Rs 1,000 crore and revenue ~Rs 500 crore, 13,000 units launched, 6,200 handed over, ~5,000 sold awaiting handover, 1,700 unsold — with land acquisition only being contemplated.
points.quote: We are also looking to expand this portfolio meaningfully by getting into some amount of land acquisitions. But at this juncture, it is premature for me to give a number to it, because this whole thing about real estate business will be covered in detail, we frame out of start plan exercise for FY26 to FY27 to '31.

points.point: No Realty separation existed in the FY25 narrative; capital-recycling talk was about exiting concessions (Hyderabad Metro, Nabha Power, IDPL) and the FY27-31 plan was only being started, to be communicated a year later.
points.quote: During the current year, we will begin exercise of creating the strategic road map for FY27 to '31. The same will be communicated to the stakeholders during the Q4 FY26 earnings call.

verdict.what_management_expects: LTRPL: dedicated management, operating agility and accountability; direct access to real-estate-focused equity, debt and strategic partners for frequent land-acquisition capital calls; 25% pre-sales CAGR, commercial annuity cash flows, governance built for listing readiness and better valuation visibility. L&T parent: unchanged ownership, retained brand/synergies, Realty's lumpy handover accounting removed from PP&M margins (FY26 restated 7.8%), sharper strategic focus.
verdict.gaps: No listing/IPO timing, no bridge from Rs 2,149 crore net worth to Rs 6,300 crore EV, no valuation method, tax effect, debt allocation, standalone return targets, or why slump sale over demerger.

verdict.rationale: Management frames AEL as an incubator whose explicit terminal step is separation: "build, stabilize, scale and unlock" — and they say on the Apr 2026 call that the first three phases are done and "AEL is now getting ready for value unlock through demergers", naming Airports, Roads, the ANIL (new energy) ecosystem and long-term-contracted MDO services as the four independent, sector-leading platforms ready to be separated. The stated reason is maturity of the capex cycle plus a changed earnings mix: core infra and services now contribute 80% of FY26 EBITDA versus 12% when the plan was laid out in 2019 (incubating EBITDA was 60% of H1 FY25, over 70% in H1 FY26), so AEL's consolidated numbers now 'mirror' the group's ~82-85% core-infra profile and the businesses no longer need to sit inside an incubator. The scale cited for Airports specifically: 8 airports, 95.3mn passengers, FY26 income INR13,081 crores (+28%) and EBITDA INR5,394 crores (+55%), 23% of India's passenger traffic and 29% of air cargo, with Navi Mumbai's ~INR20,000 crore regulatory asset base earning a 12-14% return and adding ~INR2,000-3,000 crores EBITDA alone. The problem separation is said to solve is valuation/visibility rather than funding: management says the airport business plan is already "funded", that "does the business need that from its own point of view? We are comfortable with the business plan as it is", but that outside investors are "very much" interested because "it's a premier business of its type in AEL" — i.e. the ask is coming from investors, not lenders or partners. The precondition is operational, not financial: back in Feb 2024 Robbie Singh said AEL would "wait for the demerger of this business until it achieves all these benchmarks" — security/immigration queues, car parking, check-in, and the city-side developments that are meant to make non-aero/non-pax two-thirds of airport EBITDA — flagging the event 3-5 years out. Leverage is managed to make the pieces separable: core infra net external debt ~INR45,000 crores against a ~$4bn regulatory asset base at 3.5-4.5x, versus a deliberately conservative ~$2bn against ~$6bn of operating assets in metals/materials/mining, 3.9x consolidated and expected flat-to-down. Alongside the planned demergers, AEL has already executed the same playbook in cash and paper: the Board approved the demerger of the Food FMCG business into Adani Wilmar with Adani Commodities LLP investments (Aug 2024) because it "has become self-sustained", then exited AWL entirely (13.51% OFS plus the residual 30.42%) for post-tax proceeds of ~INR14,200 crores and total exceptional gains of INR9,215 crores, arguing the swap turns INR250 crores of cash-after-tax from AWL into ~INR5,000 crores — "a 20x improvement" — by redeploying up to INR70,000 crores into core infra at 15-18% returns. The INR24,930 crore rights issue (which also converted ~INR16,000-20,000 crores of promoter shareholder loans into equity) was positioned as balance-sheet preparation "for the next phase of growth", funding airports over the next 12 months plus roads and ANIL.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as a deferral, not a plan: on the Feb 2024 call Robbie Singh said the airport demerger would wait until service benchmarks were met and flagged it "between three to five years from now", and the May 2024 call described AEL as "well poised to develop its incubating portfolio eventually as independent listed verticals in their own right". It then became concrete in reverse order — the Aug 2024 call announced an actual approved demerger of the Food FMCG business into Adani Wilmar, Jan 2025 monetised 13.5% of AWL and quantified the recycling math, and May 2025 began carving Airports out operationally (separate segment reporting and a dedicated airport management team on calls from 30th September 2025). Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 were about preparing the vehicle rather than splitting it — the INR25,000 crore rights issue, shareholder-loan-to-equity conversion, and the EBITDA unlock from Navi Mumbai, Kutch Copper and Ganga Expressway. By Apr 2026 management stated plainly that "value unlock through demergers" is the next phase and named four candidate platforms, with Airports "ready" around FY27-28 and the final decision left to the AEL Board.

points.point: Earliest reference: the Airports demerger is explicitly deferred until passenger-experience and city-side benchmarks are achieved, with the event flagged 3-5 years out (i.e. FY27-29), because the business is being built for 2033-35 (240-250mn pax capacity) and for a 65% non-aero EBITDA mix, not for today.
points.quote: That's why we will wait for the demerger of this business until it achieves all these benchmarks. That's why we flag that event between three to five years from now.

points.point: The incubation model is stated as having separate listing as its endpoint, right after describing 4 of 10 road projects over 70% complete and Ganga Expressway progressing.
points.quote: This leaves Adani Enterprises well poised to develop its incubating portfolio eventually as independent listed verticals in their own right.

points.point: First actual approved separation: the Food FMCG business is demerged into Adani Wilmar together with strategic investments in Adani Commodities LLP, with self-sustainability as the stated test and shareholder value unlock as the stated purpose.
points.quote: In line with this, the Board of Directors of Adani Enterprises have approved the demerger of Food FMCG business of Adani Enterprises to Adani Wilmar, along with its strategic investments in Adani Commodities LLP.

points.point: The separation sequence is implied by the incubation sequence: the declared first-phase focus is airports, green hydrogen, roads and data centre, with services businesses (Digital Labs, Global Capability Center) left unreported until they reach scale "towards the end of this decade".
points.quote: Our focus in the first phase over the next five years is to focus on the incubation of airports, green hydrogen and the roads business plus data center.

points.point: The economics of exiting a matured business are quantified: 13.5% of AWL sold via OFS, post-tax equity proceeds of ~INR14,200 crores enabling up to INR70,000 crores of core-infra investment at 15-18% returns, adding INR11,000 crores of EBITDA and ~INR5,000 crores of cash-after-tax against the INR250 crores of cash-after-tax given up — described as a 20x improvement and "massively accretive".
points.quote: the post-tax equity proceeds of this transaction will be roughly INR 14,200 crores , which will enable Adani Enterprise s to invest up to INR 70,000 crores in its core infra businesses.

points.point: Airports is carved out for reporting purposes because it has become too large to stay buried in AEL: FY25 airport EBITDA INR3,480 crores (+43%, ~INR1,000 crores/quarter run rate, 45% of it Mumbai), heading to INR4,500-5,000 crores, so the airport leadership team begins presenting alongside the CFO and granular segment reporting starts from 30th September.
points.quote: Actually, what we are also planning to do is that because it's now a significantly large part of AEL , meaning it will be closer to the INR 4,500 -5,000 crore s EBITDA in the coming quarters .

points.point: The mix shift that underpins the separation case is quantified, and the INR25,000 crore partly-paid rights issue is positioned as balance-sheet preparation — converting promoter shareholder loans (~INR20,000 crores) into equity and funding airports for the next 12 months plus roads and ANIL.
points.quote: The pleasing part in this result is that the EBITDA from incubating business now contributes over 70%, as against 60% in the comparative last half year.

points.point: "Unlock" is used in the EBITDA sense first: Navi Mumbai (RAB close to INR20,000 crores at a 12-14% WACC-based return), Kutch Copper (INR2,800-3,100 crores EBITDA at 70-80% utilisation) and Ganga Expressway (~INR18,000 crore traffic-risk asset that should double Roads' INR1,500 crore EBITDA) are the assets that must season before the platforms can stand alone; the rights issue closed at INR24,930 crores.
points.quote: In the coming period, first, AEL will unlock EBITDA from Navi Mumbai, Kutch Copper and Ganga Expresswa y. Post stabilization, these 3 assets are expected to add well over INR3,000 crores to EBITDA.

points.point: The clearest statement of intent: demergers are named as the mechanism and four platforms are named as the candidates — Airports, Roads, the ANIL ecosystem and long-term contracted MDO services — on the basis that 80% of FY26 EBITDA now comes from core infrastructure and services.
points.quote: AEL is now getting ready for value unlock through demergers. These businesses are independent, sector -leading , large core infra platform , spread across Airports, Roads, ANIL ecosystem and long -term contract ed MDO services, which are ready to turn into value creation mode.

points.point: The four-phase incubation playbook is spelled out, with AEL positioned as having completed the first three; the EBITDA mix is said to have gone from 12% to 80% core infra since the 2019 plan, mirroring the group's 82-85% core-infra shape.
points.quote: Incubation journey is a repeatable playbook for us: build, stabilize, scale and unlock. We are already past first 3 phases and value unlock is the next phase of our journey.

points.point: Timing and decision rights for the Airports demerger: the business will be operationally ready around FY27-28 and the call then belongs to the AEL Board; Phase 2 of Navi Mumbai (toward 60mn pax) plus city-side development across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Jaipur take ~INR17,000 crores of the INR40,000 crore FY27 capex.
points.quote: I think the airport team -- airport management would be ready by -- they are comfortable around, say, '27, '28. And then -- after that, it's very much for AEL Board to determine.

points.point: Who is asking: separation/outside capital is investor-driven, not required by the business, which management says is already fully funded — so the driver is valuation recognition for a 'premier' asset rather than a financing need.
points.quote: It is just whether our investors interested in that's the question? Yes, very much so because it's a premier business of its type in AEL. But does the business need that from its own point of view? We are comfortable with the business plan as it is for ourselves.

points.point: The balance sheet is run so the pieces can be split cleanly: core infra carries ~INR45,000 crores (just under $5bn) net external debt against a ~$4bn regulatory asset base at a guided 3.5-4.5x, while metals/materials/mining is held deliberately low at ~$2bn against ~$6bn of operating assets given its volatility; consolidated leverage 3.9x, expected flat or slightly down.
points.quote: So we guide to that in the core infra while we are growing, we will be closer to the 3.5 to 4.5 range. And obviously, we'll be lower in relation to the mining.

points.point: Executed separations/reorganisations in the filings: the ACL Scheme moved Adani Cementation and Adani Cement Industries out of AEL into listed Ambuja Cements effective 1st August 2025 for 87,00,000 Ambuja shares and an exceptional gain of INR614.56 crores; the residual 30.42% of AWL was sold, taking FY26 exceptional gains to INR9,215.37 crores and ending AWL's associate status.
points.quote: the Hon'ble NCLT has pronounced the order approving the ACL Scheme, which has become effective from 1st August, 2025 and consequently (a) ACL and a step-down subsidiary Adani Cement Industries Limited cease to be subsidiaries of the Parent Company and (b) the Parent Company has received 87,00,000 equity shares of Ambuja towards consideration and recorded exceptional gain oft 614.56 crores.

points.point: The only scheme actually filed and effected on the AEL side is a tidy-up that consolidates rather than splits: Adani Green Technology Ltd and Adani Emerging Business Pvt Ltd amalgamated into AEL and Adani Tradecom Ltd into Adani New Industries Ltd, NCLT-approved 16th March 2026, effective 1st April 2026, with 90,11,048 AEL shares allotted on 15th April 2026 — i.e. ANIL is being assembled as a single entity, not yet demerged.
points.quote: Consequent upon the Scheme becoming effective:  1. AGTL and AEBPL stands amalgamated with the Company  2. ATL stands amalgamated with ANIL

verdict.what_management_expects: Airports: standalone sector-leading platform, FY26 EBITDA INR5,394 crores (+55%) compounding on a 12-14% regulated return on a rising RAB, plus city-side revenue from FY29-30. ANIL: cash-generating, capacity 2.5x. Roads/MDO: stable long-term contracted cash flows. AEL: an 80%-core-infra incubator recycling exit proceeds (INR14,200 crores from AWL into INR70,000 crores of capex at 15-18%) at 3.5-4.5x leverage, with shareholder value unlocked.
verdict.gaps: No swap ratio, record date, scheme filing, board approval, debt/asset allocation, listing venue or dates for the Airports/Roads/ANIL/MDO demergers; no data-centre or defence treatment; no promoter-stake or tax detail.

verdict.rationale: The "separation" in JK Paper's Composite Scheme of Arrangement (Board-approved 13 Dec 2024, NCLT-sanctioned 3 Feb 2026, effective 15 Mar 2026) is a narrow one wrapped inside a much larger consolidation: the only business actually carved out is the "Demerged Undertaking" of subsidiary Enviro Tech Ventures Limited (ETVL), demerged with appointed date 1 Apr 2025 into PSV Agro Products Private Limited (the Resulting Company, later renamed Enviro Tech Ventures Private Limited), in which JK Paper took 31.12% and which is now only an associate — ETVL's post-demerger net worth transfer lifted PSV Agro from Rs 0.19 crore to Rs 174.79 crore (equity capital Rs 65.66 cr, retained earnings Rs 34.06 cr, capital reserve on merger/demerger Rs 75.07 cr). Management's stated purpose for the carve-out is enabling, not strategic: once the Demerged Undertaking left, ETVL "would be left with paper and packaging business," so it could be amalgamated into JK Paper along with its shareholding in The Sirpur Paper Mills Ltd — which converted Sirpur from a step-down to a direct wholly owned subsidiary. The companion step, reducing and converting the Redeemable Preference Shares JK Paper held in ETVL into an unsecured loan (then cancelling it on merger), was justified as reflecting "the true nature of investment… i.e., as a liability, and thereby, facilitate the demerger." Everything else is pull-in rather than push-out: the three corrugation/carton converters bought for roughly Rs 694 crore of equity (Rs 590 crore for 85%, Rs 104 crore for the residual 15%) — JKPL Utility Packaging Solutions (ex-Manipal; FY25 revenue Rs 129.93 cr, PBT Rs 1.00 cr), Securipax Packaging (Rs 88.37 cr revenue, pre-tax loss Rs 5.52 cr) and Horizon Packs (Rs 722.12 cr revenue, PBT Rs 40.81 cr) — were amalgamated into JK Paper from 1 Apr 2024 because they are in "similar line of business," to consolidate "all packaging business, manufacturing, and trading entities under the Transferee Company," give "flexibility in funding the capex" of the three, "eliminate intra-group transactions and consequent cash flow blockages," "rationaliz[e] the corporate structure and reduction of shareholding tiers," cut "multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances" and save "administration and other costs associated with managing separate entities." A reserves reorganisation was added to "right-size the balance sheet": on the 30 Sep 2024 pro-forma, securities premium falls Rs 438.32 cr to Rs 404.64 cr, Capital Redemption Reserve (Rs 11.84 cr) and Debenture Redemption Reserve (Rs 4.74 cr) are extinguished, equity capital rises Rs 169.40 cr to Rs 181.32 cr and standalone net worth moves Rs 4,426.86 cr to Rs 4,373.68 cr. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having demanded the restructuring; it was management/board-initiated, cleared by BSE/NSE observation letters dated 4 Aug 2025 (SEBI letter 1 Aug 2025), and carried by shareholders on 2 Nov 2025 with 99.66% of votes in favour (public non-institutional holders 96.89% for, 3.11% / 4,14,581 shares against).
verdict.evolution: The single supplied earnings call, Q4 FY24 on 21 May 2024, contains no mention of any scheme, demerger or restructuring — management discusses the packaging acquisitions only as acquisitions (Rs 590 cr for 85%, Rs 104 cr for 15%, ~10% corrugation EBITDA versus a 12-14% norm, 55-60% capacity utilisation) and an analyst complains that the subsidiary corrugation businesses are not even covered in the presentation; the Board only approved the Composite Scheme seven months later, on 13 Dec 2024, and filed it with BSE/NSE on 30 Dec 2024. The plan then sat in process: stock-exchange observation letters came 4 Aug 2025 (received 8 Aug 2025), NCLT Ahmedabad's first-motion order 8 Sep 2025, shareholder/creditor meetings 1-2 Nov 2025, sanction order 3 Feb 2026, effectiveness 15 Mar 2026 and allotment of 1,19,16,427 shares on 20 Mar 2026. The first public management explanation appears in the 5 Feb 2026 Q3 press release (consolidation of paper and packaging, streamlined structure, efficiencies, ease of compliance, better customer service), repeated and extended in the 18 May 2026 Q4 release which names the two concrete outcomes — Sirpur becoming a direct wholly owned subsidiary and three packaging conversion companies amalgamated. The scope did not change across the filings: the same two appointed dates (1 Apr 2024 and 1 Apr 2025) and the same parts survived from board approval to NCLT order, and the petitioners affirmed on affidavit that the scheme filed with the petition was identical to the one filed with the application.

points.point: The amalgamation leg's core rationale: the three acquired converters and JK Paper are in the same business, so all packaging manufacturing and trading entities are to sit in one listed entity.
points.quote: The Transferor Company 1, Transferor Company 2, Transferor Company 3, and the Transferee Company are engaged in similar line of business, and the Board of the respective companies has decided to consolidate all packaging business, manufacturing, and trading entities under the Transferee Company.

points.point: Capital-allocation reason: the separate subsidiary layer was blocking cash and forcing intra-group dealings, constraining capex funding at the three converters.
points.quote: Facilitate flexibility in funding the capex of the Transferor Company 1, Transferor Company 2, Transferor Company 3, eliminate intra-group transactions and consequent cash flow blockages which shall result in efficient utilization of capital at a group level;

points.point: Structural reason: cut the number of shareholding tiers — which is what turned The Sirpur Paper Mills from a step-down subsidiary (held via ETVL) into a direct wholly owned subsidiary of JK Paper.
points.quote: Assist in rationalizing the corporate structure and reduction of shareholding tiers.

points.point: Compliance and cost reason given for both the packaging amalgamation and the ETVL merger: fewer legal/regulatory filings and lower overhead from running separate companies.
points.quote: Reduction in the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances required at present to be carried out by the Transferor Company 1, Transferor Company 2, Transferor Company 3 and Transferee Company.

points.point: The actual separation step is explained only as an enabler: reducing and converting JK Paper's Redeemable Preference Shares in ETVL into an unsecured loan (cancelled later on merger) was needed to make the demerger possible and to show the holding as a liability.
points.quote: The reduction and conversion of Redeemable Preference Shares (RPS) in the manner proposed in the Scheme would enable the Transferee Company to reflect the true nature of investment in the Transferor Company 4 i.e., as a liability, and thereby, facilitate the demerger from the Transferor Company 4 (as a part of the Scheme);

points.point: Why ETVL itself then merged: stripped of the Demerged Undertaking, what was left was the paper and packaging business (including the Sirpur shareholding), i.e. the same line of business as the parent.
points.quote: Upon effectiveness of Part E of the Scheme, Transferor Company 4 would be left with paper and packaging business and management of Transferor Company 4 and Transferee Company are engaged in the same line of business, and so, the Board of the respective companies have decided to consolidate all paper and packaging business, manufacturing, and trading entities under the Transferee Company;

points.point: A balance-sheet motive was stated explicitly: reserves are reorganised so the debit balance arising from the scheme is set off against existing credit reserves (securities premium cut Rs 438.32 cr to Rs 404.64 cr; CRR Rs 11.84 cr and DRR Rs 4.74 cr extinguished on the 30 Sep 2024 pro-forma).
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to set off the debit balance of Credit Reserve arising out of effectiveness of the Scheme as on the Appointed Date against the existing credit balance lying under Transferee Company, in order to right-size the balance sheet;

verdict.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of the Commercial Vehicles business out of the old Tata Motors Limited into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, executed together with the amalgamation of the PV subsidiary back into the listed parent, under one Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai (orders of August 25, 2025 and a rectification order of September 10, 2025), with an appointed date of July 1, 2025 and effective date of October 1, 2025. The Scheme states only two objectives in these texts: to transfer the Commercial Vehicles undertaking to the Resulting Company 'on a going concern basis' in compliance with Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act, and to amalgamate Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited into TML 'with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML', after which TML was renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited and TMLCVL renamed Tata Motors Limited (w.e.f. October 13, 2025). The result is that, as the postal ballot puts it, 'the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities', each with its own reconstituted board and KMP (Shailesh Chandra as MD & CEO of TMPV from October 1, 2025; P B Balaji moved from Group CFO to CEO of Jaguar Land Rover from November 17, 2025), and TMPV left reporting one automotive segment of JLR plus Tata Passenger Vehicles, 'other than CV segment moving out'. Shareholders were handed direct ownership of both: 1 TMLCVL share for every 1 TML share held on the October 14, 2025 record date, with historical cost apportioned 31.15% to the CV entity and 68.85% to TMPV, and the new CV shares listed from November 12, 2025. Management's only economic framing on the calls is accounting and capital: a notional demerger gain of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr (CV business valued at ~Rs. 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies against ~Rs. 11,000 Cr book value of net assets transferred), fully offset by a contra deemed-dividend entry so there is 'absolutely no impact on either distributable reserves or on our net worth'; an India PV business that is net cash (~Rs. 5,000 Cr at Q3 FY26, ~Rs. 7,000 Cr at FY26-end) which 'gives a lot of flex to fund the rich product investment cycle'; and the two entities now declaring dividends separately (Rs. 3 at TMPV plus Rs. 4 at TMLCV, 'a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken' versus Rs. 6 before). Costs disclosed are stamp duty: a Rs. 400 Cr provision in Q3 FY26, included within about Rs. 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere in these texts as having asked for the separation; the only stakeholder input recorded is the shareholder vote, which management described as 'overwhelming votes in our favor', and the nine AGM resolutions passed in July 2026.
verdict.evolution: On the Feb 2025 call (Q3 FY25, January 29, 2025) the demerger was already a filed corporate action awaiting exchange/SEBI NOC, with appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025; by the Jun 2025 call (Q4 FY25, May 13, 2025) the shareholder vote had passed overwhelmingly and both dates were reconfirmed, and on the Aug 2025 call (Q1 FY26, August 8, 2025) the NCLT final hearing had concluded that same day with judgment reserved and the October 1 effective date 'on plan'. The Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, November 14, 2025) was the first set of results reported post-separation, where management walked through the demerger accounting entries, the Rs. 83,000 Cr notional gain and contra deemed dividend, and the new segment structure. Thereafter the subject narrows to residuals and costs: the Feb 2026 call (February 5, 2026) notes CV is out of the segments and books a Rs. 400 Cr stamp duty provision, and the Jun 2026 call (May 14, 2026) folds stamp duty into FY26 exceptionals and frames the two separate dividends as Rs. 7 combined; the strategic 'why' is never revisited on any of these six calls.

points.point: The Scheme bundles two steps: hiving off the Commercial Vehicles undertaking into TMLCVL on a going concern basis (structured to qualify under Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act), and amalgamating the PV subsidiary into the listed parent — the only explicit objective language in any document supplied.
points.quote: Amalgamation of TMLPV with TML with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML and consequent dissolution of TMLPV without being wound up.

points.point: The November 2025 postal ballot explains the consequence the separation was meant to produce — two self-standing entities — and uses it as the reason to rebuild both boards, appointing Shailesh Chandra MD & CEO of TMPV from October 1, 2025 and P B Balaji as a non-executive director while he became CEO of Jaguar Land Rover from November 17, 2025.
points.quote: In view of the above, it was proposed to reconstitute the Board of Directors of both  the entities .

points.point: Shareholders were given direct ownership of both businesses rather than cash, at a strict 1:1 entitlement on the October 14, 2025 record date, with historical cost of acquisition apportioned 31.15% to the CV entity and 68.85% to TMPV; the CV shares were approved for listing and trading from November 12, 2025.
points.quote: 1 (one) share of the Resulting Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up), for every 1 (one) share of the Demerged Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up) of the same class of shares outstanding and as held by such shareholder in the Demerged Company, without any further application, act or deed (‘Share Entitlement Ratio’).
