verdict.insiders: Demerged Company retains about 20% of post-listing Resulting Company to support the early-stage business; all shareholders (promoter group holds 88,465,126 of 179,109,870 shares) get 1 share free; director P.S.R.K. Prasad is on its board.
verdict.hidden_value: Agrochemicals turnover ₹60,62,03,918 (1.48% of FY25 revenue) with FY25 segment result of negative ₹1,458 million; management says FY26 sales ~₹140 crore and about EBITDA positive, business "still at its early growth stages"; parent keeps pharma plus ~₹2,400 crore net cash.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Tiny (1.48% of turnover), loss-making early-stage, different industry from pharma, 1:1 free shares to 4,22,879 shareholders.
verdict.listing_timeline: Not fixed: 24-Mar-2026 filing says "Subsequent to the Scheme coming into effect, the Resulting Company /Transferee Company shall apply for the listing of its equity shares over Stock Exchanges" (Appointed Date 1st October 2026); on the 14-Nov-2025 call management was "targeting that for the year 2026" and on 12-Feb-2026 said "roughly, we're thinking by October, November" / "the next 8, 9 months"; but on 9-Sep-2026 the Company said it "has not filed the Scheme and related applications with the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal" and will file a revised Scheme after the Rights Issue.
verdict.read_next: The revised Scheme of Arrangement to be filed with the Stock Exchanges post Rights Issue, and the NCLT filing.
verdict.quote: The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of the business verticals of the Demerged Company.

verdict.rationale: NATCO is demerging its Crop Health Sciences (Agrochemicals) division into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited, leaving the listed parent as a pure pharmaceutical company (FDFs, APIs, oncology-led branded/complex generics). Management's stated reason is that the two verticals carry different risk-reward profiles and serve entirely different customers — Rajesh Chebiyam said the demerger "gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different" — so a dedicated management, channel and product strategy (differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition molecules like the fungicide GLANZ and CTPR combinations) can be run without competing for attention inside a much larger pharma P&L. The second reason is valuation and capital: agro turnover was only INR 60.62 crore in FY25, i.e. 1.48% of total turnover, against FY25 group revenue of INR 4,784 crore and PAT of INR 1,883.4 crore, and Rajeev Nannapaneni said shareholders "will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma"; separately listed, "it can raise its own capital and grow by itself." The timing was deliberately set after the division approached breakeven — segment loss of about INR 150 crore in FY25 (including a INR 50 crore non-cash PP&E impairment taken in Q4 FY25), narrowing to a INR 3.2 crore loss in Q1 FY26 on INR 34.7 crore of sales, EBITDA-positive at INR 52.4 crore of sales in Q2 FY26, and roughly INR 140 crore of FY26 sales versus INR 60 crore the prior year, against the INR 150–170 crore management had said was needed for EBITDA breakeven. The Scheme adds the corporate-finance logic: focused growth, operational rationalisation, optimum use of resources, and the ability for each business to "address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders," plus unlocking the value of the verticals. Shareholders get 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 NATCO share, with NATCO retaining 20% of the post-listing equity to keep supporting a business "still at its early growth stages" — so holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct, 20% through NATCO). The push came from public-market shareholders, not lenders or partners: an investor on the Nov 14, 2025 call asked directly about "value unlocking for the shareholders," and management separately cited shareholder feedback that NATCO's profit base was too concentrated. Agro is almost entirely domestic ("predominantly domestic" sales, with 25–30% input cost inflation flagged in 2026), which management contrasts with the export-weighted pharma business.
verdict.evolution: On the Feb 13, 2025 and May 29, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk — only agro losses, the INR 50 crore impairment and a INR 120–170 crore breakeven target; the Aug 13, 2025 call reported the loss down to INR 3.2 crore with still no mention. The board gave in-principle approval to evaluate the demerger on Sep 25, 2025, and Rajeev first discussed it publicly on the Nov 14, 2025 call ("demerge this business from the main company and list it separately... targeting that for the year 2026"), framing it as value unlocking plus the ability to raise its own capital; the board approved incorporating the wholly-owned resulting company on Nov 14, 2025. On Feb 12, 2026 the timeline was guided to "October, November" 2026 (8–9 months), and the Scheme itself was approved on Mar 24, 2026 with a 1:1 share entitlement, appointed date Oct 1, 2026 and 20% retained by NATCO; the May 29, 2026 call reiterated focus and different customers as the primary reason. By Sep 9, 2026 the Scheme had stock-exchange observation letters but had not been filed with the NCLT, because the INR 1,279.36 crore rights issue at INR 750/share (allotted Oct 23, 2026) changes the capital structure — the board decided to re-cut and re-file the Scheme after the rights issue while keeping the same swap ratio.

points.point: First public confirmation of the plan: demerge Crop Health Sciences out of the parent and list it separately, targeted for 2026, disclosed alongside the division reaching roughly EBITDA breakeven at INR 52.4 crore of quarterly sales.
points.quote: I think we have announced earlier that we will demerge this business from the main company and list it separately and we are targeting that for the year 2026.

points.point: Rajeev defines the value-unlock logic in response to an investor question: separate listing gives the business special focus and the ability to raise its own capital and grow independently, now that it is breaking even.
points.quote: Value unlocking means I think what we see is this business now is about breaking even now. So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.

points.point: The core valuation argument: the agro business is too small to be valued inside a pharma company of NATCO's size, and shareholders will get a complete see-through into both businesses.
points.quote: I think you will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma.

points.point: Timeline guidance: the process has started, with an internal goal of completing in the next 8–9 months (around October–November 2026), but no firm date committed.
points.quote: I think we have started the process. So , I think roughly, we're thinking by October, November, but I don't want to say any definite time lines, but this is our, what should I say, goal to do.

points.point: Management's clearest operating rationale, from the head of Crop Health Sciences: a focused approach is needed because the agro customer base is entirely different from pharma, with FY26 agro sales of about INR 140 crore versus INR 60 crore the year before.
points.quote: So, as you're aware, so we're in the process of demerging the business. And one of the primary reasons we felt also it gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different.

points.point: Growth plans — new differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition products, more channel partners and more people — are tied directly back to the demerger as the reason for sharper focus.
points.quote: So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.

points.point: The Mar 24, 2026 Scheme of Arrangement grounds the demerger in differing risk-reward profiles of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals; agro turnover was INR 60.62 crore in FY25, 1.48% of total company turnover.
points.quote: The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.

points.point: The Scheme's capital-markets rationale: each business can chase its own opportunities, allocate capital efficiently and attract its own investor and lender base, alongside focused growth, operational rationalisation and value unlocking.
points.quote: Each business would be able to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: NATCO keeps 20% of the post-listing equity of the resulting company so it can keep funding and strategically supporting an early-stage business; shareholders get 1 new share for every 1 NATCO share, retaining 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct plus 20% indirect).
points.quote: Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing shareholding) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.

points.point: The Nov 14, 2025 board filing states the purpose as unlocking value in the core pharmaceutical business while giving each entity operational flexibility, dedicated management and separate brand positioning.
points.quote: To demerge the Agro business of the Company into a separate entity, the move shall enable value unlocking of the core business (pharmaceuticals) and enhance long -term growth.

points.point: Pre-demerger baseline for why the division was a drag: a INR 50 crore non-cash impairment on agro property, plant and machinery in Q4 FY25, FY25 agro revenue of about INR 60 crore, and INR 160–170 crore needed just to be EBITDA positive.
points.quote: So, I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So, I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.

points.point: The Sep 9, 2026 board update: the Scheme had received observation letters from both exchanges but was not filed with the NCLT because the INR 1,300 crore rights issue changes the capital structure, so the Scheme will be amended and re-filed post-issue with the swap ratio unchanged.
points.quote: The fund raising by way of a Rights Issue proposed at the meeting of the board of directors held on September 09, 2026 is expected to result in change to the Company's capital structure and shareholding pattern and consequently would require necessary changes to the Scheme.

verdict.what_management_expects: Agro: dedicated management focus, its own capital raising, differentiated limited-competition products, growth past breakeven from roughly INR 140 crore sales. Pharma: a cleaner, focused oncology/complex-generics entity. For shareholders: value unlocked in a business "not being valued in our system," a complete see-through into both, operational efficiency, efficient capital allocation, and distinct investor/lender bases.
verdict.gaps: No standalone agro financials, debt/asset split, valuation or swap-ratio basis; no post-demerger profitability, capital needs, board/management, listing date, or revised Scheme terms.

verdict.reason: not stated
verdict.insiders: not stated for any new entity; documents show Promoters and Promoter Group holding 55.01% of Bajaj Auto pre-buyback, 55.95% post, having declined to participate in the buyback.
verdict.hidden_value: Subsidiaries scaling fast: Bajaj Auto Credit AUM ~INR20,000 crore, Q1FY27 PAT INR227 crore, ROE over 25%; Bajaj Mobility AG/KTM now 74.9%-held step-down subsidiary under turnaround.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No demerger, share distribution or new listing of a separated business is described in the documents.
verdict.listing_timeline: No demerged entity. Documents state only debt and existing listings: BACL NCDs "has been listed on National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE) on 01 December 2025" (filed 2 December 2025) and again "on 23 June 2026" (filed 23 June 2026); "BMAG, is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and on the Vienna Stock Exchange (Official Market)" (21 July 2026 results).
verdict.read_next: BACL's own NSE debenture/financial disclosures and Bajaj Mobility AG's filings, for subsidiary standalone value.
verdict.quote: The said Non-convertible Debentures has been listed on National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE) on 01 December 2025.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe Bajaj Auto separating, demerging or spinning off any business, so no rationale for one can be reconstructed from them — the only structural moves management discusses run in the opposite direction, toward consolidation. In the Jul 2026 call the electric two-wheeler business was folded INTO an existing unit: 'to capture some synergies, we have brought our electric two-wheeler business in the umbrella of the two-wheeler business unit.' On KTM, Bajaj moved from a 49.9% associate stake to control (BAIH BV holding 100% of BAIH AG, which holds ~74.9%–75% of Bajaj Mobility AG), completed 18 November 2025 after the European Commission subsidies approval of 10 November 2025, with line-by-line consolidation from Q4 FY26 at a one-quarter lag — an acquisition, not a separation. KTM is described as being 'run as an independent company' with its own Executive Board, but that is operating autonomy inside the group, not a separation of a Bajaj business; the turnaround workstreams there explicitly include 'simplifying the organization and corporate structure' and resetting fixed costs. The capital-structure action in the filings is a buyback of up to 46,94,000 shares at INR 12,000 (INR 5,632.80 crore, 1.68% of capital, 16.93% of standalone capital+free reserves), combined with a INR 150/share final dividend (INR 4,192 crore) for a 100% payout of FY26 PAT of INR 9,825 crore — justified by surplus cash (INR 18,000 crore at FY26 close, over INR 21,000 crore at June 2026), FY26 free cash flow above INR 8,000 crore, and an expected improvement in EPS and ROE, not by any portfolio separation. Subsidiaries that are already separate legal entities — Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd (AUM ~INR 20,000 crore, PAT INR 227 crore in Q1 FY27, ROE over 25%, CP and NCD listed) and the Brazil subsidiary — are presented as scaling contributors to consolidated results, with the last equity infusion into BACL described as the final one, again with no mention of separating them. The buyback explanatory statement is explicit on the point: the Board confirmed 'there is no pendency of any scheme of amalgamation or compromise or arrangement pursuant to the provisions of the Act, as on date.'
verdict.evolution: Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 track the KTM/Pierer transaction toward control (regulatory approvals, call options on Stefan Pierer's and Pierer Industries' 50% stake, Austrian Takeover Commission clearance 23 October 2025), i.e. combination rather than separation. Feb 2026 and May 2026 report change of control effective 18 November 2025, renaming of Pierer Bajaj AG to Bajaj Auto International Holdings AG and Pierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG, and a turnaround plan whose only structural element is simplification of KTM's own organization and corporate structure. May 2026 adds the 100% payout plus buyback as the shareholder-return mechanism, and Jul 2026 reports the buyback's completion (46,94,000 shares extinguished 24 July 2026) alongside the internal folding of the electric two-wheeler business into the two-wheeler BU. At no point across these eleven months does any call or filing announce, foreshadow or explain a separation of a Bajaj Auto business.

points.point: The only portfolio-structure change announced is an internal consolidation — the electric two-wheeler (Chetak) business was moved under the domestic two-wheeler business unit to capture synergies, the opposite of a separation.
points.quote: Domestic two-wheelers, to capture some synergies, we have brought our electric two-wheeler business in the umbrella of the two-wheeler business unit.

points.point: Asked about India-KTM integration, Rakesh Sharma framed KTM's autonomy as governance of an acquired subsidiary run by its own management, not as a separation of a Bajaj business; collaboration and Indian manufacturing for KTM are being expanded.
points.quote: So first of all, I must say that KTM is being run as an independent company.

points.point: The reason given for KTM operating separately is brand/franchise difference, with KTM to be run by its own management on arm's-length competitive benchmarks — a reason for autonomy, not for carving out any Bajaj unit.
points.quote: So, they are going to be run separately.

points.point: The structural event of the period was Bajaj moving from a minority to a controlling stake in KTM, with BMAG and KTM AG becoming step-down subsidiaries consolidated line-by-line with a one-quarter lag — an acquisition and integration, not a demerger.
points.quote: With the transaction completed on 18th of November, Bajaj moved from being a minority position to a controlling stake and BMAG and KTM are now step -down subsidiaries of the group.

points.point: The KTM 360-degree turnaround plan's structural workstream is simplification of KTM's own organization and corporate structure plus cost reset and Bajaj-KTM synergies — internal restructuring inside the group, with no separation of any business.
points.quote: This broadly will encompass sharpening the product portfolio across the 3 bands of KTM, Husqvarna and GASGAS, reworking the target operating model for go -to-market and looking for synergies between the Bajaj and the KTM system, resetting the fixed cost base across all lines, simplifying the organization and corporate structure.

points.point: Pierer Mobility AG was renamed Bajaj Mobility AG and kept listed in Zurich and Vienna with Bajaj appointees replacing Pierer nominees on both boards — a change of control and rebranding of an acquired listed entity, not a separation.
points.quote: In terms of next steps, an extraordinary general meeting has been called for and will be convened on 19th of November at which the name of the company will be changed, it is proposed to be changed from P ierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG.

points.point: The buyback explanatory statement contains the Board's express confirmation that no scheme of arrangement — the vehicle a demerger or separation would require — is pending at the company.
points.quote: there is no pendency of any scheme of amalgamation or compromise or arrangement pursuant to the provisions of the Act, as on date;

points.point: The stated purpose of the only corporate action in the filings (the INR 5,632.80 crore tender-offer buyback at INR 12,000 per share, 1.68% of capital) is returning surplus cash and improving EPS and ROE — explicitly a capital-return rationale, with no portfolio or separation rationale offered.
points.quote: The Buyback reinforces the Company's commitment to its shareholders by returning surplus cash to them in an effective and efficient manner, and is expected to improve its earnings per share and return on equity.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing, because no separation was announced. Management's stated expectations concern the opposite: synergies from folding Chetak into the two-wheeler BU; KTM's turnaround via fixed-cost reset, portfolio sharpening and India sourcing; capacity going from 7 to 9 million units; and, from the buyback plus 100% payout, improved EPS and return on equity.
verdict.gaps: Everything about a separation: no business identified, no scheme, no rationale, no investor, lender or partner demand, no financial or valuation targets, no timeline.

verdict.what_is_spun: Nothing is spun off; two wholly owned subsidiaries are amalgamated into listed MTAR Technologies Limited
demerged_business_names: Gee Pee Aerospace and Defence Private Limited (Transferor Company 1, formerly Gee Pee Electrospark Private Limited)
Magnatar Aero Systems Private Limited / Magnatar Aerosystems Private Limited (Transferor Company 2)
verdict.reason: Greater integration, financial strength and flexibility maximizing overall shareholder value; simplified group and business structure; fewer legal entities cutting cost and administrative hassle; reducing time for consolidating group financials
verdict.insiders: Directors have "no material interest in the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation except as Shareholders"; no shares issued, shareholding unchanged; public holding 68.59% as on 30.09.2025 (promoters ~31.4%)
verdict.hidden_value: No new entity or value release: both transferors are tiny and loss-making (net worth negative Rs 6,00,082 and Rs 3,60,464; turnover Rs 3.24 crore and nil) folding into a profit-making parent; restatement impact "not material"
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No cash or share consideration; transferor equity simply cancelled; shareholding pattern of the listed company remains unchanged, so no new shares are distributed
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — no new entity lists; the Transferor Companies "shall be dissolved without going through the process of winding up", scheme sanctioned by NCLT order dated October 28, 2026 with Appointed Date 01.04.2025
verdict.read_next: H2 FY27 results versus the 80%±5% revenue growth and ~24% EBITDA guidance given on the 13 May 2026 call
verdict.quote: The shareholding pattern of the Company remains unchanged pursuant to this Scheme.

verdict.rationale: These texts describe no separation, spin-off or demerger of any MTAR business — the only corporate scheme in them is the opposite: a Scheme of Amalgamation merging two wholly owned subsidiaries, Gee Pee Aerospace and Defence Private Limited and Magnatar Aero Systems Private Limited, INTO MTAR Technologies Limited, with appointed date April 1, 2025, board-approved November 5, 2025 and sanctioned by NCLT Hyderabad Bench-II on October 28, 2026 (CP(CAA)/28/230/HDB/2026), after which both transferors stand dissolved without winding up. The rationale management gave is consolidation, not separation: all three companies 'pursuing same and similar business' (aerospace/defence components and precision engineering), so merging them harnesses synergies of equipment and human resources, cuts administrative costs, overheads and duplicated functions, simplifies the group and business structure, integrates operations, and reduces the time and effort of consolidating financials at group level, giving 'greater financial strength and flexibility' and an improved competitive position. The subsidiaries being absorbed are tiny and loss-making: as on 31.03.2025 Gee Pee had turnover of Rs 3,24,25,839 and negative net worth of Rs (6,00,082), while Magnatar had zero turnover and net worth of Rs (3,60,464); the Official Liquidator noted loss-making transferors merging into a profit-making transferee, and the two together carried total assets of only Rs 136.69 million at 30.09.2025, with Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 16.79 million and a net loss of Rs 7.22 million. Because they are 100% owned, there is no cash or share consideration, their paid-up capital is cancelled, MTAR's shareholding pattern is unchanged, and their authorised capital is clubbed (Rs 66,00,00,000 to Rs 66,85,00,000). Nobody external asked for it: it was driven by the three boards at meetings on 05.11.2025; SEBI/exchange approval was not required (wholly owned subsidiary into holding company, filed only for disclosure), MCA Circular 30/2014 and Reg 23(5)(b) took it outside related-party rules, and NCLT dispensed shareholder and creditor meetings on 29.04.2026. Statutory authorities, not investors, shaped it — the Regional Director (SER), Official Liquidator and Income Tax Department raised observations (MSME dues, employee protection, FEMA, a Supreme Court property-tax dispute, open charges), each answered by undertakings. Accounting is pooling of interests under Appendix C to Ind AS 103, with all prior periods restated and the impact stated to be 'not material', and post-merger no consolidated financial statements are required. On the operating side, the only structural moves management discussed were new dedicated plants and relocations — an oil-and-gas plant in the SEZ near the airport, a small nuclear support facility, and shifting entire Bloom hot-box operations to the SEZ — none of which is a business separation.
verdict.evolution: The scheme surfaced only in filings, never in an earnings call: the board-meeting intimation of 30.10.2025 listed a bare agenda item 'Scheme of arrangement', and the 05.11.2025 outcome disclosed board approval of the amalgamation of the two wholly owned subsidiaries, with the then-stated sequence being shareholder approval first, then regulatory filing. One day later, on the Q2 FY26 call of 06.11.2025, neither management nor any analyst mentioned it, and the Q3 FY26 call (30.01.2026) and Q4 FY26 call (13.05.2026) were equally silent, as were the Feb 2025, May 2025 and Aug 2025 calls. The plan then changed procedurally rather than strategically: the 29.01.2026 results noted the company was 'in the process of filing the scheme for regulatory approvals', NCLT dispensed the shareholder and creditor meetings on 29.04.2026, the 29.07.2026 results confirmed the scheme had been filed with NCLT, and the 29.10.2026 results reported the 28.10.2026 sanction with restatement of all prior periods and no further consolidated accounts.

points.point: The transaction is a merger of two wholly owned subsidiaries into MTAR, sanctioned by NCLT Hyderabad on 28.10.2026 — the direct opposite of a separation.
points.quote: we wish to inform you that the Scheme of Amalgamation providing for the merger of Gee Pee Aerospace and Defence Private Limited (Transferor Company 1) and Magnatar Aero Systems Private Limited (Transferor Company 2), both wholly owned subsidiaries of MTAR Technologies Limited (Transferee Company), with and into MTAR Technologies Limited, has been sanctioned by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Hyderabad Bench, vide its order dated October 28, 2026.

points.point: The first public trace was a single unexplained agenda line in the board-meeting intimation dated 30.10.2025, alongside the Q2 FY26 results agenda.

points.point: Stated rationale in the 05.11.2025 disclosure: fewer legal entities to cut cost and administrative burden, plus a simplified structure and faster group financial consolidation.
points.quote: The consolidation of legal entities would result in reduced number of entities within the group. This would minimize cost and administrative hassle of maintaining multiple legal entities;

points.point: The NCLT order records the synergy rationale: one entity harnessing shared equipment and manpower, with reduced overheads and duplicated functions.

points.point: Because all three companies do the same aerospace/defence and precision-engineering work, the boards argued for economies of scale rather than any split of activities.
points.quote: Since all the three Petitioner Companies are pursuing same and similar business, the proposed Amalgamation would prove highly advantageous in achieving economies of scale and cost reduction.

points.point: The absorbed entities are immaterial and loss-making — Gee Pee turnover Rs 3,24,25,839 and net worth Rs (6,00,082); Magnatar nil turnover and net worth Rs (3,60,464) at 31.03.2025.
points.quote: As seen from the Balance Sheet of the Transferor Company-1 as on 31.03.2025, the Company has incurred losses in the current Financial Year and the Transferor Company-2 is a loss making Company and does not have revenue during the last two years.

points.point: No economic transfer to shareholders: no cash or shares issued, subsidiary capital cancelled, MTAR's shareholding pattern unchanged; authorised capital clubbed from Rs 66,00,00,000 to Rs 66,85,00,000.
points.quote: There will be no cash or share consideration involved in this process.

points.point: No investor, lender or partner asked for it; SEBI/exchange vetting was not even required, and NCLT dispensed shareholder and creditor meetings on 29.04.2026.
points.quote: This Tribunal vide order dated 29.04.2026, disposed of the said Application by dispensing with convening of the meetings of Equity Shareholders, Secured Creditors and Unsecured Creditors of the Transferor Companies and the Transferee Company.

points.point: Accounting is pooling of interests with all prior periods restated, and the merger removes the need for consolidated statements entirely.
points.quote: The Company has accounted for this merger under the "pooling of interests" method for common control transactions as per the requirements of Appendix C to Ind AS 103 "Business Combinations".

points.point: The only business MTAR stepped back from was a customer programme, Fluence battery storage, dropped from the presentation for capacity reasons — not a separated entity.
points.quote: And as and when they have the requirements, we've already done the prototypes for them, so we can move ahead with them whenever they're ready with it.

points.point: The structural change management actually described was moving the whole Bloom hot-box operation into a single new SEZ plant for operational efficiency, not separating it.
points.quote: And beyond that, we are moving the entire facility to the SEZ near the airport for the entire Bloom operations to expand to up to 20,000 and then subsequently to 30,000 unit.

points.point: On the call one day after the board approved the scheme, the only de-prioritisation mentioned was pausing the SSLV space programme; the amalgamation was never raised.
points.quote: No, no, SSLV we've put a pause to it because we have so much on hand right now.

points.point: Dedicated plants, not separate businesses: a new SEZ facility for oil and gas and a small nuclear support facility beside existing units.
points.quote: No. Oil and gas, we are setting up a new dedicated facility in SEZ.

points.point: Capacity plans were framed around land banks and future expansion with no mention of any corporate restructuring or carve-out.
points.quote: We already have enough land banks, both near the airport, in the SEZ and a few other land banks that we have taken.

points.point: The nuclear order surge prompted talk of an exclusive plant within MTAR — again consolidation of capacity inside the listed company.
points.quote: So I am -- as it is we have enough on our plate right now with our own reactors, which are being expected to come, more and more of these reactors are expected to come .

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing per-entity was stated on calls. Filings expect: business consolidated into one entity; synergies of equipment and human resources; lower administrative costs, overheads and duplication; simplified structure and fewer entities; faster group financial consolidation; greater financial strength, flexibility and competitive position; maximized shareholder value. Transferors are dissolved; MTAR absorbs all assets and liabilities.
verdict.gaps: Why these subsidiaries existed, what they contributed, quantified cost savings, merger's effect on margins or guidance, and any call-level discussion — never explained; no separation or demerger appears anywhere.

The pages state repeatedly (Annual Report 2024 — page 234 and page 290; Annual Report 2025 — page 245 and page 303; Annual Report 2026 — page 247) that 'manufacturing high precision and heavy equipment, components, machines have been considered as a single business segment' and 'there are no separate reportable segments in accordance with Ind AS 108'; the MD&A adds 'The Company does not operate in the manner of different business segments. However, we do measure revenues based on various customer segments.' Consequently there is NO segment result, EBIT, EBITDA or PAT for any sub-business anywhere on these pages. The only sub-company-level disclosures are: (a) sector-wise EXTERNAL revenue only — Aerospace & Defence ₹932 Mn in FY2024-25 vs ₹587 Mn in FY2023-24 (Annual Report 2025 — page 63), ₹1,038 Mn in FY2025-26 (Annual Report 2026 — page 63); in ₹ crore the presentations show Aerospace & Defence revenue of 58.7 (FY24), 93.2 (FY25), 103.8 (FY26), 36.4 (Q1FY27) and 80.2 (H1FY27) (Presentation Aug 2026 — page 8; Presentation Nov 2026 — page 9); and (b) Schedule III share-of-profit for the two wholly-owned subsidiaries, which are consolidated and NOT being separated: Gee Pee Aerospace and Defence Private Limited loss of ₹0.23 Mn in FY2024 and ₹8.60 Mn in FY2025, Magnatar Aero Systems Private Limited loss of ₹0.07 Mn in FY2024 and ₹0.08 Mn in FY2025 (Annual Report 2024 — page 291; Annual Report 2025 — page 304), with no revenue, operating profit or FY2026 figures given for either subsidiary.

verdict.what_is_spun: Specialized storage terminal for Ammonia, 36,000 MT static capacity, at Pipavav Port, transferred via slump sale
demerged_business_names: specialized storage terminal for Ammonia at Pipavav Port
verdict.reason: Strengthens Group's position in specialized chemicals and gas logistics; transfer to ATPL consolidates terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy and a potential new growth platform in a strategically important product segment
verdict.insiders: Buyer ATPL is the Company's step-down subsidiary; related party transaction at arm's length; no change in the Company's shareholding pattern. Itochu Corporation holds 10% of ATPL, intending 25% within three years
verdict.hidden_value: Consideration INR 525 crores equals the stated INR 525 crore ammonia project cost; terminal backed by 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc on one-third capacity, two-thirds open; parent books ~25% infra-development margin and holds ~44% of AVTL
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Cash slump sale within the group, not a share distribution; "No change in the shareholding pattern of the Company"
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated for ATPL; the Aug 7, 2026 AGM speech says subsidiary AVTL achieved "successfully listing of its equity shares on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited with effect from June 2, 2025"
verdict.read_next: The August 24, 2026 Business Transfer Agreement terms and ATPL's ammonia utilisation ramp in the next quarterly results
verdict.quote: The Transfer of storage terminal for Ammonia to ATPL will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy.

verdict.rationale: Across these texts the "separation" is not a demerger of a listed division to shareholders but the carve-out and separate listing of the group's port terminalling business into Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL), the joint venture with Royal Vopak, with Aegis Logistics Limited (ALL) retaining Mumbai liquid and LPG terminals, LPG/ammonia distribution, sourcing, infrastructure development (EPC) and treasury (Feb 2026 call: "Mumbai Liquid... Mumbai LPG... Distribution... Infrastructure Development... Sourcing and... treasury"). Management's single stated primary objective was balance-sheet repair: the AVTL IPO was "to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy" (Aug 2025), with Nov 2024 adding that equity infusion is "value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies," so the increased minority interest (guided at 15-20% of profit) is offset by lower interest, leaving the IPO EPS accretive. The scale driving it: an announced capex of ~INR 4,500 crore by FY27 (May 2024) escalating to USD 1.2 billion by FY27 and USD 5 billion by 2030/FY31, to be funded at a 0.6x gearing ratio capped at 3.5x EBITDA, plus a INR 20,000 crore Vadhavan MoU — more than ALL's own cash (INR 1,700 crore in Feb 2024, INR 4,130 crore in Jun 2025, INR 5,939 crore in FY26) could fund. AVTL listed on 2 June 2025 raising INR 2,800 crore primary, ALL keeps 44.71% and management control so AVTL still consolidates line-by-line, and a Phase-II equity infusion is "legally obliged... within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations." The mechanics are a series of asset transfers, not a scheme: Sea Lord Containers' Mangalore terminal and the 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG (Haldia, 25,000 MT, anchored by an HPCL terminalling agreement to 2038) moved into AVTL, and the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT) was assigned to Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited and sold by slump sale for INR 525 crore on 24 August 2026 to "consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy"; the Haldia move was defended as a 17% effective dilution compensated by ~INR 700 crore of cash surplus. ALL is paid for building the assets at arm's length with ~25% margins, 30% on signing (INR 500 crore of the INR 1,675 crore JNPA J2 project) and 70% on completion, so cash "doesn't go away" when a terminal is housed in AVTL. Partners, not public investors, drove the structure: Royal Vopak shares the dilution equally and bought ALL's CCPS for INR 180 crore, and Itochu took 10% of Aegis Terminal Pipavav intending 25% — while minority shareholders objected, Anil Sarin of K16 Advisors saying in Aug 2024 they would rather capital be raised in the holdco. Management's own test for every asset is explicitly where "housed it will bring the maximum value," with "most of the standard port terminals... housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak."
verdict.evolution: Through the Nov 2023 (Nov 3) and Feb 2024 (Feb 2) calls there is no separation on the table — only the Vopak JV making AVTL "the unquestioned market leader" port by port and an INR 1,750 crore / INR 4,500 crore capex plan; the May 2024 (May 24) call still frames everything as one group. The idea surfaces on the Aug 2024 call (Jul 31, 2024) as press speculation that management refuses to confirm ("nothing finalized as of now"), immediately drawing investor opposition, and is confirmed on the Nov 2024 call (Nov 19) with the DRHP filed the previous day and debt reduction given as the purpose, two-phase dilution shared equally by both partners. By Aug 2025 (Aug 8) the IPO is done — listed June 2025, ALL at 44.71%, rationale formally stated, Phase-II flagged as a SEBI obligation — and the plan then widens from an IPO into continuous asset migration: Haldia/Hindustan Aegis 75% into AVTL (Nov 2025, Feb 2026), capex built at ALL then billed across at 25% margin (Nov 2025, Jun 2026), the Pipavav ammonia terminal reassigned to ATPL (board consent 26 March 2026) and slump-sold for INR 525 crore (BTA 24 August 2026), followed by a fresh INR 6,000 crore borrowing and fundraising mandate at ALL itself (board 28 September 2026, EGM 21 October 2026).

points.point: Pre-history: the Aegis-Vopak combination is presented purely as operating consolidation and port-level market leadership, with no hint of a separate listing or carve-out.
points.quote: I think with the combination of Aegis and Vopak coming together, we have noticed that in every port that we are operating, we are now -- with our joint venture, Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd., is essentially becoming the market leader -- unquestioned market leader with maximum market share.

points.point: First public surfacing, via a news item about raising capital in AVTL; management refuses to confirm and calls the discussion premature, saying only that funding options for the capex program are being explored.
points.quote: As far as the second news item is concerned, I can tell you, we always explore many possibilities of funding our capex program and nothing finalized as of now.

points.point: Investors asked them NOT to do it: Anil Sarin of K16 Advisors, speaking "on behalf of a lot of people", said separate listing confuses minority shareholders and capital should be raised in the holdco instead, since Vopak brings its own money.
points.quote: But it's not so good from the investor standpoint, from a minority shareholder standpoint because then we get confused whether to own AVTL or to own the parent co, the Holdco.

points.point: Cash was already flowing from ALL to the JV structure before the IPO: ALL realised INR 180 crore selling its compulsorily convertible preference shares in AVTL to Royal Vopak, which sits in standalone but not consolidated profit.
points.quote: we realized INR 180 crores by -- as envisage in our JV by selling our compulsorily convertible preference shares in our subsidiary AVTL to Royal Vopak as it was envisaged in the JV.

points.point: Confirmation: AVTL filed its DRHP the previous day (18 Nov 2024), with proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and general corporate purposes.
points.quote: The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes.

points.point: The core financial argument against the holdco-dilution objection: interest cost elimination at the infrastructure entity more than offsets the rise in minority interest, so the holdco is left unaffected.
points.quote: We have already said earlier that the equity infusion into the JV will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies.

points.point: Shareholders raised the holdco-discount risk directly, asking whether ALL becomes a shell once the bulk of the business sits in the listed JV.
points.quote: If you can highlight how is going to be the structure and won't the current company will become more of a holdco because bulk of the business will go to this JV which will get listed.

points.point: Structure disclosed: dilution shared equally between Aegis and Vopak, executed in two phases rather than all at once.
points.quote: And the dilution both the partners would be doing equally. So, all of it will not come to any one partner, the dilution. And we would obviously be doing in two phases equity issue.

points.point: Post-listing, the CFO states the rationale formally for the first time: debt reduction and balance-sheet strength to fund the GATI (Gateway Access To India) growth strategy; ALL holds 44.71% but keeps management control so AVTL still consolidates line-by-line.
points.quote: The primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy.

points.point: The dilution is defended as EPS accretive because reinvested proceeds outweigh profit shared with minorities; Raj Chandaria frames the listing as doubling their shareholder responsibility.
points.quote: For Aegis Logistics, the IPO has been EPS accretive where now a portion of the profit will be shared with minority shareholders.

points.point: A second equity infusion into AVTL is not optional - it is a SEBI regulatory obligation within three years, and is counted on to fund the capex program.
points.quote: With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded.

points.point: The allocation rule between entities is stated as a value test, with standard port terminals defaulting into AVTL and new energy/new port opportunities judged case by case, partly depending on whether partners are involved.
points.quote: But yes, most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak, for sure.

points.point: The economics of the split for ALL: it builds the assets and bills AVTL at arm's length with roughly 25% margin, which is eliminated on consolidation but received in cash at standalone level, so cash spent on AVTL assets comes back.
points.quote: And we do the infrastructure development at arm's length basis. Generally, the margins are 25%.

points.point: Payment mechanics quantified on the INR 1,675 crore JNPA J2 project: 30% on signing the framework agreement, 70% on completion, so ALL received INR 500 crore upfront.
points.quote: So, INR 500 crores is in advance for this infrastructure development that ALL is doing from AVTL.

points.point: Haldia/Hindustan Aegis LPG 75% stake moved from Aegis Gas and Vopak India into AVTL; the 17 percentage-point drop in effective economic interest is argued to be more than offset by roughly INR 700 crore of cash surplus and is called a consolidation strategy.
points.quote: Like I have said, this transaction is not going to affect us by in spite of diluting 51%, we indirectly continue to hold 34%.

points.point: When an investor asks what is left in ALL ex-AVTL, management enumerates the residual stub: Mumbai liquid, Mumbai LPG, distribution, infrastructure development, sourcing, treasury - plus incoming ammonia distribution.
points.quote: So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.

points.point: The migration is now routine and ongoing: capex is incurred at ALL or its 100% subsidiaries and the completed asset is transferred to AVTL, capitalised in consolidation at the value ALL bills.
points.quote: So, we will be doing capex at the Aegis level, the Aegis Logistics. And then after creating the asset, will we then transfer it to Aegis Vopak, am I right?

points.point: Business Transfer Agreement dated 24 August 2026: ALL slump-sells the 36,000 MT Pipavav ammonia terminal to Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited (step-down subsidiary of AVTL) for INR 525 crore, a related-party transaction at arm's length and explicitly outside any Scheme of Arrangement, with Regulation 37A held inapplicable because the terminal is not an "undertaking".
points.quote: The Transfer of storage terminal for Ammonia to ATPL will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy.

points.point: AGM proceedings of 7 August 2026 record the completed separation outcome: AVTL listed 2 June 2025 with INR 2,800 crore of primary equity, followed by listed NCDs, leaving the group at 0.04 debt-to-equity and no net debt.
points.quote: This year also marked a significant achievement for one of our subsidiaries, Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL), with successfully listing of its equity shares on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited with effect from June 2, 2025, raised INR 2,800 crore through a primary issuance.

points.point: Board meeting of 28 September 2026 and EGM notice for 21 October 2026: having moved terminals out, ALL now seeks its own INR 6,000 crore borrowing limit, charge-creation powers and a INR 6,000 crore fundraise (QIP/FCCB/ADR/GDR/NCD-with-warrants) for acquisitions, repayment of group borrowings, working capital and capex.
points.quote: raising of funds for an amount aggregating up to Rs. 6,000 Crores, for cash, in one or more tranches

verdict.what_management_expects: AVTL: debt repaid from the INR 2,800 crore IPO, roughly 25% EBITDA on matured assets, 0.6x gearing capped at 3.5x EBITDA, funding USD 1.2 billion by FY27 toward USD 5 billion by 2030. ALL: Mumbai terminals, distribution at about INR 7,000 per tonne, sourcing, INR 5,939 crore treasury, 25% EPC margins upfront plus 44.71% of AVTL; EPS accretive.
verdict.gaps: No demerger scheme, swap ratio, record date or shareholder entitlement exists; nor any stated AVTL valuation, Phase-II pricing, or why ALL separately needs INR 6,000 crore.

verdict.segment_name: Pipavav Ammonia Terminal — India's first independent ammonia storage terminal, 36,000 MT static capacity, held under Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited (ITOCHU 10%); not a reportable segment in the documents
verdict.unit: ₹ crore (MD&A / presentations) and INR lakh (segment notes) — but no ammonia-specific amounts are given in either unit
verdict.measure_notes: No own P&L exists for this business on the tagged pages. Reportable segments under Ind AS 108 are only Liquid Terminal Division and Gas Terminal Division (segment result = EBITDA per MD&A; revenue is revenue from operations with no inter-segment split shown). The ammonia terminal sits inside the Gas/Liquid terminal structure and is disclosed only as capacity, capex intent and commissioning dates (commissioned 10 August 2026, i.e. Q2 FY27), so it carries no separately reported revenue, EBITDA or PAT.

verdict.what_is_spun: The EPC business (EPC vertical), demerged into a separately listed entity; described as already completed, not newly announced
verdict.reason: not stated
verdict.insiders: not stated for the new entity; in the parent, Shekhar Bajaj (promoter) holds 18,14,639 shares (1.57%), Pooja Anant Bajaj (promoter group) 15,41,875 shares (1.34%)
verdict.hidden_value: Separation left a two-segment parent: Consumer Products (FY26 revenue ₹3,343 crore, negative EBIT) versus Lighting Solutions (₹1,120 crore, record 8.5% EBIT margin); parent debt-free, ₹934 crore cash, negative working capital
verdict.selling_pressure_why: not stated; documents mention the demerger only in passing, with no size, index or shareholder-distribution detail
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated as a future date; described retrospectively as "the demerger of the EPC business into a separately listed entity" (March 16, 2026 filing) and "he led the demerger of the EPC vertical" (October 31, 2025 call)
verdict.read_next: The demerger scheme and the demerged EPC entity's own filings and financials — absent from this document set
verdict.quote: During his tenure with the Company, he has played a key role in several strategic and transformational initiatives, including the successful execution of a ₹350 crore rights issue, the demerger of the EPC business into a separately listed entity, the institutionalization of key financial and governance policies, and the evaluation of strategic investments and brand acquisitions.

verdict.rationale: Across these texts the only business separation management actually explains is the carve-out of the Nirlep brand/business, announced as an in-principle board approval on the Q1FY26 call (Aug 7, 2025), where MD & CEO Sanjay Sachdeva said the Nirlep business "currently has a drag on our financial results." CFO E.C. Prasad gave three specific reasons: Nirlep runs a "totally different GTM" / go-to-market with "no synergy" to the core Bajaj business, its factories were making losses, and the company had concluded that "instead of focusing too much on different spaces, it is better to concentrate on our core" — i.e. the separation is a focus-and-loss-elimination move, not a value-unlocking demerger. Management was explicit on scope: the cooker/cookware category continues under the Bajaj brand, and only the Nirlep brand is being put up for "alternatives" (Vishal Chadha, Aug 2025); by Nov 2025 Chadha confirmed Nirlep had declined at brand level while Bajaj grew. The initiative was management/board-driven — Prasad's "we have realized" — with no lender, investor or licensing partner named as requesting it. The cited precedent is the already-completed separation of the EPC business: BEL carried "over 2,000 crores in debt" and "numerous pending EPC orders" five years earlier, became debt-free by March 2022, and demerged EPC into Bajel Projects Limited in September 2023, which Shekhar Bajaj said means "BEL is now purely a consumer Company" and called "a great success both in terms of data [distinct] identity and focus for the 2 distinct businesses and has resulted in fact, on market capitalization"; the post-demerger split of the 1981 employee welfare trust was done 67:33, "the net worth ratio of the Bajel and BEL at that point in time" (May 2025). Investors reinforced the logic retrospectively rather than requesting it: Anuj Sehgal (Manas) noted that when "the EPC business was part of the company... the allocation of costs was an issue," while still complaining the consumer margins stayed in low single digits. Notably, the opposite move was made on brands the company wanted to keep: in Oct/Nov 2025 the board principally approved acquiring the Morphy Richards brand after 18 years of licensing with 12–13 years left, because, per Shekhar Bajaj, if BEL built it to "a level of INR 1,000 crores" the licensor could "suddenly... say we don't want to deal with you" and "all our effort to create the brand... goes down the drain." The Consumer Products and Lighting Solutions verticals are run and reported separately (Lighting "crafted a separate vertical in 2022," carved out under the departing CFO) and Lighting is being expanded in-house into switchgear, solar and wires — but no legal separation of those two is proposed anywhere in these texts.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Q1FY26 call (Aug 7, 2025) as an in-principle approval to restructure Nirlep described as a drag on results, with the no-synergy / different-GTM / loss-making-factories rationale given only in Q&A, and the scope narrowed in the same call to the Nirlep brand with cookers staying under Bajaj. On the Q2FY26 call (Oct 31, 2025), asked to quantify the one-time impact, Prasad said "we don't see any major impact," that the company was "still evaluating the various possibilities," and would update "as and when we are closer to the deal" — the last substantive update; Nirlep's decline at brand level was disclosed on the same call. The Q3FY26 (Feb 9, 2026) and Q4FY26 (May 20, 2026) calls do not mention Nirlep or any separation at all, and the Oct 5, 2026 postal-ballot filing's list of corrective steps omits it. The EPC demerger is referenced only retrospectively — at the management-change call (Jul 22, 2024), the Q1FY25 call (Aug 6, 2024), the trust-bifurcation answer (May 12, 2025) and the CFO's farewell (Oct 31, 2025).

points.point: First disclosure of the separation: an in-principle board approval to restructure Nirlep, framed purely as removing a loss-making drag, mentioned alongside the switchgear entry in the CEO's opening remarks.
points.quote: We have taken an in-principle approval of restructuring our Nirlep business, which currently has a drag on our financial results.

points.point: The stated reasons, given by CFO E.C. Prasad in Q&A: a completely different go-to-market, no synergy with the core, and loss-making Nirlep factories — hence 'look at alternatives and concentrate on the core.'
points.quote: So, Nirlep is a totally different GTM. And we have realized that instead of focusing too much on different spaces, it is better to concentrate on our core, because Nirlep is a totally different go-to-market. There is no synergy, and the factories of Nirlep were making losses. So, that is the reason we thought it is best to look at alternatives and concentrate on the core.

points.point: Scope was limited explicitly: the cookware/cooker category is retained under the Bajaj brand; only the Nirlep brand is being separated.
points.quote: We will continue with the cooker under the Bajaj brand. What we are saying is that we will be looking at alternatives for the Nirlep brand.

points.point: Asked directly to quantify the one-time financial impact and the post-restructuring effect, management declined — no deal, no structure and no numbers, only 'various possibilities' under evaluation.
points.quote: So as of now, where we stand, we don't see any major impact. We are still evaluating the various possibilities. And as and when we are closer to the deal, we'll let you know.

points.point: Supporting evidence for the separation inside kitchen appliances: while Bajaj-branded kitchen grew across mixers, induction and kettles, Nirlep declined at brand level.
points.quote: At a brand level, Nirlep has seen a decline, and Bajaj has seen growth.

points.point: The precedent separation, recounted at the MD-exit call: over ₹2,000 crore of debt and pending EPC orders led to debt-free status by March 2022 and the September 2023 demerger of EPC into Bajel Projects, leaving BEL a pure consumer company.
points.quote: Additionally in September '23, we successfully demerged our EPC business creating Bajel Projects Limited, which means BEL is now purely a consumer Company.

points.point: Chairman Shekhar Bajaj's stated outcome of the EPC demerger — separate identity, focus for two distinct businesses, and a market-capitalisation benefit.
points.quote: The recent demerger of EPC Projects business, as you will appreciate, has been a great success both in terms of data identity and focus for the 2 distinct businesses and has resulted in fact, on market capitalization.

points.point: Investor framing of why separation mattered: Anuj Sehgal (Manas Asian Equities) attributed the consumer business's decade of ~10%-or-less margins partly to EPC sitting inside the company and distorting cost allocation, then pressed on why margins still had not improved post-demerger.
points.quote: Earlier, the reason was that the EPC business was part of the company and the allocation of costs was an issue. Now, of course, that also has been demerged.

points.point: On CFO E.C. Prasad's resignation, the Chairman listed the structural separations as his legacy — the EPC demerger, the debt-free balance sheet and the internal carve-out of Lighting Solutions as a separate vertical (created 2022).
points.quote: Under his leadership, he led the demerger of the EPC vertical, transformed BEL into a debt-free company, carved out a Lighting Solution vertical, and streamlined our overall business model.

points.point: Residual post-demerger housekeeping quantifies the relative size of the separated entities: the 1981 employee welfare trust (and its trustees) was split 67:33 on the Bajel/BEL net-worth ratio at demerger, which also explains a new joint-venture line on the balance sheet.
points.quote: But now after that thing has settled down, we have decided that the trust would also be bifurcated in the ratio of 67 % to 33%, which was the net worth ratio of the Bajel and BEL at that point in time.

points.point: The mirror-image transaction: rather than separating Morphy Richards, the board principally approved buying the brand after 18 years of licensing (12–13 years left), to remove licensor termination risk and save a royalty the company refused to quantify as competitively sensitive; Prasad said it is 'value accretive from day one.'
points.quote: The issue is that by then, we hope that, suppose after so many years, our brand becomes very popular, and we do -- we reach a level of INR 1,000 crores. And then suddenly, they say we don't want to deal with you.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger scheme or separation filing is present in the material supplied: the Oct 5, 2026 filing is a postal ballot on the PSOP-2023 option pool (5,75,510 to 30,02,559 options) and on revised remuneration for Shekhar Bajaj, Sanjay Sachdeva and Pooja Bajaj, and the Mar 16, 2026 filing is the appointment of Suketu Shah as interim CFO. The postal ballot's own 'Steps taken or proposed to be taken for improvement' lists channel-inventory normalisation (channel days down ~30%), 2–5% price increases from Feb 1, 2026, cost rationalisation, distribution optimisation, portfolio expansion into switchgear/solar/wires and brand investment — and no business separation.
points.quote: Portfolio expansion: Entry into adjacent categories within the Lighting Solutions vertical, including Switchgear (Q2 FY 2025-26), Solar Solutions (Q3 FY 2025-26) and Wires (February 2026), to build an integrated portfolio leveraging the Company's brand strength and distribution reach for long-term sustainable growth.

verdict.what_management_expects: For BEL: removal of a drag on results, focus on core ('concentrate on our core'), cookers retained under the Bajaj brand; no quantified margin, capital or valuation benefit given. From the earlier EPC demerger: debt-free balance sheet, distinct identity and focus for two businesses, and a gain in market capitalisation.
verdict.gaps: No scheme, record date, entity structure, consideration, buyer, employee/factory treatment or Nirlep financials disclosed; no quantified one-time impact; separation absent from Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls.

verdict.what_is_spun: No business is spun off; aluminium products business consolidated into one wholly owned subsidiary via internal amalgamation
demerged_business_names: Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Limited (formerly Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Private Limited) (Amalgamated Company)
DR Axion India Limited (formerly DR Axion India Private Limited) (Amalgamating Company 3)
verdict.reason: Aluminium business and expansion land are fragmented across entities; consolidation under a single focused operating entity gives a stronger balance sheet, unified asset ownership, simplified structure, better managerial focus and efficiency
verdict.insiders: Promoter/CMD Srinivasan Ravi sold 5,25,000 shares (2.01%) on 23 June 2026, holding falling 40.15% to 38.14%; no promoter shares issued in the merged subsidiary
verdict.hidden_value: Aluminium is now the largest segment (H1 FY27 revenue Rs 3,29,879 lakhs) but lowest-margin; DR Axion turnover Rs 1,298.52 cr on net worth Rs 511.34 cr versus Sunbeam Rs 1,237.46 cr on Rs 107.43 cr; consolidated borrowings Rs 3,61,860 lakhs
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No shares distributed to listed shareholders; Company not a party and its shareholding pattern is unaffected
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — on 11 March 2026 the Company said "Not applicable. The Company is not a party to the proposed Scheme, and the shareholding pattern of the Company will not be affected by the proposed Scheme."
verdict.read_next: Draft Composite Scheme filed with NCLT, plus Aluminium Products segment EBIT margin in the next quarterly results
verdict.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the carve-out and consolidation of the aluminium products business — Craftsman's own high-pressure die-casting aluminium division plus wholly owned subsidiaries DR Axion India and Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions — into one wholly owned aluminium operating entity, approved for evaluation by the Board on 13 February 2026 and begun as a phased composite scheme on 11 March 2026 (step-down subsidiaries Suprash Developers and Srikara Technologies into DR Axion, then DR Axion into Sunbeam, with Sunbeam's equity reorganised to Re 1 face value and 1 Sunbeam share at Rs 9 premium issued per DR Axion share of Rs 10). Management's core stated problem is subscale fragmentation: Ravi said global aluminium competitors run $3–6 billion (top ten $3–8 billion, one peer $8 billion in aluminium alone) while Craftsman is 'less than $0.5 billion in aluminium revenue', so going to the same customers as three separate businesses of $100m, $200m and $300m to win a single $100–200m order is 'becoming unwieldy… very expensive'. The three units overlap operationally — 'some equipment, some people, some processes may be redundant' — and marketing 'these small subsegments' separately is hard, so the fix is one vendor code and one customer face: 'with one vendor code or with the same customer base, we can operate the capacities.' Capacity reallocation is the second driver: Sunbeam's utilisation is being cut from ~70% to 45–50% as it exits ~10 minuscule customers (5% of revenue), legacy 10–15-year-old products and a piston line of ~INR30 crore revenue sold to Shriram Pistons for Rs 28 crore, while DR Axion is full at 80–85% and must expand, and Craftsman has no Chennai aluminium plant — 'When we going to put a plant there for the DR Axion, then again, one more plant for Craftsman doesn't make sense.' The scheme filing adds that the aluminium business and the land needed for expansion sat in different entities, 'resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership' — the ~50 acres at Sriperumbudur bought for about INR150 crore via Suprash and Srikara is leased to DR Axion — so merging aligns land, infrastructure and operations in one entity with a stronger balance sheet, broader manufacturing base and streamlined structure. Management frames all of it as the first leg toward a $1 billion aluminium business in 2–3 years, against an aluminium base it approximated at INR6,500 crore in FY2027. Asked directly whether consolidation was a deleveraging route (Karthi, Suyash Advisors), Ravi said no — 'It will be more to fund our future investments maybe' — pointing instead to net debt/EBITDA of 2.43 falling below 2 and then 1.5 naturally.
verdict.evolution: The idea began as post-acquisition synergy talk: on the Oct 2024 call (24 Oct 2024) Ravi said the plan was to 'commonize the business development strategy' across Craftsman, DR Axion and Sunbeam given their non-overlapping customers and complementary casting processes, and by the Nov 2025 call (10 Nov 2025) he described shared resources reducing 'the overhead burden on each of the companies'. On the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) the teams had been 'more or less integrated… on the working side' and exhibited jointly at EUROGUSS, and he closed by saying there were 'more interesting things to do… to make the company more strategically aligned' — two weeks later, on 13 February 2026, the Board approved evaluating consolidation of the aluminium business at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, and on 11 March 2026 decided it must be done 'in a phased manner', approving only Phase 1 (step-downs into DR Axion, DR Axion into Sunbeam). By the May 2026 call (8 May 2026) Ravi confirmed the scope had widened beyond the subsidiaries to Craftsman's own aluminium division — 'The easy one was how to do it with the DR and Sunbeam. It's also related to Craftsman aluminium business' — and the 28 October 2026 results still carry the scheme as pending NCLT approval.

points.point: Ravi confirmed the restructuring covers not just the two subsidiaries but Craftsman's own aluminium division, with the subsidiary merger treated as the easy first step.
points.quote: We look at our public disclosure, we also mentioned that not only Sunbeam and DR, we also looked at our aluminium business of Craftsman also.

points.point: The central rationale is scale versus $3–6 billion global competitors: bidding $100–200 million orders as three separate $100m–$300m businesses is unwieldy and expensive.
points.quote: When we go with each of the businesses at $200 million, $100 million revenue or $300 million revenue and try to take an order for $100 million, $200 million, it is to share the resources and to grow the business, it is becoming unwieldy.

points.point: He named duplicated equipment, people and processes and the difficulty of marketing small subsegments separately as the operational problem being solved.
points.quote: What I'm trying to say is that some equipment, some people, some processes may be redundant here. We may have customer base. It's difficult to do marketing with these small subsegments in the business.

points.point: Capacity reallocation is an explicit purpose: Sunbeam's utilisation drops from ~70% to 45–50% as it exits unviable legacy products and customers, and that capacity moves to the group's new customers under one vendor code.
points.quote: That is one of the reasons for our restructuring, if you have seen, so that we can, with one vendor code or with the same customer base, we can operate the capacities.

points.point: Plant economics drive it too — Craftsman has no Chennai aluminium plant, DR Axion's plant is full at 80–85% and needs a new campus, and building two separate plants there makes no sense.
points.quote: We want to create a separate campus for that and add aluminium business of Craftsman, which is high pressure die casting mainly. Then DR's plant is full, we have to expand DR Axion. When we going to put a plant there for the DR Axion, then again, one more plant for Craftsman doesn't make sense.

points.point: The merger is tied to the stated $1 billion aluminium ambition, with the aluminium business approximated at around INR6,500 crore in FY2027 (explicitly not guidance).
points.quote: Our stated ambition on the aluminium business, in the last year, I think I had mentioned a couple of times at least during the earnings call, that the first leg or first phase will be to touch $1 billion on the aluminium business. For that, we are also increasing the focus by merging the entities of the business model, which we have also put -up disclosures in the stock exchange.

points.point: Asked by Karthi (Suyash Advisors) whether consolidating aluminium was a deleveraging route against INR3,300 crore of debt, Ravi said it was about funding future investment, with net debt/EBITDA of 2.43 falling below 2 then to 1.5 anyway.
points.quote: It will be more to fund our future investments maybe, but I think this debt portion of it, debt to EBITDA- wise, if you look at it, the forward- looking EBITDA, I think we are already at 2.43 net debt to EBITDA.

points.point: The newly acquired land-holding vehicles Suprash Developers and Srikara Technologies (~50 acres near SIPCOT for about INR150 crore, for DR Axion's Sriperumbudur greenfield) are to be absorbed so no subsidiaries remain.
points.quote: All this will get merged when we are doing the scheme of things, whatever we have filed. There will be no subsidiary once that is. . .

points.point: Scale was already the argument before the Board acted: Craftsman is below $0.5 billion in aluminium against peers of $3–8 billion, and management said it cannot even bid for large orders without scaling.
points.quote: And you know that the stated fact is we are less than $0.5 billion in aluminium revenue. So unless we scale up capacity, we cannot even bid for the orders.

points.point: Operational integration of the three aluminium teams was already underway ahead of any legal merger, including a joint appearance at EUROGUSS Nuremberg, pending Sunbeam's full restructuring.
points.quote: While we wait for the total restructuring of Sunbeam to happen thoroughly, we have more or less integrated the three teams on the working side of it.

points.point: Closing the call, Ravi flagged a coming structural step without naming it — two weeks before the Board approved evaluating the aluminium consolidation on 13 February 2026.
points.quote: We have more interesting things to do in the -- to make the company more strategically aligned in line with the global requirements.

points.point: The synergy logic was framed in overhead and shared-resource terms, with Sunbeam expected to converge on group margin levels because resources are shared across the three aluminium businesses.
points.quote: In fact, acquiring Sunbeam is also helping Craftsman to acquire more customers and also to reduce the overhead burden on each of the companies.

points.point: Shared campuses were already producing the effect ahead of the scheme — Sunbeam's Gurgaon operations were moved into Craftsman's Bhiwadi site and run as one unit, averaging fixed costs.
points.quote: When we are having a campus, for example at Bhiwadi, it is not only we have shifted the Gurgaon facilities into Bhiwadi, Sunbeam's plant is operational as one unit inside the Craftsman Bhiwadi area.

points.point: At acquisition, the stated plan was to commonise go-to-market across the three complementary aluminium units (Craftsman high-pressure, DR Axion gravity/low-pressure, Sunbeam low-tonnage) — the seed of the later merger.
points.quote: And what we are first thinking is to commonize the business development strategy. That will be very important to tap the new opportunities across the globe.

points.point: Subscale against global peers was already the framing, with the group below $0.5 billion in aluminium versus competitors of $1.5–7 billion.
points.quote: I have always been saying that the -- our aluminum competition outside the world between $1.5 billion to $6 billion, $7 billion in revenue.

points.point: The 13 February 2026 Board filing defines the scope: consolidating Craftsman's own aluminium products business together with its aluminium subsidiaries into a single wholly owned subsidiary, by scheme of arrangement or other mode.
points.quote: This evaluation will cover the restructuring/consolidation of the aluminium products business of the Company, together with its wholly owned subsidiaries engaged in the aluminium product business, at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, as well as consolidation of other wholly owned subsidiaries, through such modes as may be considered appropriate, including but not limited to a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable laws.

points.point: The 11 March 2026 scheme names the structural defect: operating business and the land/infrastructure needed to expand it sit in different entities.
points.quote: At present, the Aluminium business and the land and infrastructure required for its expansion are housed in different entities, resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership.

points.point: The stated benefit is one focused operating entity with a stronger balance sheet, broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership and streamlined structure, to capture expected industry growth.
points.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

points.point: Absorbing the land-holding step-down subsidiaries into DR Axion is justified by the approved new aluminium facility on that leased land, to align land, infrastructure and operations in one entity.
points.quote: It is expected that consolidation of the Step-Down Subsidiaries with DRA will lead to efficient implementation of the approved expansion plans, seamless development of manufacturing facilities, and align ownership of land, infrastructure, and operations under a single entity.

points.point: Phase 1 mechanics: step-downs merge into DR Axion with no new shares, then DR Axion merges into Sunbeam after Sunbeam's equity is reorganised to Re 1 face value; Craftsman is not a party and its shareholding is unaffected. FY2025 turnover was Sunbeam INR1,237.46 crore (net worth 107.43) and DR Axion INR1,298.52 crore (net worth 511.34).
points.quote: After reorganization of the equity capital of the Amalgamated Company such that the face value of its equity shares is changed to INR 1/- each, issuance of 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Amalgamated Company having face value of INR 1/- (Indian Rupees One) each at a premium of INR 9/- (Indian Rupees Nine) each, for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of face value INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each held in the Amalgamating Company 3.

points.point: The simplification objective is stated separately from the growth case, covering managerial focus and operating efficiency.
points.quote: The proposed consolidation of DRA with Sunbeam is also expected to simplify the corporate structure and improve managerial focus and operational efficiency.

verdict.what_management_expects: One aluminium entity able to bid $100–200m orders toward $1bn scale; shared equipment, people and processes with one vendor code; Sunbeam's freed capacity reallocated as it exits legacy products (EBITDA ~7% to 10%+); unified land and asset ownership, stronger balance sheet, simpler structure. Margin gain only once capex matures and growth slows; said to fund investment, not deleverage; Craftsman's shareholding unchanged.
verdict.gaps: No valuation, listing, stake-sale or value-unlocking intent; no quantified cost or margin benefit; no timeline for moving Craftsman's own aluminium division; no tax or NCLT timeline.

verdict.segment_name: Aluminium Products (consolidated reportable segment; the entities under the Composite Scheme of Arrangement — DR Axion India, Suprash Developers and Srikara Technologies merging into Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions — sit inside this segment)
verdict.unit: ₹ lakhs for the annual segment tables; ₹ crore for the quarterly presentation figures
verdict.measure_notes: Operating profit = 'Segment Profit or Loss' as disclosed under Ind AS 108, i.e. segment EBIT before unallocable expenditure, other income, finance costs and exceptional items (not EBITDA, not PBT). Revenue is segment revenue that sums exactly to 'Total revenue as per Statement of Profit and Loss', so it is external revenue with no inter-segment figure disclosed. Figures taken on a consolidated basis because the entities in the Scheme are subsidiaries; standalone Aluminium Products segment figures are lower (FY2024 91,746 / 12,902; FY2025 1,15,957 / 11,600; FY2026 1,80,072 / 24,202 — AR2024 p93, AR2025 p172-173, AR2026 p165). The Scheme is an internal amalgamation of subsidiaries within this segment, not a separation/demerger with carve-out financials in these pages.

Annual Report 2025 — page 239
