verdict.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle (MFL) business — the four Lifestyle/Power brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England) plus the emerging portfolio of Reebok, American Eagle and Van Heusen Innerwear, and a contract-manufacturing/institutional arm — out of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd (ABFRL, the Demerged Company) into Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Ltd (ABLBL, the Resulting Company), on a going-concern basis with 1:1 shares so holders own identical stakes in both; the Board approved it on April 19, 2024, NCLT sanctioned it on March 27, 2025, it became effective May 1, 2025, 1,22,02,94,773 shares were allotted May 26, 2025 (record date May 22, 2025) and ABLBL listed June 23, 2025. The reason management gave is capital allocation, stated most bluntly by Ashish Dikshit on the Feb 3, 2026 call: 'One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth' — because inside ABFRL the cash this branded business threw off 'was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses' (Aug 14, 2025), starving the mature brands of reinvestment. The quantification: the business generates roughly INR 900 crores of EBITDA cash, part to working capital and part to capex, where historical capex was 'close to 150 to 200 in the best years, maybe INR225 odd crores'; post-demerger FY26 capex went 'north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores', funding 300+ gross store additions to 3,348 stores / 4.9 million sq ft across ~800 towns, 65 renovations in one quarter, and a new Pulivendula factory. Debt came across by formula — 'at the time of demerger, the company got the borrowings transferred based on the allocation formula' — about INR 800 crores at March 2025, peaking near INR 1,000 crores in September 2025 on festive inventory, INR 800 crores in December 2025 and INR 726 crores at March 2026 versus INR 781 crores a year earlier; INR 500 crores of NCDs repaid in January 2026 were refinanced with 'no fresh borrowing', and management guided to INR 200–300 crores of annual reduction and near-zero net debt in about three years, with capex ranked ahead of deleveraging ('Only the subsequent part will go towards debt reduction'). Management also kept repeating the structural promise that neither entity would raise equity except ABFRL's retained 'tomorrow' businesses, and demonstrated the self-funding claim with a maiden 50 paise dividend in year one and a stated 15–25%-of-PAT payout range. Growth is to be split by entity economics: Lifestyle Brands in early double digits on 6–7% (later '7%') steady-state LTL plus ~200 store adds a year, and the emerging brands at 18–20%+ (Dikshit: 'in excess of 20%'), rising to one-fourth of ABLBL in four to five years, with Reebok already doubled in sales and network tripled since acquisition and Van Heusen Innerwear losses halving on the way to break-even. Notably, no call or filing attributes the demerger request to any investor, lender or brand partner — it is presented purely as a board/strategy decision about where cash gets reinvested.
verdict.evolution: The Scheme itself dates to the April 19, 2024 board approval, with NCLT sanction on March 27, 2025 and effect from May 1, 2025, and the Aug 14, 2025 (Q1 FY26) call was the first as an independent listee — there Dikshit gave the rationale in answer to Niharika Karnani, that cash which had been used to kick-start or acquire new businesses inside ABFRL would now fund this business's own growth (capex first, debt reduction later, debt-free in 2.5–3 years, newer brands 18–20% vs Lifestyle early double digits). The Nov 5, 2025 (Q2 FY26) call barely revisited the rationale and instead exposed a transition cost: comparable prior-year segment numbers were missing because the business 'was part of the consolidated ABFRL', while net debt had risen ~INR 200 crores on festive and Bangladesh-related inventory build. On Feb 3, 2026 (Q3 FY26) the logic was restated most explicitly and tested — Ambit's Videesha Sheth challenged the INR 500 crore NCD board approval against the no-fundraise promise, management explained the demerger-allocated borrowings and pure refinancing, and Dikshit tied slower deleveraging directly to the demerger's purpose (capex INR 320–330 crores vs INR 150–225 crores historically), while guiding emerging brands to one-fourth of the company in 4–5 years. By May 8, 2026 (Q4 FY26) the narrative shifted from rationale to proof: 'a strong start to being an independent entity', 300+ stores added, net debt down to INR 726 crores, and the first dividend (50 paise) with a 15–25% payout framework, debt-free in three years but explicitly 'not something that we are chasing'.

points.point: Dikshit states the core demerger rationale outright — creating an entity that can reinvest its own cash flow aggressively into growth — and cites ~INR 900 crores of EBITDA cash split between working capital and capex.
points.quote: One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.

points.point: Answering Niharika Karnani on use of cash, Dikshit says the branded business's cash was previously consumed by ABFRL's new-business acquisitions, and the demerger's purpose was to keep that cash for this business's growth.
points.quote: The cash generated by this business in the past has -- was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses. And the whole purpose of demerger was actually to need the cash for this business to grow faster.

points.point: Capital allocation priority post-demerger is explicitly growth capex (especially retail) ahead of deleveraging, with INR 200–300 crores of annual debt reduction and debt-free status in 2.5–3 years.
points.quote: Only the subsequent part will go towards debt reduction.

points.point: The demerger's reinvestment logic is quantified: capex rose from a historical INR 150–225 crores to INR 320–330 crores in FY26, which management says is exactly why net debt fell little that year.
points.quote: This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores , perhaps INR320 crores , INR330 crores . And that's really why the debt reduction is not very large this year.

points.point: Debt was allocated to ABLBL at demerger by formula; the INR 500 crores of NCDs approved by the board in Feb 2026 were only to refinance debentures repaid in January, not new money — answering Ambit's challenge to the no-fundraise promise made for both entities except the 'tomorrow' business.
points.quote: at the time of demerger, the company got the borrowings transferred based on the allocation formula. The INR500 crores debentures which we repaid recently in the month of January, we intend to raise it and to refinance the existing, the debentures repaid. There is no fresh borrowin g.

points.point: Management frames the standalone cash flow case as proven: a maiden 50 paise dividend in the first year post-demerger, a 15–25% of net profit payout range, and debt-free capability in about three years though not chased.
points.quote: As you know, we had announced at the time of formation of company that looking at the predictable, consistent, historical cash flows of the company, we are very confident that this company over a period of time will become a debt-free company and equally will be able to pay dividends as it goes forward.

points.point: First full year as a separate company is presented as validation: 300+ store additions to 3,348 stores / 4.9 million sq ft across ~800 towns, revenue INR 8,396 crores (+7%), EBITDA INR 1,429 crores (17%, +90bps), net debt INR 726 crores vs INR 781 crores.
points.quote: The year marked a strong start to being an independent entity supported by encouraging business momentum and several positive operating milestones across brands and channels.

points.point: The separated portfolio's growth is to be re-weighted toward the emerging brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle), targeted at a quarter of the company within four to five years, versus early-double-digit Lifestyle Brands.
points.quote: This portfolio is expected to be one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4 -5 years.

points.point: Differential growth rates by entity sub-portfolio were set at the post-demerger analyst meet: newer businesses 18–20% (elsewhere 'in excess of 20%') against Lifestyle Brands in early double digits, with capex ~80%+ going to Lifestyle expansion and renovation.
points.quote: We expect the newer business to grow anything between 18 % to 20 %, while Lifestyle Brands business will grow in early double digits.

points.point: A cost of the split surfaced: analysts could not get comparable prior-year segment data because the business had been reported inside consolidated ABFRL, and reporting definitions had changed.
points.quote: Yes, Yes, Devanshu, you know, it was part of the consolidated ABFRL, so we are splitting up, but, you know, we'll provide you separately.

points.point: The Scheme of Arrangement demerged the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle business from ABFRL into ABLBL on a going-concern basis for shares, so shareholders hold identical stakes in both entities; effective May 1, 2025, 1,22,02,94,773 shares allotted May 26, 2025, listed June 23, 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme provided for demerger, transfer, and vesting of the MFL Business from the Demerged Company to the Resulting Company on a going concern basis, with the Resulting Company issuing equity shares to the equity shareholders of the Demerged Company as a consideration.

points.point: Legacy liabilities of the demerged business still follow ABLBL: multiple GST orders issued in the name of ABFRL in March 2026 (including a INR 310.13 crore demand) relate to the business demerged effective May 1, 2025 and are being appealed.
points.quote: Order is in the name of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL). However, it relates to the business of the Company, which got demerged from ABFRL, pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement effective from May 1, 2025.

verdict.what_management_expects: ABLBL: its own ~INR 900cr EBITDA cash reinvested in growth — FY26 capex INR 320–330cr, 300+ new stores, Lifestyle early-double-digit growth with gradual margin expansion, emerging brands 18–20%+ reaching one-fourth of revenue in 4–5 years; net debt INR 726cr falling INR 200–300cr yearly toward zero in three years; dividends 15–25% of PAT. Only ABFRL's retained 'tomorrow' businesses raise capital.
verdict.gaps: No one is named as asking for it — no investor, lender or brand partner; no debt-allocation formula, no ABFRL-side rationale, no valuation re-rating or dis-synergy/separation-cost estimate.

verdict.rationale: On these texts there is no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement at Choice International — the premise is not supported, and management rejected it each time it was raised. Asked directly in Jul 2025 about carving out the government-advisory/consulting vertical (Choice Consultancy Services, then a Rs. 586 Cr order book, 22-25% margins), Arun Poddar said a demerger was "not in our plan" and that the focus was purely business growth; asked in Oct 2025 about demerging the broking entity, Ayush Sharma said there were no immediate plans and that Choice Equity Broking would "continue as a subsidiary of Choice International in the medium term"; asked in Apr 2026 about demerging all four businesses and listing them separately, he conceded only that "value unlock will be one of the target" with no immediate plans. The stated reasons for keeping the group intact are that all four segments (broking & distribution ~59%, advisory ~28%, NBFC ~13% of revenue in Q4 FY26) are treated as equally core with dedicated CEOs per vertical and an annual operating plan tracked monthly at the hold-co, that each business is "self-sufficient" and needs little capital while the hold-co has enough internal accruals to fund growth, and that the unrelated advisory business deliberately "balances the market macroeconomic scenarios" when broking is weak. What the filings actually show is the opposite of separation plus partial monetisation at the subsidiary level: a Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT Mumbai order dated May 11, 2026, appointed date Apr 1, 2025) merging Choice Wealth Private Limited into Arete Capital Service Private Limited at 92:100 for "operational synergies, cost efficiencies, optimal utilisation of resources, and improved overall profitability"; a Rs. 9,000 million primary CCPS issue by material subsidiary Choice Equity Broking (42,25,350 CCPS at Rs. 2,130, face value Rs. 10 plus Rs. 2,120 premium, proceeds received Oct 27, 2026) to NH Investment & Securities of Korea, explicitly growth capital for the MTF book, technology, customer acquisition, talent and scalability with no change in control, where CEBPL contributed 25% of CIL net worth and 51% of turnover in FY26; and only at the green-energy fringe anything resembling separation — a 49% dilution of Choice Green Energy MH-1 and MH-2 to SolarEra Green Renewables (Rs. 22.54 lakh and Rs. 27.44 lakh, Nov 2025) and the full exit from step-down subsidiary SKP Green Ventures to Arrowbridge Trade for Rs. 1.275 Cr (Nov 4, 2026), a unit contributing 0.37% of consolidated turnover. Nobody — not investors, not lenders, not the Korean partner — is recorded as asking for a separation; the investor questions on demerger came from retail participants (Nakul Dev of ND Investments, Shruti Sharma, Ramesh Thorani of Mehta Brothers) and were each declined.
verdict.evolution: The idea only ever surfaced as unprompted investor questions and was refused each time: Apr 23, 2025 brought only a segment-reporting split (insurance to become a fourth reported segment), and Jul 22, 2025 added wealth "coming out as a separate vertical" post-Arete, both reporting-level, not legal. Jul 22, 2025 (advisory) and Oct 17, 2025 (broking) saw explicit denials of demerger; Feb 4, 2026 had no demerger question at all. By Apr 24, 2026 the answer softened only to "not immediately" with value unlock acknowledged as an eventual target, while the Jul 9, 2026 NHIS CCPS deal and the May 2026 amalgamation show the group instead raising capital inside, and consolidating, the broking/wealth stack rather than separating it.

points.point: Asked outright about demerging the four businesses and listing them separately, IR declined but for the first time named value unlock as an eventual (not immediate) objective.
points.quote: Not immediately. Of course, the value unlock will be one of the target, but there are there are no immediate plans to do so.

points.point: A family-office participant asked specifically about demerging the broking entity; IR said it stays a subsidiary through the medium term.
points.quote: Currently we don't have any immediate plans to demerge the broking business. It is going to continue as a subsidiary of Choice International in the medium term from here.

points.point: Nakul Dev (ND Investments) asked whether the advisory/consulting vertical — then a Rs. 586 Cr order book at 22-25% margins — would be demerged; the Group CEO ruled it out in favour of growth.
points.quote: As far as the demerger of this activity is concerned, as of now, it's not in our plan. We are purely focusing on business growth and getting the major numbers. As of now, there is no plan in terms of demerger or disengaged services.

points.point: The structural case against separation: dedicated CEOs per vertical, hold-co AOP tracked monthly, every segment self-funding, so no capital or bandwidth argument for splitting.
points.quote: Although all of our businesses are self-sufficient now, they don't need much of the capital.

points.point: Management refuses any core/non-core ranking of the four segments — the usual precondition for a carve-out — and guides to a steady 50-40-10 revenue mix (broking/advisory/NBFC).
points.quote: There is no segment which is of non-core focus.

points.point: The only "separation" management itself proposed was reporting-level: insurance distribution to be broken out as a fourth reported segment alongside broking, NBFC and advisory.
points.quote: However, at the same time, we expect that insurance distribution, as it has been growing rapidly over the couple of years, we see that in the foreseeable future, insurance will be a separate segment.

points.point: Post the Arete Capital acquisition, wealth was flagged as emerging as its own vertical out of broking — again a management/reporting construct, not a legal separation.
points.quote: So, we expect that segment also as coming out as a separate vertical out of the broking segment.

points.point: The rationale for holding the unrelated advisory business inside the group: it offsets broking cyclicality, which is a positive case for conglomerate structure.
points.quote: However, at the same time, this diversification support us in the challenging or turbulent times as the markets have performed not very well over the last couple of months.

points.point: Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT Mumbai, order dated May 11, 2026, appointed date Apr 1, 2025) merged Choice Wealth into Arete Capital Service at 92 shares for every 100 — consolidation of two wholly owned wealth subsidiaries, the opposite of a separation.
points.quote: The amalgamation has resulted in operational synergies, cost efficiencies, optimal utilisation of resources, and improved overall profitability of the amalgamated entity.

points.point: Instead of separating broking, CIL raised Rs. 9,000 mn of primary capital inside it: 42,25,350 CCPS at Rs. 2,130 to NH Investment & Securities (Jul 9, 2026 agreements; proceeds received Oct 27, 2026), CEBPL being 25% of CIL net worth and 51% of turnover in FY26, with an aim of 5x growth in three years and no change of control; the SHA carries board-composition, reserved-matter, put-option, non-compete, transfer and lock-in covenants.
points.quote: The infusion of capital will strengthen CEBPL's financial position and capital base, providing the resources required to support its growth and expansion plans, pursue strategic opportunities, and meet its evolving business requirements.

points.point: The only genuine separations are peripheral green-energy assets: a 49% dilution of Choice Green Energy MH-1/MH-2 to SolarEra Green Renewables (Rs. 22.54 lakh and Rs. 27.44 lakh, Nov 5, 2025) framed as an EPC/O&M partnership, and the full sale of SKP Green Ventures to Arrowbridge Trade for Rs. 1,27,50,000 on Nov 4, 2026 — a unit that was 0.37% of consolidated turnover and 0.056% of net worth.
points.quote: SolarEra brings in proven expertise for developing the projects using advanced asset management tools for maximizing plant performance.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation is expected, so no per-entity benefits were claimed. Management expects group-level gains instead: 30% revenue/PAT growth, EBITDA and PAT margins expanding on a fixed cost base through tech, a 50-40-10 revenue mix, hold-co internal accruals funding any vertical, and — for broking specifically — NHIS's Rs. 9,000 mn funding 5x growth, MTF scale-up and institutional capability. Value unlock is only an eventual, unquantified aim.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no separation rationale, entity perimeter, timeline, record date, debt or capital allocation, or shareholder/lender treatment — because no demerger or spin-off was ever announced in these texts.

verdict.rationale: On these documents REC is not separating a business — the corporate action is the opposite: REC Limited is being merged by absorption INTO its own parent, Power Finance Corporation (PFC), after which REC ceases to exist; the only genuine 'separations' in the record are RECPDCL's routine sales of project-specific transmission SPVs (Barmer HVDC, Vizag, Bhadla Ramgarh, WR ER Part A/C, Luhri, Jalna, Umred, Bellary Davanagere and others) to winning bidders under tariff-based competitive bidding, each disclosed as contributing 'Negligible' turnover and net worth, i.e. REC's bid-process-coordinator role rather than a demerger. The merger was not asked for by investors, lenders or partners: it originated with the Government of India, announced by the Finance Minister in the Union Budget 2026-27 on 1 February 2026 as a restructuring of PFC and REC 'to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs', described as 'a first step'; REC's Board gave in-principle approval on 6 February 2026, and because REC's Articles vest director/major decisions with the President of India, the Board on 16 May 2026 reserved the proposal for Presidential approval, which the Ministry of Power conveyed on 10 June 2026. The stated problems it solves are scale and capital capacity for the power sector's investment needs toward 'Viksit Bharat 2047': the merged entity is pitched as the Government's principal institution for implementing power sector reforms and flagship programmes (RDSS, PM Surya Ghar, UMPPs, IPDS, ITP bid coordination), with an aggregate loan book of over ₹11 lakh crore and, on consolidated metrics, 'the largest power sector financer in India'. Management cited FY2025-26 numbers of REC standalone net worth ₹84,290 crore and turnover ₹59,140 crore (consolidated ₹85,054 crore / ₹59,584 crore) against PFC standalone ₹1,02,532 crore / ₹58,504 crore (consolidated ₹1,73,441 crore / ₹1,15,444 crore), and argued the combination improves balance-sheet strength, capital base, operational efficiencies, borrowing capacity, pricing for customers, project bankability, risk sharing and access to longer-tenor capital, and positions it to fund green hydrogen, CCUS, energy storage, small modular nuclear reactors and grid modernisation. Lenders feature only as a constraint to be managed, not as petitioners: the 12 February 2026 joint PFC-REC update explains RBI single-borrower/group exposure norms tied to Tier I capital — pre-2019 the two were separate 20% single-entity limits (40% combined), post-PFC's 2019 acquisition of 52.63% they fell under a 25% group limit, and post-merger a single 20% limit applies — asserting adequate headroom given top-ten banks' aggregate Tier I of roughly ₹18 lakh crore and a borrowing mix of about 18% domestic bank/FI, 25% foreign currency and 57% domestic bonds. The Scheme, approved by the Board on 28 June 2026 under Sections 230-232, fixes consideration at 88 PFC shares of ₹10 for every 100 REC shares of ₹10 (joint valuations by Ernst & Young Merchant Banking Services LLP and RBSA Valuation Advisors LLP; fairness opinions from Nuvama for REC and SBI Capital Markets for PFC; Deloitte as transaction/tax advisor, Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas as legal advisor), with REC dissolved without winding up and the hard condition that the merged entity remain a 'Government Company' with the Government of India retaining majority voting rights and control. Notably, none of the six earnings calls supplied (Aug 2024 through Nov 2025, all predating the Budget announcement) mentions any separation, demerger or merger at all — through Nov 2025 management was still guiding a single integrated balance sheet to a ₹10 lakh crore loan book by 2030 with 30% renewables.
verdict.evolution: Across all six transcripts (Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025 and the Oct 29, 2025 call reported in Nov 2025) there is zero discussion of separating or merging anything — management instead repeats a standalone growth story (₹10 lakh crore loan book by 2030, ₹3 lakh crore renewables, NIM 3.5-3.75%), notes PFC's 52.60-52.63% holding as a mere shareholding fact, and the only 'separation' analysed is a borrower's, TANGEDCO's trifurcation, in the Nov 2024 call. The idea therefore surfaced entirely outside the calls: a media report prompted REC's 3 February 2026 clarification flatly denying any such discussions, two days after the Finance Minister's 1 February 2026 Budget announcement; the Board gave in-principle approval on 6 February 2026, a joint PFC-REC explanatory update followed on 12 February 2026, the Board reserved the matter for the President of India on 16 May 2026, Ministry of Power approval came on 10 June 2026, and the full Scheme with the 88:100 ratio was approved on 28 June 2026. It then hardened from intent into an approved transaction — the 57th AGM on 25 August 2026 covered 'Merger of REC into PFC' in the Chairman's speech and in shareholder questions, RBI's No Objection Certificate arrived 15 October 2026, and BSE/NSE observation letters followed on 19 October 2026 with SEBI conditions. Over that period the plan changed from an unspecified 'restructuring' of two companies to a one-directional merger by absorption in which REC, the transferor, is dissolved and its shareholders are paid only in PFC stock, with no cash consideration.

points.point: The only separation discussed on any call is a borrower's: TANGEDCO's trifurcation into generation, transmission and distribution entities, which management said relieved REC's single-borrower exposure constraint and left government guarantees intact — nothing about REC's own structure.
points.quote: Whatever loan was guaranteed by the government continues to remain guaranteed by the government even after the trifurcation.

points.point: On the last call before the Budget announcement, CMD Jitendra Srivastava was still guiding a single consolidated REC balance sheet doubling to ₹10 lakh crore by 2030 with 30% renewables — no hint of any separation, demerger or merger.
points.quote: As all of you know, we have very categorically said that by 2030, our loan book will touch Rs. 10 lakh crores, out of which the renewable sector, we are anticipating it to contribute to 30% of our loan book, which is Rs. 3 lakh crores.

points.point: PFC's majority holding — the structural precondition for the later absorption — was presented on the calls only as a line in the shareholding pattern, with no strategic commentary.
points.quote: The shareholding pattern of REC has been given in the presentation, where you can see the PFC holds 52.60% of REC shares, while the FII holds almost 18% of the total equity of REC.

points.point: The idea came from the Government, not from investors, lenders or partners: the Finance Minister's Union Budget 2026-27 speech of 1 February 2026 proposed restructuring PFC and REC to achieve scale and efficiency among public sector NBFCs, explicitly as a 'first step'.
points.quote: In order to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs, as a first step, it is proposed to restructure the Power Finance Corporation and Rural Electrification Corporation.

points.point: Two days later, responding to exchange queries on a news report headlined 'Govt. considering merger of state-run entities PFC and REC', REC denied being party to any negotiations, saying the Budget announcement would be deliberated at the next Board meeting (which then approved it in-principle on 6 February 2026).
points.quote: The Company is not engaged in any such discussions or negotiations.

points.point: The 12 February 2026 joint PFC-REC update frames the purpose as scale for Viksit Bharat 2047 capital needs and new technologies (green hydrogen, CCUS, small modular nuclear reactors, storage), with the combined entity ranked first in the sector.
points.quote: Based on consolidated metrics, the merged entity would be positioned as the largest power sector financer in India.

points.point: Bank lenders appear as a regulatory constraint to be managed rather than a party asking for the deal: the same update walks through RBI exposure limits — 20% each pre-2019, a 25% group limit after PFC's 52.63% acquisition, and a single 20% limit post-merger — claiming headroom from top-ten banks' ~₹18 lakh crore aggregate Tier I capital and a borrowing mix of ~18% bank/FI, 25% foreign currency, 57% domestic bonds.
points.quote: Prior to the acquisition, both entities were subject to a single-entity exposure limit of 20% each (combined limit of 40%).

points.point: Because REC's Articles reserve such matters to the President of India, the Board on 16 May 2026 only reserved the proposal for Presidential approval (granted via Ministry of Power on 10 June 2026), making clear REC is extinguished rather than separated.
points.quote: Upon the merger being duly approved under applicable law and being made effective, all the assets and liabilities ofREC shall be transferred to PFC, and REC shall stand dissolved in accordance with the provisions of Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013.

points.point: The 28 June 2026 Scheme fixes an all-stock consideration with no cash, valued jointly by Ernst & Young Merchant Banking Services LLP and RBSA Valuation Advisors LLP with fairness opinions from Nuvama (REC) and SBI Capital Markets (PFC); aggregate loan book of the combined entity is put at over ₹11 lakh crore.
points.quote: The Share Exchange Ratio for the Proposed Merger of REC into PFC shall be 88 equity shares of PFC of INR 10/- each fully paid up for every 100 equity shares of REC of INR 10/- each fully paid up.

points.point: The stated institutional rationale is that one merged lender becomes the Government's delivery vehicle for power-sector schemes (RDSS, PM Surya Ghar, UMPPs, IPDS, ITP bid coordination), alongside claimed gains in balance-sheet strength, borrowing capacity, customer pricing, project bankability and longer-tenor capital.
points.quote: The merged entity would become the primary vehicle for implementing a majority of government schemes for the power sector and would maximize sector benefits through these programs.

points.point: The only actual divestments in the record are RECPDCL's continuing par-value transfers of project-specific transmission SPVs (e.g. Barmer HVDC at ₹18.98 crore and Sakoli at ₹3.06 crore on 23 Sep 2026; Vizag to Adani Energy Solutions at ₹18.66 crore; Lakadia II and Jam Khambhaliya Jamnagar at ~₹18.4 crore each) to TBCB winners, each disclosed as contributing 'Negligible' turnover and net worth and explicitly not a slump sale.
points.quote: Hence, with effect from the aforesaid date, the above project specific SPY / subsidiary is not the subsidiary ofRECPDCL & REC Limited.

points.point: Approvals progressed to near-completion: the 57th AGM on 25 August 2026 listed 'Merger of REC into PFC' in the Chairman's address and in shareholder Q&A, RBI issued its No Objection Certificate on 15 October 2026, and BSE/NSE issued observation letters on 19 October 2026 conditional on RBI approval and settlement of outstanding dues.
points.quote: Further, the shareholders asked questions pertaining to Merger of REC & PFC, CSR, Future roadmap, ESG Rating, Borrowing Strategy and other aspects related to business and operations of the Company.

verdict.what_management_expects: No two entities emerge: REC is dissolved into PFC. For the single merged entity they expect improved balance-sheet strength, a stronger capital base, operational efficiencies, greater borrowing capacity and financial flexibility, more competitive pricing for customers, better project bankability and longer-tenor capital, headroom under RBI exposure limits, India's largest power-sector loan book (over ₹11 lakh crore), and continued Government Company status with GoI control.
verdict.gaps: No separation exists; calls (all pre-Budget) never mention it. Unquantified synergies, cost savings, EPS/NIM/rating impact, basis of the 88:100 ratio, integration, staffing, effective date.

verdict.segment_name: Single business segment — lending to power, logistic and infrastructure sector (REC Limited, standalone; no separate reportable segment under Ind AS 108)
verdict.measure_notes: No segment result/EBIT is disclosed because the Company reports only one business segment, so segment-level profit lines do not exist. Revenue = 'Information about Revenue from major products and services' (Income from Loan Assets + Fee for Implementation of Government Schemes + Income from Treasury Operations), standalone, all external (no inter-segment revenue). operating_profit, where populated, is Profit Before Tax (PBT) from the investor presentation's standalone P&L — not EBIT or EBITDA, since finance cost is the Company's main operating cost as an NBFC. PAT for FY2025/FY2026 is REC Limited (parent) standalone net profit from the Schedule III 'Share in profit and loss' table; FY2024 PAT is standalone PAT from the investor presentation. Note the FY2025 revenue figure was later restated: AR2025 shows 55,445.24 while AR2026's comparative shows 55,457.60.

verdict.rationale: These texts contain no plan to separate, demerge or spin off any business out of OneSource — the corporate action running through all seven calls and filings is the opposite: a Composite Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation (merger by absorption) that would have folded promoter/family-office and TPG-owned Steriscience assets INTO OneSource, namely Steriscience Specialties, Brooks Steriscience's integrated carbapenem/penem plant at Baroda (OneSource group already owned 51%), Steriscience Pte and Strides Pharma Services, plus the US-FDA-approved Polish multi-dose sterile fill-finish site. Management's stated reasons were a pre-IPO promoter commitment to investors to bring family-office CDMO assets under OneSource; de-risking the single-site customer concentration that customers themselves 'have been emphasizing'; a global footprint with Poland having space to add a GLP drug-device line in time for Europe and the US opening; and complementary capability (ampoules, large-scale vials, high-viscosity pre-filled syringes, penems alongside OneSource's penicillin franchise). The numbers cited: ~US$65m revenue in FY26 at 36–40% EBITDA, contracted to deliver at least US$100m revenue and US$36–40m EBITDA in FY27, near debt-free (under US$7–8m debt), H1FY26 combined incoming revenue US$29m/EBITDA US$11m at 38% margin (US$110m combined with OneSource at 30%), funded purely by ~2.5 crore new shares with no debt added, lifting the FY28 outlook from US$400m revenue/US$160m EBITDA to US$500m+/US$200m+. The only genuine separations described are historical and completed: OneSource was itself carved out of Strides through an NCLT scheme and listed in January 2025 — the group's 'second big distribution value unlocking after Agila', ~INR8,000 crore delivered to Strides shareholders — with its genesis being customers' wish for a one-stop CDMO and a larger wallet share; and Unit-3 (multimodal) was sold to Syngene International on a slump sale and reported as discontinued operations, with INR100m withheld, INR50m provided, INR43.1m received and a further INR6.9m provision. A residual of that separation persists: soft gel capacity sits under a limited-period transition agreement with Strides (the business 'under Strides was primarily focused on captive IP-led products'), prompting a greenfield site. The inbound merger was then abandoned in current form on 13 May 2026 for valuation and related-party-governance reasons: large shareholders were committed but 'a long tail of smaller investors' had valuation concerns, the listed Brooks price had dropped sharply from an intended ~INR2,200/share, and the board lacked its customary 95%+ RPT voting comfort, so it deferred until OneSource delivers US$400m/US$160m and the incoming assets US$40m EBITDA — a re-look 'in about two years'. Separately, two wholly owned Singapore subsidiaries (Stelis Pte and OneSource Specialty Pte) were amalgamated effective 1 January 2026 purely to simplify the corporate hierarchy and cut duplicate administrative, compliance and legal costs.
verdict.evolution: Feb 2025 marks the completed separation — OneSource's NCLT carve-out from Strides and listing, framed as value unlocking for Strides shareholders. On the Aug 2025 call the board gave a go-ahead to evaluate the inbound Steriscience/Brooks transaction as the promised pre-IPO promoter commitment; Nov 2025 raised the FY28 outlook to US$500m+ 'subject to shareholder approvals'; Jan 2026 said SEBI/exchange discussion was 'working very well' with approvals expected by Q3 FY27. Exchanges issued no-objection letters on 25–26 Feb 2026, but the board ordered a further review before NCLT filing on 6 Mar 2026 and on 13 May 2026 (and the May 2026 call) dropped it in current form on valuation and RPT-approval grounds, deferring ~two years. By the Jul 2026 call the scheme was never mentioned again; only the Strides soft gel transition agreement and a new greenfield came up.

points.point: Arun Kumar frames OneSource's own separation from Strides as the group's second large value-unlocking distribution to shareholders, quantifying it at about INR8,000 crore delivered.
points.quote: Almost 8,000 crores has been delivered in this process and this continues to be our theme for several years and this is our second big distribution value unlocking after Agila and by far the largest, so we are very delighted that we continue with this strategy.

points.point: Neeraj Sharma gives the genesis of carving the CDMO assets into one listed vehicle: customers wanting one-stop supply chains, and OneSource getting a higher share of their wallet.
points.quote: Why OneSource, the whole inception was basically coming from our customers' desire to simplify supply chains, to go for one-stop-shop providers, especially in the areas of CDMO.

points.point: Arun explains that the Poland and Baroda/Brooks assets were deliberately left out of the original NCLT scheme because they were still 'in the making' and complicated it — hence the later inbound merger.
points.quote: So, as you all know that OneSource is a culmination of an NCLT process where three parts of the businesses of the group combined and at that time both the Polish facilities and the Baroda joint venture with Brooks was still in the making and was complicating the NCLT process.

points.point: Who asked for the transaction: investors. It is presented as delivery of a promoter commitment made on the pre-IPO roadshows to bring family-office CDMO assets under OneSource.
points.quote: As part of our roadshows pre-IPO, we as promoters made commitments to investors that we would bring our CDMO assets in the group or in the family office under the OneSource umbrella and this announcement, subject to various approvals, is the beginning of that commitment that we made as promoters.

points.point: The problem it solves, per management: customers' concentration risk on a single site, plus headroom in Poland to add a GLP line for the Europe and US openings.
points.quote: More importantly, this also gives us the ability to kind of de-risk the concentration risk that our customers have been emphasizing.

points.point: The financial case cited: ~US$65m current-year revenue at 36–40% EBITDA, contractually committed to at least US$100m revenue and US$36–40m EBITDA the following year.
points.quote: We currently have approximately $65 million of revenues for this year with an EBITDA in the 36% to 40% range and fully booked and committed to deliver $100 million of revenues at the bare minimum in the next year and that's $36 million to $40 million of EBITDA.

points.point: Consideration structure: equity dilution only (later quantified as roughly 2.5 crore additional shares), no incremental debt on OneSource, hence accretive.
points.quote: It will not require, apart from an equity dilution, it will not require OneSource to lever any kind of debt or add debt to its books, so this will be accretive from that nature, but obviously these are very early days and we will keep our investors and analysts' community fully updated as we progress on this.

points.point: With the incoming businesses, the FY28 outlook is raised from US$400m organic to US$500m, explicitly conditional on shareholder approval of the scheme.
points.quote: So we are now very bullish on what the next year will look like, and we are very confident and we are willing to reiterate our 2028 guidance for INR400 million on the base business, and then with the inorganic businesses that are also performing strongly to now reiterate our INR500 million outlook for FY 2028 subject to shareholder approvals.

points.point: CFO Anurag Bhagania reports the SEBI/stock-exchange process progressing and guides to all regulatory approvals by Q3 FY27 — the last optimistic datapoint before the reversal.
points.quote: We anticipate, us to be able to get the final all regulatory approvals in place by third quarter of FY27.

points.point: The 26 Feb 2026 filing confirms NSE and BSE no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters for the scheme, valid six months, still subject to NCLT, Singapore court, shareholders and creditors.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that The National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited (“Stock Exchanges”) by their respective letters dated February 25, 2026 have conveyed their “No-objection /No Adverse Observation Letter”, for the Proposed Scheme.

points.point: SEBI's comments relayed via NSE force OneSource to justify the merger to public shareholders, including the accumulated losses of the transferor entities landing on its balance sheet and the rise in promoter shareholding.
points.quote: Details w.r.t. accumulated losses of transferor entities getting merged with Onesource and reason as to how is such merger beneficial/ in the interest of public shareholders of Onesource considering that these losses will form part of balance sheet of Onesource;

points.point: The scheme also bundled a financial restructuring, setting off OneSource's negative retained earnings against its securities premium account.
points.quote: wherein Brooks Steriscience Limited, Steriscience Pte Limited and Strides Pharma Services Private Limited, will be amalgamated with the Company and financial restructuring to set-off the negative balance in the Retained Earnings Account, against the balance lying in the Securities Premium Account.

points.point: On 6 March 2026 the board paused ahead of the NCLT application, promising to complete its review inside the six-month exchange approval window.
points.quote: After due deliberation, the Board has decided to undertake a further review before proceeding with the filing of the application with the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

points.point: On 13 May 2026 the board formally dropped the transaction in its current form, tying any revival to both companies hitting FY28 guidance.
points.quote: The Board of Directors at their meeting held today deliberated the proposed transaction and in the best interest of all stakeholders decided to not pursue the transaction in the current form and revisit it following successful delivery of respective companies’ FY28 guidance.

points.point: Arun attributes the reversal to valuation pushback from a long tail of small shareholders, even though large investors were committed and a majority vote was achievable.
points.quote: Having said that, we had a long tail of smaller investors who believed that there would be concerns on the valuation.

points.point: He cites the listed Brooks price falling far below the intended ~INR2,200/share valuation, and sets explicit delivery conditions for revisiting: OneSource at US$400m/US$160m and the incoming assets at US$40m EBITDA.
points.quote: Having said that, and also because the pricing of both -- I mean, the pricing of the listed company significantly dropped from the intended valuation price of approximately INR2,200 -- a share, we decided that it's best that we defer this transaction until such time both OneSource delivers on its US$400 million 160 and the incoming assets deliver on its US$40 million of EBITDA.

points.point: The governance test applied to this related-party transaction was the group's customary 95%-plus shareholder support, which was not in evidence this time.
points.quote: We haven't had any significant RPT transactions which hasn't gone through with at least a 95% and above shareholders voting in favor of a scheme.

points.point: The deal is shelved for roughly two years, with both units to pursue growth separately in the meantime and OneSource refocused on its organic US$400m FY28 target.
points.quote: So, for now, this is on the back burner, and OneSource is very focused on building out its business to its US$400 million target which was guided for FY '28.

points.point: Arun notes the lost upside and keeps open other, non-Steriscience inorganic routes to beyond-FY28 growth.
points.quote: Of course, the Steriscience assets would have added to the whole story, but that's for another day.

points.point: The one completed internal consolidation: two wholly owned Singapore subsidiaries amalgamated effective 1 Jan 2026 purely to cut hierarchy and duplicate costs — no shareholding or consolidated-accounts impact.
points.quote: The Company proposed to consolidate Stelis with Onesource Specialty Pte. to simplify the existing corporate hierarchy to enhance operational efficiency and eliminate redundant administrative, compliance, and legal costs.

points.point: The only genuine divestment on record: Unit-3, the multimodal facility, sold to Syngene on a slump-sale basis and reported as discontinued operations.
points.quote: During the year ended March 31 2024, the Company entered into a Business Transfer Agreement with Syngene International Limited for sale of Unit-3 (multimodal facility) on a slump sale basis.

points.point: A live residual of the Strides separation: soft gel capacity sits with Strides under a limited-period transition agreement, forcing OneSource to build its own site.
points.quote: And that's why if you also know that we have a limited period agreement, transition agreement with Strides, and we would be expanding into our own site.

points.point: Neeraj explains how the separated soft gel business changes character outside Strides — from captive IP-led products to third-party CDMO services — with a greenfield now initiated.
points.quote: Having said that, you know that this business under Strides was primarily focused on captive IP-led products.

verdict.what_management_expects: For OneSource: accretive scale with no added debt (only ~2.5 crore new shares), FY28 outlook lifted from $400m/$160m to $500m+/$200m+, de-risked customer concentration, a global footprint, and Poland headroom for GLP drug-device lines. For the Steriscience assets: $100m revenue and $36–40m EBITDA in FY27, near debt-free. Post-deferral, both units pursue growth independently.
verdict.gaps: No separation rationale exists; calls never give Steriscience's valuation, swap ratio, fairness opinion, the dissenting investors' identity, or segment-wise margins for the businesses being combined.

verdict.segment_name: Steriscience Singapore (Steriscience Specialties / Steriscience Pte. Limited) and Brooks Steriscience Limited (BSL) — the Poland (Warsaw) and Vadodara specialty injectable assets; not a reportable segment in OneSource's accounts
verdict.unit: US$ million (only forward forecast figures shown; OneSource's own segment tables are in ₹ million)
verdict.measure_notes: No historical own financials for Steriscience/Brooks are carried on these pages. The only figures are FY27 forward forecasts in the Sep 2025 transaction presentation: Steriscience Singapore — Revenue $73m, EBITDA $29m, equity value $520m, 18.3x FY27 EV/EBITDA; Brooks Steriscience — Revenue $34m, EBITDA $10m, equity value $105m, 10.4x FY27 EV/EBITDA. These are projections, not reported results, so they are not placed in any fiscal-year row. OneSource's own segment reporting (standalone and consolidated, Ind AS 108) discloses a single reportable segment, CDMO, plus the divested Unit-3, with the profit line stated as 'Loss before tax' — these are the acquirer's figures, not the target's. Note also that the transaction was a proposed acquisition of Steriscience/Brooks by OneSource, not a spin-off, and the May 2026 presentation (page 20) states the Board decided not to pursue it in its current form, to be revisited after FY28.
verdict.not_found: All actual FY2024-FY2026 revenue, operating profit and PAT for Steriscience/Brooks. Pages carry only FY27 forecasts (Presentation Sep 2025 — page 7); segment tables cover only OneSource's CDMO segment.

verdict.rationale: Siemens Ltd. has separated two businesses, and the one management explained in the most detail is the Low Voltage Motors (LVM, plus geared motors and related customer service) business, sold as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to Innomotics India Private Limited for an enterprise value of INR 22 billion (INR 2,200 crore), cash-free/debt-free. The trigger was not Indian: on 1 October 2024 Siemens AG sold the global Innomotics business — and all of its intellectual property — to KPS Capital Partners, leaving the Indian unit as, in Sunil Mathur's words, a licensed sales organisation with no IP, no manufacturing (contract-manufactured to Innomotics design, ~97% of the Business's revenue) and survival dependent on an Agency & Distributorship Agreement and a Technical Cooperation & License Agreement with an entity now controlled by a private-equity owner. So the counterparty, not investors or lenders, effectively forced the decision: the Board stated the Business could not be sold to anyone else because Innomotics owns the IP, making the only alternatives selling to Innomotics India or restructuring the Business and bearing those costs. The numbers management cited were small and deteriorating: for the 12 months to 30 September 2025, revenue from operations of INR 9.67 billion (INR 967 crore) and profit from operations of INR 0.35 billion (INR 35 crore) — 6% of the company's revenue and ~2.2% of its profit from operations ex-Energy — with net capital employed of negative INR 1.38 billion, orders down 6.9% y/y in Q2 FY25, H1 EBITDA of 7.8% (down 130bps on lower price realisation and higher royalties paid to Innomotics), volumes that 'have not increased', cyclicality tied to private-sector capex and copper, and only 89 sales employees; the filing also recorded negative net worth of INR 1,175.66 million and 4.53% of revenue in FY24. Management said synergies with the rest of Siemens Ltd. were 'very limited' and framed the exit as portfolio optimisation that creates value and cash while giving customers and employees continuity. Price was set after negotiation using two independent valuations (Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP) as at 30 September 2025, and Mathur stressed INR 22 billion was 'the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company' despite volumes having since declined. The earlier, larger separation was the Energy demerger into Siemens Energy India Limited (appointed date 1 March 2025, effective 25 March 2025), justified as creating two independent pure-play companies focused on their relevant markets, each with a large backlog; it transferred net assets of INR 37,846 million including INR 25,478 million of cash, cost INR 1.0 billion of demerger expenses in FY25 versus INR 0.1 billion in FY24, and under the November 2023 disclosure the promoters agreed procedures to let Siemens Energy AG acquire a majority in the new listed entity.
verdict.evolution: Dec 2024 call (20 Dec 2024): only the Energy demerger is discussed as a separation — 'on track', creating two independent companies, with LVM not yet flagged as a portfolio issue. May 2025 call (20 May 2025): after the Siemens AG–KPS Innomotics deal of October 2024 and visible margin pressure from royalties paid to Innomotics, management formally said it would 'explore options for the future' of LVM. Dec 2025 (board 8 Dec 2025; analyst meet 12 Dec 2025): the option became a signed slump-sale agreement with Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, justified by lost IP, no local manufacturing, declining volumes (6% of revenue, 2% of profit) and shareholder interest, with closing guided to mid-2026. Jun 2026 call (28 May 2026) reconfirmed completion 'on track for June 2026'; the sale closed 1 June 2026 with a provisional gain of INR 20,990 million, while in the opposite direction the Board approved amalgamating subsidiary Siemens Rail Automation into the parent (26 May 2026) and took C&S Electric to 100% via capital reduction (NCLT order 24 September 2026).

points.point: CFO Wrumnig first links LVM's fate to the parent's global divestment of Innomotics to KPS Capital Partners and to the Indian unit's technical dependence on that business, announcing an options review.
points.quote: In view of this sale and the dependency on the global Innomotics business, we will now explore options for the future of the Low Voltage Motors business.

points.point: The economics were already visibly impaired: weak orders, price pressure and royalties payable to the new KPS-owned owner of the IP compressing margins.
points.quote: Year-to-date, the business reported an EbitDA margin of 7.8%, down by 130bps due to lower price realization and higher royalties paid to Innomotics, the former global Siemens business, now owned by KPS Capital Partners.

points.point: Mathur describes what Siemens Ltd. actually owned in LVM — a licence to sell someone else's product, with outsourced manufacturing and no IP rights in India.
points.quote: It is within Siemens Limited. It is outsourced manufacturing. Revenues are cyclical, as you know, for motors.

points.point: The volume thesis that justified keeping the business had failed, tied to muted private-sector capex and copper prices.
points.quote: The expectation was that the volumes will increase. Those volumes have not increased in the country.

points.point: Board approval of the slump sale to Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, explicitly the same price the parent had offered earlier, with closing guided to mid-2026.
points.quote: And this was then finally approved by the board of Siemens Limited in terms of a sale and transfer on a slump sale basis to Innomotics India at a purchase price of 22 billion, which I will remind you was the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company.

points.point: Materiality and shareholder-interest framing: the business had shrunk to 6% of volumes and 2% of profits.
points.quote: Considering the fact that the volumes have declined, in the meantime, it is only 6% of the overall volume of Siemens and only 2% of Siemens profits in the meantime.

points.point: The prior, bigger separation is presented as completed and successful — Energy is now a separately listed pure-play, leaving Siemens Ltd. with DI, SI and Mobility.
points.quote: A major development during this period has been the demerger of Siemens Energy India Limited, which is now a separately listed pure play energy company.

points.point: Rationale originally given for the Energy demerger: two focused, independently capitalised companies each with large backlogs.
points.quote: Both companies are very well prepared for the future growth, focusing on their relevant markets.

points.point: Final status update before closing; the quarter also shows demerger-related expenses falling by INR 500 million as separation costs roll off.
points.quote: And third, on the portfolio topic, the sale of the low-voltage motors business is on track for completion in June 2026.

points.point: Filing of 8 Dec 2025 states the hard constraint: without Innomotics/KPS support Siemens Ltd. cannot run the business, which is why the only buyer was the counterparty itself.
points.quote: The Company itself does not have the requisite intellectual property or other capabilities to service the Business without support from Innomotics GmbH which is now owned by KPS.

points.point: Strategic-fit argument plus the stated financial benefit of exiting — portfolio optimisation generating value and cash.
points.quote: Synergies between the Business and the rest of the Company’s businesses are very limited.

points.point: Price discovery and process: negotiated against two independent valuations as at 30 September 2025, outside any scheme of arrangement and not a related-party transaction.
points.quote: The consideration for the sale and transfer of the Business has been determined after negotiation between the Company and the Buyer, taking into account two separate independent valuation reports of the Business as at 30th September 2025 pursuant to independent valuation exercises conducted by each of Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and                 KPMG Valuation Services LLP .

points.point: Completion on 1 June 2026 at INR 22 billion enterprise value, booking a provisional one-time gain of INR 20,990 million (INR 2,099 crore) in discontinued operations.
points.quote: Basis the preliminary sale consideration, a provisional gain of Rs. 20,990 million is recognized during the quarter ended 30 June 2026 and six months period ended 30 September 2026.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Siemens Ltd.: a cleaner three-business technology portfolio (DI, SI, Mobility), removal of a sub-scale, negative-capital-employed, royalty-burdened unit worth 6% of revenue but only 2% of profit, INR 22 billion of cash plus an INR 2,099 crore gain, and portfolio optimisation 'creating value and cash'. For Innomotics India: ownership aligned with the IP it already holds, continuity for LVM customers and the 89 sales staff. For Energy: an independent pure-play.
verdict.gaps: No post-sale margin, ROCE or capital-deployment guidance; no bridge from the 2024 parent offer to INR 22 billion; silent on employee transfer terms, ADA/TCLA wind-down, and buyer-selection alternatives.

verdict.segment_name: Energy (reported as the "Energy" segment / Energy Division of Siemens Limited; demerged into Siemens Energy India Limited (SEIL) w.e.f. 1 March 2025, shown as Discontinued Operations in the Annual Report 2026)
verdict.measure_notes: Revenue = External revenue from segment note 46(i) (standalone); total revenue incl. inter-segmental revenue shown separately in the documents (FY ended 30 Sept 2024: external 63,179 + inter-segment 273 = 63,452). Operating_profit = segment 'Results' i.e. profit from operations (after depreciation/amortisation, before finance costs, interest income, other income and tax); it is NOT EBITDA. verdict.rationale: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the reasoning below is reconstructed only from the filings. The separation is the demerger of Valor Estate Ltd's (formerly D B Realty Ltd) hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement that also amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor; the Explanatory Statement to the 12th December 2025 EGM says the Scheme was entered into 'mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.' NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 12 June 2025, it became effective 1 July 2025 (demerger appointed date 1 April 2025; Esteem amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2024), and shareholders on the 18 July 2025 record date received 1 AHIL share of Rs. 10 for every 10 Valor shares. The carve-out moved consolidated net assets of Rs. 1,02,194.65 lakhs (standalone Rs. 1,01,512.91 lakhs) out of Valor — Rs. 1,49,386.00 lakhs of property, plant and equipment, Rs. 54,858.00 lakhs of goodwill, Rs. 29,117.12 lakhs of intangibles, against Rs. 46,196.17 lakhs non-current and Rs. 16,028.03 lakhs current borrowings, Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs of other non-current financial liabilities and Rs. 28,951.71 lakhs of deferred tax liability — and took out a business that had FY25 revenue of Rs. 36,650.21 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 4,468.06 lakhs, now shown as discontinued operations. Management's stated problems solved are focus and structure: Valor 'is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment,' so segment reporting ceased, while Advent gets 'its own Board and Management team,' NSE/BSE listing on 13 November 2025 for 'enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure,' and an asset-heavy growth path (five projects, 3,100 keys, EBITDA from under Rs. 200 crore to over Rs. 1,200 crore by FY32, targeted mid-teens compounded ROE) that a combined entity would have had to fund alongside real estate. The second, smaller separation/consolidation strand is non-core cleanup: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy Private Limited (dairy farming, milk procurement and trading), taken to 76.63% via enforcement of security and then to 100% 'as the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets,' sold its entire dairy business under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees booked as an exceptional item, is now 'evaluating opportunities to engage in the business of real estate development,' and was amalgamated into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited for structural simplification, synergies, avoidance of duplication and lower compliance and overhead costs. Running alongside is balance-sheet repair the filings tie to the same strategy: consolidated secured debt down to Rs. 730 crore, full redemption of Rs. 235 crore of NCDs out of the Rs. 262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance, and the Scheme-driven reduction and consolidation of the 8% RPS (Clause 32: Rs. 10 face value cut to Rs. 9, then 10 consolidated into 9) plus Clause 20's 1:10 allotment of AHIL preference shares, followed by the November 2025 proposal to convert KRPL's 6,45,75,000 RPS into 0.0001% CCPS converting into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 'with a view to conserve the financial resources of the Company.' No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having demanded the separation; the only named partner is Prestige Group, which sits on Advent's side as a 50:50 JV partner in the Sahar project and co-developer at Aerocity.
verdict.evolution: There are no transcripts on file, so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the paper trail runs through filings and the Scheme itself. The Composite Scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 12 June 2025, became effective 1 July 2025 with demerger appointed date 1 April 2025, and the 1:10 entitlement was fixed on the 18 July 2025 record date; the SADPL-into-HVPL amalgamation was approved by both boards on 18 August 2025 with appointed date 1 April 2025. The plan then became visible in public filings in quick succession: Advent's listing press release (12 November 2025), Valor's Q2FY26 results and press release (14-15 November 2025) which first framed the demerger as completed and as the basis for debt reduction, the EGM notice and corrigendum (20 November and 8 December 2025) which disclosed the Scheme's preference-share reduction, consolidation and 1:10 AHIL allotment and layered the RPS-to-CCPS conversion on top, and finally the NCLT order of 29 January 2026 and effective date of 12 March 2026 completing the SADPL consolidation. The shape of the plan therefore widened over time from a single hospitality demerger into a package: demerger plus listing, plus non-core dairy liquidation and merger, plus capital-structure conversion.

points.point: The Composite Scheme's stated purpose, as put to shareholders in the EGM explanatory statement, was to demerge the hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited and unlock shareholder value; it simultaneously amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor.

verdict.rationale: Read strictly against these texts, DLF is not separating a business in the demerger/spin-off sense: there is no scheme of arrangement for a spin-off in the filings, and the statutory notes repeat that 'The Company's business activities which are primarily real estate development and related activities falls within a single reportable segment.' What the record does contain is three distinct, narrower 'separations'. First, a presentational/managerial separation: from the 21 March 2025 Analyst Day onward management stopped describing itself as DLF-vs-DCCDL and instead reports two businesses — DevCo (development, ~INR 20,000 crore of annual presales, ~45% target gross margin, ~INR 9,000-10,000 crore of annual embedded margin, ~INR 7,000-8,000 crore of annual free cash, now zero gross debt) and RentCo/Annuity (49-50 mn sq ft operating, 95-96% occupancy, FY26 rental ~INR 6,400 crore going to ~INR 7,400-8,200 crore in FY27 and ~INR 10,000 crore by FY30, INR 20,000 crore of RentCo capex, net debt/EBITDA ~3.1-3.6x), explicitly because the accounting entities do not match how capital is allocated between a cash-generating development arm and a capex-hungry annuity arm; Rajiv Singh called them 'two strong independent businesses, both complementing each other' and 'two sides of the same coin', with DevCo cash funding RentCo capex and RentCo cash later funding development. Second, an actual legal separation of one asset: the Kolkata IT/ITeS SEZ undertaking (DLF TechPark II, ~10,54,357 sq ft GLA on ~8.15 acres) sold as a slump sale to Makalu Builders LLP/Srijan Realty for ~INR 409.86 crore, plus ~17.75 acres of adjacent vacant land to Gangapurna Projects LLP for ~INR 260 crore — aggregate ~INR 710.23 crore, completed 30 March 2026; the stated reason is only 'business strategy to enhance shareholders' value', with the sold business contributing FY25 turnover of ~INR 66.88 crore (INR 41.74 crore rent + INR 25.14 crore maintenance), ~1.49% of company turnover, and the filing stresses it does not even meet the 'Undertaking' threshold under Section 180(1)(a)/Reg 37A. The operating logic management gave for exiting SEZ is that 'SEZ is not something which is growing. It is showing a decline in trend' — ~10% SEZ vacancy (Hyderabad 17-20%), ~4 mn of 16-17 mn sq ft already converted to non-processing or de-notified, and the SEZ/non-SEZ rent gap in Cyber City narrowed only to 10-12%; the problem the sale solved was a slow multi-layer approval chain (Development Commissioner, state government, Board of Approvals, then de-notification), partly compensated by ~INR 2.5 crore a month accruing to the sale consideration plus rent until closing. Third, a DCCDL monetisation that has repeatedly been deferred rather than pursued: it is partner-led, not DLF-led — 'the timing and the form would largely be driven by what our partners want' — GIC has signalled no exit ('the answer is a very straight no'), REITs are rejected for now because DCCDL is only ~33% mature versus the 80-90% mature portfolio a REIT effectively requires and growth would mean repeatedly returning to unit-holders for capital. Notably, the only completed corporate actions point the other way — towards consolidation: NCLT approved 16 wholly-owned subsidiaries (including DLF Universal Limited) merging into DLF Limited on 14 January 2026, two (Bhamini Real Estate Developers and DLF Urban) into DLF Home Developers on 13 February 2026, and eight into Highvista Buildcon on 18 February 2026.
verdict.evolution: At the 21 March 2025 Analyst Day DLF first recast its disclosure into DevCo and RentCo ('that is not the way we actually run the business'), and in the same session ruled out a near-term DCCDL REIT and any GIC buyout; the 20 May 2025 call repeated the DevCo/RentCo framing and asked analysts to track RentCo separately, while 5 August 2025 added that SEZ space (13% vacant) was being converted to non-processing areas. The Kolkata exit then moved from intent to execution: 31 October 2025 flagged the slow SEZ/state/Board-of-Approvals chain and ~3.5 months to monetisation with ~INR 2.5 crore a month of delay compensation, and also restated that Cyber City monetisation 'would largely be driven by what our partners want' with nothing serious for ~three years; 23 January 2026 reported the DCCDL-held Kolkata asset closed in December 2025 and first-stage Board of Approvals clearance for the DLF-held SEZ. Definitive BTA/ATS were signed 3 February 2026 (INR 409.86 crore + INR 260 crore) and completed 30 March 2026 for ~INR 710.23 crore; the 14 May 2026 call framed SEZ as a structurally declining concept and otherwise spoke of DevCo and RentCo as two growth engines, not as entities to be split.

points.point: Management explicitly replaced the legal-entity view (DLF vs DCCDL) with a business view (DevCo vs Annuity/RentCo) because the statutory structure does not reflect how the business is actually run; Badal called it a management estimate, not an accounting representation.
points.quote: But that is not the way we actually run the business. The business is run really as DevCo and Annuity business.

points.point: Rajiv Singh framed the two arms as independent but mutually funding — DevCo cash pays for RentCo capex and RentCo cash later funds development — which is the stated reason for presenting them apart rather than splitting them.
points.quote: it's two strong independent businesses, both complementing each other, both having their own needs, but fortunately both being contributive.

points.point: A DCCDL REIT (the most-asked separation route) was ruled out for the short term, with the reason given that a REIT must return to unit-holders for capital every time it grows, and that DCCDL is only ~33% mature versus the 80-90% mature portfolio REIT structures effectively require.
points.quote: We cannot rule out anything, but definitely for sure in the short run it is not part of our agenda, number one.

points.point: Investors, not management, pushed the separate-entity question — Puneet Gulati asked which of the two businesses earns better returns on capital and time and how capital is split between them; Rajiv Singh declined to rank them.
points.quote: And between the two, which one do you think gives you better return on your capital and time and how do you allocate capital between the two?

points.point: DLF kept the DevCo/RentCo split in its reporting and asked analysts to value RentCo on its own — DCCDL plus DLF's own rental assets plus Atrium Place — even though statutory disclosure remains DLF Limited and DCCDL.
points.quote: In the spirit of what we had done in the analyst call, we continue to present the overall progress around the DevCo and the RentCo verticals.

points.point: The SEZ problem that eventually drove the Kolkata exit was laid out: ~13% SEZ vacancy, government-mandated conversion to non-processing areas, and an approval chain from unit area commissioner up to the Board of Approvals and Ministry of Commerce taking 4-5 months.
points.quote: The process itself with the government, where you have to get the approval from the unit area commissioner going right up to the Board of approvals and Ministry of Commerce is a 4 to 5 months affair.

points.point: Khattar explained why the Kolkata IT SEZ divestment was slow — it needs SEZ approval, state government approval, Board of Approvals sanction and then de-notification — and said DLF was ~3.5 months from monetisation, with ~INR 2.5 crore per month of delay compensation plus rent accruing to the sale consideration.
points.quote: But since it is an SEZ and there is a land parcel as part of the integrated sale, the approval process is rather slow because it not only makes the SEZ approval, but the state government approval also.

points.point: Any separation/monetisation of the Cyber City (DCCDL) annuity platform was described as partner-driven, with nothing serious contemplated for about three years and GIC showing no intent to exit.
points.quote: So, in all fairness, as we have said earlier also, that for us, the entire strategy of cyber city monetization, the timing and the form would largely be driven by what our partners want.

points.point: Asked directly whether GIC wants out of DCCDL, Khattar denied any exit signal and said GIC is instead looking to invest more — removing the most commonly assumed trigger for a DCCDL carve-out or listing.
points.quote: So the answer is a very straight no.

points.point: Two Kolkata exits were sequenced: the DCCDL-held Kolkata asset closed in December 2025, while the DLF-held Kolkata SEZ had only first-stage Board of Approvals clearance and awaited state approvals, with rent continuing to accrue to DLF until final payment.
points.quote: Kolkata SEZ, which is in the books of DLF, we have got the first stage approval from the Board of Approvals.

points.point: The structural case for exiting SEZ assets was stated plainly: SEZ is a shrinking format, with ~4 of 16-17 mn sq ft already converted to non-processing/de-notified space, ~10% overall SEZ vacancy and Hyderabad at 17-20%.
points.quote: So, as a concept, SEZ is not something which is growing. It is showing a decline in trend.

points.point: The two arms remain financially interlocked rather than separable: about two-thirds of DLF's INR 8 per share dividend is funded by Cyber City's dividend upstream to DLF, with DCCDL debt/NOI below 3.5x.
points.quote: A large chunk of this dividend is driven by Cyber City's dividend to us, frankly.

points.point: The 3 February 2026 filing is the only business-separation document in the record: a slump-sale BTA for the Kolkata IT/ITeS SEZ undertaking (DLF TechPark II, ~10,54,357 sq ft GLA on ~8.15 acres) for ~INR 409.86 crore to Makalu Builders LLP/Srijan Realty, plus an ATS for ~17.75 acres of vacant Kolkata land for ~INR 260 crore to Gangapurna Projects LLP.
points.quote: The proposed sale is being undertaken as part of the Company's business strategy to enhance shareholders' value.

points.point: The disposal was deliberately framed as immaterial: FY25 turnover of the sold Kolkata SEZ business was ~INR 66.88 crore (INR 41.74 crore gross rent plus INR 25.14 crore maintenance and other income), about 1.49% of company turnover, and it falls below the 'Undertaking' threshold under Section 180(1)(a) and Regulation 37A.
points.quote: The turnover of Kolkata IT/ITeS SEZ Business proposed to be sold for FY 2024-25 was ~Rs. 66.88 crore (comprising of Gross rental of Rs. 41.74 crore and Maintenance & other income of Rs. 25.14 crore) i.e. ~1.49% of turnover of the Company.

points.point: The Kolkata transactions closed on 30 March 2026 for an aggregate ~INR 710.23 crore after conditions precedent and regulatory approvals; buyers are Srijan Group entities and not related parties.
points.quote: The aggregate consideration for the aforesaid transactions is ~Rs. 710.23 crore (Rupees Seven Hundred Ten Crore and Twenty Three Lakhs only).

points.point: Every approved scheme of arrangement in the record moves towards consolidation, not separation: NCLT approved 16 wholly-owned subsidiaries (including DLF Universal Limited) merging into DLF Limited on 14 January 2026, two into DLF Home Developers on 13 February 2026 (which adjusted tax expense), and eight into Highvista Buildcon on 18 February 2026.
points.quote: has approved the Scheme of Amalgamation involving merger of 16 (sixteen) wholly-owned Subsidiary Company(ies)

verdict.what_management_expects: Not stated as a separation outcome. For DevCo: ~45% gross margin, INR 9,000-10,000 crore annual embedded margin, INR 7,000-8,000 crore free cash, zero gross debt, 50% PAT payout. For RentCo: mid-teens NOI growth to ~INR 10,000 crore rentals by FY30 on INR 20,000 crore capex, net debt/EBITDA ~3x. Kolkata exit: only 'enhance shareholders' value' and INR 710.23 crore cash.
verdict.gaps: No spin-off rationale, scheme, entity, ratio, timeline or listing is discussed; no explanation of Kolkata sale pricing, gain, or valuation uplift expected from separate reporting.

verdict.segment_name: Kolkata SEZ Business — IT/ITeS SEZ (freehold land ~25.90 acres with building 'DLF Tech Park', Kolkata), sold on slump-sale basis
verdict.measure_notes: No profit or revenue line exists for this undertaking on the tagged pages. Both DLF's standalone and consolidated accounts report a single reportable segment ('colonization and real estate business' / 'real estate development') under Ind AS 108, so no segment revenue, segment result, EBIT/EBITDA or PBT is disclosed for the Kolkata SEZ business. The undertaking appears only as an Ind AS 105 'held for sale' disposal group (balance-sheet carrying amounts) in FY2025, and in FY2026 as a completed slump sale: total consideration ₹71,022.80 lakhs with a gain of ₹35,255.52 lakhs recorded (Annual Report 2026 — page 170 standalone and page 236 consolidated). Disposal-group assets at 31 March 2025 were ₹30,852.72 lakhs (investment property ₹30,518.22 lakhs net of accumulated depreciation ₹9,107.77 lakhs, trade receivables ₹302.18 lakhs, other assets ₹32.32 lakhs) against liabilities of ₹2,997.08 lakhs (trade payables ₹43.76 lakhs, other financial liabilities ₹2,953.32 lakhs); ₹6,000.00 lakhs earnest money was received in FY2025. Quarterly presentations mention the asset only as ~1 msf of Kolkata SEZ excluded from the operational rental portfolio because it is contracted to be transferred (Presentation Aug 2025 — pages 20 and 22; Presentation Nov 2025 — pages 20 and 22; Presentation Jan 2026 — pages 20 and 24), and note that DCCDL's FY25 PAT includes a one-time gain on sale of the Kolkata asset (Presentation Aug 2025 — page 31) — a DCCDL-level figure, not a figure for this undertaking.
