verdict.rationale: The separation is a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232, approved by the boards of Meesho Limited, Meesho Grocery Private Limited (MGPL), Meesho Technologies Private Limited (MTPL) and Meesho Inc. (the erstwhile US holding company), filed with NCLT Bengaluru on April 25, 2024, sanctioned by NCLT on May 27, 2025 and given effect from June 1, 2025: the Grocery undertaking went to MGPL, the Marketplace (e-commerce) undertaking went to MTPL, and Meesho Inc. was amalgamated into Meesho Limited by pooling-of-interests, i.e. the US-to-India 'reverse flip' that made an Indian listing possible — the IPO followed on December 10, 2025 (fresh issue Rs 42,500 million plus Rs 11,712.04 million offer for sale at Rs 111/share). Mechanically, net assets of only Rs 1,147.24 million (MTPL Rs 586.83m, MGPL Rs 560.41m) moved out against consideration of Rs 265,937.44 million in equity and CCPS (MTPL Rs 258,623.89m, MGPL Rs 7,313.55m), producing an exceptional 'gain on demerger' of Rs 264,790.20 million in the standalone accounts, plus Rs 7,607.24 million of interest income on the CCPS — with no consolidated effect, and the flip itself cost real cash: Rs 24,868.42 million of 'tax payable on account of business combination' (GILTI, business combination and passive income) in FY25 and a further Rs 698.26 million in FY26, Rs 7,338.16 million of perquisite tax, Rs 4,824.80 million of incremental ESOP charge on plan modification, Rs 620.55 million of accelerated vesting charge and Rs 1,410.91 million of business-combination expenses. The effect is that the listed parent kept only the Valmo logistics channel, and from June 1, 2025 'generated revenue from providing logistics services through its delivery channel - Valmo - exclusively to MTPL', while the marketplace, grocery, payments (MPPL, a Lending Service Provider) and new initiatives sit in separate wholly owned subsidiaries, and IPO proceeds are pushed down by rights issue (Rs 28,900 million into MTPL on December 10, 2025; Rs 75 crore into MGPL in July/August 2026; Rs 100 crore in May 2026 and up to Rs 400 crore in October/November 2026 into MPPL). A second, narrower separation followed: the board on March 31, 2026 approved an internal reorganisation moving functions, employees and contracts into Valmo Transportation Private Limited (VTPL, incorporated January 28, 2026), stated reasons being 'to enhance administrative efficiency, enable functional specialization, and allow more focused management of the logistics business' — with mid-mile and last-mile in VTPL (which holds a Goods and Transport Agency licence under GST), while first-mile and sort-centre operations stay in Meesho Limited and the parent now bills sellers directly. Management's own framing on the calls is transparency and tax/GST classification rather than value unlocking: Dhiresh Bansal said in January 2026 the logistics subsidiary was set up 'primarily to explore how should we kind of structure the Valmo financials, so that they are more clearly visible for people to understand. There is no plan of opening this up to other third parties', and in July 2026 that consolidated numbers do not change materially, only standalone flows between Meesho Limited, MTPL and VTPL. The problems the structure is said to solve are therefore: an offshore holdco incompatible with an Indian IPO, a logistics business whose economics (a fulfilment spread management keeps at roughly 2%-2.5% of NMV, with 145 bps of one-time FY26 disruption cost and contribution margin recovering from 2.3% in Q3 FY26 to a ~4% Q4 exit) were invisible inside a blended marketplace P&L, a grocery/perishables supply chain Vidit Aatrey says needs 'a fundamentally different logistics network' from Valmo's national network, and loss-making adjacencies (new initiatives capped at about Rs 200 crore annual EBITDA burn; Rs 39 crore loss in Q1 FY27) ring-fenced from the core. No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; a proxy advisory firm did question the VTPL/GTA model to SEBI, and management replied it had law-firm and accounting opinions, that no tax or regulatory authority had queried it, and that it had received no communication from SEBI.
verdict.evolution: The Scheme predates the calls (NCLT filing April 25, 2024; order May 27, 2025; effective June 1, 2025) and surfaced publicly only in the first post-listing call on January 30, 2026 (Feb 2026 transcript), where Sachin Salgaonkar asked about 'a new subsidiary on logistics' and Dhiresh Bansal said it existed to structure Valmo's financials for visibility, with no intent to open the network to third parties. By the March 31, 2026 board meeting the plan had hardened into an executed internal reorganisation into VTPL, which the May 6, 2026 call never addressed — that call instead split economics into ads margin versus fulfilment margin and talked about restoring the fulfilment spread after the 145 bps one-time hit. On the July 23, 2026 call the structure was explained in operating detail for the first time: VTPL houses mid-mile and last-mile under a GTA licence, first-mile and sort centres stay in Meesho Limited, VTPL's annual financials will not be a clean read of Valmo volumes, and a proxy advisory firm's GST question had gone to SEBI. Separation then continued by filing rather than by call — Kirana Club/Retail Pulse Labs bought for Rs 2,020.85 million (SPA June 12, 2026) and a new wholly owned lending subsidiary approved on October 28, 2026.

points.point: The Composite Scheme has three legs: grocery to MGPL, marketplace to MTPL, and amalgamation of the US holding company Meesho Inc. into Meesho Limited — the reverse flip that enabled the Indian IPO.

points.point: Net assets of only Rs 1,147.24 million left the parent against Rs 265,937.44 million of equity and CCPS consideration, creating a Rs 264,790.20 million exceptional standalone gain with no consolidated effect.
points.quote: The surplus/deficit which had arisen after taking effect of consideration over the carrying value of net assets of MTPL and MGPL was recognised as an "exceptional item" in the standalone financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 and the year ended March 31, 2026 respectively.

points.point: Post-demerger the listed parent is effectively the Valmo logistics entity, selling delivery services exclusively to the marketplace subsidiary MTPL.
points.quote: Consequently, from June 01, 2025, the Company generated revenue from providing logistics services through its delivery channel -Valmo -exclusively to MTPL.

points.point: The March 31, 2026 board approved a second, logistics-only reorganisation into VTPL for administrative efficiency, functional specialisation and focused management; it makes standalone Q1 FY27 non-comparable.
points.quote: Pursuant to this reorganization, the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively, the "Group") are reorganising the logistics business across different Group entities to enhance administrative efficiency, enable functional specialization, and allow more focused management of the logistics business.

points.point: The flip carried a large cash tax and compensation cost: Rs 24,868.42 million of business-combination tax in FY25 plus Rs 698.26 million in FY26, Rs 7,338.16 million perquisite tax, and Rs 5,445.35 million of ESOP modification/acceleration charges.
points.quote: During the year ended March 31, 2025, the Company had provided for taxes towards Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income, business combination and passive income collectively referred to as "Tax payable on account of business combination" arising on account of the aforesaid business combination.

points.quote: This investment is a part of utilization of the proceeds as specified in Prospectus dated December 05, 2025.

points.quote: Line of Business: Local logistics network for daily essentials and groceries.

points.quote: The incorporation of Wholly Owned Subsidiary will enable the group to build in-house underwriting, control product design, directly own borrower relationships, and capture full lending margins while gaining access to institutional funding.

points.point: Management's stated reason for the logistics subsidiary was investor visibility into Valmo's financials, explicitly not opening the network to third-party shippers.
points.quote: I think we are setting up that subsidiary primarily to explore how should we kind of structure the Valmo financials, so that they are more clearly visible for people to understand.

points.point: Logistics is run as a separate economic unit with a deliberately capped spread, with all further efficiency passed back, so margin growth must come from ads and other services.
points.quote: we keep the logistics margin in a certain trajectory, which is about 2% - 2.5% of NMB from a contribution perspective.

points.point: By contrast, Meesho Mall was explicitly kept inside the marketplace rather than carved out, so the separation lines are entity/function-based, not product-based.
points.quote: So, Meesho Mall is part of the core marketplace , all of the numbers are captured within the marketplace financials.

points.point: The asset-light philosophy explains why logistics can be housed in a thin aggregator entity: investment goes into technology, not warehouses or fleet capex.
points.quote: So, even today in Valmo, the entire software stack end -to-end is our own.

points.point: Management framed consolidated margin as two separable pools — ads margin and fulfilment margin — mirroring the marketplace/logistics entity split, with the FY26 one-time logistics disruption (145 bps) behind them and a 4% Q4 exit as the new base.
points.quote: So I think when you look at contribution margin, specifically we kind of look at this as a split between two components which is the ads related sort of margin as well as what we kind of have on the fulfilment side.

points.point: Valmo's share is not a strategic target but a cost outcome, which is why the logistics entity is kept flexible against 3PLs rather than built up to a fixed in-sourcing goal.
points.quote: At this point in time at 50% we were the most or at around that mark, we were the most optimized in terms of cost structure.

points.point: VTPL now houses mid-mile and last-mile under a Goods and Transport Agency classification under GST law, while first-mile and sort centres stay in Meesho Limited; consolidated results are unaffected and only standalone inter-entity flows move.
points.quote: So Valmo Transportation Private Limited or VTPL is the entity under which the middle -mile and last -mile operations are now housed under.

points.point: Because the split is partial, VTPL's standalone financials will not be a clean proxy for Valmo volumes, and management has not committed to further disclosure.
points.quote: First-mile operations as well as sort center operations in relation to Valmo will continue to remain as part of Meesho Limited.

points.point: A proxy advisory firm questioned the GTA structure with SEBI; management says the model follows industry precedent, is backed by law-firm and accounting opinions, and that no authority has queried it.
points.quote: Just to clarify, there has been no question asked by any regulatory authority or tax authority to us on this matter.

points.point: Grocery/perishables are kept in a separate entity and network because the national Valmo network cannot serve them; this is still pre-product-market-fit and funded inside the new-initiatives cap (about Rs 200 crore EBITDA a year; Rs 39 crore loss in Q1 FY27).
points.quote: But we've realized over time there's certain categories, especially perishable categories or fast -moving consumer goods, they require a fundamentally different logistics network to be viable on Meesho.

points.point: The AoA amendment put to the first AGM formalises post-IPO board rights: founder nomination at 3% or 75,62,14,937 shares, one seat each for the two largest investors at 8% fully diluted, with the old lender nomination right retained.
points.quote: On the Articles of Association, there are standard amendments for nominee investors, their sort of Director position as well as Founder positions, which are typical of post -IPO sort of that one seeks at the Annual General Meeting.

verdict.what_management_expects: Clearer, separately visible Valmo logistics financials; administrative efficiency, functional specialisation and focused management of logistics; an India-domiciled listed parent able to IPO and push IPO cash into each subsidiary; ring-fenced grocery, payments and new-initiative losses under a ~Rs 200 crore cap; fulfilment spread held at 2%-2.5% of NMV with margin growth from ads; in-house lending capturing full margins.
verdict.gaps: No valuation basis for the Rs 265,937m CCPS consideration, no Valmo standalone P&L or disclosure timetable, no GST-saving quantum, no value-unlock or future listing rationale.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain or explain any separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement by Minda Corporation — no scheme document is present, no call in the last 36 months mentions one, and no filing references Regulation 37/Section 230-232, a record date, a share-entitlement ratio or a resulting-company listing. The one filing item in the set that moves a business out of the group is the Board approval of September 24, 2026 to sell the investment held in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited, a step-down associate in which the wholly owned subsidiary Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited holds a 29.5% equity stake; the filing explicitly states the transaction is not a related-party transaction, is not a slump sale and is 'Not Applicable' under Regulation 37A, i.e. outside any Scheme of Arrangement. The only quantification given for it is immaterial: the FY2025-26 consolidated share of profit from that entity was Rs. 3,95,197, and on the May 22, 2026 call management said of associate contributions that 'EVQ did not contribute' (versus Flash ~INR 70 crore, Furukawa ~INR 8 crore, Minda VAST ~INR 5 crore). The filing gives no rationale, no buyer, no consideration ('shall be intimated at the time of execution') and no expected date. Everything management actually explained over these three years runs in the opposite direction — consolidation and bolt-ons, not separation: acquiring 49% of Flash Electronics for INR 1,372 crore cash at a INR 3,100 crore valuation (Jan 2025), consolidating associate Minda VAST (c. INR 500 crore revenue, ~7% EBITDA, >90% PV) into Minda Corporation from FY27 after a shareholder-agreement change, JVs with Toyodenso (60:40, ~INR 150 crore, switches), HCMF (50:50, sunroof/power tailgate) and Turntide (axial-flux motors, controllers), a new wholly owned subsidiary in China (up to USD 1 million), rights-issue infusions into Spark Minda Green Mobility (INR 25 crore, July 2026) and Spark Minda-Toyodenso (INR 18 crore, October 2026), and up to INR 500 crore of NCDs for 'various funding requirements'. No investor, lender or JV partner is recorded in these texts as asking for a separation; the only partner-driven structural change cited is the Minda VAST shareholder-agreement change, which pulls a business in rather than pushing one out. On this evidence the premise of a separation cannot be supported from these documents alone.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea surfaces in any of the eight calls (Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026); the recurring structural theme is inorganic addition — HCMF JV (Aug 2024), Sanco TLA (Nov 2024), Flash 49% completed (Feb 2025), Toyodenso JV (Aug 2025), sunroof order and Vision 2030 (Nov 2025), Turntide JV and Minda VAST consolidation (May 2026). The single divestment appears only in filings, with the Board approval dated September 24, 2026 to sell the EVQ Point Solutions stake held via Spark Minda Green Mobility, after which the October 5, 2026 filing shows further capital still going into subsidiaries. Between those, the July 20, 2026 filing records a further INR 25 crore rights-issue subscription into the same wholly owned subsidiary that holds the EVQ stake, so the exit is not framed as part of any wider restructuring.

points.point: The only out-of-group transaction in the set is the September 24, 2026 Board approval to sell the EVQ Point Solutions stake held through wholly owned subsidiary Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems; no rationale, buyer or consideration is disclosed.
points.quote: The Board has approved the sale of investment held in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited through Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited (Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company).

verdict.rationale: The texts describe the opposite of a separation: Orient Cement is not carving out or demerging anything — it is being extinguished into its own parent. Ambuja Cements, which already holds 72.66% of Orient's paid-up equity (14,92,92,730 of 20,54,59,873 shares) after acquiring control effective 22 April 2025 for roughly INR5,910 crore, had its board approve on 22 December 2025 a Sections 230–232 amalgamation of Orient (FY25 standalone revenue INR2,708.83 crore, net worth INR1,807.91 crore) into Ambuja (FY25 standalone revenue INR19,453.58 crore, net worth INR48,605.65 crore; consolidated INR35,044.76 crore and INR63,811.42 crore), with no cash and a swap of 33 Ambuja shares of Rs 2 for every 100 Orient shares of Re 1 — about 1,85,35,158 new shares, taking Ambuja's public float from 32.30% to 32.80% and promoter from 67.65% to 67.15%. The scheme's stated reasons are that both companies are in the same line of business (Orient's capacity concentrated in West and South India), so Ambuja should 'assume complete ownership and direction' for long-term strategic alignment, 'reduc[e] multiple entities in the same line of business', unify manufacturing and commercial functions, speed up decision-making and production execution, and pool financial, operational and logistical resources for economies of scale and efficient capital deployment. On the calls, management branded it the 'One Cement Platform', promising accelerated growth, EBITDA expansion, better logistics density, higher capital efficiency and a 'higher degree of compliances', with value creation over 24–36 months. The concrete problem it solves is the artificial plumbing already in place: Orient's own brand and direct sales had been migrated into Ambuja and ACC under Master Supply Agreements, so Orient had no standalone commercial identity, intercompany MSA receivables pushed ACC's operating cash flow negative (requiring a shareholder-approved ICD to knock them off), coal sales had to be grossed up at ACC and eliminated at consol, and standalone EBITDA/ton (Ambuja INR708, ACC ~INR900) diverged from consol INR1,060 purely because of intercompany eliminations. Nobody in the texts — no investor, lender or partner — is recorded asking for the merger; analysts only asked about the resulting accounting distortions and entity-wise reporting, and the approval was management-driven, with the promoter voting 100% of its 72.66% in favour. The reconstructed 'why', then, is tidying a controlled, already-integrated subsidiary out of existence — and, read as a special situation, the trade is the fixed 33:100 share-exchange into Ambuja plus delisting, not any value release from a separated business.
verdict.evolution: Nov 2023 and Aug 2024 calls are pre-Adani Orient under Desh Deepak Khetrapal: no merger talk at all, only a stalled standalone INR2,000 crore Chittapur/Devapur/Sarni expansion held up by environment and forest clearances, 15% volume degrowth and visible pricing pressure from the consolidating majors. By the 31 July 2025 (Aug 2025) call Orient had already been acquired (effective 22 April 2025) and its brand and direct sales folded into Ambuja/ACC under MSAs, and by the 3 November 2025 call management called Penna/Orient integration 'the fastest'; Orient capex was deprioritised in favour of efficiency. The legal merger surfaced on the 30 January 2026 (Feb 2026) call — weeks after the 22 December 2025 board approval — as 'our defining development this quarter', recast as the One Cement Platform. By the 4 May 2026 call Sanghi and Penna were completed while 'ACC and Orient Cement is under process', purchase price allocation for Orient was finalised, and the plan then cleared BSE/NSE on 4 June 2026, the NCLT order on 20 July 2026, and shareholder approval on 28 September 2026 (97.83% of votes polled, but only 64.19% of institutional public votes).

points.quote: In terms of the ACC Ambuja, if you see ACC has receivable from Ambuja under the MSA.

points.point: Orient's commercial identity was gone long before the legal merger: its sales ran under the Ambuja and ACC brands from within days of acquisition, which management credited with sharply improving its profitability.
points.quote: Integration of Penna and Orient Cement has been of the fastest, I would say, wherein the entire sales, except the initial few days for Orient, otherwise, the entire sales has been under the Ambuja and ACC brands.

points.point: Orient's own growth plans were explicitly shelved in favour of cost and debottlenecking; the Chittapur, Devapur and MP projects it had carried as a standalone were pushed out, with any Orient-specific plan promised 'separately'.
points.quote: So far as the second question, which is about the CapEx at Orient, I think right now our priority is to improve the overall efficiency at Orient then immediate expansion.

points.point: Orient standalone could not execute its INR1,950-2,000 crore Chittapur/Devapur/Sarni programme because clearances kept slipping — the growth paralysis that later made absorption into a larger balance sheet the path of least resistance.

verdict.rationale: Management presented the separation as a three-way demerger of the old conglomerate Quess Corp — effective 1 April 2024 and legally completed during FY25 "well ahead of stated timeline" — into three separately listed companies: Quess Corp (pure-play workforce/staffing: General Staffing, Professional Staffing/IT staffing, Overseas staffing, digital platforms Hamara Jobs/Taskmo), Digitide Solutions (Global Technology Solutions — BPM, customer lifecycle management, platform/payroll/InsurTech, plus foundit and the Brainhunter US/Canada business), and Bluspring Enterprises (Operating Asset Maintenance — IFM, food & beverage incl. the acquired Archer business, security, and Vedang telecom infra, plus the Golden Star facility-management contracts). The stated reasons were a sharper strategic identity and unlocking shareholder value: four unlike platforms sitting in one listed entity were split so each would have "its own focus and its own management", be "agile, strategically focused" with their own boards and leadership teams (Quess's board was strengthened post-demerger; key leadership hires completed; Lohit Bhatia later made CEO from 1 Jan 2026 and ED/Group CEO from 1 June 2026, Neeraj Jain CFO from 3 Dec 2025). The demerger was explicitly used as the trigger for a portfolio clean-up: a "comprehensive review" led the Board and management to discontinue non-core, long-gestation, outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities (meter reading/bill distribution), producing a Q4 FY25 exceptional charge of INR 158 crore — INR 119 crore of accelerated expected credit loss on discontinued projects, INR 26 crore goodwill impairment (INR 7 crore Stellarslog, INR 19 crore Quess International Services, the repurposed Golden Star) and INR 13 crore of demerger costs (mainly stamp duty) — forfeiting roughly INR 300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin from skilling, with Digitide likewise "rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts" ahead of separation. Balance-sheet repair was part of the thesis: gross debt was cut (INR 224 crore at Dec 2024) to INR 12 crore by 31 March 2025 and zero later, leaving net cash of INR 255 crore (INR 271/273 crore subsequently), a new dividend policy of up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, and an adjusted ROE target crossing 20%. Management repeatedly conceded the cost: standalone EBITDA margin optically reset from the 2.4–2.5% the workforce division earned pre-demerger to 1.8%, because standalone corporate overheads now sit in Quess and because the high-margin skilling and Brainhunter businesses left, making history "noncomparable"; demerger expenses hit reported PAT by INR 22 crore in Q3 FY25, INR 13 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR 2 crore in Q1 FY26, and the stock "saw some weakness immediately following the demerger". Nothing in these texts says any investor, lender or partner asked for the separation — it is presented throughout as a management-and-Board decision, with shareholders and creditors merely approving it on 9 December 2024 and the NCLT sanctioning it; the only external parties named are the demerger-linked cross-sell partners (Quess selling Origint GCC-as-a-Service using Bluspring and Digitide capabilities).
verdict.evolution: On the 30 Jan 2025 call (Q3 FY25) the demerger was already in flight — first NCLT approval obtained, shareholder and creditor approvals secured on 9 December, INR 22 crore of demerger costs booked, leadership/controls being built per entity, and Digitide pre-emptively rationalizing low-margin contracts — with listing guided for Q1 FY26. By the 20 May 2025 call it was done "well ahead of stated timeline" and Quess held its "first earnings call as an independent entity", pairing the split with the INR 158 crore exceptional clean-up of skilling/utilities projects, zero-ish gross debt, net cash of INR 255 crore, the new 75%-of-FCF dividend policy, and a frank reset of margin guidance from 2.4–2.5% to 1.8% rising to 2%. Through 29 Jul 2025 ("pure-play staffing leader", residual INR 2 crore of demerger fees) and 29 Jan 2026 (the demerger invoked to explain why 4–4.5% historic margins are "noncomparable", and the Q4 FY25 ECL recalled as "the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger"), the story shifted from execution to justification; on 5 May 2026 management closed the loop by exiting the last non-conforming business — a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project worth ~INR 200 crore (1.3% of revenue) — citing the commitment made "closer to our demerger timeline". At the 25 Aug 2026 AGM the Chairman recast it retrospectively as value creation: three listed companies, ~INR 500 crore combined EBITDA, 600,000+ people, Quess debt-free, and a forward plan ("Quess 2.0") to lift dollar-linked revenue from 7% to 20% and Professional Staffing plus Overseas profit share from 50% to 65%.

points.point: With first NCLT approval in hand and shareholder/creditor approvals obtained on 9 December 2024, management framed the split as unlocking shareholder value and building separate leadership teams, internal controls and processes for each demerged entity.
points.quote: Our aim is to create independent entities that are agile, strategically focused and well positioned to unlock value for all stakeholders in the long term.

points.point: Ahead of separation, the soon-to-be Digitide entity was already pruning its own book, with the stated purpose of lifting the separated company's long-term operating margin.
points.quote: As a run-up to demerger, with a new entity, Digitide, we are examining our existing service lines and rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts, which would give a sustainable upside to our long-term operating margins.

points.point: The demerger carried visible cash and margin costs during execution: INR 22 crore of demerger expenses in Q3 FY25 drove a 9% sequential PAT decline, and platform margins compressed on sales/leadership investment made in the run-up.
points.quote: Demerger -related expenses of INR 22 crores were recognized during the quarter, which resulted in a PAT decline of 9% on a sequential basis.

points.point: First call as a standalone company: the 3-way demerger was completed ahead of the stated timeline and sold as sharper focus plus value unlocking, alongside a seamless leadership transition (Kamal Pal Hoda moving to Bluspring as CEO, Sushanth Pai joining Quess as CFO).
points.quote: This important milestone leads to a sharper focus and unlocking value, strategic transformation, and delivering sustained growth.

points.point: The demerger was the explicit trigger for exiting non-core projects in skilling and utilities (meter reading/bill distribution), long-gestation outcome-based work the Board decided not to carry into the new structure.
points.quote: As part of the demerger transformation, we have revisited some of our businesses through a comprehensive review, and we will be exiting certain non -core projects, in line with the position taken by the management and the Board to discontinue such projects pursuant to the scheme of demerger.

points.point: That clean-up cost INR 158 crore of exceptional items in Q4 FY25 — INR 119 crore accelerated ECL on discontinued projects, INR 26 crore goodwill impairment (INR 7 crore Stellarslog, INR 19 crore Quess International Services) and INR 13 crore of demerger expenses, mainly stamp duty — with no cash outflow, and forfeited roughly INR 300 crore of ~20%-margin skilling revenue.
points.quote: This has impacted reported PAT by INR 158 crores in the quarter.

points.point: Management conceded the standalone margin optics: the workforce division earned 2.4–2.5% inside the old group, but standalone corporate overheads reset Quess to 1.8%, with a staged recovery to about 2% by the exit of FY26 (delivered: FY26 at 2.0%, Q4 FY26 at 2.2%).
points.quote: I mean, if you look at the overall margin was hovering between 2.4% to 2.5% prior to demerger, specifically for the workforce as a division.

points.point: Capital allocation was redefined around the separated entity: gross debt cut to INR 12 crore and net cash of INR 255 crore at 31 March 2025, a new policy to return up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, DSO improved 7 days to 37, and adjusted ROE guided above 20%. Asked about new geographies, management said focus came first.
points.quote: See, as part of this demerger, Siddharth, our focus is going to be on the core businesses and how much more we can do and bring in more efficiency and stay profitable.

points.point: Quess positioned itself as a pure-play staffing company, while still monetising the separation by partnering its demerged siblings: the new Origint GCC-as-a-Service line is delivered by bringing Bluspring and Digitide capabilities together on a cost-plus, asset-light basis.
points.quote: So, as we strengthen our position as a pure -play staffing leader, we remain deeply committed to operational excellence, innovation and continuously evolving our offerings to meet the dynamic needs of our clients.

points.point: Asked why margins are ~2% versus 4–5% historically, management used the demerger to explain the break in the series — Bluspring and Digitide are out, skilling was discontinued, and Brainhunter (US/Canada) moved to Digitide.
points.quote: With all of those business with high EBITDA margins, we were averaging around 4%, 4.5%, but that businesses have been discontinued and Brain hunter as part of demerger has moved into Digitide.

points.point: The INR 120 crore Q4 FY25 ECL was re-confirmed as demerger-driven, relating to the discontinued government skilling project, with collections still being pursued (delayed from Q3 to Q4 FY26 by a new RBI escrow process) and any recovery to be reported as upside.
points.quote: If you recollect, in Q4, these were the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger that we had announced to the Street, and we had taken an exceptional credit loss on that.

points.point: The portfolio-discipline promise made at the time of the demerger was carried through: a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project worth about INR 200 crore (1.3% of revenue) was fully exited in FY26, with no further such events known.
points.quote: So, as you would remember, closer to our demerger timeline, we had said any business which does not meet the financi al metrics of the company and does not yield us the cash realization , we will exit and discontinue such businesses.

points.point: One year on, management summarised the outcome as balance-sheet and execution strength in the standalone entity: FY26 revenue INR 15,305 crore, EBITDA INR 312 crore (+19%), 2.0% margin, 20% ROE, zero gross debt, net cash INR 271 crore, and INR 6 per share of final plus special dividend.
points.quote: As we said, we are foundationally strong in our 19th year and one year post our demerger.

points.point: At the 25 Aug 2026 AGM the Chairman described the end state: one company became three separately listed companies, each with its own focus and management, funded historically by INR 1,270 crore raised through the Quess IPO and IPP, now together generating about INR 500 crore of EBITDA and employing over 600,000 people.
points.quote: Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.

points.point: What shareholders retain is deliberately single-mandate: a debt-free workforce company that will not diversify outside workforce management, with Quess 2.0 targeting dollar-linked revenue from 7% to over 20% and Professional Staffing plus Overseas profit share from 50% to about 65% in three to four years.
points.quote: We are not diversifying outside our workforce management and following the demerger  of the company is deliberately a pure play business with a single mandate.

points.point: Management acknowledged the de-rating immediately after separation and claimed subsequent recovery, while noting the demerged businesses went on to build their own technology and industrial-services platforms.
points.quote: While the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger, it has since recovered strongly and delivered a return of around 25% over the past year.

verdict.rationale: The premise does not hold in these texts: Share India Securities Ltd. is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business — every transaction documented here moves in the opposite direction, pulling businesses INTO the listed parent by amalgamation. Two schemes are described. First, Silverleaf Capital Services Pvt Ltd (an unlisted HFT/quant technology firm that combines machine learning, AI and in-house low-latency software and hardware for low-latency statistical arbitrage and market making) was amalgamated into Share India with appointed date 1 April 2026 (rectified by NCLT from 1 October 2023), effective 3 November 2026, at 500 Share India shares of Rs. 2 for every 1 Silverleaf share of Rs. 10, resulting in allotment of 44,02,000 shares and 3,80,500 replacement ESOS options; management said it would add to the technology stack, add product portfolio, diversify revenue and 'expedite global expansion', with Silverleaf's founder Piyush Kedia citing access to more trading capital, operating leverage, faster addition of new exchanges and geographies, and talent acquisition, and Sachin Gupta guiding to Rs. 50-60 crore gross revenue initially, scalable 2x-3x in one to two years. Second, on 30 October and 6 November 2026 the Board approved amalgamating Ace Alpha Tech Limited — a listed company making customised automated trading systems, OMS/RMS integration, back-testing and simulated trading environments for institutions, HNIs and retail traders, with net worth Rs. 8,149.99 lakh, FY26 income Rs. 2,706.11 lakh and PAT Rs. 1,540.88 lakh — into Share India (consolidated net worth Rs. 2,78,890.04 lakh) at 863 shares of Rs. 2 for every 1,000 Ace Alpha shares of Rs. 10, diluting promoter holding from 47.66% to 45.96%. The stated problems solved are organisational fragmentation, duplicated corporate structure and uncoordinated deployment of managerial, technological and financial resources — not separation. The only separation-adjacent facts in the record are the unrealised idea that subsidiaries become 'eligible for listing once they have matured', a new wealth-management subsidiary approved 21 September 2026 with up to Rs. 120 crore equity, and dilution in Silverleaf Securities Research from 73.09% to 64.81% through non-participation in its rights issue.
verdict.evolution: The direction of travel was consolidation from the start: on the Nov 2023 call management said it had 'recently finalized acquisition of Silverleaf Technology' and that its ~11 subsidiaries each contributed to consolidated profit and would be 'eligible for listing once they have matured business profile' — the closest thing to a future separation, never pursued. Jun 2025 called Silverleaf a milestone 'aimed at leveraging our HFT capability and expanding our proprietary trading into the international market'; Aug 2025 reported SEBI and exchange approval and the file moving to NCLT; Nov 2025 explicitly closed the door on carve-outs, saying 'there is no proposal in terms of any value unlocking that's there on the table'; Jan 2026 quantified Silverleaf at Rs. 50-60 crore revenue; May 2026 and Jul 2026 described it as in the 'last leg' of NCLT. The merger became effective 3 Nov 2026 and the Ace Alpha amalgamation was approved 6 Nov 2026 — i.e. the plan evolved toward more consolidation, not a separation.

points.point: The Ace Alpha Tech scheme (Board approval 6 November 2026) is an amalgamation INTO Share India, justified by complementary technology and financial-services capabilities, a simplified corporate structure and reduced organisational fragmentation — the opposite of a separation.
points.quote: The proposed Amalgamation is expected to bring together complementary technology and financial services capabilities, facilitate operational integration, simplify the corporate structure, support the development of technology-enabled financial solutions and create a stronger platform for the future growth of the combined business.

points.point: The Ace Alpha scheme names fragmentation of the group structure as the problem being solved, with the combined business carried on by Share India as one undertaking.
points.quote: The resulting consolidation is expected to facilitate closer coordination between technology development and financial market operations, reduce organisational fragmentation and provide a unified platform for the continued development of the combined business.

points.point: The Silverleaf Capital Services scheme states the merger rationale as adding technology stack, product portfolio, revenue diversification and faster global expansion — again inbound consolidation, with Silverleaf dissolved without winding up.
points.quote: The merger of Transferor Company into Transferee Company would enable the Transferee Company to have valuable addition to its technology stack, provide additional product portfolio, aid in diversifying revenue and expedite global expansion, thereby adding value to its shareholders.

points.point: Asked directly about value unlocking from subsidiaries and 'the listing of our subsidiaries', Abhinav Gupta said all subsidiaries are at a nascent stage and no separation or value-unlocking proposal exists.
points.quote: Currently, there is no proposal in terms of any value unlocking that's there on the table.

points.point: The only separation-adjacent idea ever raised: subsidiaries (then ~11, contributing ~30% of consolidated profit) might one day be listed once their business profiles mature. It was never advanced in any later call or filing.
points.quote: And going forward, there is a lot of value creation also coming out of the subsidiaries as all these subsidiaries are eligible for listing once they have matured business profile.

points.point: Silverleaf founder Piyush Kedia framed the deal as the small HFT entity needing the parent's capital, platform and operating leverage to scale and add exchanges — a case for combining, not separating.
points.quote: With this acquisition, the synergies that are created -- that have been created are; one, our existing operations scaled up, we get access to more trading capital, Share India is a much bigger organization, we get to scale up currently the strategies that we're running currently.

points.point: Kamlesh Shah listed the Silverleaf merger among the year's key milestones, tied to HFT capability and taking proprietary trading international.
points.quote: Key milestone achieved during the year include strategic investment in Metropolitan Stock Exchange, obtaining PMS license and merger of Silver Leaf securities, a subsidiary aimed at leveraging our HFT capability and expanding our proprietary trading into the international market.

points.point: Sachin Gupta quantified what the Silverleaf merger brings in once consolidated, and the scaling expected from parent capital and risk appetite.
points.quote: So, Silverleaf, once the merger will be done, we are expecting top line of Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60-odd crores, and that's the initial revenues.

points.point: The merger was still pending NCLT sanction a quarter before completion, presented as adding a new diversified revenue stream to the parent.
points.quote: So, Silverleaf merger as last call we spoke still in NCLT we hope it is in last leg of the approval.

points.point: Asked why a Mumbai tech company was acquired, Abhinav Gupta tied Silverleaf to the HST protocol, the technology backbone and overseas expansion — integration into the fold, not separation.
points.quote: So, it is a strategy in line with our global expansion plan, apart from just being focused on India -based products, along with strengthening our technology backbone and the back stack of the current strategy.

points.point: The nearest thing to carving out a business is forward-looking, not a separation of an existing one: on 21 September 2026 the Board approved a brand-new wealth-management subsidiary with up to Rs. 120 crore of equity, plus up to Rs. 200 crore of convertible warrants.
points.quote: The proposed subsidiary is envisaged to focus on providing wealth management and allied financial services.

points.point: The only reduction of ownership in the record is passive: Share India let its stake in Silverleaf Securities Research fall by not subscribing to that unit's rights issue, with no sale, transfer or change of control.
points.quote: The aforesaid dilution has occurred solely on account of the Company's non -participation in the Rights Issue and does not involve any sale, transfer or disposal of shares by the Company.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation is described, so no per-entity split economics exist. For the combined entity management expects a stronger technology backbone, improved operating efficiency, better profit margins and higher growth potential; faster product development, cross-selling, global expansion; Silverleaf adding Rs. 50-60 crore revenue scalable 2x-3x and being EPS accretive; and simpler structure with better use of managerial, financial and technological resources.
verdict.gaps: No spin-off, demerger or separation is explained anywhere — because none is proposed. Subsidiary listing, raised in Nov 2023, was never costed, timed or revisited.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is ABB India's Robotics (reported segment "Robotics & Discrete Automation"), and the trigger was not an India problem but the parent's global decision: ABB Ltd., Switzerland announced on 17 April 2025 that it would spin off its robotics division as a separate listed company, then on 8 October 2025 announced it would instead sell that division to SoftBank Group, which management said was chosen over a listing "in the interest of the shareholders" after "a very good offer." Management's India-specific case, set out in the 26 January 2026 board approval and the postal-ballot explanatory statement, is dependence: the Indian Robotics Business "primarily serves as a sales channel, provides maintenance support and some degree of application engineering" and has "a high degree of operational, technological integration and dependence upon ABB Limited's Robotics division for patented technology and product R&D, as well as for operations, supply chain, marketing and branding" — so once ABB Group support goes to SoftBank, it is neither attractive to a third-party buyer nor viable in its current form inside ABB India. They argued there are no material synergies with the rest of the company and that exiting lets ABB India "strengthen its position in its core business divisions, namely, Electrification, Motion, and Automation." The numbers they cited to show immaterriality: Robotics was 3.6% of FY2024 revenue (Rs 444.42 crore) and 2.4% of PBT, had negative net worth (-Rs 29.27 crore in FY2024, -Rs 45.45 crore in FY2023), and in 9M to September 2025 was 5.9% of revenue (Rs 566.77 crore) and only 3.3% of EBITDA (Rs 50.33 crore vs Rs 1,492.26 crore for the rest). Crucially, the Board explicitly rejected a demerger/separate listing because the "size, nature and scale of operations" did not warrant a listed entity, the compliance cost would not be commensurate, and such a company would be "unlikely to attract adequate investor interest or provide sufficient trading liquidity to shareholders" — so the chosen route was a related-party slump sale of the business to ABB Robotics India Private Limited (incorporated 22 September 2025, then sold to ABB Robotics Schweiz AG for Rs 1,00,000) for Rs 1,568.20 crore, priced off two independent valuations (Ernst & Young Merchant Banking Services LLP and Bansi S. Mehta/Bansi Mehta S Valuers LLP, using DCF, comparable-transaction and comparable-company methods, with the global SoftBank deal as a comparable transaction) plus an ICICI Securities fairness opinion. Nobody external asked for it: there was no bidding process, only an expression of interest dated 21 January 2026 from ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd; because the size (13% of consolidated turnover vs the 10% turnover threshold of Rs 1,218.83 crore and 10% net-worth threshold of Rs 707.54 crore) made it a material related-party transaction, promoters could not vote and minority approval was required, which it got on 27 February 2026 with 94.08% of votes polled in favour (2,91,72,366 shares) and 5.92% against — though non-institutional public holders voted 96% against.
verdict.evolution: On the 4 August 2025 call, five months after the parent's April spin-off announcement, management still presented Robotics as a growth business and said "we stay committed on this particular division as such." By the 7 November 2025 call the posture had changed: Sridhar said ABB had globally announced the divestment and the India decision was "fully dependent on the Board's evaluation," while Sanjeev Sharma explained the shift from listing to the SoftBank sale and said that after independent valuation "separation of this asset will be done into a new company," subject to ABB India's Board — answering a Jefferies question about how Indian shareholders would be compensated. The Board approved the slump sale on 26 January 2026, shareholders approved it on 27 February 2026 and the BTA was executed on 1 March 2026, yet the 23 February 2026 call made no mention of the pending transaction and still reported Robotics as a live segment; only on the 8 May 2026 call was the exit acknowledged, with Robotics gone from the mix and the Rs 1,568 crore of proceeds sitting outside the reported cash balance.

points.point: Three months after the parent's April 2025 spin-off announcement, ABB India's CFO still publicly backed the division, with Robotics president Subrata Karmakar presenting its outlook and no mention of any India separation.
points.quote: And we stay committed on this particular division as such.

points.point: First acknowledgment on a call that the India Robotics asset was in play, with the decision explicitly pushed to the local Board and described as undecided.
points.quote: ABB globally announced the divestment of robotics, so we still have, the decision in India is fully dependent on the Board's evaluation and the next set of processes which will happen, which is at this point of time not decided.

points.point: Sanjeev Sharma explained the change of route at group level — an intended separate listing was dropped in favour of SoftBank's offer, which the global Board judged better for shareholders.
points.quote: And then initial interest was to list that company. But then in the interest of the shareholders, we got a very good offer from SoftBank and Global Board decided to choose SoftBank to be the future owner and take this business forward.

points.point: Asked by Lavina Quadros (Jefferies) how Indian shareholders would be compensated and whether a separate listing would happen, management said listing was unlikely and the asset would be valued by the Board, including independent directors, before being moved into a new company.
points.quote: After the valuations are done like we have done in the past and the local Board is satisfied, based on that valuation, separation of this asset will be done into a new company.

points.point: Management framed governance by precedent — the 2019 Power Grids demerger to Hitachi Energy India — saying ABB India's own Board, not the parent, controls such separations.
points.quote: And if you see the history of similar assets separated from ABB India Limited, we follow a very tight governance model and that is led by the ABB India Limited Board.

points.point: The core rationale in the 26 January 2026 postal-ballot statement: the Indian unit is a distribution-and-service arm dependent on the parent's robotics division for patented technology, R&D, supply chain and brand, so it cannot stand alone once ABB Group support transfers to SoftBank.
points.quote: Access to ABB Group’s support is accordingly necessary for the Company to continue the Robotics Business in its current form.

points.point: The Board considered and rejected a demerger/separate listing on grounds of scale, compliance cost and liquidity, which is why the structure is a related-party slump sale for Rs 1,568.20 crore rather than a spin-off to shareholders.
points.quote: An independently listed Robotics Business of the aforesaid scale would also be unlikely to attract adequate investor interest or provide sufficient trading liquidity to shareholders.

points.point: Robotics was presented as immaterial and dilutive to mix: 3.6% of FY2024 revenue (Rs 444.42 crore) and 2.4% of PBT; 5.9% of 9M-Sept-2025 revenue but only 3.3% of EBITDA (Rs 50.33 crore vs Rs 1,492.26 crore); net worth negative at -Rs 29.27 crore, so the exit is net-worth accretive.
points.quote: The Robotics Business does not enjoy material synergies with the other businesses of the Company.

points.point: No auction was run; the only interest was an expression of interest from a promoter-group entity five days before board approval, with price set by two independent valuers (EY, Bansi S. Mehta) and an ICICI Securities fairness opinion, and promoters barred from voting on the 13%-of-turnover material RPT.
points.quote: The Company has not undertaken a bidding process for choosing a party for the proposed Business Transfer. However, the Company has received an expression of interest dated January 21, 2026 from ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd for purchase of the Robotics Business.

points.point: Minority approval was secured on 27 February 2026 with 94.08% of votes polled in favour (2,91,72,366 shares) against 5.92% opposed — institutions voted ~99% for, but non-institutional public shareholders voted roughly 96% against.
points.quote: the Ordinary Resolution as set out in the Notice of Postal Ballot, has been duly approved by the Members of the Company with requisite majority

points.point: The BTA was signed and the transfer made effective 1 March 2026; Q1 CY2026 results booked a Rs 1,658.48 crore gain in discontinued operations (total PAT Rs 1,783.65 crore) and the Robotics & Discrete Automation segment disappeared from reporting.
points.quote: on March 1, 2026, at 11.51 pm the Company has executed a Business Transfer Agreement (“BTA”) with ABB Robotics India Private Limited for the Business Transfer.

points.point: At approval the Board gave no plan for the proceeds; a Rs 90 per share special dividend was declared only with the Q2 CY2026 results on 31 July 2026, never explicitly tied to the sale.
points.quote: Following completion of the Business Transfer and receipt of the proceeds therefrom, the Board may, in due course, determine the utilization of the proceeds from the transaction.

points.point: Despite board approval on 26 January and an open postal ballot, the Q4 CY2025 call never mentioned the sale and discussed Robotics as an ongoing segment with Rs 570 crore of quarterly orders.
points.quote: Robotics, I think they also grew definitely higher, INR570 crores for the quarter.

points.point: First post-completion commentary: Robotics' former 4–5% share of the business mix is gone, leaving Electrification plus Motion at 81% and Automation at 19%.
points.quote: We don't have robotics at this point of time, so robotics used to be 4% to 5%.

points.point: Proceeds lifted liquidity materially — reported cash of Rs 6,042 crore excludes the sale money, roughly Rs 7,600 crore including it — in a quarter where margins were under pressure from copper, silver and rupee depreciation.
points.quote: So we have, at this point of time, INR6,042 crores, but this is without the cash which we got from the sale of Robotics. If I include that, it is roughly round about INR7,600 crores.

verdict.what_management_expects: ABB India retains Electrification, Motion and Automation (EL+MO now 81% of revenue) and sheds its lowest-margin, parent-dependent unit: -Rs 444 crore turnover, -Rs 60 crore net profit, but +Rs 29 crore net worth, Rs 1,568 crore cash (total ~Rs 7,600 crore), a Rs 1,658 crore book gain, one segment eliminated, and a Rs 90/share special dividend.
verdict.gaps: No stated use of proceeds at approval; no valuation range, SoftBank read-across, explanation of retail's dissent, or post-sale supply/branding terms; the February 2026 call omitted the pending sale entirely.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these transcripts and filings, Aarti Pharmalabs is NOT separating, demerging or spinning off any business — no such plan is announced, discussed or even asked about on any of the seven calls, and the company continues to report itself as a single segment: 'The Company has identified only one segment i.e. Pharmaceuticals.' The only Scheme of Arrangement anywhere in these documents is the historical INBOUND demerger that created the company: the pharmaceutical undertaking / Pharma Division of Aarti Industries Limited was demerged into Aarti Pharmalabs, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on September 21, 2022, and it surfaces in 2026 only because the Collector and Additional Superintendent of Stamps, Gandhinagar, by order dated August 29, 2026, determined stamp duty of Rs. 25 crore under Article 20(d) of the Gujarat Stamp Act, 1958 plus penalties of Rs. 34.50 crore (Rs. 59.50 crore in total), against which the company took a Rs. 2.04 crore provision as an exceptional item, disclosed Rs. 57.46 crore as contingent liability, and filed a writ petition in the Gujarat High Court on September 30, 2026. Two lesser de-couplings from the former parent do appear: Ganesh Polychem Limited (the 50:50 Bandodkar-family venture at Dombivli/Vapi) was reclassified from proportionate consolidation to equity-method joint venture from Q1 FY26 'following the amendment in the Subscriptions and Shareholders Agreement', so consolidated turnover drops optically (Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue Rs. 386 crore vs Rs. 555 crore) while EBITDA and PAT remain comparable; and Aarti USA Inc., retained by Aarti Pharmalabs at the 2022 split for its licences, lost the Aarti Industries distribution business (down to ~Rs. 7 crore in Q4 FY25) as Aarti Industries moved it to its own new US subsidiary. Management explicitly denied any entity transfer when asked: Rashesh Gogri corrected an analyst in Feb 2025 that no subsidiary was being shifted to Aarti Industries. Far from separating the three verticals (Xanthine derivatives ~Rs. 792 crore FY26, API/Intermediates ~Rs. 650 crore FY26, CDMO/CMO Rs. 276 crore FY26), management repeatedly stresses that they share fungible plants, backward-integrated intermediates and a common Atali site, and that CDMO gets first call on those shared assets — an argument for keeping them together, not splitting them. The only 'separation' language on the calls is operational: carving out dedicated single-project manufacturing blocks at Atali (1.5x–2x asset turn, Rs. 250–300 crore topline potential per block) so that multipurpose capacity stays free for new projects.
verdict.evolution: Feb 2025: an analyst mistakenly asks whether Ganesh Polychem is being transferred to Aarti Industries; management corrects that only the Aarti USA trading arrangement with Aarti Industries is ending, as Aarti Industries has incorporated its own US subsidiary. May 2025 and Aug 2025: the Aarti USA run-down is quantified (~Rs. 7 crore in Q4 FY25) and Ganesh Polychem is reclassified to an equity-method joint venture from Q1 FY26 after an amendment to the Subscriptions and Shareholders Agreement, making consolidated revenue optically lower. Nov 2025 to Jun 2026: no separation is raised at all; the discussion is capacity, Atali ramp-up and, by Jun 2026, dedicated manufacturing blocks — a plant-level, not entity-level, separation. Sept 2 and Sept 30, 2026 filings and the Oct 28, 2026 results: the 2022 inbound demerger resurfaces purely as a Gujarat stamp-duty adjudication of Rs. 59.50 crore, now under writ petition in the Gujarat High Court.

points.point: The only demerger in the record is inbound and historical: Aarti Industries' Pharma Division was demerged INTO Aarti Pharmalabs under an NCLT Ahmedabad order of September 21, 2022; it appears in 2026 only as a stamp-duty adjudication.
points.quote: The order pertains to the adjudication of stamp duty on the Scheme of Arrangement (Demerger) between Aarti Industries Limited (Demerged Company) and Aarti Pharmalabs Limited (Resulting Company) sanctioned by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Ahmedabad Bench vide its order dated September 21, 2022.

points.point: The Gandhinagar stamps authority levied Rs. 25 crore duty plus Rs. 34.50 crore penalties (Rs. 59.50 crore) on that 2022 scheme; the company provided only Rs. 2.04 crore as an exceptional item, disclosed Rs. 57.46 crore as contingent liability and filed a writ in the Gujarat High Court.
points.quote: The Company has challenged the order by a writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat, which is pending; no interim order has been passed.

points.point: There is no segment being carved out — the company reports a single reporting segment across all three verticals in both standalone and consolidated results.
points.quote: The Company has identified only one segment i.e. Pharmaceuticals.

points.point: Asked directly whether a subsidiary was being transferred to Aarti Industries, Rashesh Gogri denied it; what was ending was only the shared US trading arrangement, since Aarti Industries had incorporated its own US entity.
points.quote: No, we have not mentioned about the subsidiary getting shifted to Aarti.

points.point: He explained that Aarti USA Incorporation's ownership had come to Aarti Pharmalabs at the 2022 split because of licences and investments held there, and that Aarti Industries would henceforth use its own 100% US subsidiary.
points.quote: So instead of doing, using Aarti USA Incorporation which was a stock of arrangement from next financial year, mostly Aarti Industries will use their own 100% subsidiary to do the distribution in USA.

points.point: The de-coupling from the former parent's US distribution business is quantified as a revenue decline at Aarti USA Inc., with the business having moved to Aarti Industries' own US subsidiary.
points.quote: This is due to limited business activities in the subsidiary which were earlier carried out for Aarti Industries' distribution business which has now shifted to the Aarti Industries subsidiary in the US.

points.point: Ganesh Polychem Limited (50:50 with the Bandodkar family) was reclassified from proportionate consolidation to equity-method joint venture from Q1 FY26 after an amendment to the Subscriptions and Shareholders Agreement — the only corporate-structure change management announced.
points.quote: Following the amendment in the Subscriptions and Shareholders Agreement, GPL (Ganesh Polychem) is a joint venture from Q1 FY '26 onwards.

points.point: The effect is presentational, not a sale: consolidated revenue excludes GPL (Q1 FY26 consolidated topline Rs. 386 crore vs Rs. 555 crore in Q1 FY25) while EBITDA and PAT still include its share.
points.quote: Basically, the consolidated turnover for Q1 FY '26 onwards will not include GPL's contribution and hence will look optically lower year-on-year.

points.point: Management's reasoning runs the other way from separation: Xanthine, API/intermediates and CDMO share fungible plants, with CDMO given priority on the same assets — the integration is presented as the operating model.
points.quote: So, as you know that, you know, we have fungible plants which are being used for the CDMO business as well as the intermediate business.

points.point: The same shared-asset logic is used to explain quarterly margin swings, with API/intermediate volumes deliberately sacrificed to CDMO campaigns rather than being ring-fenced into a separate business.
points.quote: Yes, Prakashji, you know, the CDMO sales always get first priority.

points.point: The only 'separation' management plans is physical, not corporate: moving commercialised CDMO projects into dedicated blocks at Atali to free multipurpose capacity, with 5–10 year customer visibility.
points.quote: Those products will move to a dedicated block where we have 5 to 10 year visibility of this project.

points.point: The dedicated-block economics management cited — better asset turns and per-block revenue — are the closest thing to a 'what it unlocks' case in the record, and they are block-level, not entity-level.
points.quote: I think depending on how we configure this, it can have potential of close to Rs.250 Crores to Rs.300 Crores topline also from a single block.

points.point: Even on promoter-level questions management signalled continuity of control rather than any restructuring or separation of the group's holdings.
points.quote: So I think there will be minor selling here or there, but it will not affect overall control of the company or anything.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is stated, because no separation is proposed. On the structural changes that do exist, management expects only presentational effects: consolidated revenue optically lower from Ganesh Polychem's equity-method treatment with EBITDA and PAT unchanged, and the Aarti USA revenue run-down as the former parent's distribution shifts away. No margin, capital, valuation or focus benefit is claimed for any separation.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no separation is proposed, so no rationale, structure, timeline, asked-by party, valuation, capital or margin case exists anywhere in these calls or filings.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is Ashok Leyland's vehicle- and housing-finance arm — Hinduja Leyland Finance Ltd (HLFL), together with its subsidiary Hinduja Housing Finance (HHF) — which is being taken out of the Ashok Leyland consolidated structure and given its own listing via a reverse merger (merger by absorption) of HLFL into the already-listed NDL Ventures Ltd (formerly NXTDIGITAL), a near-empty vehicle with FY26 turnover of only ₹489.37 lakhs whose objects were amended to permit NBFC business. Management's first stated reason is valuation: Shenu Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that 'our share price of Ashok Leyland actually does not fully reflect the value that we have in our subsidiaries', and Dheeraj Hinduja closed the same call saying HLF and HHF 'do not really figure as we see it showing a true value in Ashok Leyland shares today, but it will through the listing process unlock this' — 'value unlocking from subsidiaries' was one of the six stated medium-term goals alongside mid-teen EBITDA and 35% MHCV share. The second reason is capital: the finance books were compounding 15–26% a year (HLFL standalone AUM ₹42,000cr on+off book in Nov 2023, ₹44,400cr Dec-24, ₹48,000cr Mar-25, ₹50,430cr Jun-25, ₹52,635cr Sep-25, ₹56,470cr Dec-25, ~₹59,000cr Mar-26; HHF ₹13,400cr to ~₹16,000cr), and Balaji repeatedly said growth was being throttled by capital — 'their business opportunities are restricted with the availability of the cash... the Tier-1 capital is also pretty low where RBI has been insisting on the requirement of more investment in Hinduja Leyland Finance' (Nov 2025), and again in Feb 2026 and Jun 2026 that 'Tier 1 capital sometimes is low compared to the peers.' Ashok Leyland had been plugging that gap itself — ₹200cr into HLFL in Q4 FY25 to meet RBI capital adequacy, with carrying value rising from ~₹60 to ~₹64 per AL share — so a listed platform lets HLFL raise its own growth equity instead: the Scheme rationale says HLFL 'will need growth capital to accelerate growth' and that listing 'will increase the avenues for raising growth capital both from public and interested investors', giving 'greater efficiency in capital raising by the merged entity, and unfettered access to both cash flow generated by the business and external capital raising.' The Scheme adds housekeeping benefits: avoidance of duplicated administrative functions, 'reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances and cost', an increase in the transferee's net worth, and 'higher level of corporate governance as required by listed entity.' It is being done as a reverse merger rather than an IPO (swap of 25 NDL shares of ₹10 for every 10 HLFL shares of ₹10), which dilutes Ashok Leyland from 61.12% in HLFL to 59.64% in NDL, with NDL becoming the material listed subsidiary and HLFL dissolved without winding up; metrics cited alongside were PAT ₹160cr/qtr (Q1 FY26) rising to ₹220cr (Q3 FY26), FY26 HLF PAT ₹491cr (+20%) and HHF PAT ₹387cr (+4%), CAR 18.2%, GNPA 3.5%/NNPA 2.1% (FY25) improving to consolidated NNPA ~1.4%.
verdict.evolution: The listing was already in train by the Nov 2023 call, when Gopal Mahadevan said HLFL expected it 'sometime in Q4' and flagged that 'it's a reverse merger, there are a lot of compliance that are to be done additionally other than a standard DRHP'; by Feb 2025 it was 'on track... likely to be concluded by the end of Q1 FY26.' In May 2025 the rationale was reframed explicitly as value unlocking after repeated analyst prodding (Raghunandhan, Pramod Kumar), with management conceding delay pending approvals; Aug 2025 brought RBI's final clearance to merge with NXT Digital and Balaji's long list of remaining steps (valuers, swap ratio, RBI/exchange intimation, ROC, SEBI, EGM, NCLT) with a 'minimum of 2, 3 quarters' guide, while simultaneously disclosing RBI pressure on Tier-1 capital. Nov 2025 said it was 'progressing as per plan', the boards of HLFL and NDL approved the Scheme on 25 November 2025 (appointed date 1 April 2026) — prompting a 27 November 2025 rumour-verification filing correcting a report that Ashok Leyland's own board had approved it — then Feb 2026 admitted 'some initial delays' with approvals now in place, and the Jun 2026 call (Q4 FY26) said it 'should get consummated within this or the next quarter'; shareholders and unsecured creditors approved on 30 July 2026 (100% of HLFL equity by value, 99.99% of unsecured creditors) and NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 3 November 2026.

points.point: Mahadevan frames the HLFL listing as a reverse merger expected in Q4 FY24, warning it carries extra compliance versus a normal IPO; total HLFL book then ~₹42,000cr on- and off-book, with HHF called one of the fastest-growing housing finance companies.
points.quote: I think they are expecting this to happen sometime in Q4. Some it's a reverse merger, there are a lot of compliance that are to be done additionally other than a standard DRHP.

points.point: Reverse merger of HLFL into NDL Ventures declared on track for conclusion by end of Q1 FY26, alongside AUM growth of 26% (HLF ₹44,400cr) and 43% (HHF ₹13,400cr); the board simultaneously approved ₹200cr more equity into HLFL to support its capital adequacy.
points.quote: The reverse merger of Hinduja Leyland Finance with NDL Ventures is on track. As mentioned earlier, this is likely to be concluded by the end of Q1 FY26.

points.point: Agarwal states the separation's purpose is closing a holding-company discount — AL's share price does not reflect subsidiary value — and Dheeraj Hinduja lists 'value unlocking from subsidiaries' among the six medium-term goals; HLFL consolidated AUM ~₹62,000cr (+25%), revenue ₹6,281cr (+35%), GNPA 3.5%/NNPA 2.1%; AL's carrying value ~₹64/share.
points.quote: So we would take those actions to unlock this value at the right time.

points.point: Dheeraj Hinduja ties the unlocking explicitly to the listing route in his closing remarks, noting HHF is now the fourth-largest affordable housing finance company yet invisible in AL's share price.
points.quote: Although HLF and HHF do not really figure as we see it showing a true value in Ashok Leyland shares today, but it will through the listing process unlock this.

points.point: RBI's final clearance to initiate the merger with NXT Digital is announced as the gate that opens the listing; Balaji then enumerates the full approval chain (valuers, swap ratio, RBI, exchanges, ROC, SEBI, NCLT, EGM) and guides to a minimum of two to three quarters. HLF AUM ₹50,430cr, HHF ₹14,265cr (both +25%), PAT ₹160cr, NNPA 1.63%, CAR 18.2%, AL stake 61.12%.
points.quote: Very recently, HLF also received the final clearance from RBI to initiate a merger process with NXT Digital paving the way for its listing.

points.point: Balaji gives the capital-constraint reason for separating the finance arm: HLFL's growth is limited by cash and Tier-1 capital, with RBI pressing Ashok Leyland for further investment — the dependence a separate listing is meant to end. HLF AUM ₹52,635cr (+26%), HHF ₹14,903cr (+20%), PAT ₹196cr, book value ₹7,418cr, NNPA 1.59%.
points.quote: So there is plenty of business opportunity and their business opportunities are restricted with the availability of the cash, availability of the money and the Tier-1 capital is also pretty low where RBI has been insisting on the requirement of more investment in Hinduja Leyland Finance.

points.point: After boards approved the Scheme on 25 Nov 2025, management concedes slippage but says all approvals are now in hand and the process is in final closure; Balaji again cites sub-peer Tier-1 as the reason AL keeps having to inject capital into HLF and HHF. Finance subsidiaries' quarterly PAT ₹220cr; HLF AUM ₹56,470cr (+18%), HHF ₹15,454cr (+16%).
points.quote: Reverse merger of HLF with NDL Ventures had some initial delays, but now with all the necessary approvals in place, the process is being followed for a final closure.

points.point: Completion guided to within one or two quarters, with the finance arm now the largest piece of the non-CV value: HLF AUM ~₹59,000cr (+24%) and PAT ₹491cr (+20%), HHF AUM ~₹16,000cr (+15%) and PAT ₹387cr (+4%), consolidated net NPA ~1.4%; Balaji still flags Tier-1 below peers as a reason AL may have to invest again.
points.quote: Reverse merger of HLF with NBL Ventures is progressing as per plan and should get consummated within this or the next quarter.

points.point: The NCLT-sanctioned rationale states HLFL needs growth capital and that becoming the listed entity widens access to public and investor capital — the capital-access argument management made on the calls, now formalised.
points.quote: The Transferor company being a successful NBFC, will need growth capital to accelerate growth and believes that merging with the Transferor company will increase the avenues for raising growth capital both from public and interested investors thereby resulting in value enhancement for its shareholders.

points.point: Beyond capital, the Scheme claims efficiency and governance gains for the separated entity: no duplicated administration, fewer overlapping compliances, higher net worth, focused management and listed-company governance standards.
points.quote: (b) Greater efficiency in capital raising by the merged entity, and unfettered access to both cash flow generated by the business and external capital raising which can be deployed more efficiently to fund growth opportunities;

points.point: Mechanics and cost of the separation: swap of 25 NDL shares of ₹10 for every 10 HLFL shares of ₹10, HLFL dissolved without winding up, Ashok Leyland diluted from 61.12% in HLFL to 59.64% in NDL, which becomes AL's material listed subsidiary; sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 3 November 2026 with appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: Consequently, Ashok Leyland's shareholding shall stand diluted from 61.12% in HLFL to 59.64% in NDL and NDL shall become the material listed subsidiary of the Company.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Ashok Leyland: the holding-company discount closed, HLF/HHF value visible in the share price, and an end to recurring equity injections (₹200cr in Q4 FY25) made for RBI capital adequacy, while retaining 59.64% of a listed NBFC. For the finance arm: direct public and investor access to growth capital and Tier-1, higher net worth, fewer duplicated compliances, focused management and listed-company governance to sustain 15–25% AUM growth.
verdict.gaps: No standalone valuation, discount quantified, target raise, ROE goal, or why a reverse merger into a shell beat an IPO; dilution to 59.64% and its cost never discussed on any call.
