verdict.rationale: There is no business separation in these texts: across all four calls (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) and all four filings, Oswal Pumps never announces a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, or listing of any division — the only entity being separated from the group is a dormant shell, wholly owned subsidiary Oswal Green Private/Industries Private Limited, which the board resolved to strike off because 'it has no significant business operations', with a written-off investment of just INR 0.10 million. Every other structural move runs the opposite way — toward consolidation and deeper backward integration of the same solar-pumping value chain. On 08 June 2026 the company bought an additional 13,07,000 shares of associate Walso Solar Solution Pvt Ltd (mounting structures, BOS, turnkey solar pumping components) at Rs 28/share for Rs 3.66 crore via rights issue, taking it from 38.5% (plus 4.5% on 08 April 2026 and 8% in June) to 51% and converting it from associate into subsidiary, on the stated logic that vertical integration lets the group 'design and develop new products, optimize our operational costs and improve our margins'; Walso's FY26 turnover was INR 1,702.65 million versus INR 720.54 million in FY25. On 10 October 2026 the board approved a greenfield 1.2 GW solar cell plant at Karnal under WOS Oswal Solar Energy Pvt Ltd (formerly Oswal Solar Structure), total project cost INR 4,558.50 million, funded partly by re-directing INR 1,598.50 million of unutilised IPO proceeds away from the Aluminium Frame Facility, the remaining 300 MW EVA encapsulant line and the remaining 500 MW of module capacity, because DCR cells — not frames — are 'the binding constraint', with domestic cell makers offering long-term contracts 'only at elevated prices' and demanding 'very large deposits'; the captive plant is to cover ~75% of cell requirement. Earlier, the December 2025 postal-ballot 'First Variation' merely relocated the module plant to a larger adjacent Karnal parcel (28,000 sq m vs 13,983 sq m, 15-year lease from 25 June 2024) to share workforce, R&D, admin infrastructure and an existing electricity feeder. The one genuinely new legal vehicle is additive, not a carve-out: Oswal Solar Energy incorporated SPV Oswal Doon Baran Bundi Solar Projects Limited with Doon Infrapower Projects Pvt Ltd, holding 60%, to execute HAM rooftop PV on Rajasthan state government buildings. Management's answer to its real problem — single-scheme dependency on PM-KUSUM, whose 2.0 rollout slipped from 'before the end of this fiscal' to June 2026+ — is diversification inside the existing group (rooftop/PM Surya Ghar, utility, C&I, ~300 MW pipeline, exports, private network, in-house inverters), explicitly kept as backward integration and never 'a revenue model', not separation.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea ever surfaces. Aug 2025 describes a fully integrated group (pumps/motors/controllers in-house, modules via Oswal Solar, structures/BOS via 38.5% associate Walso) and a backup plan of exports and private-market pumps if KUSUM 2.0 slips; Nov 2025 adds the module-plant land shift and the Oswal Green strike-off. Feb 2026, after receivable days hit 157 and Maharashtra's Magel Tyala payments stalled, management says the KUSUM 2.0 delay 'brought a point of diversification to our mind' — new verticals, EPC for large rooftops, invoice discounting — all housed internally. May 2026 formalises that with the first PM Surya Ghar order and the 60% Rajasthan HAM SPV, and the October 2026 cell-plant variation pulls capital further into the group rather than out of it.

points.point: The only entity exiting the group is a dormant wholly owned subsidiary being struck off — not a business separation but the wind-up of a shell with no operations (investment of INR 0.10 million written off).

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these three years of earnings calls or in the filings provided describes Premier Energies separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving off any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement in the record — so the premise of the question cannot be supported from these texts. The direction management describes is the opposite: consolidation and diversification into one group. Across the Nov 2025, Jan 2026 and May 2026 calls the company adds businesses rather than sheds them — a 51% stake in transformer maker Transcon Ind Limited for up to ₹5,003.00 million (₹2,500.02 million for 34.21% in Dec 2025, the balance ₹2,502.98 million in April 2026, taking Transcon and its subsidiary Neotrafo to subsidiary/step-down status), a 51% inverter JV with Syrma SGS around KSolare (FY25 revenue cited at ₹143 crores), a 6 GWh-per-phase cell-to-pack BESS line at ₹280 crores, aluminium frames at ₹260 crores, a 10 GW ingot-wafer project at about ₹5,900 crores, and a 51% stake in HeliosAnthos Energies for ₹10.45 lakh. Management's stated rationale for keeping these together is synergy, not separation: Vinay Rustagi argued 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of renewable capacity added, with roughly 80% of installs now renewable, so transformers, inverters and BESS go to 'the same clients who we are selling our modules', 'reducing the cost of customer acquisition', and the new businesses together with BESS are expected to contribute 'approximately 30% of our revenue over time'. The only two events in the record that even resemble a separation are (a) the voluntary winding-up by strike-off of IBD Solar Powertech (Pvt.) Ltd, a Bangladesh step-down wholly owned subsidiary with nil revenue, nil turnover contribution and negative net worth of ₹2.09 lakh, where the Reg. 30 annexure marks every sale/disposal/scheme field 'Not Applicable'; and (b) the abandonment of the KSolare acquisition in Q1 FY27 — a reversal of an inbound deal, not a carve-out, with 'no financial implications arising from the same'. There is also an accounting-only split — Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment became a separate reportable segment under Ind AS 108 from the Transcon acquisition date — but that is segment disclosure, not a legal or structural separation. On these texts alone, there is no separation to explain, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for one.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces: in Feb 2025 and May 2025 management frames 'Mission 2028' as a single integrated 10 GW ingot-wafer-cell-module platform plus BESS and inverters, with ₹125,000 million of capex inside one group. Jul 2025 and Nov 2025 add, not subtract — the 4.8 GW cell line is scaled to 7 GW, and the KSolare (inverter) and Transcon (transformer) acquisitions are announced as 'highly complementary and value accretive'. Jan 2026 reports the Transcon acquisition completed in Dec 2025 and KSolare closing 'in the next one month'; by May 2026 the KSolare deal is dropped for lack of agreement on final documentation while Transcon's 51% is completed, and the Aug 2026 and Sep 2026 filings record only a new reportable segment and the strike-off of the dormant Bangladesh shell. At no point in May 2025, Jul 2025, Nov 2025, Jan 2026 or May 2026 does any analyst or executive mention a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme.

points.point: The only disposal-type disclosure in the filings is the strike-off of a dormant, non-operating Bangladesh step-down subsidiary — not a business separation; the Reg. 30 annexure marks turnover contribution nil, net worth negative ₹2.09 lakh, and every sale/disposal/scheme-of-arrangement field 'Not Applicable'.
points.quote: IBD, had no revenue or commercial operations and had filed an application for voluntary winding-up by way of strike off of name on 10th October, 2023 with the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms, Bangladesh.

points.point: Management's stated logic is combination, not separation: the inverter and transformer acquisitions are kept inside the group precisely because they are complementary and are expected to supply about 30% of revenue over time.
points.quote: Both these acquisitions are highly complementary and value accretive.

points.point: Rustagi quantified the cross-sell synergy that argues against separating the equipment businesses — roughly 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of capacity added, sold to the same module customers.

points.point: Transcon is described as a future growth engine being scaled sevenfold inside the group (2.5 GVA to 16.75 GVA by July 2026) and moved up into MV/HV/EHV, with a ₹1,000 crore-plus top line targeted by FY28 — the opposite of a carve-out.
points.quote: This business is expected to become a key growth contributor for us.

points.point: The one deal that was unwound was an inbound acquisition (KSolare), dropped over documentation terms, with the inverter ambition retained in-house via the SMA/Syrma SGS JV route — again no separation of an existing Premier business.
points.quote: I think that is the reason why the transaction could not be completed.

points.point: The only 'split' in the record is an accounting one: a new reportable segment created by the Transcon acquisition under Ind AS 108, effective from the April 3, 2026 acquisition date.
points.quote: Consequently, the Company has identified Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment as a separate reportable segment in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 108 - Operating Segments.

points.point: Forward capital plans are framed as one diversified platform funded centrally (FY27 capex ₹5,100 crores across cells, ingot-wafers, batteries and inverters; ₹5,000 crores enabling fundraise resolution), with no mention of releasing capital by separating an entity.

verdict.what_management_expects: Not applicable — no separation is described. Management's stated expectations are for the combined group: ~30% of revenue from inverters, BESS and transformers over time; Transcon margins rising toward 20-25% EBITDA as mix shifts to MV/HV/EHV with 7x-10x fixed-asset turns; cross-sell synergies lowering customer-acquisition cost; and debt/equity held near 1.0 and debt/EBITDA near 1.5 through the capex cycle.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe Power Mech Projects separating, demerging or spinning off any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no NCLT filing, no record date, no share-entitlement ratio, and no management discussion of hiving off a division on any of the six calls (May 2025 through May 2026) or in either filing (postal ballot of 10 November 2025 and AGM notice of 8 August 2026). The only occurrences of the words 'merger/demerger, sale of division/undertaking' are inside the standard corporate-action adjustment clause of the proposed 'Power Mech Projects Limited -Employee Stock Option Plan -2026' (10,00,000 options, of which up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees, 3.16%–3.19% of capital on a fully diluted basis), which merely says options would be re-priced fairly if such an action ever occurred; it is boilerplate, not a plan. What the texts actually show is the opposite of separation — consolidation and the use of subsidiaries/SPVs inside one listed entity: the Transmission/Electrical division was wound down and its portfolio 'shifted' into the Civil business while a new BOP EPC vertical was added (May 2026); a 100% subsidiary, PM Green, was incorporated for the 250 MW / 1,000 MWh West Bengal BESS BOO project (INR 800 crore capex, INR 103 crore/year over 15 years, INR 1,563 crore, 51% Power Mech-led consortium, 16–18% equity IRR) which was later cancelled by the West Bengal State Electricity department; MDO assets sit in SPVs (Tasra SPV carrying INR 400 crore of coal-handling-plant and railway-siding capex, KBP raising a INR 256 crore term loan, the INR 690–700 crore washery built in Power Mech's own books) and riverbed-mineral/sand mines sit in LLPs taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated effective tax rate to 28–29%. Portfolio pruning that did happen was order-book, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders (Kawai, Tiroda, Mundra) were removed by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi job, and management said it is 'not showing interest' in new water projects, with the UP Jal Jeevan Mission book run down to about INR 900 crore pending central funding. Management's stated strategic direction is to concentrate the same listed company on power, O&M, BOP EPC and MDO (visibility to FY30, 12.3% FY26 EBITDA rising toward 14% by FY30) — not to separate anything. If a separation exists, it is documented somewhere outside the material supplied here.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces: across CALL Feb 2025, CALL May 2025, CALL Aug 2025, CALL Nov 2025, CALL Feb 2026 and CALL May 2026 no analyst asks about a demerger and no manager raises one; the only corporate-structure questions concern succession (Rohit Sajja's induction to the Board, May 2025) and fund-raising (QIP of INR 240 crore, borrowing limit raised from INR 5,000 crore to INR 7,500 crore in the November 2025 postal ballot). The two filings in the window are an ESOP-2026 postal ballot (10 November 2025, voting 21 November–20 December 2025, with a 1%-of-capital grant resolution) and the 27th AGM notice (8 August 2026, meeting 17 September 2026) re-tabling the same ESOP plus a INR 1.50 dividend, independent-director appointment and director remuneration — none of which mention a separation. The nearest thing to a structural change evolves as consolidation: PM Green is created for BESS (disclosed CALL Feb 2026), the BESS order is then cancelled (CALL May 2026), and the Electrical/Transmission division is declared 'over' and merged into Civil while BOP EPC is created as the new vertical (CALL Nov 2025 signalling, confirmed CALL May 2026).

points.point: The closest actual restructuring is internal consolidation, not separation: the Transmission/Electrical segment was discontinued and absorbed into the Civil division, with BOP EPC created as the replacement reporting vertical.
points.quote: No, it is a different business because, actually, earlier the Transmission division used to do the transmission erection of the lines and other things. That business is over now.

points.point: Management explicitly folded the electrical/T&D portfolio into civil rather than separating it, and added BOP EPC as a new line of activity.
points.quote: So, now we shifted that entire portfolio to the civil business, and we added a new line of activity of BOP EPC business.

points.point: New energy-transition activity was housed in a wholly owned subsidiary (PM Green) kept inside the group, described as a cautious experiment, not a business being carved out.
points.quote: So , we have incorporated a 100% subsidiary as a PM Green for this, and this is a small attempt we to see where the renewable segment fits into the Power Mech's vision of sustained growth and margins.

points.point: MDO assets are held in SPVs within the consolidated group, with capex split between the Tasra SPV and Power Mech standalone - a financing structure, not a separation.
points.quote: And in TASRA SPV, INR 400 crores of Capex Tasra Coal Handling Plant and railway siding is added.

points.point: Riverbed-mineral/sand-mine operations run through LLP entities taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated tax rate to 28-29% - the only structure-driven economic friction management quantified.
points.quote: The exceptional revenue generat ed from the Riverbed Minerals business was booked through L LP. Where applicable tax rate is 35%, compared to 25% at the company level .

points.point: Portfolio pruning that did occur was contractual, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders were removed from the order book by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi package.
points.quote: So, we have taken a djustment of non moving FGD orders – after discussion and negotiations with the client.

points.point: Management said it is stepping back from the water/Jal Jeevan Mission business to concentrate on power and O&M - a reallocation of bidding focus, with no entity-level separation proposed.
points.quote: As of now, we are not showing interest, ma'am, because the power orders, we are getting more power orders.

points.point: The only 'demerger / sale of division' language in the filings is the standard option-adjustment clause of the proposed PMPL ESOP-2026 (10,00,000 options, up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees), appearing identically in both the 10 November 2025 postal ballot and the 8 August 2026 AGM notice; it is contingent boilerplate, not an announced transaction.

verdict.rationale: The premise of a separation does not hold on these texts: the only corporate restructuring Rubicon Research Ltd. has proposed in this 36-month window is a consolidation, not a spin-off — the fast-track amalgamation of its wholly owned subsidiary Kia Health Tech Private Limited (CIN U24239MH2021PTC364174, incorporated July 19, 2021, formerly KIA Biopharma Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) into Rubicon under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013, with Appointed Date April 1, 2026. Kia is a pre-revenue vehicle: as on March 31, 2025 its net worth was ₹815.80 lakhs on total revenue of Nil, against Rubicon's net worth of ₹66,778.57 lakhs on revenue of ₹1,09,352.40 lakhs; Kia was incorporated solely to set up a pharmaceuticals manufacturing plant at Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra, which it is still 'setting up'. The stated reasons are entirely consolidation logic: the two companies are 'engaged in similar activities', so merging gives 'business synergy and pooling of their resources into a single entity', the 'usual economies of a centralized and a large company, including elimination of duplicate work, reduction in overheads', and a 'significant reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances'. Two reasons are more concrete — 'greater efficiency in cash management… and unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined business' to fund organic and inorganic growth, and augmenting 'the manufacturing footprint and capabilities of Rubicon, by increasing the scale of manufacturing operations and bettering capacity utilisation', thereby 'rationalising the number of vendors, aggregating the purchase quantity and managing the procurement supply chain'. The Feb 3, 2026 exchange filing compressed all of this to one line: 'Proposed merger of Kia with the Company will ensure operational synergies.' Mechanically it is a non-event for holders: no shares are issued and no consideration is payable, Rubicon's and its nominees' shares in Kia are cancelled, the shareholding pattern and voting rights are unchanged, Kia 'shall stand dissolved without being wound-up', Rubicon's authorised capital rises from ₹23,89,90,000 to ₹40,69,90,000 (Kia's 1,68,00,000 ₹10 shares split into 16,80,00,000 Re-1 shares and merged in), and Kia's accumulated business losses and unabsorbed depreciation carry forward to Rubicon. Nobody external asked for it — no investor, lender or partner raised it on any of the three calls, and management never mentioned Kia, the merger or any separation on any call; the only adjacent commentary is the capacity narrative (own-manufacturing constraints forcing outsourcing, Pithampur acquired June 2025 for ₹149 crores, ramp-up guided to Q1 CY27), which runs in the same direction of pulling manufacturing in-house.
verdict.evolution: Nothing appeared on the Nov 13, 2025 call (the first post-IPO call) — Kia was never named. The idea surfaces only in filings: the Board granted in-principle approval on Feb 3, 2026, the same day as the Q3 FY26 call, on which management discussed Pithampur, R&D productivity, Dr. Pradnya Saravade's appointment and General Atlantic nominee Anand Agarwal's resignation, but said nothing about the merger. The Board then approved the actual Scheme on July 20, 2026 (Appointed Date April 1, 2026), filed it with BSE/NSE for disclosure only on July 22, 2026 (exempt from Reg 37 NOC as a WOS-into-parent merger) and with the RoC Navi Mumbai on August 3, 2026; the May 29, 2026 Q4 call likewise carried no mention. Shareholders approved it at the 27th AGM on August 26, 2026 with 99.4482% in favour (14,67,54,654 for vs 8,14,232 against), and the Q1 FY27 results of August 14, 2026 confirmed no accounting effect yet as the Scheme is not effective.

Kia ceases to exist — dissolved without winding up, no consideration, no shareholding or voting change.

verdict.rationale: Across these texts there is no demerger or spin-off of a business line at all — no scheme of arrangement exists; the only separation Puravankara actually executed is the outright sale of 100% of a wholly-owned commercial SPV, Purva Ruby Properties Private Limited, to Prishal Office Parks III Private Limited (owned by ICICI Prudential Office Yield Optimiser Fund – AIF II, a Category II AIF managed by ICICI Prudential AMC) for ₹145 crore, board-approved 26 June 2026, SPA signed 30 June 2026 and completed 30 September 2026, with the company stating it is 'outside Scheme of Arrangement', not a related-party transaction, and not an 'undertaking' under Section 180(1)(a) so no shareholder approval was needed. The filings size it as immaterial: the subsidiary's turnover of ₹25.38 crore is 1.06% of Puravankara's ₹2,399.01 crore, and its net worth is negative, so its contribution to group net worth is Nil. The calls never name this entity, but they lay out a consistent two-track commercial-assets logic that the sale fits: Puravankara built two Bengaluru commercial assets, Purva Zentech (its share ~6.5 lakh sq ft, a JDA) and Aerocity (2.2–2.3 million sq ft, Phase 1 of 1.2 million sq ft), and from Feb 2025 management said it would exit/strata-sell one while retaining the other for annuity — Abhishek Kapoor: Zentech 'we are evaluating an exit there... we will care of the debt and move ahead', Aerocity 'we intend to hold that asset and build the platform'. The problem the exit solves is explicitly capital and debt, not strategic focus: commercial development carried non-self-liquidating capex debt (debt/sq ft of ₹252 on commercial vs ₹859 on residential at Sept 2025; earlier ₹479 crore of commercial capex debt out of ₹2,800 crore), which management said would be 'paired off' by monetising the sale asset and by converting SBI construction finance on the retained asset into an LRD facility at lower cost. The quantified prize moved up over time: FY25 call put Zentech plus Aerocity surplus at ₹1,870 crore; the May 2026 cash-flow slide values the two commercial assets at ₹2,131 crore of surplus 'if we choose to come exit out of those assets', inside ₹19,290 crore total estimated surplus. The pressure came from analysts and investors (Deepak Purswani of Svan, Harsh Pathak of Emkay/Motilal, Chintan Mehta of Puniska Family Office repeatedly pressing on net debt of ₹2,825–2,949 crore, 1.68–1.7x gearing, interest of ₹600 crore and when rentals/monetisation would arrive) and from lenders/partners — SBI construction finance to be refinanced as LRD, HDFC Capital's ₹1,150 crore payable-when-able platform at 16–17% with a 12-month lock-in now beginning to be repaid (₹110 crore), and Zentech being a JDA where only Puravankara's share could be sold. Alongside this, the only other corporate separation/consolidation in the filings is the opposite direction: the 12 Feb 2026 merger of IBID Home Private Limited (WATABID.COM) into Purva Woodworks Private Limited, whose stated rationale is to 'salvage and optimize the substantial investment made in IBID', expand Woodworks' market reach and strengthen its competitiveness through digital enablement.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced in the Feb 2025 call, where Abhishek Kapoor first split the commercial portfolio — exit Zentech (a JDA), hold Aerocity and 'build the platform'; the Jun 2025 (Q4FY25) call restated it as a 'dual' lease-and-sale strategy, 'primarily sales as of now', with ₹1,870 crore of surplus from the two assets. Aug 2025 reported ~15–20% of the asset monetised plus the IKEA LOI (80,000 sq ft at ₹150/sq ft carpet) and Ashish Puravankara's three-bucket debt framing in which the sale asset's debt 'should be paired off automatically'; Nov 2025 made the split explicit — 'we are planning to sell this project' while Aerocity is 'planning to retain and lease it out', with the SBI loan to convert to LRD. Feb 2026 showed execution (127,000 sq ft sold, IKEA ~90,000 sq ft leased, OC by end-March, ~₹200 crore combined annuity when fully leased) and the same board meeting (12 Feb 2026) approved the unrelated IBID–Woodworks merger; May 2026 framed the two commercial assets as a ₹2,131 crore optional exit alongside FY27 guidance of ₹11,200 crore presales and ₹750 crore debt reduction. Only then did it become a corporate separation: board approval 26 June 2026, SPA 30 June 2026, connected documents 6 July 2026, a 30-day slip announced 11 August 2026 for pending CP documents, and completion of the 100% transfer on 30 September 2026 for ₹145 crore.

points.quote: So all these -- both the assets of Aerocity and Zentech once fully leased, will set us a rental of close to around INR200 crores annuity.

points.quote: After that, we have two commercial assets. If we choose to come exit out of those assets, what kind of surplus we're going to generate.

points.quote: On the balance sheet front, we are targeting a debt reduction of approximately INR 750 crores for FY26-27, excluding any incremental borrowing undertaken for strategic business development opportunities.

points.quote: However, financial statement of Starworth is currently separately published and uploaded on our website.

points.quote: the transfer of   the entire equity shareholding of the Company in Purva Ruby Properties Private Limited  as per the transaction documents  in relation to the Share Purchase Agreement (“SPA”)  has been completed today i.e., September 30, 2026 .

verdict.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of Sanofi India Limited's consumer healthcare (CHC) business into Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India Limited (SCHIL), done under a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Mumbai bench of the NCLT and effective 1st June 2024, leaving the prescription-pharma business behind in Sanofi India and giving SCHIL a 'dedicated focus on the Consumer Healthcare sector' 'in alignment with Sanofi's global strategy'. Management's stated case is that the four legacy brands carried into SCHIL — Avil (number one by volume in its category), Allegra (number three by value), Combiflam (number five) and DePURA (top five in Vitamin D) — were being run inside a pharma operating model that could not fund them: 'a typical pharma approach... more about winning with patented formulations, very prescription driven, patented brands funding new launches, looking at disease and therapy areas and, more importantly, the investments on brands on low single digit.' Inside the pharma company the cash was being recycled into patented launches, so advertising and promotion (ANP) sat at 'very low single digit' and the plan post-separation is to take it to 'mid-teens'; Himanshu Bakshi said plainly that this 'was the whole case of separation which would have led to this business as a standalone growing much faster than what it was in the past.' He quantified the neglect: before the demerger only two of the brands, Allegra and DePURA, got any HCP work, there was 'no work with consumers, nothing on point of sale,' and Combiflam had not been detailed to doctors 'for the last 15 years' yet still ranked top five — evidence, in his telling, of brand equity that investment could unlock. The problem the separation solves is therefore capital-allocation and model mismatch: the standalone entity can chase self-choice/self-medication demand (3 in 10 Indians had an allergy episode in six months, 9 in 10 a pain episode, 7 in 10 are Vitamin D deficient, 53 million people searching health online, roughly 1 in 4 self-medicating, 15% asking the pharmacist) with a 'true FMCH model' of brand building, direct retail coverage and HCP reach rather than a prescription-only one. Management says the standalone is genuinely autonomous — 'complete ownership of the entire P&L,' India-First initiatives, an in-house AI creative team, an independent supply chain with 'almost 100%' of production in India, and no reliance on global supply — while still drawing on Opella's R&D and scale. The economics presented at the first investor meet: close to ₹880 crore turnover, profit from operations near 37%, ROCE 62.5%, and 2025 revenue +21%, operating profit +13%, PAT +33%; separation and listing costs ran to ₹70 million of demerger expense and ₹77 million of listing-formality expense in 9M 2024 (with a ₹66 million provision reversal in 2025), and voluntary recalls of Depura Adult, Depura Kids, Allegra Suspension and Combiflam Suspension cost a further ₹108 million and knocked out roughly a year of domestic sales before all four were relaunched by Q3 2025. No investor, lender or commercial partner is named anywhere in these texts as having asked for the separation; it is presented throughout as a parent-driven global strategic decision.
verdict.evolution: The record here contains only one call, the first-ever institutional investor meet on 24th March 2026, so the idea does not surface call-by-call: it is reconstructed retrospectively, with Bakshi framing the meet as the first conversation 'over the last two years a lot has happened.' The filings date the decision earlier — the NCLT-sanctioned Scheme became effective 1st June 2024, with demerger and listing costs booked across 2024 and a ₹66 million demerger-provision reversal in the nine months to 30th September 2025 (filed 12th November 2025). The plan then changed ownership rather than content: on 30th April 2025 Sanofi closed the sale of a 50% controlling stake in Opal JVco S.a.r.l (Opella) to Clayton, Dubilier & Rice Fund XII, keeping 48.2% with Bpifrance at 1.8%, so SCHIL's ultimate parent became Opal JVco — a change Bakshi listed on 24th March 2026 alongside the demerger, the listing, the recalls and the rebuild of the organisation. By the March 2026 meet the stated rationale had hardened into a three-lever execution plan (2x HCP reach, scaled consumer engagement, 2x direct retail coverage, targeted within 2026), with the scope question — products marketed in India but still outside the listed entity — left explicitly open and 'the decision is to continue with what we have right now.'

points.point: Bakshi framed the whole purpose of carving the business out of Sanofi as reigniting profitable growth in a division he says was underexploited inside the pharma company.
points.quote: I think when we took over this business from Sanofi, I think we had a single minded objective, which was all about reigniting profitable growth because this was a vertical or division which had immense opportunity in the waiting.

points.point: He named the pre-demerger operating model explicitly — patented, prescription-led, with patented brands funding new launches and brand investment at low single digits — as the thing the separation was meant to escape.
points.quote: Of course, a typical pharma approach which was there in the past, which was more about winning with patented formulations, very prescription driven, patented brands funding new launches, looking at disease and therapy areas and , more importantly, the investments on brands on low single digit.

points.point: The core financial mechanic of the separation: lifting ANP spend from very low single digit to mid-teens, which he called the case for separating.
points.quote: And that was the whole case of separation which would have led to this business as a standalone growing much faster than what it was in the past.

points.point: Quantified the neglect under the old structure — only two of four brands got HCP support, with nothing spent on consumers or point of sale.
points.quote: Only two brands, Allegra and DePURA, where we did some work with healthcare professionals.

points.point: The starkest evidence he gave for latent brand equity: Combiflam held a top-five position despite 15 years without any HCP detailing.
points.quote: We all heard of Combiflam as a brand like and when I joined this business I was amazed to know that we had not gone to the HCPs to speak about Combiflam for the last 15 years and still continued to be amongst the top five brands.

points.point: Standalone scale and returns disclosed at the first investor meet: roughly ₹880 crore revenue, ~37% profit from operations, 62.5% ROCE, with Avil #1 by volume, Allegra #3 by value, Combiflam #5 and DePURA top five in Vitamin D.
points.quote: So , close to 880 crore turnover that we have. If you look at our Profit from Operations, it's close to 37 %, ROCE of 62.5 %.

points.point: First full year of the rebuilt standalone delivered double-digit growth on all three lines, which management presented as validation of the separation.
points.quote: Our Revenue from Operations has gone up by 21%, Operating Prof it up by 13% and a 33% increase on PAT.

points.point: The demand rationale: a shift to self-care and self-medication that a prescription-only pharma model could not address — 53 million people researching health online, 1 in 4 self-medicating, 15% asking the pharmacist.
points.quote: Almost 1 in every 4 consumers are self -medicating today .

points.point: Asked how empowered the Indian entity really is, he claimed full P&L ownership for global and local brands with decisions taken in-country, plus an independent supply chain with almost all production in India.
points.quote: There is complete ownership of the entire P&L be it any brand, be it global brands, be it country brands.

points.point: Pressed by Monica of SBI Mutual Fund on whether India is a growth or profitability outpost for Opella, he said growth and penetration, with the global group aligned.
points.quote: So, growth is the agenda for India, very clearly.

points.point: Saurabh Kapadia of Sundaram Mutual Fund asked about Indian products left outside the listed entity; management said the same team markets them on a cross-charge and the perimeter stays as-is for now, with group discussions ongoing.
points.quote: On your second question, which is about the other products which are not a part of the listed entity, yes, these discussions continue to happen with the group.

points.point: The three post-separation growth levers and their 2026 timing: double face-to-face doctor reach, add 50,000 HCPs digitally, and double direct retail coverage.
points.quote: So, we plan to double our doctor reach face to face.

points.point: A pending regulatory catalyst management says would amplify the FMCH model: an OTC policy still in the works, which would permit direct consumer advertising for brands like Allegra.
points.quote: So, I think the biggest unlock will be direct consumer communication, you know, the moment OTC comes in, and then that gives us the freedom to really, again, build the category from where we want to today, which is today a constraint as we speak.

points.point: The filings state the legal mechanics and the parent's stated reason: a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai, effective 1st June 2024, separating SCHIL from Sanofi India Limited so it can focus solely on consumer healthcare.
points.quote: This demerger, executed under the Scheme of Arrangement, was sanctioned by the Mumbai bench of the National Company La w Tribunal and became effective on 1st June 2024. In alignment with Sanofi's global strategy, SCHIL is now operating independently, with a dedicated focus on the Consumer Healthcare sector.

points.point: The cost of separating, booked as exceptional items: ₹70 million of demerger expenses, ₹77 million of listing costs and ₹108 million of recall costs in 9M 2024, plus a ₹29 million intangible written off that came in under the Scheme and a ₹66 million provision reversal in 2025.
points.quote: Exceptional item for the nine months ended September 30, 2024, was Rs. 255 million,  which include d product recall related cost towards Sales return and inventory write off Rs.108 million, expenses towards listing formalities amounting to Rs.77 million and demerger expenses amounting to Rs.70 million.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence supplied there is no demerger or business separation at Trident Limited to reconstruct: the only documents on file are two Regulation 30 intimations of the same February 09, 2026 board meeting (11:30 A.M. to 03:15 P.M. IST), and no earnings-call transcripts were provided at all. That board approved two distinct, small-scale corporate actions, neither framed as a separation of an existing business. First, the incorporation of a new domestic wholly owned subsidiary, to be named Trident Global Industries Limited (TGIL) 'or such other name as may be approved by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs,' in India, classified under 'Textile Industry/ Trading of Goods and Services,' whose stated purpose is 'to enhance brand presence, brand-building initiatives, selling and marketing for Trident products in overseas markets, with a special emphasis on the U.S. market' — Trident will subscribe to 100% of its initial paid-up capital in cash at face value, so this is a forward-looking distribution/branding vehicle, not a carve-out of an existing division. Second, the disinvestment of its entire stake in MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED, a non-material wholly owned subsidiary with NIL turnover acquired only during the current financial year, sold for INR 1,00,000 (10,000 equity shares at face value of INR 10 each) to Trident Global Corp Limited, an associate and promoter-group entity — a related party transaction the company says was 'made at fair value on arm's length basis.' The filing expressly answers 'Not Applicable' to whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement and to the Regulation 37A compliance question, and 'Not Applicable' to slump-sale disclosures, which means the company itself disclaims any scheme-based separation. No revenue, net worth, margin, capital-allocation, valuation or focus rationale is given for either step, because the divested entity had none to disclose. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for anything, and no management commentary, strategy framing or financial target accompanies these actions in the texts provided.
verdict.evolution: There is no call-by-call evolution to trace: the transcript section reads 'no transcripts on file,' so the idea's surfacing and development were never captured in any earnings call in this record. Both documents are dated February 09, 2026 and are duplicates of one another — the same cover letter, Annexure A (incorporation of TGIL) and Annexure B (disinvestment of MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED) filed under two event headings, 'Diversification/Disinvestment' and 'Incorporation.' The only sequencing visible is internal to that single board meeting, where the U.S.-focused marketing subsidiary was approved alongside the transfer of the dormant MYTRIDENT.COM vehicle to promoter-group entity Trident Global Corp Limited, effective the same day. Nothing in the file shows how the plan changed over time, because only one day's disclosure exists.

points.point: The February 09, 2026 board approved a new Indian wholly owned subsidiary whose entire stated purpose is overseas brand-building and marketing of Trident products, explicitly weighted to the U.S. market — a sales/branding vehicle rather than a separation of any existing business.
points.quote: Incorporation of a New Domestic Wholly Owned Subsidiary (DWOS), to enhance brand presence, brand-building initiatives, selling and marketing for Trident products in overseas markets, with a special emphasis on the U.S. market.

points.point: The new entity is named Trident Global Industries Limited (TGIL), not yet incorporated, proposed to be in India, and classified under textiles and trading of goods and services; it needs only MCA approval.
points.quote: Trident Global Industries Limited [TGIL] or such other name as may be approved by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

points.point: Trident funds TGIL entirely itself, taking 100% of the initial paid-up share capital in cash at face value, so no partner, investor or swap counterparty is involved.

points.point: The same board approved exiting MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED entirely, with the subsidiary ceasing to be a DWOS on the same day the definitive share purchase agreement was executed, February 09, 2026.
points.quote: Disinvestment of entire stake in MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED, a Domestic Wholly Owned Subsidiary (DWOS) of the Company.

points.point: The company pre-empts any materiality concern by stating the divested entity was not a material subsidiary, which is why no financial impact is quantified.
points.quote: MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED was not the material subsidiary of the Trident Limited.

points.point: No turnover, revenue, income or net-worth contribution is disclosed because the entity had none and had only just been acquired within the same financial year — it was effectively a dormant shell.

The buyer, Trident Global Corp Limited, is an associate and promoter-group entity, making this a related party transaction that the company asserts was done at fair value on an arm's length basis.

points.quote: Not Applicable

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing was stated for either entity — no margin, capital, valuation or focus expectation appears. The only forward-looking claim is for the new subsidiary TGIL: enhanced brand presence, brand-building, selling and marketing of Trident products in overseas markets, especially the U.S. For MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED, a NIL-turnover non-material shell sold at face value, no expected benefit is articulated at all.

verdict.rationale: There is no separation in these documents — the corporate action is the reverse: a merger by absorption of TPL Plastech Limited (a 74.86% listed subsidiary, FY26 consolidated turnover Rs.422.66 cr, net profit Rs.29.07 cr, net worth Rs.168.90 cr) into Time Technoplast Limited (FY26 turnover Rs.6,114.40 cr, PAT Rs.468.72 cr, net worth Rs.4,166.21 cr), with Appointed Date April 1, 2026 under Sections 230-232. The stated reasons are: integrating the manufacturing units and product lines of both companies so each distinct product category sits in a dedicated unit inside TTL; rationalised product-focused unit-wise operations to push product development, innovation and manufacturing/operational efficiency; simplification of the group structure and reduction in related party transactions, thereby lowering compliance and administrative burden; pooling of financial, managerial and technical resources for optimal utilisation and cost efficiencies; strengthening the financial position of the consolidated entity; and operational and financial synergies for long-term sustainable growth. The two businesses overlap heavily — TPL makes jerry cans, drums and IBCs, all of which TTL also makes — and management had described their plants as geographically complementary (TPL at Ratlam, Bhuj, Vizag, Dahej, Silvassa plus a new Lote-Parshuram/Chiplun unit of Rs.30-35 cr capex targeting Rs.100 cr revenue), with TPL contributing only 8-9% of TTL's revenue though at a higher ROCE (22%+ vs TTL's 20%). The logic is the same one Bharat Vageria had been applying to plants for 18 months: why run two plants, two administrative costs, two commercial managers and two quality managers when one bigger unit can do it. Nobody is recorded as asking for the merger — no investor, lender or partner is named; it was board-initiated (in-principle Aug 26, 2026, scheme approved Sept 29, 2026 on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and the Committee of Independent Directors). TPL's 25.14% public shareholders receive 403 TTL shares of Re.1 for every 1,000 TPL shares of Rs.2, i.e. 79,01,516 new TTL shares, taking TTL from 49,36,35,379 to 50,15,36,895 shares and diluting promoters from 47.47% to 46.73%; the ratio came from registered valuer Nitesh Chaturvedi with a fairness opinion from Axial Capital Private Limited. The only genuine separation question in three years of calls was asked in May 2025 and refused: management said a separate composite-cylinder company was not advisable at Rs.500 cr of composite revenue and could only be revisited at Rs.2,500 cr, because the group was moving the other way — consolidating.
verdict.evolution: Feb 12, 2025: consolidation enters the narrative two ways — a 'strategic decision to consolidate its products and the manufacturing units,' and the NED Energy / Power Build merger then in process, justified as administrative and marketing cost saving. May 28, 2025: that merger is reported done, and when an investor asks for a separate composite/hydrogen SBU, management refuses it outright and says it is instead 'consolidating our companies in operations.' Aug 12, 2025 through Feb 13, 2026 and May 29, 2026: the theme stays entirely at plant and product level — Jambusar folded into Ahmedabad, Daman's 480 cascades moved into the new 1,080-cascade Morai plant, Gummidipoondi split by product, with the 'why two administrative costs' argument spelled out in February 2026 — and no entity-level separation or merger is ever mentioned on a call. The TPL Plastech merger appears only after the last transcript: board in-principle approval on Aug 26, 2026, flagged at the AGM on Sept 22, 2026 as 'consolidation of Group Structure,' and the scheme plus swap ratio approved on Sept 29, 2026.

points.point: Board in-principle approval (Aug 26, 2026) frames the deal as group-structure consolidation that re-arranges the two companies' plants and product lines so each product category gets its own dedicated unit inside TTL, with Appointed Date April 1, 2026.
points.quote: The proposed merger is expected to facilitate consolidation of the group structure, and re-arrangement of the manufacturing units and product lines of TPL Plastech Limited and Time Technoplast Limited, enabling each distinct product category to be handled by a dedicated unit within Time Technoplast Limited.

points.point: Rationale (a) in the Sept 29, 2026 Regulation 30 annexure: integration of manufacturing units and product lines, each distinct product category handled by a dedicated unit within TTL.
points.quote: integration of the manufacturing units and product lines of both companies, enabling each distinct product category to be handled by a dedicated unit within Time Technoplast Limited;

points.point: Rationale (c): a listed subsidiary generates related-party transactions and duplicate compliance; the merger removes both.
points.quote: simplification of the Group structure and reduction in related party transactions, thereby lowering compliance and administrative burden;

points.point: Rationale (b) and (d)-(f): product-focused unit-wise operations to drive product development and innovation, pooled financial/managerial/technical resources, a stronger consolidated balance sheet and operational and financial synergies.
points.quote: rationalised, product-focused unit-wise operations expected to provide greater impetus to product development, foster innovation, and improve overall manufacturing and operational efficiency;

points.point: Consideration is paper, not cash: TPL's 25.14% public holders get 403 TTL shares per 1,000 TPL shares; TTL's own 5,83,96,260 TPL shares are cancelled and TPL is dissolved without winding up. Ratio from registered valuer Nitesh Chaturvedi, fairness opinion from Axial Capital Private Limited.
points.quote: TPL shareholders will receive 403 fully paid-up equity shares of TTL (face value Rs. 1/- each) for every 1,000 fully paid-up equity shares of TPL (face value Rs. 2/- each) held by them.

points.point: Chairman Sanjaya Kulkarni's Sept 22, 2026 AGM speech places the TPL merger in a sequence after the completed NED Energy / Power Build Batteries merger, under the heading 'Consolidation of Group Structure.'
points.quote: the Board has given In-principle approval for the merger of TPL Plastech Limited, our subsidiary, into Time Technoplast Limited, under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013, bringing our group's manufacturing, financial and management resources under a single entity.

points.point: Asked directly whether a separate SBU or company would be carved out for composite/hydrogen/CNG/oxygen, Vageria said no — the group is going the other way, and a separate company for a Rs.500 cr business is financially unjustified; revisit at Rs.2,500 cr.
points.quote: If you ask me the separate company, not now. We can talk about 3 years down the line when the sizable business of more than INR 2,500 crores business, we will have as against current business of INR 500 crores, we can think the separate company. Otherwise, one way, we are consolidating our companies in operations.

points.point: The precedent merger — NED Energy into Power Build Batteries — was justified as same-sector overlap plus team and administrative savings, the identical logic later applied to TPL.
points.quote: one of the subsidiary company, we had an NED Energy Limited and Power Build Batteries Private Limited, a step-down subsidiary, which is now merged because both the companies were in same sector energy storage devices. So there is a kind consolidations of the team: administrative team, marketing that will give the savings.

points.point: The duplicate-overhead argument, given for plants but describing exactly what two companies making the same drums, jerry cans and IBCs cost: double administration, double managers.
points.quote: So why I should have a 2 plants, why I should have a 2 administrative cost? Why I should have a 2 commercial manager, why I should have a 2 quality manager.

points.point: TPL Plastech's scale and quality as of the last discussion of it: ~Rs.450 cr FY26 revenue estimate (actual Rs.422.66 cr), 8-9% of TTL revenue, 20%+ growth, ROCE above TTL's — plus a Rs.30-35 cr Lote-Parshuram/Chiplun IBC unit due in FY27.
points.quote: And I'm glad to tell you their ROCE is also more than us. Our ROCE is 20%, we are doing this year in '25, '26, but they are more than 22% ROCE.

points.point: The two companies' plants were described as deliberately non-overlapping geographically — Ratlam, Bhuj, Vizag for TPL — which is what makes a single-entity, product-dedicated unit map possible.
points.quote: So TPL Plastech will grow separately and definitely continue, because wherever the time is present, the TPL Plastech is not there. And wherever the TPL Plastech is there, time is not there.

points.point: Consolidation named as a formal company decision and an EBITDA growth driver in the final call before the merger surfaced — centralising machinery, cutting overheads and raising ROCE, with Daman's cascade capacity physically folded into Morai.
points.quote: Consolidation of products and unit streamlining products and consolidating units to enhance operational efficiency and reduce overhead costs, lowering manpower costs to strategic work for optimization and process reengineering to eliminate redundancies and improve productivity and automation for cost reduction.

verdict.what_management_expects: One entity, not two: each product category in a dedicated TTL unit; faster product development and innovation; better manufacturing and operational efficiency; a simpler group structure with fewer related-party transactions and lower compliance/admin cost; pooled financial, managerial and technical resources with cost efficiencies; a stronger consolidated financial position; operational and financial synergies. TPL minority holders exchange paper at 403:1,000.
verdict.gaps: No earnings call ever discusses the merger. No quantified synergy, cost saving, EPS/ROCE/margin impact, valuation method, completion timetable, or why TPL's higher-ROCE separate listing was given up.

verdict.rationale: These texts contain no management explanation of the separation. Across the five extractable calls (May 14 2025, Aug 5 2025, Nov 11 2025, Feb 10 2026, May 13 2026) neither Saurabh Mashruwala nor Rishi Shah mentions the demerger and no analyst asks about it; the six earlier calls (Nov 2023–Feb 2025), i.e. exactly the window in which it was conceived and sanctioned, are scanned PDFs with no extractable text. The only description of the separation anywhere in this record is Note 2 to the November 11 2025 results and Price Waterhouse's emphasis paragraph, and both give mechanics, not motive: NCLT (order January 27 2025, modified February 18 2025, received March 7 2025) sanctioned a Scheme of Arrangement under sections 230–232 transferring 'the Renewable Power Undertakings' — 316.60 MW of solar and wind — out of Torrent Power Ltd into Torrent Green Energy Private Limited (TGEPL), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated August 2 2023, on a going concern basis by way of slump sale, appointed date April 1 2024, effective April 1 2025 on ROC filing, with slump-sale consideration of ₹121.56 cr (H1 FY25), ₹186.07 cr (FY25) and ₹694.05 cr (H1 FY26). No tax, lender, partner, valuation or focus reason is stated, and no investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for it. What the filings do establish — without management ascribing it as the reason — is a subsidiary-housed renewable growth vehicle: Renewables is a separate Ind AS 108 segment (Q2 FY26 revenue ₹326.62 cr, result ₹281.37 cr, assets ₹12,172.51 cr, liabilities ₹7,636.35 cr, rising to assets ₹20,479.72 cr and liabilities ₹12,845.37 cr by Sept 30 2026); all new renewable capacity sits in subsidiaries (dozens of Torrent Urja SPVs under TGEPL; the Nov 2025 call notes a 250 MW FDRE LOA won by 'subsidiary of the company'); and the parent funds them by equity and loans (standalone investments in subsidiaries ₹1,655.07 cr at Mar-25 → ₹5,083.14 cr at Sep-25 → ₹12,864.06 cr at Sep-26), against renewable capex of ₹2,500 cr (FY25), ₹7,000–8,000 cr planned and ₹6,500 cr spent (FY26), a 4 GW/₹28,000 cr pipeline inside a ~₹80,000 cr five-year plan, after a maiden ₹3,500 cr QIP. Two further separations sit in the same window: the Power Cable business left the T&D segment on October 16 2024 (₹77 cr non-recurring gain, flagged in the Feb 2026 call), and on March 30 2026 three pumped-storage SPVs were moved under Torrent Energy Storage Solutions Private Limited while UNM Foundation was sold up to promoter Torrent Investments Limited for ₹5,00,000.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces in any call that is readable here: the extractable transcripts begin with Q4 FY25 (May 14 2025), after the Scheme was already effective (April 1 2025), and the Nov 2023, Feb 2024, May 2024, Jul 2024, Nov 2024 and Feb 2025 calls — spanning TGEPL's incorporation (Aug 2 2023), the April 1 2024 appointed date and the January 27 2025 NCLT order — are image-only PDFs. The first and only trace in this record is retrospective: Note 2 and the auditor's emphasis paragraph in the November 11 2025 filing, which also restate the Sept 30 2024 comparatives. The plan's only visible later movement is structural rather than explanatory: the Feb 10 2026 call books the cable-business exit as a prior-year one-off, and the March 30 2026 filings reorganise the pumped-storage SPVs under one holding subsidiary and push UNM Foundation up to the promoter; by the May 13 2026 call management discusses renewables purely as capex and commissioning, never as a separated entity.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not support the premise: across the eight transcripts and three filings, UltraTech never announces, explains or hints at separating, demerging, spinning off or carving out any of its own businesses, and management is repeatedly asked and says the direction of travel is the opposite — consolidation into one entity. The only 'Scheme' of arrangement in the corpus runs inward: the Composite Scheme between Kesoram Industries and UltraTech (NCLT Kolkata 14 Nov 2024, Mumbai 26 Nov 2024, effective 1 Mar 2025, appointed date 1 Apr 2024) separated Kesoram's Cement Business Division out of Kesoram and vested it in UltraTech, i.e. UltraTech is the acquirer, not the separator. On the acquired 81.49%-owned (later 74.99%) subsidiary The India Cements Ltd, management was asked about merging it into UltraTech on four calls (Jul 2025, Jan 2026, May 2026, Jul 2026) and said it stays a separate listed entity for now because of inherited 'donkey's years old' litigation including an ED attachment on a Hyderabad property and financial securities, a large stamp-duty cost on transfer, an unfinished ~INR2,000 crore efficiency capex, and non-core land still to be sold, with the integration journey ending around Q4 FY28. Businesses an investor might expect to be hived off were explicitly ruled out: RMC ('I don't see a need... to monetize it', 477 plants, ~3.5% of volumes), the UBS retail store network ('listing it as a separate entity, no, there's no plan like that'), and Cables & Wires, which is a new INR1,800 crore in-house growth venture launching Q3 FY27, not a separation. The only genuine disposals are small and framed as deleveraging/portfolio clean-up, not a strategic separation: India Cements' Indonesian coal mining company (sold, proceeds to cut ICL debt), ICL land parcels (INR500 crore minimum expected, INR200-250 crore realised by Jan 2026), the sale of ICL subsidiaries Coromandel Electric/Travels/Sugars and Raasi Cement up to 28 Mar 2025, the OFS/open-market sale of 5.89% + 0.60% of ICEM purely to meet minimum public shareholding, and the 16 Jan 2026 sale of non-material subsidiary Bhumi Resources (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. with its non-operating subsidiaries to Celestial Energy Pte. Ltd. for USD 107 (turnover nil, net worth USD 104, completion by 31 Mar 2026, buyer not a promoter-group entity). No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for a separation; the only outside pressure cited is SEBI's minimum-public-shareholding rule on ICEM and investor questions about ring-fencing UltraTech's balance sheet from group items (RCB, Vodafone Idea), which the CFO answered by saying not a penny has moved out.
verdict.evolution: Jan 2025 and Jul 2025: asked about the 'end plan' for India Cements, Daga says it is too premature, the company will stay separate while it is cleaned up, and a merger would carry heavy stamp duty. Jan 2026: the question narrows to 'simplifying the structure' and he adds the ED attachment and non-core land sales as blockers, while confirming the Indonesian coal company has been sold; May 2026 he says UltraTech will not take legal risk onto the parent board until those decades-old cases close. Jul 2026: the merger question returns and he sets the end-state at roughly Q4 FY28 after the capex and land disposals — so the arc moves toward absorbing a subsidiary, never toward separating a UltraTech business; the only separation-shaped documents are the inward Kesoram demerger scheme and the 16 Jan 2026 sale of a nil-revenue Singapore shell.

points.point: The only Scheme of Arrangement in the corpus is a demerger of Kesoram's cement business INTO UltraTech (appointed date 1 Apr 2024, effective 1 Mar 2025) — UltraTech is the recipient, not the separating party.
points.quote: Upon the Scheme becoming effective and with effect from the Appointed Date, the Cement Business Division of Kesoram ("the Demerged Undertaking") as defined in the Scheme stands transferred to and vested in the Company as a going concern.

points.point: Asked whether India Cements would be merged into UltraTech or kept separate, management said the decision was open, flagged stamp duty as the deterrent, and kept ICL a separate entity.
points.quote: As of now, it will continue as a separate entity.

points.point: The 'separation' activity at India Cements is non-core asset disposal and the sale of its Indonesian coal company, to keep debt under control — not a business separation.
points.quote: Noncore there are land parcels essentially . We just sold off the coal mining company in Indonesia.

points.point: Legal attachments, including an ED case over a Hyderabad property and financial securities, are the gating item before any further structural step.
points.quote: We are seeking legal opinion what will be the implications of that case, and then only we'll take a decision further.

points.point: On merging ICL, Daga cited inherited litigation and refused to put the parent at risk, pointing to further integration only once cleared.
points.quote: Once we are convinced that there is no risk to us. We could look at the next phase of integration.

points.point: RMC was explicitly ruled out as a monetisation or separation candidate despite 477 plants and being only ~3.5% of volumes.
points.quote: I don't see a need or don't see that thought process as of now to monetize it.

points.point: The remaining steps before any ICL merger are the capex programme and non-core land disposals, with completion expected around Q4 FY28.
points.quote: There is a capex program underway, which we mentioned has to get completed.

points.point: The UBS retail store network is monetised through cement throughput, with no plan to list or separate it.
points.quote: If you're talking about listing it as a separate entity, no, there's no plan like that.

points.point: The Indonesian coal asset exit at ICL was framed purely as debt reduction for the subsidiary.
points.quote: As a post -balance sheet event in India Cem ents, we have exited the coal assets held in Indonesia and the cash flows that will be realized from the sale of these assets will help reduce their debt.

points.point: The 16 Jan 2026 filing is the only outright divestment by UltraTech itself: a nil-revenue Singapore shell with non-operating subsidiaries sold for USD 107, with no strategic rationale given.
points.quote: We write to inform you that the Company has entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Celestial Energy Pte . Ltd. for sale of its entire stake in Bhumi Resources (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. (non-material subsidiary ) along with its non -operating subsidiaries .

points.point: The ICEM stake sales (5.89% via OFS Aug 2025, 0.60% in Q3 FY26, taking holding to 74.99%) were regulatory float compliance, not a separation of a business.
points.quote: Consequently, ICEM has achieved compliance with the minimum public shareholding requirements prescribed under Rule 19A of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957, read with the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, well within the stipulated period of 12 months from the completion of the Open Offer.

points.point: Cables & Wires is an added adjacency funded with INR1,800 crore of capex against ~INR1 lakh crore of cement capital employed, with all other adjacencies ruled out — the opposite of a separation.
points.quote: Yes, we are not venturing into anything else.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing: no separation economics are given anywhere. The expectations stated are for integration instead — India Cements reaching INR1,000/t EBITDA by Q4 FY28 on ~INR2,000 crore efficiency capex, green power from 3% to 86%, brand migration complete, debt-light at ~0.5x, and eventual merger into UltraTech once litigation and stamp-duty issues clear.
verdict.gaps: Everything: the calls and filings never mention any UltraTech demerger, spin-off, carve-out or listing of a division, nor its rationale, structure, timing or beneficiaries.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain any business separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale of a division, or scheme of arrangement by Aarti Industries Ltd. — so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them, and none should be inferred. The only business actually separated from the group in the record is a small step-down subsidiary: on June 23, 2026 Aarti Corporate Services Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of AIL) sold its entire 100% equity stake in Shanti Intermediates Private Limited for ₹150.18 lakh, and the filing of June 24, 2026 states that Shanti Intermediates thereby ceased to be a step-down subsidiary. The filing gives no rationale whatsoever; it discloses only that the entity was immaterial (total income ₹880.55 lakh, 0.11% of consolidated income, and negative net worth of ₹(147.80) lakh, i.e. (0.02%) of consolidated net worth, per FY26 audited financials), that the buyers were Mr. Vallabh Bachubhai Trada and Ms. Rekha Vallabhbhai Trada, who do not belong to the promoter/promoter group, and that the transaction fell within related party transactions and was done at arm's length; against the question on whether the disposal of an undertaking is outside a Scheme of Arrangement, the Company answered 'N.A', confirming no scheme. None of the six earnings calls (May 2025 through May 2026) mentions Shanti Intermediates, a demerger, a carve-out, a listed spin-off, or any separation of the energy/MMA business from the non-energy base business, even though analysts repeatedly probed the rising weight of energy (MMA was ~40-43% of revenue) — management's answer was always operational portfolio management, i.e. energy settling at 30-40% of the mix as Zone IV non-energy capacity commissions, not a structural separation. The one structural theme in the texts is the opposite direction of the question: new businesses are being built in separate legal vehicles from the start — Augene Chemical Pvt Ltd (the 50-50 JV with UPL/Superform, which management said 'will not consolidate into AIL' at EBITDA and will be reported separately) and Re Aarti Pvt Ltd (plastic chemical recycling, held through the wholly owned subsidiary Aarti Circularity Limited with Re Sustainability). The balance-sheet problem that a separation is often used to solve was instead addressed by two other levers: capex taper (FY26 ₹1,125 crore, FY27 guided ₹700-800 crore) plus the October 2026 enabling approval for up to ₹1,000 crore of equity/equity-linked fund raising (QIP, preferential, private placement), whose stated use of proceeds is pre-payment/repayment of outstanding loans against net debt of ~₹4,300 crore and 3.6x net debt/EBITDA versus a 2.5x target.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced: across the May 8, 2025 (Q4FY25), Aug 1, 2025 (Q1FY26), Nov 7, 2025 (Q2FY26), Feb 3, 2026 (Q3FY26) and May 5, 2026 (Q4FY26) calls — and the Feb 3, 2025 (Q3FY25) call — management discussed Zone IV commissioning, cost optimisation, MMA scale-up, JVs and leverage, but never a demerger or separation of any business, and no analyst asked for one. The only entity-level change appears outside the calls, in the June 24, 2026 filing disclosing that Shanti Intermediates Private Limited was sold on June 23, 2026 and ceased to be a step-down subsidiary, with no reason given. After that, the structural news flow turns to capital raising rather than separation: the Board's October 1, 2026 enabling resolution for up to ₹1,000 crore and the EGM of October 31, 2026, where the Chairman framed the raise and 'subsequent deleveraging, if any' as the value-accretive step. So the plan did not evolve over time — there is no separation plan in these documents to trace.

points.point: Filing dated June 24, 2026: Aarti Corporate Services Ltd (AIL's wholly owned subsidiary) sold its entire 100% stake in Shanti Intermediates Private Limited on June 23, 2026 for ₹150.18 lakh, so that entity ceased to be a step-down subsidiary. This is the only business actually separated in the record, and no rationale is stated anywhere in the filing.
points.quote: With the completion of the aforesaid transactions, Shanti Intermediate Private Limited has ceased to be a step-down subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The same filing shows the divested entity was immaterial — total income ₹880.55 lakh (0.11% of consolidated income) and negative net worth of ₹(147.80) lakh ((0.02%) of consolidated net worth) per FY26 audited accounts — and that the sale was a related-party transaction done at arm's length to two individual buyers outside the promoter group.
points.quote: Transaction fall within related party transactions and same is done at arm's length.

points.quote: whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations.

points.point: The only corporate action with an articulated rationale is the Oct 1, 2026 Board enabling approval and Oct 31, 2026 EGM special resolution for up to ₹1,000 crore of securities (QIP/preferential/private placement), explicitly to repay debt and strengthen the balance sheet — a capital-structure fix rather than a business separation.
points.quote: The Company intends to utilize the proceeds of the Issue (after adjustment of expenses related to the Issue) ("Net Proceeds") towards, inter alia, (i) Pre-Payment and/or Repayment of certain outstanding loans of the Company

points.point: At the Oct 31, 2026 EGM the Chairman, Shri Rajendra V. Gogri, tied the raise to the debt profile and deleveraging, and the MD/CEO said the Company would keep all permissible fund-raising routes open rather than commit to one — again, no mention of separating any business.
points.quote: Your Board of Directors has carefully evaluated the Company’s debt profile and funding options. We are of the firm conviction that this capital raise, and the subsequent deleveraging, if any, is a highly value-accretive step.

points.point: On the Q4FY26 call (May 5, 2026) leverage was discussed as a capex/EBITDA problem — net debt ~₹4,300 crore on FY26 EBITDA of ₹1,172 crore (3.6x) against a 2.5x target, to be fixed by FY27 capex of ₹700-800 crore and rising cash flow — with no suggestion of separating or monetising any business.
points.quote: I think we closed the year at roughly INR 1,172 and our net debt was around INR4,300 crore .

points.point: The closest thing to structural separation is that new ventures sit in separate vehicles from inception: the 50-50 Augene JV (with Superform/UPL, commissioning H1FY27) will be reported separately and will not consolidate into AIL's EBITDA, and management expects JV margins slightly better than AIL's.
points.quote: But from a consolidation point of view, given it is a 50-50 JV, it will not consolidate into AIL.

points.point: Asked by Morgan Stanley whether he was comfortable with energy/MMA becoming an even larger share of the portfolio, the CEO answered with mix management and Zone IV ramp-up — energy settling at 30-40% of the portfolio — not with any plan to separate energy from the specialty base business.
points.quote: We feel MMA will ultimately settle anywhere between 30% to 40% of our portfolio, right, if you take a 2 -3 year’s outloo k and I think we continue to maintain that strategic stance.

points.point: On the Q2FY26 call the CEO said segment exposure is not actively managed and future capital allocation is driven by economic rationale rather than application-segment logic, with focus on medium-ticket projects — the opposite of a portfolio-separation narrative.
points.quote: Frankly, at this point in time, we are not actively managing exposure to a particular application segment, right?

points.point: The circularity business was set up in a separate wholly owned subsidiary, Aarti Circularity Limited, which then formed the Re Aarti JV with Re Sustainability (₹100 crore committed, ₹50 crore each; 100 TPD in 18 months, 500 TPD by 2030) — again new-entity creation, not separation of an existing business.
points.quote: Re Sustainability and Recycling Private Limited; and Aarti Circularity Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of AIL, have joined hands to establish transformative first-of-its-kind India joint venture company for driving the development of plastic material recycling facilities which will use advanced chemical recycling technology.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is said, because no separation is announced. The only stated structural expectations: the ₹1,000 crore raise plus deleveraging is 'highly value-accretive', widens the investor base and improves share liquidity; the 50-50 Augene JV will be reported separately, outside AIL's consolidated EBITDA, and should run at margins slightly better than AIL's.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no demerger, scheme, carve-out or listed separation exists here. The Shanti Intermediates sale filing gives no rationale, valuation basis, or who asked; calls never mention it.
