verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not the Visa & Consular or Digital segment discussed on the calls, but the Joint Liability Group (JLG) financial-lending business housed inside Atyati Technologies Private Limited (ATPL), a step-down subsidiary of BLS that became part of the group only on July 2, 2026 — after the last transcript on record (May 20, 2026). On September 28, 2026 ATPL's board approved a Business Transfer Agreement to sell and transfer the JLG Business Undertaking on a going-concern basis, as a slump sale, to TVAM Technologies Private Limited for Rs. 59,49,000, subject to post-closing adjustments based on closing accounts, and subject to lender, regulatory and other consents, expected to close in about 90 days. The only reason management has given anywhere in these texts is in the filing itself: the transaction 'forms part of the Company's broader business re-organisation and operational restructuring initiatives' and is 'intended to streamline business operations, optimise deployment of resources and enable greater strategic and operational focus through an appropriate business structure.' The numbers cited are that JLG turnover was Rs. 100.56 crores, i.e. 26.8% of ATPL's total FY2025-26 turnover, while its net worth, computed as at July 1, 2026 (no separate March 31, 2026 net worth exists), was only Rs. 59.49 lakhs, or 0.9% of ATPL's total net worth — so a quarter of ATPL's revenue sits on under 1% of its net worth, and the consideration is set exactly at that book net worth. ATPL keeps its Business Correspondent services for banks for last-mile connectivity and its technology solutions; only the micro-lending book goes. The buyer is a related party — 'TVAM is a Private Company in which a director of ATPL is a Director and Member' — and the company states the deal is on arm's length terms; TVAM is not a promoter/promoter-group entity. It is not a Scheme of Arrangement, Regulation 37A does not apply since the transferor is a step-down subsidiary, and there is no change in BLS's shareholding pattern. No lender, investor or partner is named as having asked for it; the filing frames it purely as internal reorganisation.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces on the earnings calls: across all ten transcripts (Feb 2024 through May 20, 2026) neither Atyati, the JLG lending book, nor any divestment is mentioned, and the only structural logic management ever articulates is the opposite direction — the Aug 6, 2024 call explains the BLS E-Services IPO as wanting to run the two businesses separately and keep visa cash out of digital, and on Feb 12, 2025 management flatly rejected a suggestion to spin off the Digital business, calling it not a drag. The restructuring instead appears only in filings, and in escalating steps: Nov 11, 2025 (board approves strike-off of dormant WOS Reired BLS International), Aug 17-18, 2026 (Turkish step-down subsidiary BLS International Vize Hizmetleri merged into iDATA 'to align the business synergies of step down subsidiaries'), then Sept 28-29, 2026, when ATPL's board approves the JLG slump sale to TVAM — within three months of ATPL joining the group on July 2, 2026. The plan therefore did not evolve in public commentary at all; the first and only explanation is the September 2026 Regulation 30 disclosure.

points.point: The stated rationale is internal reorganisation, not a problem with the business: the JLG transfer is positioned as part of BLS's broader re-organisation and operational restructuring, aimed at streamlining operations, optimising resource deployment and sharpening strategic and operational focus.
points.quote: The proposed transaction forms part of the Company’s broader business re-organisation and operational restructuring initiatives.

points.point: The purpose clause names the three intended outcomes — streamlining, resource optimisation and focus — delivered via an 'appropriate business structure', with no quantified benefit attached.
points.quote: The transfer of the JLG Business Undertaking of Atyati Technologies Private Limited (“ATPL”) to TVAM Technologies Private Limited (“TVAM”) is intended to streamline business operations, optimise deployment of resources and enable greater strategic and operational focus through an appropriate business structure .

points.point: Scale of what leaves: JLG contributed Rs. 100.56 crores of revenue, 26.8% of ATPL's FY26 turnover — a material revenue line for the subsidiary, though immaterial to consolidated BLS revenue of Rs. 2,998 crores.
points.quote: Turnover of JLG Business Undertaking was                   Rs. 100.56 Crores (Indian Rupees One Hundred Crore and Fifty-Six Lakh Only) which represents 26.8% of the Total Turnover of ATPL for Financial Year 2025-26.

points.point: The undertaking carries almost no net worth — Rs. 59.49 lakhs, 0.9% of ATPL's net worth, computed as at July 1, 2026 because no divisional net worth existed at March 31, 2026 — and the consideration was set at exactly that figure, Rs. 59,49,000, subject to closing-account adjustments.
points.quote: However, the Net worth as computed as on July 1, 2026 for the unit or division or undertaking is Rs. 59.49 lacs (Indian Rupees Fifty-Nine Lakhs and Forty-Nine Thousand Only) which represents 0.9% of the total Net Worth of ATPL.

points.point: The buyer is an ATPL-related party — a private company in which an ATPL director is both director and member — and the company asserts arm's-length pricing; TVAM is not in BLS's promoter or group.
points.quote: TVAM is a Private Company in which a director of ATPL is a Director and Member. Therefore, TVAM is a related party of ATPL.

points.point: Mechanics and ring-fencing: a going-concern slump sale rather than a Scheme of Arrangement, needing lender/regulatory consents, targeted to close in roughly 90 days, with no impact on BLS shareholders' holdings.
points.quote: There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the listed entity pursuant to the Transaction.

points.point: An earlier step in the same restructuring: the Turkish step-down subsidiary BLS International Vize Hizmetleri (FY26 standalone revenue INR 167,858,678) was merged into iDATA (INR 1,877,772,130) on August 17, 2026, with no cash or new shares and its capital cancelled.
points.quote: To align the business synergies of step down subsidiaries.

points.point: Asked directly whether the Digital business would be spun off into a separate entity as E-Services was, management refused and defended it as a volume, INR-denominated business whose profit had doubled year-on-year to INR 18 crores.
points.quote: See, first of all, we do not believe it's a drag.

points.point: The only separation logic management ever volunteered on a call was for the BLS E-Services IPO — keeping the visa and digital businesses insulated so that neither funds the other's growth.
points.quote: Jaiprakash, we basically wanted to deal in both the businesses separately.

points.point: That insulation rationale was explicitly about cash ring-fencing between segments — the same 'appropriate structure' language later used for JLG, but applied to keeping capital pools apart rather than exiting a business.
points.quote: We do not want to use the cash generated by Visa business into the digital business requirement as well the digital business cash generation into Visa.

points.point: Context for what remains: digital was described as three verticals — business correspondent, loan distribution and e-governance — with loan distribution (Aadifidelis, ~3-5% EBITDA margin) the acknowledged drag on digital's margin, which fell from 14.2% to ~7%.
points.quote: So in digital offering, we have currently 3 verticals. One is the business correspondent which is a banking business wherein we provide the last mile banking. Then we have our loan distribution company, which we acquired last year, and the third is the E -governance where we provide, (we call it G2C ) government to citizens.

points.point: The last call before the sale gave no hint of any divestment — capital priorities were framed entirely as more acquisitions and contract deployment, in both Visa and Digital, with Rs. 1,434 crores net cash.
points.quote: So major utilization of the cash will be for the expansion of the existing business as well as for inorganic growth, which we plan to do.

verdict.what_management_expects: Only the filing speaks: streamlined operations, optimised resource deployment, and greater strategic and operational focus for the retained business through an appropriate structure. ATPL keeps Business Correspondent last-mile banking and technology solutions, shedding 26.8% of its turnover carrying 0.9% of its net worth. BLS shareholding is unchanged. No margin, capital-release, valuation or re-rating benefit is claimed anywhere.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention Atyati, JLG or the sale. Unexplained: valuation basis for Rs. 59.49 lakh, margin/loss profile of JLG, use of proceeds, lender consents needed, related-party safeguards, and who initiated it.

verdict.rationale: On the texts supplied, Capillary is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business, and no scheme of arrangement, slump sale or business-transfer document is present — so no management rationale for one exists to reconstruct. The only corporate separation of any kind disclosed is the November 2, 2026 intimation that Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., a non-operative step-down wholly-owned subsidiary, has completed voluntary deregistration in China; the company's stated reasons are simply that it 'was not carrying on any business operations', that its proposed closure had already been flagged in the RHP dated November 18, 2025, and that it is not a material subsidiary. The quantified impact given is nil: FY26 revenue 'Nil' and net worth of INR 0.50 million, with the Annexure A disclosure marking consideration, buyer, agreement date and 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' all as 'NA' — i.e. no sale, no consideration, no counterparty. Both earnings calls (February 6, 2026 for Q3 FY26 and May 6, 2026 for Q4/FY26) run in the opposite direction: management describes consolidating businesses in, not out — four completed acquisitions (Persuade, Brierley, Rewards, Kognitiv in May 2025) plus the $35 million SessionM merchant-loyalty business bought from Mastercard at ~0.5x revenue, announced February 24 and closed May 1, 2026, taking the group toward $115 million ARR, and 'a couple of other letters of intent' outstanding. The only 'separations' management discusses are platform sunsets inside the group — one of Brierley's two platforms 'fully sunset' in Q3 FY26 — done to lift gross margin from ~30% on acquired stacks to 65–70% on Capillary, not to separate a business from the listed entity. Management does segment the P&L for investors (loyalty stack ~90% of revenue, Engage and Rewards each ~5–7%, aiRA a few million dollars, ~INR 80–100 crores of the INR 735 crores being low-margin acquisition revenue, organic NRR 114–115% vs inorganic 94–96%), and Aneesh Reddy said 'We'll probably change the slides hopefully next time' to show core and inorganic margins separately — but that is disclosure presentation, not a legal or structural separation. No investor, lender or partner on either call asked for a separation; the questions were on margins, ACV-to-ARR bridge, AI disruption, US healthcare payer exposure and cost leverage. Treating the China deregistration as a 'business separation' would misread it: it is housekeeping on a dormant shell already disclosed pre-IPO.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced as a separation: on the February 6, 2026 Q3 FY26 call management framed the group as a roll-up ('let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue'), with two LOIs live and Brierley's second platform sunset. On the May 6, 2026 Q4/FY26 call the direction was reinforced — SessionM acquired from Mastercard and closed May 1, 2026, FY27 revenue guided to INR 1,000–1,050 crores — with only a promise to split core versus acquired margins in future slides. The November 2, 2026 filing then completed the one separation in the record: deregistration of the dormant Capillary Shanghai, a step already disclosed in the RHP dated November 18, 2025, so the plan did not evolve, it simply closed out.

points.point: The only separation disclosed is the completed voluntary deregistration of Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., justified solely on the basis that the entity had no operations and the closure was pre-flagged in the RHP dated November 18, 2025.
points.quote: Capillary Shanghai was not carrying on any business operations, and its proposed closure was disclosed in the RHP.

points.point: Materiality is expressly denied — no revenue, earnings or balance-sheet consequence for the company or group, and Annexure A shows FY26 revenue 'Nil' and net worth of INR 0.50 million, with sale agreement, consideration, buyer and scheme-of-arrangement fields all 'NA'.
points.quote: Capillary Shanghai is not a material subsidiary of the Company, and its cessation does not have any impact on the business operations, revenue, or financial position of the Company or its group.

points.point: Strategy on the latest call is acquisition and consolidation, not separation: the SessionM merchant-loyalty business was bought from Mastercard (announced Feb 24, closed May 1, 2026) at about 0.5x revenue, $35 million of revenue, 40+ logos, five Fortune 500 customers, pushing the group toward $115 million ARR.
points.quote: We closed that transaction on May 1st. So it's a sizeable $35 million business, 40 plus logos, including five Fortune 500 companies.

points.point: Management's framing of the two 'parts' of the business is a margin-reporting distinction, not a structural one — core Capillary revenue carries essentially all EBITDA while roughly INR 80–100 crores of FY26's INR 735 crores is acquisition-linked low-margin revenue, and the only action promised is a change to the slides.
points.quote: For the organic platform side, you will continue to see this 2%, 3% more margin growth and probably that's a better way to show it.

points.point: The stated purpose of the M&A machine is to absorb competitors and migrate their customers onto one platform, moving gross margin from ~30% on acquired stacks to 69–70% on Capillary and paying back purchase price in four to five years — the economics of combining, not separating.
points.quote: So what we've done is we say let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue and migrate those customers over ourselves.

points.point: The only businesses being 'separated out' are acquired legacy platforms being shut down inside the group, with Brierley (bought 2023) having one of its two platforms fully sunset in Q3 FY26 to release gross margin and below-the-line technology cost.
points.quote: Like for example, the last quarter we got done with the Brierley, which was one of the companies that we bought in 2023 had two platforms, so one of those platfo rms is fully sunset now.

points.point: No investor, analyst, lender or partner on either call asked about a demerger, spin-off or carve-out; questions covered AI disruption risk, US healthcare payer exposure, cost leverage, the ACV-to-ARR bridge and aiRA monetisation, and management added that it intends to stay confined to loyalty rather than hive anything off.
points.quote: No, we will obviously monetize this actively, but we'll stay in the loyalty space only.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is claimed for a business separation, because none is proposed. For the China deregistration the company states zero effect: no impact on operations, revenue or financial position, nil FY26 revenue, INR 0.50 million net worth, no consideration. Margin, capital and valuation benefits management does cite come from acquiring and migrating customers onto one platform — 30% to 65–70% gross margin, 45% contribution margin, four-to-five-year cash payback.
verdict.gaps: Everything a separation rationale would need: no scheme, no business identified for separation, no entity structure, record date, valuation, consideration, lender or investor demand, or Scheme document.

verdict.rationale: These texts contain no announcement, scheme or rationale for Borosil Renewables separating one of its own businesses into a new entity — the only forward-looking corporate-action question, on reported 'strategic investment' talks (Jul 2026 call), was met with 'I cannot offer any comment on this.' The separation management does explain at length is the severing of the European solar-glass business from the Indian one, executed through insolvency rather than a demerger: the hot end (melting furnace) of step-down subsidiary GMB Glasmanufaktur Brandenburg was cooled on 31 December 2024, GMB filed for insolvency on 4 July 2025, its holding company Geosphere Glassworks filed on 22 December 2025, and the marketing arm Interfloat Corporation was progressively impaired. The cause given was that from June 2023, roughly 6–7 months after the takeover, about 80 GW of Chinese modules were dumped into Europe in a couple of months, destroying local module manufacturing so that GMB's tailor-made customers disappeared and it could not sell beyond 50% of production, while promised EU/German policy support never turned into action. The cost of staying was quantified repeatedly: EBITDA losses of about INR 8 crore per month before shutdown, targeted down to INR 4 crore (employee cost ~INR 2 crore plus ~INR 2 crore other fixed cost), an inventory write-off of ~INR 16 crore, and standing charges of about EUR 900,000 (~INR 9 crore) a month that Geosphere would have had to keep funding. Management's stated purpose was that 'this filing of insolvency of the subsidiary would arrest recurring losses and permit reallocation of capital and managerial focus towards the India operations,' and that the one-time INR 325.91 crore provision against Geosphere/GMB (Rs 32,590.81 lakhs; written off in the FY26 accounts, with a INR 75 crore tax provision written back in Q4 FY26) would remove the continued drag on consolidated results so that 'the ROCE and EPS will substantially improve'; Laxman AG separately impaired INR 33.87 crore of its INR 57.59 crore exposure to Interfloat. The push came from several directions: GMB's own managing director was obliged under the German Insolvency Code to file once no further shareholder funding was available; German state bank ILB demanded repayment of the EUR 4.81 million capital subsidy, which Geosphere could not honour and which triggered its own filing; Borosil had already paid INR 185 crore from the February 2025 preferential issue to settle the SBLC given to GMB's lenders, while roughly INR 120–125 crore of GMB's remaining external liabilities (severance plus the government grant) were said not to travel to Borosil; and investors on the November 2025 call explicitly pressed management to shut Interfloat down as well. The group's only genuine demergers appear incidentally in a share re-lodgement filing — the NCLT-approved composite scheme of 15 January 2020 that amalgamated Gujarat Borosil (solar glass) into Borosil Renewables while demerging the consumer and scientific & industrial businesses to Borosil Limited, and the 2 November 2023 scheme demerging scientific & industrial out of Borosil Limited into Borosil Scientific — producing the 'three listed companies with different products, different businesses' and separate CEOs/teams described on the Jul 2026 call. Notably, the newest business, Borosil-branded rooftop solar kits (module, inverter, battery; ~INR 36–75 crore first-year revenue target, single-digit margins, no capex), is being built as a division inside Borosil Renewables, not separated out.
verdict.evolution: On the Nov 2024 call management was still 'reviewing all our options' for Germany, trying to fill the furnace with orders from the USA and EU; by Feb 2025 it had cooled the GMB furnace on 31 December 2024 pending the German election, and in May 2025 it sounded hopeful about the new Christian Democrat/Social Democrat government and was evaluating a cold-end-only restart using imported annealed glass. The Jul 2025 call reversed that: insolvency had been filed on 4 July 2025, the full INR 325.91 crore exposure was provisioned, and the stated purpose became arresting losses and reallocating capital and managerial focus to India. The Nov 2025 call extended the exit to Interfloat (INR 33.87 crore impaired; a shutdown decision promised 'by next quarter'), Feb 2026 confirmed GMB and Geosphere were fully deconsolidated so that consolidated and standalone results were now nearly identical, and May 2026 recorded the formal write-off after the Cottbus administrator's 1 December 2025 report said creditors would receive nothing; Jul 2026 only cleaned up the associated INR 75 crore tax shield.

points.point: Germany's problem was framed as collapsed demand, not cost: with local module makers unprotected and Chinese modules cheap, GMB's local demand fell to about 40% of production, and management said it was still weighing alternatives.
points.quote: So we are reviewing all our options. We are trying to first get the orders from other geographies so that we can still run at higher capacity, bring down the per unit cost of production and manage to bring both ends together in terms of revenue and cost, failing which we will have to look at more alternatives.

points.point: First physical step in the separation: the GMB melting furnace was cooled on 31 December 2024 while the German government was in crisis, with EBITDA losses of ~INR 8 crore/month to be halved to ~INR 4 crore and most workers put on state-funded short-time work.
points.quote: Since no decision could be expected until the formation of a new government, we decided to cool down the furnace on 31st December 2024, thus temporarily pausing the hot-end operations.

points.point: Still trying to save it — a cold-end-only restart processing imported annealed glass was being evaluated, an INR 16 crore inventory write-off was taken, and INR 185 crore of fresh Indian equity money was pushed out to settle GMB's lender liability.
points.quote: INR185 crores from this amount has been utilized to repay the loan liability of our step-down subsidiary, GMB.

points.point: The decisive explanation of the separation: insolvency filed 4 July 2025, INR 325.91 crore provisioned in full, and the stated gain was stopping ~INR 9 crore/month of standing charges and redirecting capital and management attention to India.
points.quote: For our Company, this filing of insolvency of the subsidiary would arrest recurring losses and permit reallocation of capital and managerial focus towards the India operations where we see a long-term potential and policy support.

points.point: The root cause given for the European exit was the June 2023 dumping of roughly 80 GW of Chinese modules into the EU, which wiped out GMB's customers for tailor-made glass and left it unable to sell beyond 50% of output.
points.quote: In June '23, just immediately after 6 to 7 months of our takeover of the Company, the imported Chinese modules started to be dumped in European markets, almost 80 gigawatts of modules were dumped in couple of months' time over there, which destroyed the local manufacturing.

points.point: The accounting purpose of taking the hit in one quarter was explicitly to clean up the entity left behind — no further consolidated drag, with better ROCE and EPS.
points.quote: However, this one-time provision will ensure that there is no continued drag on the consolidated results and performance, and that the ROCE and EPS will substantially improve.

points.point: The separation was extended to the European marketing arm: Interfloat lost its customers after GMB stopped annealed glass on 31 December 2024, and Laxman AG impaired INR 33.87 crore of its INR 57.59 crore exposure, with an investor pressing management to shut it entirely (answer: a decision 'by next quarter').
points.quote: Following an independent review by the management of Interfloat, it is assessed that there are no clear indicators of demand recovery in the near term that would support a return to profitable operations.

points.point: Separation complete in accounting terms — both GMB and its holding company Geosphere were deconsolidated, control lost to the court-appointed administrator, so consolidated results now essentially equal standalone India.
points.quote: So from the perspective of accounting and losses, we already deconsolidated the balance sheet by deconsolidating GMB, which is an operating step-down subsidiary and now we also deconsolidated Geosphere, which was a holding company of GMB.

points.point: Final step: after the Cottbus administrator's 1 December 2025 report said GMB's assets were insufficient and creditors would get nothing, the INR 325.91 crore exposure was written off, with no additional loss because it was already provided.
points.quote: In view of this, the company in its books of accounts for the financial year ended 31 March, 2026 has written off the above exposure in Geosphere and GMB.

points.point: The only governance rationale offered for keeping businesses in separate listed vehicles was management bandwidth: three listed companies, each with its own chairman/MD, CEO and functional teams, with Borosil Renewables' policy-heavy solar business needing P.K. Kheruka's full attention.
points.quote: So we have three listed companies with different products, different businesses.

points.point: Asked directly about press reports of a strategic investment, management declined to say anything — no further corporate restructuring was disclosed on any call.
points.quote: I cannot offer any comment on this.

points.point: The group's actual demergers appear only in a 4 March 2026 share re-lodgement filing: the 2020 NCLT composite scheme amalgamated solar-glass maker Gujarat Borosil into Borosil Renewables and demerged the consumer and scientific/industrial businesses out to Borosil Limited (50 shares of each per 100 Gujarat Borosil shares).
points.quote: In terms of the Composite Sheme of Amagalmation and Arrangement approved by Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal ( NCLT ), Mumbai, on January 15, 2020, inter-alia, Gujarat Borosil Limited (producer of solar glass) had been amalgamated with the Company, and the consumer and scientific & industrial product business of the Company had been transferred by way of demerger to Borosil Limited ("Scheme 1").

points.point: A second, later demerger split scientific & industrial products out of Borosil Limited into Borosil Scientific (37 shares for every 50 Borosil Limited shares), completing the three-company group structure.
points.quote: Further, as per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement of Borosil Limited ("Scheme 2"), approved by NCLT Mumbai on November 02 , 2023, its scientific and industrial product business had been transferred by way of demerger to Borosil Scientific Limited.

points.point: A lender forced the last leg: German state bank ILB demanded back the EUR 4.81 million capital subsidy because GMB's five-year operating condition was unmet, and Geosphere — a non-operating SPV holding GMB — filed for voluntary insolvency on 22 December 2025, its INR 13,003.09 lakh exposure already provided for.
points.quote: Geosphere in its response to the German Bank has clarified that GMB's shutting down of production was a result of inaction by the European Union and Federal Government of Germany to protect the solar PV manufacturing in Europe and conveyed that it has filed for insolvency due to lack of sufficient resources for honouring the aforesaid demand of German Bank.

verdict.what_management_expects: India: end of the consolidated loss drag, substantially improved ROCE and EPS, capital and managerial focus redeployed to the Bharuch 600 TPD expansion, and sustained 30–33% EBITDA margins. Europe (GMB/Geosphere/Interfloat): handed to court-appointed administrators, with roughly INR 120–125 crore of liabilities staying there rather than travelling to Borosil, and nothing expected back for shareholders.
verdict.gaps: No demerger scheme, swap ratio, record date, valuation, listing plan or shareholder vote is discussed; nor why rooftop solar stays an in-house division.

All supplied pages relate to Borosil Renewables Ltd.'s own flat-glass (solar glass) business, which the company states is a single reportable segment under Ind AS 108, so no segment result/EBIT/EBITDA is disclosed for any separated consumer and scientific business. verdict.rationale: The separation under discussion is Bosch Ltd.'s exit from part of its Building Technologies segment — the Video Solutions, Access & Intrusion and Communication Systems business — sold under a Business Transfer Agreement approved by the Board on January 28, 2025 to Keenfinity India Private Limited for Mio INR 5,950 (excluding purchase price adjustment), completed on May 1, 2025, producing a Mio INR 5,560 exceptional gain. Management framed it first as a mechanical consequence of a Bosch Group decision taken 'some time ago as part of a global realignment': the group's Building Technologies division was carved out worldwide and sold to the PE firm Triton, and in India the business was transferred 'to subsidiary of our parent who will then take it back to Triton' (Feb 2025 call). The second, substantive rationale was portfolio management against the group's 'top 3 in every segment' test: Guruprasad said in Aug 2025 that making Video Solutions/Access/Communication a top performer would need 'significant additional investment, a lot of IP and a lot of change dynamics' that 'was not in our focus', so they decided to hive it off; Karin Gilges added it was 'a product business' and they must keep asking 'what is our core and what is our strategy.' The numbers cited were deliberately small: roughly INR 400–450 crores of revenue leaving, at about 6% margin (clarified as EBIT, not PAT), so 'not a major impact on our business operations in any way' — the carve-out was sold as margin-neutral-to-positive and non-disruptive, and in the accounts it was not even treated as a discontinued operation under Ind AS 105 because it 'did not qualify as a separate major line of business.' The visible effects were a 65.3% y-o-y (64.7% q-o-q) collapse in Building Technologies sales in Q1 FY26 and a large one-off PAT lift — 9M FY26 PAT up 50.8% to INR 22,017 mn and FY26 PAT up 37.6% to INR 27,702 mn, both attributed mainly to the gain on this sale. It sits in a sequence of smaller separations management described the same way: Project House Mobility Solutions (PJMS) was 'taken out of the listco a couple of years ago because of the very heavy investments required… market is largely outside of India… it was very heavily negative' (gain INR 7,850 mn), and OE/OES Diagnostics was sold in Q2 FY25 for a INR 485 mn gain, alongside a INR 471 mn Q3 FY25 provision 'towards restructuring its operations to be competitive in the Mobility business.' Nobody external demanded the separation — no investor, lender or partner asked for it; it was promoter/parent-driven ('discussions that are going on in the RBIN and Board with the promoter'), while analysts on these calls were pressing in the opposite direction, for group entities to be folded INTO the listed company, which management eventually delivered via the RBIC (Bosch Chassis Systems) acquisition announced April 8, 2026.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as vague portfolio language in the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 calls, where Guruprasad refused to 'speculate on things which are very sensitive' but said portfolio decisions were being discussed 'in the RBIN and Board with the promoter'; the Feb 2025 call (results for Q3 FY25, after the Jan 28, 2025 Board approval) first named the deal, explained it as the India leg of the global Building Technologies carve-out to Triton, and sized it at ~INR 400–450 crores of revenue at ~6% EBIT margin. The Jun 2025 and Aug 2025 calls reported completion (Q1 FY26 PAT at 23.3% of revenue, Building Technologies down 65.3%), and in Aug 2025 management gave the fuller doctrinal rationale — top-3-or-exit, and an unwillingness to fund the investment and IP the business needed. The Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls treated it purely as the arithmetic driver of PAT growth (50.8% for 9M FY26; 37.6% for FY26), and by the Apr 2026 and May 2026 calls the narrative had flipped from subtraction to addition — the INR 9,068.68 crore RBIC acquisition, funded from existing funds and internal accruals, plus the Tata AutoComp e-axle JV and the Brakes India/Wheels India air-systems JV.

points.point: The Board approved the Business Transfer Agreement on January 28, 2025 with Keenfinity India Private Limited for Mio INR 5,950, completed May 1, 2025, with a Mio INR 5,560 gain booked as an exceptional item.
points.quote: On January 28, 2025, the Board of Directors of the Company approved to execute the Business Transfer Agreement with Keenfinity India Private Limited ("the Purchaser") for transfer of its "Video solutions, Access and Intrusions and Communication systems" Business (Specified Business) for a consideration of Mio INR 5,950 (excluding purchase price adjustment).

points.point: Despite its size, the carved-out unit was not accounted for as a discontinued operation because it was not a separate major line of business under Ind AS 105.
points.quote: The specified business did not qualify as a separate major line of business under IND AS 105: Non current Assets held for sale and discontinued operations and accordingly was not considered as a "discontinued operation" for the purpose of these unaudited standalone financial results.

points.point: Guruprasad explained the India sale as the local leg of Bosch's global Building Technologies carve-out to private equity firm Triton, routed through a parent subsidiary.
points.quote: And you may have seen that the building technologies division globally has been sold to venture capitalist Triton, and this is an ongoing part of that sequence and in India, we are doing it to subsidiary of our parent who will then take it back to Triton.

points.point: Karin Gilges gave the portfolio-management rationale: it is a product business and the company must keep testing what is core against overall Bosch strategy.
points.quote: This is a product business, and therefore we all the time also have to look at our portfolio and we have to manage our portfolio. And we have to see what is our core and what is our strategy.

points.point: Management sized the exit at roughly INR 400–450 crores of revenue at about 6% margin (clarified as EBIT margin), i.e. immaterial to operations.
points.quote: It's a very small business. About the revenue that goes out is about Rs. 450 crores.

points.point: Asked whether margins would be re-based next year, Guruprasad insisted the exit was not material to the company's margin profile.
points.quote: About 6%. Margin is about 6%. It's not a major impact on our business operations in any way.

points.point: Guruprasad set out the governing portfolio test — top 3 in every segment — and said this business failed it because of the investment, IP and change dynamics required.
points.quote: We want to be in the top 3 in every segment we operate.

points.point: The explicit reason for hiving off: making Video Solutions, Access and Communication Systems a top performer needed investment and IP that was not in focus.
points.quote: So based on this, certain portfolio actions are taken and one of them was the building technologies area of Video Solutions, Access and Communication systems, where we realized that significant additional investment, a lot of IP and a lot of change dynamics are required to make this into a top performer, which we believed at that point of time was not in our focus.

points.point: First post-completion quarter showed the revenue effect: Building Technologies sales fell 65.3% y-o-y and 64.7% sequentially.
points.quote: Building technologies business declined by 65.3% mainly due to the sale of Video Solutions and Access and Intrusion and Communication systems business.

points.point: The separation became the dominant driver of reported profit growth — 9M FY26 PAT of INR 22,017 million, up 50.8%.
points.quote: The profit after tax for 9 months ending December 2025 stood at INR22,017 million, which is a growth of 50.8% over the same period of previous year.

points.point: Full-year FY26 PAT of INR 27,702 million (up 37.6%) was attributed mainly to the gain on this divestment.
points.quote: The significant growth impact is mainly due to the profit on sale of the Video Solutions, Access and Intrusions and Communication Systems under the Building Technologies segment.

points.point: Management described the comparable earlier separation of the mobility solutions business (PJMS) from the listed company on the same logic — heavy investment, market outside India, deeply loss-making.
points.quote: Yeah, see, we had one mobility solutions business which we actually took out of the listco a couple of years ago because of the very heavy investments required. Market is largely outside of India. Very little market in India. And it was very heavily negative.

points.point: Before disclosure, the separation sat inside a continuous promoter- and Board-level portfolio review, not an investor demand.
points.quote: We are constantly looking at our product portfolio, our business activities in the listed company and also business activities outside the listed company in the Indian context.

points.point: An adjacent, smaller divestment in the same programme: the OE/OES Diagnostics business sold in Q2 FY25 for a INR 485 million exceptional gain.
points.quote: Likewise, in the current quarter, that's July-September 2024, also has an exceptional item via sale of OE/OES Diagnostics business of INR485 million.

points.point: The flip side of decluttering: analysts, not management, pushed for group entities to be brought INTO the listed company, which management answered with the RBIC acquisition while declining to pull in the low-margin, capex-heavy electronics entity.
points.quote: So, at this point of time, we did not find a good commercial logic to bring this business in when it does not add turnover, doesn't contribute much to the margins, and there is very heavy intensity on investments.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Bosch Ltd.: a cleaner mobility-focused portfolio, no material operating impact (a ~6% EBIT, ~INR 400–450 crore business exits), a one-off gain lifting FY26 PAT 37.6%, and a strong, near debt-free balance sheet with substantial liquidity to fund strategic investments — later deployed into the e-axle JV and the INR 9,068.68 crore RBIC acquisition. For the divested unit: ownership by Triton, which will supply the investment and IP Bosch would not.

verdict.rationale: The separation these texts actually describe is not a demerger by Castrol India but the carve-out of the whole Castrol lubricants business out of BP p.l.c., which reaches Castrol India indirectly because its 51% promoter, Castrol Limited, sits under Castrol Group Holdings Limited. Management said the trigger was a parent-level portfolio and balance-sheet problem, not anything wrong inside India: Kedar Lele described it as 'the global compulsion that a large oil and gas major faces' and said BP's global CEO had stated 'they would want to retire the debt and they see in Castrol a good asset that can be monetized,' with BP announcing the strategic review around February 2025 'with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery.' The second strand of the reasoning is strategic mismatch and trapped value: Castrol's growth agenda — core mobility, a bigger push into industrial lubricants, mobility/maintenance services (750+ Castrol Auto Service centres, 33,000 bike workshops, 12,000 multi-brand workshops, the ki Mobility stake of roughly INR 487-500 crore) and diversification into data-centre immersion/direct-to-chip coolants where Western gross margins are about USD 1 per litre — were described as businesses 'different from the oil and gas business,' so a standalone/JV owner would fund and focus them better. India was presented as a prize asset within that perimeter: 'a little over 10% of the volume of global Castrol and a little better than that in terms of profitability' because of its 2-wheeler and car mix, on 234 million litres in CY2024, roughly 20%+ automotive retail market share, 21-24% EBITDA guidance and ~90% dividend payout. Who asked for it: BP itself (its CEO and global M&A team, which ran a data room for potential investors under NDA while the India MD explicitly did not participate); no lender or partner demand was cited, and analysts (Abinash, Nitin Tiwari, Kirtan Mehta, Lokesh, Harsh) only probed for consequences — brand licensing, R&D access from BP's global centres, the Q4 global base-oil volume rebates, and whether data-centre revenue would land in the listed entity. On those, management insisted continuity: the base-oil rebate contracts 'are with Castrol,' not BP ('BP globally does not make any base oil'), on 2.2-2.3 billion litres of global Castrol purchasing, so 'none of these discounts that we see in the Q4 will get affected by any strategic sales.' The outcome in the filings is a 23 December 2025 SPA in which BP sells 100% of Castrol Group Holdings Limited to Motion JVCo Limited (Stonepeak's Stonepeak Motion Holdco, funded by Stonepeak Infrastructure Fund V vehicles, with CPP Investment Board Private Holdings (6) Inc. taking a non-controlling stake), BP Motion Holdings taking back 35% of the acquirer and Stonepeak keeping 65% and sole control — which indirectly transfers control of Castrol India's 51% block (50,44,52,416 shares) and forces a mandatory 26% open offer for 25,71,71,820 shares at INR 194.04 (up to INR 4,990.16 crore), taking the acquirer to 77% and flagging the 25% minimum-public-shareholding constraint, subject to about 25 antitrust clearances, a dozen FDI/national-security approvals and EU foreign-subsidies review.
verdict.evolution: Nothing was said on the 4 Feb 2025 (CALL Feb 2025) call beyond Deepesh Baxi's remark that 'diversification is very much an important pivot of our forward strategy,' and a hedge that where data-centre revenue books is 'a matter of structuring'; the review surfaced on the 29 April 2025 call (CALL May 2025) as BP's 'strategic review... with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery,' considering 'all options.' By 6 August 2025 (CALL Aug 2025) it was explicitly a 'carve out' driven by BP's debt retirement, with India sized at just over 10% of global volume and better on profit, and by 6 November 2025 (CALL Nov 2025) it had become a live process — a data room for potential investors run by BP's global M&A team, with India supplying data but the MD excluded from the transaction. The 23-24 December 2025 SPA and public announcement fixed the form: BP sells 100% of Castrol Group Holdings to Stonepeak's Motion JVCo, BP retaining 35%, triggering a 26% open offer at INR 194.04. On 4 February 2026 (CALL Feb 2026) Saugata Basuray confirmed the 65/35 joint venture and guided closure 'toward the end of the year,' and on 29 April 2026 (CALL May 2026) the message narrowed to pending worldwide approvals plus 'no change in our structure, strategy or operating model' at Castrol India.

points.point: Before the review was public, the CFO already framed portfolio diversification (EV fluids, data-centre fluids, service/maintenance via the ki Mobility stake) as the forward pivot, and declined to commit on which legal entity new revenue streams would sit in.
points.quote: But the intent is that diversification is very much an important pivot of our forward strategy for Castrol, not only in India but globally as well.

points.point: First disclosure on a call: BP's strategic review of Castrol globally, with the stated purpose of accelerating value delivery and unlocking value, considering all options, and with Castrol's own ambitions in core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services and data-centre fluids named as what the review should accelerate.
points.quote: So BP announced the strategic review of its Castrol business globally with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery.

points.point: Lele also framed the logic historically — Castrol is a 125-year-old brand that has only been inside BP for the last 25 years — implying the brand can stand outside an oil major.
points.quote: Because history of Castrol is 125-year-old, out of which last 25 years is the time when Castrol as a brand has been with BP.

points.point: The clearest statement of motive: the carve-out is BP's problem, not Castrol's — a large oil and gas major needing to retire debt and monetising a good asset.
points.quote: Now BP's decision to carve out Castrol is driven by the global compulsion that a large oil and gas major faces. And it is, the global CEO of BP has said this that they would want to retire the debt and they see in Castrol a good asset that can be monetized.

points.point: The strategic-fit argument: Castrol's growth lines — core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services and data-centre fluids — are not oil-and-gas businesses, so separation puts the focus on value creation for Castrol.
points.quote: All of these businesses are different from the oil and gas business. And with this, there will be a focus on value creation for Castrol.

points.point: India's weight in the perimeter was quantified for the first time: just over 10% of global Castrol volume and a better share of profit, because the India mix is skewed to higher-margin 2-wheelers and cars rather than average trucks.
points.quote: See, Nitin, at an overall level, we do about a little over 10% of the volume of global Castrol and a little better than that in terms of profitability because our business is structured around 2-wheelers and cars, which is really more profitable part of the business versus the average trucks and the average profitability that you see in the segment.

points.point: The process was live and run entirely above the India entity: India/South Asia is one of the performance units feeding a BP-administered data room for potential investors, with the India MD deliberately walled off from the transaction.
points.quote: We have been supplying data into a data room for p otential investors, and that gets run from our central team bound by the NDA and administered by B P's global M&A team directly. And I do not participate in any of that transaction.

points.point: Answering Harsh's question on whether a sale would jeopardise the Q4 volume rebates, management said the global base-oil contracts belong to Castrol (BP makes no base oil) and are earned on Castrol's own 2.2-2.3 billion litres, so the rebate — worth roughly the 24% full-year vs 26% Q4 EBITDA gap — survives the deal.
points.quote: So none of t hese discounts that we see in the Q4 will get affected by any strategic sales.

points.point: Lele used Valvoline as the template for why the services layer has separate value — Valvoline kept its 2,000-outlet Quick Lube network when it sold the lubricant brand — positioning Castrol's 750+ CAS network as a strategic lever rather than an appendage to lubricants.
points.quote: I was in the U.S. with the leadership team, and I s aw how Valvoline Quick Lube change network of 2,000 outlets across U.S. is a very large busine ss that Valvoline did not sell along with its lubricant brand when they did the transaction.

points.point: The 24 December 2025 public announcement sets out the mechanics: a 23 December 2025 SPA under which BP p.l.c. sells 100% of Castrol Group Holdings Limited to Motion JVCo Limited, with BP Motion Holdings taking 35% of the acquirer and Stonepeak's Motion Holdco keeping 65% and sole control.
points.quote: The Acquirer has entered into an agreement for sale and purchase with BP p.l.c. ("Seller") dated December 23, 2025 ("SPA"), pursuant to which the Seller has agreed to sell and transfer to the Acquirer, and the Acquirer has agreed to acquire from the Seller, 100% (one hundred percent) of the equity share capital of Castrol Group Holdings Limited ("CGHL").

points.point: Because CGHL owns Castrol Limited, the promoter holding 50,44,52,416 shares (51%) of Castrol India, the deal is an indirect change of control that triggers a mandatory 26% open offer — 25,71,71,820 shares at INR 194.04, up to INR 4,990.16 crore, taking the acquirer to 77% and putting the 25% minimum public shareholding at issue.
points.quote: The Acquirer and the PAC s hereby make this Open Offer to the Public Shareholders to acquire u p to 25,71,71,8 20 (twenty five crore seventy one lakh seventy one thousand eight hundred and twenty ) Equity Shares ("Offer Shares "), constituting 26.00% (twenty six percent) of the Equity Share Capital ("Offer Size "), at a price of INR 194.04/- (Indian Rupees one hundred and ninety four and four paise only) per Offer Share aggregating to a total consideration of up to INR 4,990,16,19,952.80/-

points.point: Saugata Basuray confirmed the structure to Lokesh — a 65/35 joint venture with an investor, flagged after the February 2025 strategic review — and guided closure toward end-2026 subject to regulatory approvals, deferring brand-licensing and R&D questions as 'business as usual.'
points.quote: So at the parent level, BP has signaled that they will form a joint venture with an investor, where BP will remain a 35 % shareholder and the investor will take 65%.

points.point: A year into the process the India message is pure continuity: the deal awaits worldwide regulatory approvals, any disclosures will come from the new shareholders, and nothing changes in the listed entity's structure, strategy or operating model.
points.quote: From Castrol India standpoint, there's no change in our structure, strategy or operating model.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Castrol under new owners: focus and funding for its non-oil-and-gas growth lines — core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility/maintenance services and data-centre coolants — and an accelerated 'next phase of value delivery.' For BP: debt retirement by monetising the asset while keeping 35% upside. For Castrol India: explicitly no change — same strategy, 21-24% EBITDA band, retained global base-oil rebates and R&D access, strong balance sheet, continued payouts.
verdict.gaps: No Castrol India-level demerger exists or is explained; calls never give deal value, brand-licence, royalty or R&D terms, minority-shareholder impact, or the post-77% minimum-public-shareholding plan.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe a separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any Capri Global Capital Ltd. (CGCL) business — no Scheme document is present among the ten filings, and across all eight transcripts no participant or manager uses the words demerger, spin-off, separation, hive-off or unlocking value, and no swap ratio, record date, resulting-entity listing or appointed date is ever mentioned. The only structural change these documents actually evidence is CGCL placing fee-based, capital-light businesses into wholly-owned subsidiaries while keeping them inside the consolidated group: the car loan origination/distribution business was moved out of CGCL into a newly formed subsidiary, Capri Loans Car Platforms Private Limited, disclosed in the Q1 FY25 (Aug 2024) call as a completed shift, with the Q2 FY25 (Nov 2024) call attributing a temporary dip in that vertical's profit to 'various transition from old CGCL to the new company' plus the cost of launching used-car distribution on the same team; two further entities were incorporated in Q1 FY26 (Aug 2025) — one for debt-capital-market investment banking and one securities company for institutional debt placement, an online bond platform and exchange trading — which management said would consume little capital and be profit-accretive from year one, and in Q4 FY26 (May 2026) were tied to earning INR40–50 crore gross / INR20–25 crore net fee income and to cutting the 2–3% negative carry on an earmarked INR600–800 crore treasury bond book; and the Jan 29, 2026 filing/Q3 FY26 results record Capri Global Insurance Brokers Private Limited becoming a subsidiary with effect from December 2, 2025, alongside Capri Global Capital Markets and Capri Global Securities (funded with INR100 mn, INR600 mn and INR7.5 mn respectively in 9M FY26). The stated logic for this subsidiarisation is monetisation and cost-sharing, not separation: the car loan platform spans 14 partner banks and a pan-India network with 'potential to monetize further for distribution of other products', the same 1,800-person supervisory team is to carry used cars, credit cards, personal loans and mortgages over 3–4 years so that 'cost allocation will happen on the higher revenue', and the entity alone is guided to about INR20 crore profit next year rising to INR60–70 crore of pure fee income over 4–5 years. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as having asked for any of this; the only lender/rating-driven structural actions discussed are funding diversification (NCDs, CPs, a INR489 crore public NCD issue, a USD 30 mn GIFT-City bond, a USD 1 bn GMTN programme) and a INR200 crore rights-issue infusion into the housing subsidiary CGHFL — i.e. capital going into subsidiaries, not businesses being let go.
verdict.evolution: The idea that surfaces in these texts is subsidiarisation of fee businesses, not separation: it first appears in the Aug 6, 2024 (Q1 FY25) call as an already-done transfer of car loans to a new subsidiary, is revisited on Oct 30, 2024 (Q2 FY25) only to explain a one-year profit dip from the 'transition from old CGCL to the new company'. On Aug 5, 2025 (Q1 FY26) it widens to two newly incorporated entities for debt capital markets and securities, pitched as capital-light and accretive from year one. By Feb 2, 2026 (Q3 FY26) the Jan 29, 2026 filing shows a fourth entity, Capri Global Insurance Brokers, added from Dec 2, 2025, and on May 4, 2026 (Q4 FY26) management quantifies the car loan entity (INR20 crore profit next year, INR60–70 crore fee income in 4–5 years) and the capital-markets entity (INR40–50 crore gross fee income, INR20–25 crore net, plus reduced treasury negative carry). At no point in this sequence does the plan change into, or get described as, a separation of a business from CGCL.

points.point: First disclosure of any structural move: the car loan origination business had been transferred out of CGCL into a newly formed subsidiary; the only reason given for the softer quarter was seasonality, not strategy.
points.quote: Car loan, we have shifted the business from the Capri Global Capital Limited to the newly formed subsidiary.

points.point: Management framed the subsidiary move as a one-year cost of transition plus new-product launch (used car finance on the same team), with profit and volume to peak the following year — no separation rationale offered.
points.quote: This year, we will have profitability slightly lower than the last year because of various transition from old CGCL to the new company.

points.point: Two further entities were incorporated — a debt-capital-market investment bank and a securities company for institutional debt placement, online bond platform and exchange trading — explicitly described as capital-light and profit-accretive from year one, set up in FY26 with guidance to follow.
points.quote: There are two companies we have incorporated. One is going to carry out the investment banking activities only for the debt capital market. And another company is a securities company, which is going to engage in the sales and distribution of the debt placement at institutional level, online bond platform and exchange trading.

points.point: The stated economics of housing the new businesses separately was zero capital drag and no hit to the cost-to-income ratio, with exact projections deferred to the following year.
points.quote: Both of these will not consume much capital, and they will be from the year 1 that will be accretive to the profit rather than taking any dent on the cost income side.

points.point: Asked about an abrupt senior exit (CEO Monu Ratra leaving within four months), management addressed only continuity of vertical heads and denied any underlying issue; no structural or separation plan was mentioned in response.
points.quote: There's an adequate number of professionals in team in each vertical, be it MSME, be it Gold, Micro LAP, Housing Finance, Car Loan.

points.point: The car loan subsidiary is characterised as a pure distribution (DSA) model with no balance-sheet risk, to be loaded with used cars, credit cards, personal loans and mortgages over 3–4 years so the same 1,800-person team spreads cost over higher revenue.
points.quote: So currently, car loan is a completely distribution business model.

points.point: First quantified standalone target for a separated-out entity: about INR20 crore profit next year from car loans alone, scaling to INR60–70 crore of pure fee income in 4–5 years.
points.quote: And next year, we will be able to see that about INR20 crores of profit is able to deliver by the car loan entity alone.

points.point: Rationale for the capital-markets entity is treasury-driven: it reduces a 2–3% negative carry on an earmarked INR600–800 crore bond book while earning INR40–50 crore gross / INR20–25 crore net fee income once the licence is received (expected end-June).
points.quote: So, if we earmark about INR600 crores to INR800 crores book retain, we expect to reduce almost 3% negative carry on this portfolio.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is said about a separation's effects. For the subsidiarised fee businesses they expect: car loans ~INR20 crore profit in FY27 rising to INR60-70 crore fee income in 4-5 years, with margin rather than volume focus and 12-15% origination growth; capital markets INR40-50 crore gross / INR20-25 crore net fees plus ~3% less treasury negative carry; little capital consumed, no cost-to-income drag, accretive from year one.
verdict.gaps: No demerger rationale, swap ratio, record date, listing plan, or lender/investor demand appears anywhere; no scheme filing is included; margin or valuation effects of subsidiarisation are never explained.

verdict.rationale: The premise does not hold in these documents: CIE Automotive India (CIEINDIA) is not separating a business — it is doing the opposite, absorbing one. The only corporate action in the filings is a Scheme of Merger by Absorption, approved by the Board on 23 April 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2026), under which CIE Aluminium Casting India Limited (CIEALCAST, the aluminium die-casting/HPDC vertical bought in April 2019, FY2025 turnover INR 11,728 million and PAT INR 948 million) is merged into CIEINDIA (FY2025 turnover INR 48,964.02 million, PAT INR 6,169.27 million); because CIEALCAST is a 100% subsidiary, no shares are issued and its 29,40,000 shares of Rs 10 are simply cancelled. The Scheme gives five reasons: production and marketing synergies (one larger, more diversified portfolio, coordinated capacity planning and load balancing, direct use of assets without inter-company transfer mechanisms); cross-selling across OEM relationships, since CIEALCAST brings near sole-supplier positions in aluminium die-cast parts in two-wheelers and passenger vehicles, letting CIEINDIA offer OEMs 'multi-technology sourcing bundles'; organisational and operating efficiencies by removing managerial overlap and duplicated IT, HR, finance, secretarial, legal and compliance functions and simplifying the group; a stronger balance sheet (net worth Rs 4,469.50 crore post-merger vs Rs 4,375.28 crore standalone) so OEMs award bigger, longer-lifecycle projects, plus unfettered access to combined cash flow for organic and inorganic growth and dividends; and elimination of inter-company payables/loans (CIEALCAST carried one unsecured borrowing of Rs 169 crore and 688 sundry creditors of Rs 112.05 crore). The acquisition logic cited is lightweighting — 'OEMs globally were increasing aluminium usage per vehicle' — and the merger is framed as finally realising that 2019 bet. Context from the calls explains why aluminium was the unit chosen: Ander said EBITDA went from ~10% at purchase in 2019 to ~15% but was 'still below our expectations', Bajaj dependence fell only from 75–80% to 60–65%, a CNG programme collapsed, a change to recognising only value-add depressed reported sales, and the vertical was under 'portfolio restructuring' with European engineers deployed for technology transfer. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for it; NCLT dispensed with shareholder and creditor meetings (there are no secured creditors in either company) and only directed that notices be served, which the company dispatched on 8 October 2026. The nearest things to actual separations in these texts are historic or external to the Scheme: the 2023 sale of CFG's four German forging subsidiaries to Mutares (INR 3.3 billion of discontinued-operations profit in CY23, proceeds kept at Galfor and used to retire Mexico debt), Mexico being re-parented under CIE Galfor and reported in Europe from CY25, BF Precision Private Limited dissolved 5 June 2025, and the 27.89% Ojaha Renewables stake sold on 25 June 2026 — while CIE Hosur stays a subsidiary and even received a Rs 120.76 crore rights injection in September 2026, and the group's sunroof business is deliberately held outside the listed company by CIE Spain.
verdict.evolution: Across the earlier calls (21 Feb 2025, 30 Apr 2025, 22 Jul 2025, 17 Oct 2025, 20 Feb 2026) there is no mention of any separation or of this merger; aluminium is discussed only as an underperforming vertical being restructured, re-customered and re-tooled toward higher-tonnage machined castings, with a new factory flagged on 20 Feb 2026. The plan surfaces fully formed with the Board approval of 23 April 2026 and is confirmed only in passing on the 24 April 2026 call, where Rishi Vora asks whether the aluminium business now merges into standalone and CFO K. Jayaprakash answers that this is the intent, Vikas Sinha adding that India will then consist of the standalone entity plus CIE Hosur. It then advances purely procedurally: NCLT Mumbai allowed application CA(CAA)-115/MB/2026 on 24 September 2026, dispensing with shareholder and creditor meetings, and notices to 1,00,114 shareholders and the unsecured creditors went out on 8 October 2026; the 22 October 2026 results note the Scheme as pending NCLT and regulatory approval.

points.point: First stated rationale: production and marketing synergies — one combined entity offering a larger, more diversified portfolio, with coordinated capacity planning, optimisation and load balancing, and direct use of assets instead of inter-company transfer mechanisms.
points.quote: Creation of production and marketing synergies by enabling the combined entity to offer a larger and more diversified product portfolio to a broad base of customers.

points.point: Second rationale: cross-selling across OEM relationships, because CIEALCAST brings near sole-supplier positions for several aluminium die-cast components in two-wheelers and passenger vehicles.
points.quote: Post-merger, the Transferee company will be positioned to offer multi-technology sourcing bundles to OEMs, enabling customers to consolidate sourcing with a trusted supplier to the customers.

points.point: Third rationale: removing the cost of running two legal entities — duplicated IT, HR, finance, secretarial, legal, compliance and general management, plus a simpler, more transparent group structure.
points.quote: Delivery of substantial organisational synergies through the elimination of managerial overlaps inherent in operating multiple legal entities, resulting in improved decision-making speed and clearer governance structures.

points.point: Fourth rationale: a bigger balance sheet wins bigger OEM projects — net worth goes from Rs 4,375.28 crore (CIEINDIA standalone) to Rs 4,469.50 crore post-merger, absorbing CIEALCAST's Rs 325.83 crore.
points.quote: A strong net worth signifies that the company possesses enough financial resources to successfully complete larger projects without negative repercussions.

points.point: Related capital argument: pooled cash can be redeployed for organic and inorganic growth and supports dividends — relevant given consolidated net financial debt of negative INR 18.8 billion and repeated investor questions about idle cash.
points.quote: Further, unfettered access to cash-flow generated by the combined businesses can be deployed more efficiently to fund organic and inorganic growth opportunities and to maximize shareholders value.

points.point: Fifth rationale: wiping out inter-company balances — CIEALCAST carried 688 sundry creditors of Rs 112.05 crore, 31 capex creditors of Rs 3.32 crore and one unsecured borrowing of Rs 169 crore as at 31 March 2026.
points.quote: Elimination inter-company payables/loans/other transactions leads to a stronger, more resilient financial position and enhanced business's creditworthiness.

points.point: The original 2019 acquisition thesis is restated as the backdrop: lightweighting and OEM sourcing moving toward full-system, lightweight suppliers, which the merger is meant to finally capture.
points.quote: OEMs globally were increasing aluminium usage per vehicle to reduce weight and improve efficiency.

points.point: No consideration and no dilution: because the target is wholly owned, no shares are issued and CIEALCAST's entire paid-up capital (29,40,000 equity shares of Rs 10) is cancelled; shareholding pattern and capital structure are unchanged.
points.quote: Since Transferor Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Transferee Company, no shares will be issued as consideration for the amalgamation and the entire issued share capital of the Transferor Company held by the Transferee Company shall be cancelled.

points.point: Why aluminium is the unit being absorbed: Ander Arenaza says margins rose from ~10% EBITDA at the 2019 purchase to about 15%, but remain below internal expectations, with European engineers deployed in India for technology transfer.
points.quote: I would say that the aluminum, when we entered, when we bought the company in 2019, was about 10% EBITDA. Now, it can be around 15%.

points.point: Management attributes part of CY25's India growth shortfall to the aluminium (and magnetics) portfolio restructuring and to recognising only value-add on some aluminium categories from Q4, alongside the CNG bike collapse.
points.quote: First, the restructuring of our business portfolio that we are carrying out at our aluminum and magnetics verticals.

points.point: At the same time the aluminium vertical is being expanded, not shrunk — new customers, higher-tonnage higher-value parts and a possible new factory, consistent with absorption rather than disposal.
points.quote: Also, we are working with other customers to add new products to our portfolio, and we will probably launch a new factory for these products.

points.point: Customer-concentration context for the aluminium unit: Bajaj was 75–80% of that business at acquisition and is still 60–65%, which the cross-selling rationale in the Scheme is meant to dilute.
points.quote: At the time of acquisition, Bajaj used to be 75% to 80% of our aluminum business. Today, it is down to 60% to 65%, not because we have neglected Bajaj, we have developed other players, Nidec GPM and so on.

points.point: The one business genuinely kept separate from the listed entity is the fast-growing sunroof business, held directly by CIE Spain; an investor objected that minority shareholders do not share in it and management declined to change the arrangement.
points.quote: I think the basic logic was that this is a tier 1 kind of business with a lot of design support required, which they get from a centralized team and therefore it is run as a separate global unit within CIE and that's the reason why it has been kept separate.

points.point: A separate structural change, purely reporting: the Mexican forging plant became a subsidiary of CIE Galfor after a Galfor capital increase, so it is reported under Europe from CY25 with CY24 restated (India 65% / Europe+Mexico 35%).
points.quote: But after the capital increase subscribed by Galfor, Mexican activity became a subsidiary of Galfor, CIE Galfor that is in Europe.

points.point: The group's actual past divestment was the German forgings business (JECO, GSA, FUG, SCG) sold to Mutares in 2023, whose proceeds stayed in Europe at Galfor and were partly used to retire Bill Forge Mexico's debt — not a separation of an Indian business.
points.quote: Please note that the PAT of C '23 includes INR 3.3 billion of profit from discontinued operations , pertaining to our erstwhile Forgings business in Germany.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these four earnings calls (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026) or the two filings (postal ballot of February 12, 2026 and the board outcome of August 19, 2026) describes Aditya Infotech Ltd. separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business; the premise cannot be supported from these texts, and I will not supply a rationale from memory. The corporate direction management actually describes is the opposite — consolidation and backward integration into one listed entity: the September 2024 purchase of Dixon Technologies' 50% stake in the manufacturing JV AIL Dixon, which became a wholly owned subsidiary (Dixon taking ~6.5-6.6% of Aditya Infotech via share swap at a ~INR 4,000 crore deal value), and the 'fully integrating AIL Dixon' benefit cited as a margin lever in the FY26 guidance (EBITDA 10-11%, PAT 6-7%). Further structure is being added, not removed: a wholly owned Taiwan R&D subsidiary (Aditya Infotech Taiwan Company Limited), a 50:50 JV with Orient Cables for coaxial/network/CCTV cable, the Kadapa housing-enclosure plant (30 million enclosures p.a.) and lens assembly line, the L&T Semiconductor agreement for 9 million IP cameras over three years, and the Qualcomm collaboration (revenue-share, no capex). The only business that shrinks is the third-party Dahua distribution line, and management attributes that to the April 9, 2025 STQC/trusted-supply-chain mandate disqualifying Chinese brands — not to a scheme: Dahua falls from a >25-30% revenue decline in FY26 to 'not even INR100-150 crores' and INR10-15 crores a month in FY27, while CP PLUS rises to 86-87% of revenue; Aditya Khemka notes the margin differential is 'almost 3x' in favour of the own brand. Capital actions in the filings are an equity raise of up to INR 1,500 crore by public issue/QIP (board approval August 19, 2026) and ESOP ratification, an Articles amendment preserving Dixon's right to nominate one director while it holds at least 4%, and promoter remuneration revisions — none of which involves a separation. The words 'demerger' and 'spin-off' appear only inside standard ESOP corporate-action adjustment boilerplate, which lists them hypothetically alongside rights issue, bonus, merger and amalgamation.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea surfaces at any point: on Aug 20, 2025 management presents AIL Dixon as a newly 100%-owned subsidiary and an integration-driven margin lever; on Nov 13, 2025 Dixon is described as a shareholder/board partner with a continuing service agreement; on Feb 13, 2026 the only structural news is the new Taiwan R&D subsidiary and the Orient Cables 50:50 JV; on May 28, 2026 (Jun 2026 transcript) the plan is 2x capacity by FY28, full backward integration and EPS-accretive inorganic deals. The only 'change over time' is the planned shrinkage of the Dahua distribution business under STQC, and the only separation-related wording is hypothetical ESOP boilerplate in the February 12, 2026 postal ballot notice.

points.point: Management describes the manufacturing JV being absorbed, not separated: Dixon's 50% stake in AIL Dixon was bought in September 2024 (share swap, ~INR 4,000 crore deal value; Dixon retained ~6.6% of Aditya Infotech), making it a wholly owned subsidiary.
points.quote: Last year in September 2024, we then acquired Dixon's 50% stake in the JV, making AIL Dixon a wholly owned subsidiary .

verdict.rationale: There is no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale, hive-off or scheme of arrangement for separating a business anywhere in these texts — the premise cannot be supported from the material provided, and I will not invent one. What the texts actually describe is the opposite direction of travel: consolidation of six formerly separate family-owned businesses plus two acquisitions into one listed platform. The only scheme discussed is the amalgamation of Cohance into Suven Pharmaceuticals (shareholder approval with 99.99% of votes in favour, final NCLT hearing February 18, 2025, renaming to Cohance Lifesciences), alongside the acquisitions of Sapala Organics (oligonucleotides, consolidated from July 11, 2024) and a 56% stake in NJ Bio, Princeton (US$32 million revenue, 70% four-year CAGR, pre-money equity value ~US$100 million, US$64.4 million invested of which US$49.4 million secondary and US$15 million primary, with call/put on the balance after five years). The only 'separation' language in the texts is internal and organisational, not corporate: three distinct business verticals — Pharma CDMO (FY26 revenue INR 8.89 bn), API+ (INR 10.88 bn, –8%) and Specialty Chemicals (INR 2.913 bn, –2.1%) — each given a dedicated CEO with full operational ownership and P&L accountability reporting to the Executive Chairman, created after the resignations of Dr. Sudhir Singh and then Managing Director Dr. Prasada Raju. Investors did press hard on the structure — Varun Bang of Bandhan Life told the Nov 12, 2025 call that 'execution discipline seems to have collapsed' under Advent's ownership, Chirag Shah raised corporate-governance and selective-information concerns on May 12, 2026, and several analysts probed the ~4–5 percentage point gap between consolidated (21% FY26) and standalone (24.6%) adjusted EBITDA margins caused by loss-making subsidiaries — but management answered with remediation, BD hiring and recovery timing, never with a plan to separate anything. Nor did lenders or partners ask for a separation; funding is described as internal, with the stated intent to 'remain cash positive' and minimise borrowing. The nearest thing to a forward-looking structural review is new Executive Chairman and Group CEO Umang Vohra's statement on May 12, 2026 that a 'strategic blueprint' will be created by the end of FY27 — an intent, with no business named and no separation mentioned.
verdict.evolution: Dec 2024 and Feb 2025: the direction is combination — NJ Bio and Sapala acquired, Suven–Cohance merger cleared by shareholders (99.99%) with NCLT listed for Feb 18, 2025. Jun 2025 and Aug 2025: the merged platform is institutionalised into three 'engines of growth' and management explicitly frames organic and inorganic as 'two sides of the same coin', i.e. more bolt-ons, not disposals. Oct 28 and Nov 12, 2025: after the MD's exit the verticals are given standalone CEOs and full P&L accountability, and M&A is still described as hunting 'capabilities, not capacities'. Feb 2026 and May 2026: with revenue guidance cut to an early-to-mid double-digit decline and subsidiaries dragging margins, analysts press on the standalone-versus-consolidated gap and segment disclosure, yet the only structural signal given is Umang Vohra's promised FY27 strategic blueprint — no separation is ever proposed, and the April 27, 2026 filing covers only Vivek Sharma's resignation, Vohra's appointment and a new 25,918,613-option ESOP.
